output: Prescription Drug Monitoring Act of 2016 This bill requires a state that receives funding under the prescription drug monitoring program (PDMP) or the controlled substance monitoring program to comply with specified requirements, including a requirement to make data contained in a PDMP available to other states through a data-sharing single technology solution.

Promoting Financial Literacy and Economic Opportunity Act of 2015  Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for 50% of the cost of providing economic education and financial literacy programs to disadvantaged small businesses. Limits the amount of such credit to 20 for profit organizations.

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to revise the procedures for determining whether a State-appointed Board of Regents or Regents of the College of William and Mary (CWM) of the University of California will accept an accrediting agency or association as a basis for determining whether it will accept a CWM as a crediting institution. 
Requires such agency or association to apply procedures throughout the accrediting process, including evaluation, interim sanction, and withdrawal or termination of accreditation proceedings that comply with due process, including the right to:  (1) adequate specification of the agency's accrediting requirements; (2) written notice of deficiencies at the CWM's institution of higher education or program being examined and a reasonable time period to express such deficiencies to correct them; (3) advance notice of and an opportunity for a hearing by any such institution before the agency's decision making body prior to the agency's final consideration of imposition of an adverse action; (4) appeal any adverse action by the agency against any such institution to an independent and impartial arbitration panel appointed jointly by the CWM and the institution; and (5) the CWM's arbitration panel's decision, which may affirm

Contributions Legally Interdicted from Noncitizens To Our Nonprofits Act of 2016 or the CLINTON Act of 2016  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to prohibit a federal official organization from being treated as a contributor to a tax avoidance agreement with a foreign government if the organization: (1) accepts or solicits any contribution from any person connected to a foreign government, and (2) learns that such person is connected to a foreign government after the acceptance of the contribution. A federal official organization must: (1) knowingly or willfully accepts or solicit any contribution from any person connected to a foreign government, and (2) return any such person's noncitizen status to such person within 30 days after the person learns the status.  A federal official organization must also knowingly or willfully solicit or receive any contribution from any person connected to a foreign government if the organization: (1) accepts or solicits any contribution from any person connected to any foreign government, and (2) learns that such person is connected to a foreign government after the acceptance of the contribution.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to deny special rules for certain campaign committees in the case of a political organization to which this Act applies for any taxable year.  Exempts such committees from the prohibition against the award of campaign contributions if the committee's contribution limitations are not satisfied by the candidate for election to the House of Representatives or the appropriate congressional caucus.  Denies the lowest gross income (earnings) tax credit to a candidate for election to the House of Representatives if the candidate certifies, at the time of entering into a contract for the use of such broadcasting station, that he or she has not obtained any excess campaign contributions for the current election cycle.  Expands the election cycle to include the current election cycle, with specified exceptions.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish a limited fee for private activity bond issuance dates.

United States-Afghanistan Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) Act of 2011 - Directs the President to seek to negotiate and enter into a bilateral status of forces agreement with the government of Afghanistan. Provides that the status of forces agreement shall, to the maximum extent practicable: (1) prohibit the permanent basing or military presence of U.S. Armed Forces in Afghanistan; (2) provide a date, no later than one year after the agreement is entered into, for the complete, safe, and orderly redeployment from Afghanistan of all members of the U.S. Armed Forces, Department of Defense civilian employees, and contractors working for the Department of Defense; and (3) establish that the temporary presence of U.S. Armed Forces in Afghanistan is at the request and invitation of the sovereign Afghan government.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to establish a Return of Talent Program to permit eligible aliens to temporarily return to the country of citizenship in which they are engaged in post-conflict reconstruction activities, if the country is engaged in post-conflict reconstruction activities, and if an exception is granted to meet the special immigrant requirements described in the preceding clause.

Strategic Withdrawal of Agencies for Meaningful Placement Act of 2018 or SWAMP Act This bill repeals the requirement that the head of an executive agency: (1) submit a request for the Administrator of General Services (GSA) to issue a solicitation for the relocation of the headquarters of such agency; or (2) allow any state or local political subdivision to submit a bid for the relocation.  The GSA must establish a process to allow an agency to solicit a bid for the relocation within a specified time frame. The GSA may use the proceeds from the sale of any federal building or land to offset the cost of relocating the headquarters of an agency.

Minority Business Development Improvements Act of 2010 - Directs the Director of the Minority Business Development Agency (MBA) to establish the Minority Business Development Program to assist qualified minority businesses. Authorizes the Director to certify as a qualified minority business any entity that: (1) is not less than 51% owned or controlled by historically disadvantaged individuals; (2) each officer or other individual who exercises control over the regular operations of the entity is a historically disadvantaged individual; (3) the net worth of each principal of the entity is not greater than $2 million; (4) the principal place of business of the entity is in the United States; (5) each principal of the entity maintains good character; (6) the entity engages in competitive and bona fide commercial business operations in not less than one sector of industry that has a North American Industry Classification System code; (7) the entity submits reports to the Director at such time containing such information as the Director may require; and (8) any additional requirements that the Director determines appropriate. Authorizes the Director to enter into agreements with persons to provide technical assistance under this Act.

Directs the Secretary of Labor to make a grant to a public university with a school of public policy, a school of business, and a center devoted to the education of women, to establish the Center for the Study of Women and Workplace Policy.

Small Business Access to Capital Act of 2009 - Amends the Small Business Act to allow certain small businesses to include specified percentage of debt financing, but not more than 80% of the value of the collateral for the financing.

Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to authorize the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to approve, and revise, up to 50% of the financing of a small business.

Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 to require the Administrator to provide $150 million of SBA discretionary assistance to accredited institutions of higher education to include a business plan for the establishment of a business in such institutions.

Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009 to require the SBA to provide $150 million of SBA discretionary assistance to accredited institutions of higher education to include a business plan for the establishment of a business in such institutions.

Census Improvement Act - Prohibits the inclusion in the 2010 census of a person who is: (1) employed by or with the affiliation of an organization which has been indicted for a violation of federal or state law relating to an election for federal or state office; or (2) acting on behalf of, or with the express or apparent authority of, such an organization, and has been indicted for such a violation.

Requires the succeeding provisions of this Act to be enacted by Congress as an exercise of the rulemaking power of the Senate and the House of Representatives, respectively, and to supersede other rules only to the extent that they are inconsistent with such other rules.

Prohibits the government accountability office from considering legislation which would have the effect of repealing, suspending, or otherwise limiting the application of certain information collection and information sharing provisions relating to the procedures of that house.

Directs the Commission to: (1) establish a public Internet site at the address of a federal election campaign voter registration page; and (2) require the public to obtain the required reports from the site, or from the electronic method, during an election cycle if the aggregate amount of contributions or expenditures reported previously by the person during the cycle exceeds $25,000.
Provides for the sharing of the costs of obtaining such reports electronically with: (1) the public; and (2) the candidate and the candidate's office.
Provides for a program to allow the public to make software required by this Act available to the public on the Internet.
Provides for a requirement that the Commission provide for a report from the Internet to be included in the annual report of a principal campaign committee.
Expands the types of contributions eligible for primary campaign committee (PCC) elections to: (1) include all contributions received by the PCC in a report electronically during an election cycle; and (2) include the date of receipt of such a report.
Revises the election cycle requirements for a principal campaign committee to require the committee to file reports electronically during an election cycle after the date on which the subsection first applies to the committee as if

Requires the Civil Air Patrol (CAP) to be administered by the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, under the direction of the Secretary of the Air Force.  Outlines administrative responsibilities and Board of Directors. 
Provides for the appointment of National Biosciences Board members and Executive Directors.  Authorizes the Chief to assign officers and enlisted members of the Air Force on active duty and civilian employees of the Department of the Air Force to serve on the staff of the national headquarters of the CAP.  Prohibits the appointment or assignment of officers or enlisted members of the Air Force under this Act by any law or regulation prohibiting active duty members of the Air Force from participating in the management of non-Federal entities. 
Authorizes the Executive Director and National Board of Directors to use such CAP personnel and employees as the Executive Director and National Board of Directors consider necessary to administer the CAP and to ensure that it is capable of assisting the Department of the Air Force in the performance of its noncombat mission.  Subjects such powers to the requirements of the Federal Grant and Cooperative Agreement Act and the Federal regulations governing the provision of appropriated funds to private, nonprofit organizations.

Children's Bicycle Helmet Safety Act of 1993 - Authorizes the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to make grants to States, State political subdivisions, and nonprofit organizations for programs that require or encourage individuals under the age of 16 to wear approved bicycle helmets. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) Federal requirements for bicycle helmet use; (2) standards for bicycle helmet manufacture and compliance; (3) procedures for determining whether a bicycle helmet is in compliance with Federal requirements; and (4) failure to meet interim standards. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Electronic Employment Verification Reauthorization Act of 2008 - Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to extend the 11-year period beginning on the first day the pilot program is in effect.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to terminate the 11-year pilot program at the end of such period.

Requires the U.S. contractors who enter into a contract with the federal government to participate in the E-Verify program.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to verify the employment eligibility of existing federal employees by: (1) 10 days after notifying DHS of such election, if the employer has a violation of the Immigration and Nationality Act; or (2) 30 days after notifying DHS of such violation, if the employer has engaged in material violations of the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Requires the Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to establish a demonstration program to assist small businesses in verifying the employment eligibility of newly hired employees.

Requires the Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to submit a monthly

Selected Reserve Home Loan Equity Act - (Sec. 2) Revises the federal mortgage loan formula for eligible veterans to: (1) provide for a permanent mortgage loan for members of the Selected Reserve Home Loan (SRL) community; and (2) eliminate the 50% federal mortgage loan percentage limit for SRL home loans to veterans.

Revises the federal mortgage loan formula for home loan guarantee companies to: (1) provide for a permanent home loan guarantee fee table; and (2) eliminate the 50% federal loan guarantee percentage limit for such firms.

Revises the federal mortgage loan formula for home loan refinancing companies to: (1) provide for a permanent home loan refinancing loan subsection (2) loan to a Native American veteran; and (2) eliminate the 50% federal loan guarantee percentage limit for such companies.

Revises the federal mortgage loan formula for direct loan under section 3711 to: (1) provide for a mortgage loan to a Native American veteran of 1.25 and 0.50 NA; and (2) eliminate the 50% federal loan guarantee percentage limit for such loans.

New Aid for Trustworthy, Affordable Drugs Act (NAFTA Drugs Act) This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to seek to harmonize regulatory requirements for drugs approved for commercial distribution in any NAFTA country with those for other countries.  The bill requires the USTR to: (1) seek to enter into agreements with other NAFTA countries to harmonize such requirements; and (2) place a seal on the labeling of certain drugs in any NAFTA country that does not have such a seal.

Older and Disabled Americans Criminal Protection Act of 1998 - Authorizes a shared housing (a residential arrangement involving a caretaker and at least one elderly or disabled person) referral agency to request the Attorney General to conduct a search and exchange of criminal related information regarding any applicant for participation in a shared housing arrangement. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) who may use such information; and (2) penalties for misuse of such information.

Amends Federal civil service retirement system provisions to: (1) extend the retirement system to all Federal employees; (2) allow Federal employees to make contributions to and pay taxes under the system; and (3) allow a Federal Government account to be used to pay for retired officers' services.

Assault Weapons Prohibition Act of 1993 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit possessing, or transferring, an assault weapon or a possession by or under the authority of the United States or any State department or agency, or transferring such weapons after the 90-day period beginning with the effective date of this Act, except as provided under this Act, to:  (1) terminate; or (2) withdraw.

Open Our Democracy Act of 2014 - Election of House Members by State (House of Representatives) This bill requires a House of Representatives candidate to be elected to the office of Member of the House regardless of the candidate's political party preference.

Natural Gas Reserve Act of 2001 - Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to authorize the Secretary of Energy to establish, maintain, and operate a Natural Gas Reserve. Authorizes the Secretary to: (1) purchase, contract for, lease, or otherwise acquire, in whole or in part, storage and related facilities, and storage services; (2) use, lease, or dispose of such facilities; (3) acquire by purchase, exchange (including exchange of petroleum products from the Reserve), lease, or otherwise natural gas for storage in the Reserve; (4) store natural gas in facilities not owned by the United States; and (5) sell, exchange, or dispose of natural gas in the Reserve, including to maintain the quality or quantity of the natural gas in the Reserve or to maintain the operational capability of the Reserve. Conditions the Secretary's release of natural gas on a determination by the Secretary of Energy that there is a natural gas supply shortage. Requires the Secretary to submit to Congress a plan describing: (1) the acquisition of storage and related facilities or storage services for the Reserve; (2) the acquisition of natural gas for storage in the Reserve; (3) the anticipated methods of disposition of natural gas from the Reserve; (

Hospital Price Disclosure Act of 2005 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require hospitals to report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services specified data and to post notice regarding such data in accordance with the requirements of this Act.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) promptly post such data at each admission site of a hospital or center; and (2) annually update the procedures and drugs selected.

Requires the Secretary to establish rules for the classification of different procedures and for the assignment of items and services to those procedures.

Radio Broadcasting Preservation Act of 2000 - Directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to modify the rules authorizing the operation of low-power FM radio stations to prescribe minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels and prohibit any applicant from obtaining a low-power FM license if the applicant has engaged in any manner in the unlicensed operation of any station in violation of the Communications Act of 1934, except as expressly authorized by Act of Congress enacted after the date of the enactment of this Act. Prohibits any licensee from obtaining a low-power FM license if the licensee has engaged in any manner in the unlicensed operation of any station in violation of this Act. Declares that the FCC may not: (1) eliminate or reduce the minimum distance separations for third-adjacent channels; or (2) extend the eligibility for application for low-power FM radio stations beyond the organizations and entities as proposed in the FCC's (FCC) proposed MM Docket No. 99-25, subject to congressional approval. Prohibits any license that was issued by the FCC to a low-power FM station prior to the FCC modify its rules to

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) permit the use of qualified zone academy bonds for construction; (2) repeal the limitation on the taxpayers' ownership interest in such bonds; (3) allow creditors to offset the interest on such bonds by charging creditors a percentage of their proceeds which shall be used to pay off the bonds; and (4) allow the use of such bonds to fund state programs for the acquisition of qualified zone academy bonds.

Turkish Human Rights Act - Prohibits assistance under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 from being provided for the Government of Turkey (Greek: Kratis) for FY 1998 unless the Secretary of State determines that progress has been made in certain areas related to human rights monitoring and that the Turkish Government has:  (1) ceased all efforts to deny the recognition of the civil, cultural, and human rights of its Kurdish citizens; (2) has ceased its military operations against Kurdish civilians; and (3) has taken steps and instituted policies to demilitarize Cyprus and provide for the total withdrawal of Turkish military forces from Cyprus.  Directs the Secretary to report to the Congress on the determinations made by the Secretary.

Environmental Finance Act of 1995 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to establish an Environmental Financial Advisory Board to provide expert advice on issues affecting the costs and financing of environmental activities at the Federal, State, and local levels. 
Requires the Board to:  (1) work with the Science Advisory Board to identify and develop methods to integrate risk and finance considerations into environmental decision making; (2) identify and examine strategies to enhance environmental protection in urban areas, reduce disproportionate risks facing urban communities, and promote economic revitalization and environmentally sustainable development; (3) develop and recommend initiatives to expand opportunities for the export of U.S. financial services and environmental technologies; (4) develop alternative financing mechanisms to assist State and local governments in paying for environmental programs; (5) develop alternative financing mechanisms and strategies to meet the unique needs of small and economically disadvantaged communities; and (6) undertake such other activities as the Board determines will further the purpose of this Act. 
Directs the Administrator to establish and support an Environmental Finance Center in an institution of higher education. 
Authorizes appropriations.

High School Sports Information Collection Act of 2009 - Amends the Education Sciences Reform Act of 2002 to direct the Statistics Commissioner to: (1) collect annually from each coeducational secondary school that receives federal financial assistance that has an athletic program, information about the number of male and female students attending the school, the identification of teams that competed in athletic competition and for each such team, the identification of the teams that competed in competitive competition and for each such team, the identification of the teams that competed in postseason competition, and the number of practices and competitions scheduled; and (2) make such information available to students and public.
Generating American Income and Infrastructure Now Act - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to sell certain distressed notes and other obligations held by the Department of Agriculture (USDA).
National Youth Summer Jobs Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Labor to award competitive grants to eligible entities for summer job placement during the summer for out-of-school youths.

Medicare Pharmacist Services Coverage Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for Medicare coverage of pharmacy services furnished by a pharmacist, individually or on behalf of a pharmacy provider, and such services and supplies furnished as an incident to the pharmacist's drug therapy management service.

Reducing Barriers to Veterans' Benefits Act - Requires a military occupational specialty or equivalent (MOSA) to be considered incurred in or aggravated by service for which the Secretary of Veterans Affairs determines a presumption of service connection or a determination based on a presumption of service connection warranted by a military occupational specialty or equivalent. Requires the Secretary to issue regulations establishing the presumption of service connection and to issue a report on such determination within 60 days after it is determined that a presumption of service connection is warranted. Requires the Secretary to ensure that a member of the Armed Forces who receives an audiometric test at the 8000 Hz frequency (or other test that the Secretary determines has the ability to discover potential future hearing loss) receives an audiometric test at the 8000 Hz (or other test that the Secretary determines has the ability to discover potential future hearing loss) to evaluate the hearing of the member during the 90-day period before the date of the member's discharge, separated, or retired.

Coal Cleanup Taxpayer Protection Act - Amends the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to approve as part of a State or Federal program an alternative bonding system that will achieve the objectives and purposes of the coal mining bonding program and result in no greater risk of financial liability to the Federal Government or a State Government than the bonding program under this Act. Prohibits the Secretary from accepting the bond of the applicant itself (referred to in this section as a "surface coal mining contracting bonding system" or SCCB) or replacing it with another bond acceptable to the Secretary under this Act by the earlier of: (1) renewal of the permit; and (2) any major permit modification.

Requires the Secretary to notify all State regulatory authorities that allow coal mining operations to self-bond within 90 days after this Act's enactment.

Requires the Secretary to issue rules establishing limitations on surety bonds accepted under this Act to minimize the risk of financial liability to the Federal Government or a State Government, including rules regarding: (1) the maximum quantity of corporate surety bonds issued by any one corporate surety; (2) the minimum percentage of surety
United Nations Oil-for-Food Accountability Act of 2004 - States that the President submits to the Congress a certification that satisfies the requirements of this Act.

TANF Recipients' Lifeline Act - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to: (1) repeal the five year limitation on the benefits of assistance under TANF; (2) require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to determine whether a State to which a TANF program grant is made has violated the provisions of such program during the fiscal year; and (3) require the Secretary to reduce the annual TANF block grant program by 1996 percent if the Secretary determines that a State has violated the provisions of such program.

Stop Assistance to Counterfeiters Act - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to prohibit assistance for a fiscal year until a person submits to the President a certification for such assistance.  Defines "person seeking U.S. assistance" as a person, including an international or domestic organization that is not an association of national governments, that: (1) is seeking assistance under this Act or any other Act directly from the United States; or (2) subsequently receives such assistance pursuant to a contract, grant, cooperative agreement, or other agreement.  Suspends or terminates assistance if the President determines that the assistance will be used for a contract, grant, cooperative agreement, or other agreement that includes use of any intellectual property, provides evidence of the right to use the intellectual property, and provides evidence of the right to use the date of the first commercial use of the intellectual property, and if such assistance will be used for a contract, grant, cooperative agreement, or other agreement that includes use of any intellectual property provides evidence of the right to use the intellectual property, including a written license agreement for the use, the date of the first commercial use of the intellectual property, and any registration for the use with an appropriate government.

Developing Resources Immediately and Long-Term through Leases on Our Nation's Offshore Waters Act of 2008 or the DRILL NOW Act of 2008 - Declares that all federal oil and natural gas leasing and preleasing activities for any area of the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS) have no force or effect.

Revokes all withdrawals of federal submerged lands of the OCS from leasing, including withdraws by the President under the authority of the OCS.

Revokes all authorities given to the President regarding the leasing of federal submerged lands of the OCS, given under the Act.

Revokes all authorities given to the Secretary of the Interior regarding the leasing of federal submerged lands, given under the Act.

Authorizes the Secretary to petition the Secretary for authorization to conduct oil and natural gas exploration and extraction activities in any area that is at least 50 miles beyond the coastal zone of the state.

Requires the Secretary to deposit: (1) 25% of qualified revenues in a Clean and Alternative Energy Fund in the Treasury; (2) 25% of qualified revenues in the general fund of the Treasury; (3) 37.5% of qualified

Energy-Efficient Cool Roof Jobs Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to classify certain commercial and residential property as eligible for the tax deduction for depreciation (a process of reducing the value of business assets over time) of certain property used for energy conservation. Defines "qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property" as any roof system placed in service above conditioned or semi-heated space on an eligible commercial building and which has a slope equal to or less than 2:12, 36, or 48 hours of temperature change per degree Celsius, and which has a 3-year-aged solar reflectance of at least 0.55 and a 3-year-aged thermal emittance of at least 0.75. Defines "cool roof surface" as the roof surface of which a roof system placed in service above a commercial building's conditioned or semi-heated space and which has a solar reflectance and thermal emittance index of at least 64.

Federal Propaganda Prohibition Act of 2005 - Requires an executive agency (including the executive director of a nonprofit corporation or individual) to submit to each covered congressional committee a written notification containing the name of the contractor, the amount of the contract, the purpose of the contract, a summary of the statement of work for the contract, and any other information the agency considers relevant.

Prohibits an officer or employee of the United States from making or authorizing an expenditure or obligation of funds for publicity or propaganda purposes within the United States unless authorized by law.

Subjects an officer or employee of the United States to administrative discipline, including suspension from duty without pay or removal from office.

Requires: (1) an officer or employee of the United States to inform the target audience that the advertisement or other communication is paid for by the executive agency of the agency, and (2) the agency to disclose such communication prominently in its advertisement or other communication.

Requires each federal advertising or other communication paid for by an executive agency to include a prominent notice informing the target audience that the communication is paid for by the agency.

Confederate Commemorative Works Inventory and Joint Resource Study Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to conduct a full inventory of Confederate commemorative works and submit a copy of that inventory to the Director of the National Park Service.  Requires the Director to conduct a special resource study of works, commemorating and interpreting the Civil War, the commemoration thereof, the soldiers, people on the home front and battle lines, and related locations in the United States from 1861 through 1865.  Requires the Secretary of the Interior to submit a copy of that inventory to the Director for a report.

Ozone National Ambient Air Quality Standard Deadline Harmonization Act of 2015 This bill directs the Governors of each state to designate all areas of the governor's state as attainment, nonattainment, or unclassifiable with respect to the 2015 ozone standards.  The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shall promulgate final designations for all areas in all states with respect to the 2015 ozone standards, including any modifications to the designations submitted. The bill prohibits the 2015 ozone standards from applying to the review and disposition of a preconstruction permit application if: (1) the EPA or state, local, or tribal permitting authority determines the application to be complete on or before the date of promulgation of final designations, or (2) the EPA or state, local, or tribal permitting authority publishes a public notice of a preliminary determination or draft permit for the application before the date that is 60 days after promulgation of final designations. The bill also prohibits the CDC from: (1) completing, before October 26, 2025, any review of the criteria for ozone published under the

Endangered Species Community Advisory Board Act of 1995 - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish an Endangered Species Community Advisory Board in connection with the designation of an area as critical habitat or as a National Wildlife Refuge.  Requires that the Board:  (1) be comprised of 12 members appointed by the Secretary from among individuals recommended by the Governor of the State in which is located the area for which the advisory board is established; and (2) have as its chairperson a member of the advisory board who is an elected official of a local government and who is designated as chairperson by the Secretary. 
Provides for the payment of routine administrative expenses of the board established for an area from funds available for activities relating to study of the area to determine whether to designate the area as critical habitat or as a National Wildlife Refuge. 
Directs the Secretary to make available funds to facilitate the participation of individuals from the private sector on community advisory boards for the purpose of ensuring public input into the designation of areas as critical habitat or National Wildlife Refuge. 
Requires the Secretary, before designating any of the area under this Act as critical habitat or as a National Wildlife Refuge,

Freedom to Mourn in Peace Act of 2011 - Prohibits any person from carrying out a demonstration on the property where a funeral for a veteran is held that takes place within 150 feet of a road, pathway, or other route of ingress or egress from such property or from a cemetery or other property on which a funeral is held, any part of which demonstration: (1) takes place within 150 feet of a road, pathway, or other route of ingress to or egress from such property; and (2) includes as part of such demonstration, any individual willfully making or assisting in the making of any noise or diversion that disturbs or tend to disturbs the peace or good order of the funeral, or is within 1,000 feet of such property and impedes the access to or egress from such property, if there is visible, at each place that is at the applicable distance specified from such property.

Helping to Encourage Real Opportunities (HERO) for At-Risk Youth Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the work opportunity tax credit, to: (1) expand the work opportunity credit for employees who are certified as: (2) having attained age 16 but not age 25, on the hiring date, (3) as not regularly attending any secondary, technical, or post-secondary school during the six-month period preceding the hiring date, (4) as not regularly employed during such six-month period, and (5) as not readily employable by reason of lacking a sufficient number of basic skills.  The bill also extends the eligibility for such credit through 2019.

Save America's Utility Infrastructure and Secure America Now Act of 2008 - Amends the Federal Power Act to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to issue a rule regarding the enforcement of regulations establishing standards for the protection of consumers and property in connection with the generation, transmission, or distribution of electricity by power plants and substations.

Directs the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security, acting through the Assistant Secretary of the Office of the Infrastructure Protection, to conduct a study to examine gaps in emergency planning preparedness and management as related to vulnerable populations, including: (1) individuals with physical and mental disabilities, visual impairments, hearing impairments, limited English proficiency, and literacy barriers; (2) socially and economically disadvantaged households and communities; (3) individuals over 65 years old; (4) minor children; and (5) individuals with pets or service animals.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Assistant Secretary of the Office of the Infrastructure Protection, to report to Congress on the study and any recommendations of the Secretary.

Small Company Capital Formation Act of 2011 - Amends the Securities Act of 1933 to add a class of securities to the securities exempted under the Securities Act of 1933 (Act).

Directs the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to add a class of securities to the securities commonly known as the "exempted securities" (i.e., securities offered and sold within the prior 12-month period in reliance on the exemption added in accordance with this Act).

Allows the SEC to solicit interest in the offering before filing any offering statement, on such terms and conditions as the SEC may prescribe in the public interest or for the protection of investors.

Declares that: (1) the aggregate offering amount of all securities offered and sold within the prior 12-month period in reliance on the exemption shall not exceed $50 million; and (2) securities offered and sold publicly shall not be restricted by the issuer, the public interest, or investors.

Authorizes the SEC to require the issuer to file with the SEC and distribute to prospective investors an offering statement concerning the issuer, its business operations, its financial condition, its corporate governance principles

Federal Election Integrity Act of 2004 - Amends the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 to require a federal voter registration application to require a citizen to provide a photographic copy of any document that provides proof that the voter is a U.S. citizen.

Amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to prohibit state and local election officials from providing voters with a ballot for an election for federal office unless the individual presents to the official a current and valid photo identification. Prohibits state and local election officials from accepting any ballot for an election for federal office provided by an individual who votes by mail unless the individual submits a copy of a current and valid photo identification.

Amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to require state and local election officials to provide voters with a ballot for an election for federal office if they refuse to accept any ballot for an election for federal office provided by an individual who votes by mail.

Child Care Lending Pilot Act of 2003 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to authorize the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to make loans to small, non-profit child care businesses provided that: (1) the loan will be used for a sound business purpose approved by the SBA; and (2) each such business meeting all of the same eligibility requirements applicable to for-profit businesses.

Requires the Administrator to report to the congressional small business and entrepreneurship committees on the implementation of the program, including the date on which it is implemented, the rules issued pursuant to that implementation, and the number and dollar amount of loans under the program applied for, approved, and disbursed during the previous six months.

Flexible Refinancing for American Families Act of 2012 - Requires the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to each carry out a program to provide for the refinancing of single-family housing owned by such an enterprise through a refinancing mortgage having a 50-year term, and for the purchase of and securitization of such refinancing mortgages, in accordance with this Act and policies and procedures that the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) shall establish.

Requires the Comptroller General (GAO) to report to Congress on the adequacy and accuracy of the Department's budget projections for FY2010-FY2012, including the budget projections for health care expenditures, with respect to the fiscal year involved and the subsequent four fiscal years.
