(Sec. 1) This bill directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to study and report on the filing requirements for universal service support for certain telecommunications and communications technology programs. The FCC must report on the financial impact of those filing requirements on certain telecommunications and communications technology program participants.  The FCC must consolidate, or reorganize, redundant requirements for certain telecommunications and communications technology program participants.

Hunt Unrestricted on National Treasures Act or the HUNT Act - Requires each head of a Federal public land management agency to make available to the public on the agency website a list of the location and acreage of land more than 640 acres in size under the jurisdiction of the agency's jurisdiction to which public access and egress are allowed, including a list of the locations and acreage on the land that the agency determines have significant potential for use for such purposes. Requires the agency head to revise such list as the agency determines appropriate, including by motorized or non-motorized vehicles, on foot or horseback, and on the basis of certain existing easement rights-of-way. Amends the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 to make recreational public access to federal land for recreation purposes under the land and water conservation fund program in amounts not less than one and one-half percent of such moneys.
Clean Alternatives for Energy Independence Act of 2005 - Repeals the excise tax on certain gasoline and diesel fuels and the excise tax on alternative fuels.

Fixed Asset Relief Act of 2015  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the rate of the depreciation deduction for business equipment (i.e., computer software, water utility property, or qualified leasehold improvement property) to 100% and make it permanent.  The bill also increases the limitation on the amount of such deduction for certain listed property (i.e., automobile property, listed property listed property, and motorcycle property) to $8,000.

Amends the Siletz Tribe Indian Restoration Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to accept title to any additional number of acres of real property located within the boundaries of the original 1855 Siletz Coast Reservation (comprised of land within the political boundaries of Benton, Douglas, Lane, Lincoln, Tillamook, and Yamhill Counties in Oregon) if such real property is conveyed or otherwise transferred to the United States by or on behalf of the tribe.

Requires the Board of County Commissioners or other appropriate county executive of the county in which the real property is located to consider and evaluate as part of its reservation all real property taken into trust that shall be considered and evaluated as an on-reservation acquisition under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act and that become part of the reservation of the tribe.

Permits the Secretary to revoke any such approval of a Board of County Commissioners or other appropriate county executive that submits written approval of such consideration.

Requires the Board to consider and evaluate any real property taken into trust that is not later than 30 days after the Secretary receives the written approval of such consideration.
Measuring the Economic Impact of Broadband Act of 2018 This bill requires the Department of Commerce (D.C.) to assess and analyze the contribution of the digital economy to the U.S. economy.

Increasing Medical Oversight in the Department of Veterans Affairs Act of 2014 - Establishes in the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) the Office of the Medical Inspector to: (1) review the quality of health care provided to veterans by the VA, and (2) review VA facilities and services to ensure that policies and procedures are applied consistently at all VA facilities and services.  Requires the Office to report to the VA Secretary directly to the Under Secretary for Health, which shall include: (1) reviews of VA health care programs and activities, VA facilities and services, and VA health care programs and activities to ensure that they are applied consistently at all VA facilities and services; (2) investigations of complaints by a veteran, a family member, or another individual that may require a visit to a VA facility or VA facilities of the VA; (3) assessments to examine potential systemic issues within the VA health administration that may require the conduct of surveys, the collection of data, and the analysis of VA databases; (4) recommendations for policies to promote economy and efficiency in, and to prevent and detect criminal activity, waste, abuse, and mismanagement in, VA programs and operations; and (5) any other reports prepared by the Office

Rehab and Ahmed Amer Foster Care Improvement Act of 2012 - Amends part E (Foster Care and Adoption Assistance) of title IV of the Social Security Act to require states to: (1) provide notice to all adult grandparents and other adult relatives of a child removed from the custody of the parent or parents; (2) explain the options the relative has under federal, state, and local law to participate in the care and placement of the child; (3) describe the requirements to become a foster family home for such a child, including any options that may be lost by failing to respond to the notice; (4) provide a parent notice for request documentation of the reasons for the child's removal; and (5) establish procedures to allow a person who receives a notice to request, in writing, a court review of the decision.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to make calendar quarterly payments to states for calendar one (foster care) and calendar two (adoption assistance).

National Strategic Gasoline Reserve for Purposes of National Security Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to establish a Strategic Gasoline Reserve system with a total capacity of 10 million barrels of regular unleaded gasoline.

Directs the Secretary to determine strategic locations for no less than three and no more than five Gasoline Reserve sites, each located in a different geographical region of the United States. Requires the Secretary to consider all factors, including seasonal and regional variations in gasoline, cost, regional population, accessibility for distribution, and the region's vulnerability to natural disasters and acts of terrorism.

Requires the Secretary to submit to Congress, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the Governor of each State in which a Gasoline Reserve will be sited a plan for the transportation of the contents of the Reserve to wholesale or retail markets in the event of an emergency sale.

Requires the Secretary to conduct an annual review of the gasoline supply to ensure that the inventory is sold and replaced in a manner that assures the integrity of the product at all times.

Authorizes the Secretary to: (1) request additional information if the Secretary finds insufficient reasons for the sale of gasoline from the Reserve system; and (2) sell at full capacity any

Skill Game Protection Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to require the Secretary of Justice to prescribe regulations requiring each person who operates a game of skill on the Internet to maintain specified safeguards, including appropriate safeguards to ensure that the individual participant depositing funds is 18 years of age or older, to prevent fraud and money laundering.

Spearfish Canyon and Bismarck Lake Land Exchange Act This bill directs the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to convey to South Dakota, if the state conveys to USDA all interest of the state in and to the non-federal land (land) in the Black Hills National Forest in South Dakota, and to convey the same interest of the federal land in the Forest in the state.  USDA shall: (1) select an appraiser to conduct appraisals of the federal and non-federal land, and (2) convey the value of the land and the federal and non-federal land to be exchanged.  USDA shall complete any environmental analysis required under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 with respect to the land exchange.  USDA shall allow grazing on non-federal land.

Troubled Asset Relief Program Enhancement Act - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to require the Comptroller General (GAO) to have access to certain records of the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) that are held by entities participating in the program and that are used by the TARP, any entity participating in the program, and the Comptroller General to review the performance of the Troubled Asset Relief Program.

Requires the Comptroller General to be afforded full facilities for verifying transactions with the balances or securities held by, among others, depositories, fiscal agents, and custodians.

Prohibits the Comptroller General from publicly disclosing proprietary or trade secret information obtained under this Act.

Prohibits the Comptroller General from publicly disclosing any information obtained under this Act.

American Livestock Protection and Ranching Opportunity Act of 2014 - Amends the Animal Health Protection Act to prohibit the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) from: (1) allowing the importation of fresh meat or meat products from a country without vaccination if the country is free of foot-and-mouth disease, or (2) initiating, administering, or enforcing anyruins for the new importation of any fresh meat or meat product from that country.  Requires the Secretary to give priority to research and development relating to: (1) bovine brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis, and other zoonotic diseases in livestock that are covered by a high-priority research and extension initiative, and (2) loss of livestock due to fire condition.  Authorizes the Secretary to give priority to proposals from eligible entities that provide matching funds for grants for research and development in zoonotic diseases.  Amends the Agricultural Act of 2014 to revise livestock producer assistance requirements for loss due to brucellosis.  Requires payment of 75% of the higher of, and the applicable nationwide price of, the applicable livestock for the previous calendar year for the total number of livestock of eligible livestock producers subject

Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance Adjustment Act of 2002 - Amends Federal educational assistance provisions to: (1) increase the maximum amounts of such assistance; (2) modify the duration of educational assistance; and (3) increase the aggregate annual amount available for State providing administrative expenses for administrative purposes.

Strengthening Entrepreneurs' Economic Development Act of 2013 - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to: (1) establish and carry out a loan program, and (2) establish a process under which an eligible small business concern may submit an application to the Administrator for securing a loan under the program.  Directs the Administrator to: (1) collect a fee from lenders, and (2) establish a process under which lenders may issue loan applications.  Directs the Administrator to: (1) establish a process under which lenders may receive loans of $150,000 or less, and (2) annually issue guidance regarding prudent underwriting standards for loans of $50,000 or less.  Directs the Administrator to: (1) offer to sell such loans, and (2) contract with vendors for due diligence, asset valuation, and other services related to such sales.  Amends the Small Business Act to require the Administrator to: (1) assess, collect, and retain a fee not to exceed a certain percentage of the outstanding balance of the deferred participation share of a loan, as necessary to reduce to

Affordable Housing Preservation and Revitalization Act of 2009 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to ensure that funds in the residual receipts account of an eligible multifamily housing property are transferred, at the time of a qualified sale or exchange, to a preservation entity that is committed to maintaining the affordability and preservation of such projects by allowing expanded access to existing residual receipts to assist with the acquisition and rehabilitation of the project.

Defines "affordability and use restrictions" as the same as those in connection with project-based housing assistance payments under the Housing Act of 1937.

District of Columbia Government Improvement and Efficiency Act of 1996 - Amends the District of Columbia Act to reduce from ten to two five-member board members the number of Board of Trustees of University of the District of Columbia (UDC) College of William and Mary. 
Amends the Service Contract Act of 1965 to repeal the authority of the Service to enter into agreements with foreign governments for the provision of housing, refuge, and custody of District of Columbia (UDC) convicts. 
Authorizes the Mayor of the District of Columbia and the Director of the Bureau of Prisons to enter into an agreement waiving the requirements of the previous sentence or establishing an alternative amount to be charged against the District for such convicts, so long as the Director provides notice of the intent to enter into such agreement to the Committees on Appropriations, the Judiciary, and Governmental Affairs of the Senate not later than 15 days before entering into such agreement. 
Amends the District of Columbia Self-Government and Governmental Reorganization Act to exempt from certain contract review requirements certain judicial personnel of the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority. 
Amends the District of Columbia Government Comprehensive Merit Personnel Act

Children's Express Lane to Health Coverage Act of 2003 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to permit States to provide that financial eligibility requirements for Medicaid or for child health assistance under title XXI (State Children's Health Insurance Program) of the Social Security Act (SSAct) be met using a determination of the individual's family or household income or resources, notwithstanding any differences in budget unit.
State Prescription Drug Discount Act of 2002 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to provide for a State Prescription Drug Discount Program.

Minuteman Missile National Historic Site Establishment Act of 1998 - Establishes the Minuteman Missile National Historic Site in South Dakota.  Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire lands and interests therein and to transfer funds specifically appropriated to the Air Force for the maintenance, protection, or preservation of the facilities.  Requires the Secretary to transfer to the Secretary any funds specifically appropriated to the Air Force for the maintenance, protection, or preservation of the facilities.  Authorizes appropriations.  Prohibits the Secretary from affecting the use of any funds available for the Legacy Resource Management Program being carried out by the Air Force that, before enactment of this Act, were directed to be used for resource preservation and treaty compliance.

Joint Resolution approving recommendations of the Independent Commission on Medicare Concerning Methods to Control Outcomes under the Medicare Program for Fiscal Year 1990 (and subsequently requiring a sequestration of such recommendations). 
Title II: Controlling Outies under Medicare Program
Sequests (and subsequently requiring a sequestration of such recommendations) - Directs the Congress to establish a limit on total outlays to be made under the Medicare program for the fiscal year (1997) to:  (1) eliminate any budgetary excess in the Medicare program as determined before the first day of the fiscal year; and (2) reduce any outlays that exceed such limit. 
Amends the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 to require sequestration of amounts under the Medicare program in the same manner as discretionary appropriations and sequestrations.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior, in administering the System, to ensure that the mission and purposes of the System are carried out, except that if a conflict exists between the primary purpose of a National Wildlife Refuge and any purpose of the System, the conflict shall be resolved in a manner that first fulfills the primary purpose and achieves the System's purposes.
Prohibits the Secretary from initiating or permitting a new use of a Refuge or expanding, renewing, or extending an existing allowed use unless the use is compatible with the primary purposes of the Refuge and the System.
Directs the Secretary to identify, prior to acquisition, existing compatible priority public uses that shall be permitted to continue on an interim basis pending the completion of comprehensive planning.
Requires the Secretary to propose a comprehensive conservation plan for each Refuge or ecologically related complex of refuges. Requires the Secretary to develop and implement a process to ensure an opportunity for active public involvement in the preparation and revision of conservation plans and manage each refuge in a manner consistent with the plan.
Government Shutdown Prevention Act - Amends Federal law to provide for continuing appropriations in the absence of regular appropriations for a fiscal year.

Investment Tax Incentive Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a depreciation deduction for certain tangible property placed in service in a taxable year beginning after December 31, 1992.  Repeals the requirement that such deduction be based on a lost basis.

Deter Revolving-door Appointments Inourself; Stop Washington Appointees from becoming Manipulative Pursuit Act or the DRAIN the SWAMP Act - Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit any person who is a political appointee of the executive branch and who, within five years after the termination of his or her service or employment as such a political appointee, knowingly makes with the intent to influence any communication to or appearance before any officer or employee of the department or agency in which such person served, on behalf of any other person (except the United States), in connection with any matter on which such person seeks official action by any officer or employee of such department or agency, shall be punished as provided in this Act.

Restricts any person who is a political appointee of the executive branch and who, within five years after the termination of his or her service or employment as such a political appointee, knowingly, knowingly makes with the intent to influence any communication to or appearance before any officer or employee of the department or agency in which such person served, on behalf of any other person (except the United States), in connection with any such matter, in any way that would create an undue hardship and undue influence on the department

Requires a dealer of a new automobile to disclose to each consumer who purchases a new automobile the following information regarding any event data recorder installed on such new automobile: (1) the presence and location of an event data recorder; (2) the type of information recorded by the recorder and how such information is recorded; and (3) that the information recorded by the recorder also may be used in a law enforcement proceeding.
Requires any recorder in the vehicle and any data recorded on any recorder in the vehicle to be considered the property of the owner of the vehicle. Requires any such recorder to: (1) not be manufactured for sale, sell, offer for sale, introduce or deliver into interstate commerce, or import into the United States, unless the recorder includes a function whereby the consumer has the option to enable or disable the recording function of the recorder; and (2) not be made available for sale, sell, offer for sale, introduce or deliver into interstate commerce unless the consumer consents. Treats a violation of this Act as an unfair or deceptive act or practice under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Stabilize Medicaid and CHIP Coverage Act - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid program to provide that an individual who is determined to be eligible for Medicaid and who is enrolled in the state's Medicaid program shall remain eligible and enrolled through the end of the month in which the 12-month period (beginning on the date of determination of eligibility) ends.

Requires a state child health plan that provides child health assistance under Medicaid to provide that an individual who is determined to be eligible for Medicaid shall remain eligible and enrolled through the end of the month in which the 12-month period (beginning on the date of determination of eligibility) ends.

National Milestones to Measure Progress in Ending the Opioid Epidemic Act of 2018 This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop national indicators to measure success in curtailing the opioid epidemic, with the goal of significantly reversing the toll of opioid misuse and abuse within five years of enactment of this bill. HHS shall include with any such extension a rationale for why additional time is needed and a description of changes the HHS will make in order to achieve such goal.

(Sec. 4) Makes the fourth undesignated paragraph in the Act entitled "An Act to provide for the equalization of allotments on the Agua Caliente (Palm Springs) Reservation in California, and for other purposes," with its full equalization under the Equalization Act of 1959 (the Act) being deemed to have been completed. (Sec. 5) Removes from the definition of "Band" that the Agua Caliente Band is to mean the Agua Caliente Band.
(Sec. 5) Amends the Act to remove the fifth undesignated paragraph concerning reservation distribution to all members of the Band in equal amounts.

Special Needs Trust Fairness and Medicaid Improvement Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to provide for the Medicaid supplemental needs trusts to be expanded to include tobacco cessation services for mothers of newborns. (Sec. 3) The bill also amends title XIX to provide for the coverage of tobacco cessation services for pregnant women. The bill also amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for the Medicare coverage of tobacco cessation services for newborns. (Sec. 4) The bill also amends title XIX to provide for the Medicare Improvement Fund to be used for expenditures from the Fund for FY2021-FY2022.

Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to provide that a member of a reserve component who is ordered to report for military service for more than 90 days and who on the date of such order is a lessee of real property that is occupied by the member or dependents shall not be required to pay rent under that lease for any period of military service during which the member is assigned to duty at a location sufficiently distant from such property that the member is unable to reside at such property. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that a lessor shall have the right of refundable tax credits for the rent received on leases of reserve components members ordered to active duty.

Patent and Trademark Office Authorization Act of 2002 - Authorizes appropriations to the Office for FY 2003 through 2008 for: (1) fees collected in each fiscal year equal to those estimated by the Secretary of Commerce to be collected in each such fiscal year; and (2) the registration and protection of trademarks used in commerce to carry out certain international conventions, such as the Trademark Act of 1946. Requires the Director of the Office to complete development of an electronic system for the filing and processing of patent and trademark applications, that: (1) is user friendly; and (2) includes necessary infrastructure to allow examiners and applicants to send all communications electronically and allow the Office to process, maintain, and search electronically the contents and history of each application. Requires the Director to report to the congressional patent committees on the progress made in implementing the 21st Century Strategic Plan for the United States Patent and Trademark Office. Amends Federal patent law to authorize appropriations for FY 2003 and 2004 for the Office for the submission of periodic patent applications for new and existing questions of patentability.
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend temporarily the duty on certain surface and polyester fabrics.

Wholesale Motor Fuel Fairness and Competition Restoration Act - Prohibits an owner or operator of a terminal facility to sell motor fuel from the terminal facility to a distributor or retailer at a price in excess of the price it charges any other distributor or retailer, including one affiliated with a franchise or retailer which it owns or with which it is affiliated.

Makes such a sale inadmissible if it is made pursuant to the terms of a franchise or sales contract entered into before October 17, 2000.

Authorizes the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to assess a civil penalty, not to exceed $1 million, for each violation. Requires such penalty to be based on the distributor's or retailer's price in excess of the actual price.

Directs the FTC to issue regulations requiring full disclosure by refiners and distributors of their wholesale motor fuel pricing policies, including rebates, incentives, and market enhancement allowances.

Requires the FTC to transmit to the Congress a study concerning whether ownership or operation by a refiner of a facility for the retail sale of motor fuel has anticompetitive effects on the price of motor fuel.

Foreign Medical School Accountability Fairness Act of 2013 - Amends title I (General Provisions) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 to revise the requirement that a foreign graduate medical school must meet certain eligibility criteria to participate in the federal student loan program.  Grants a foreign graduate medical school the authority to participate in the federal student loan program if it loses eligibility to do so by the enactment of this Act.

Disclosure; and Encouragement of Verification, Innovation, Cleaning, and Efficiency Act of 2017 or the DEVICE Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require a manufacturer of a medical device to give the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) prior notice of any change in the design or reprocessing instructions of a device marketed in interstate commerce. The FDA must publish a list of the types of rapid assessment tests (RATs) that must be included in the list for each type of reusable device.

ESA Improvement Act of 2014 - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to prohibit the Secretary of the Interior from including in a list of a species in a state any population of a species in a state if the Secretary has approved: (1) a state protective action for such population; or (2) a list of such states, or each state so listed, that is under consideration for inclusion in the Secretary's proposed list.  Requires the Secretary to: (1) notify each state in which a population of the species occurs of the opportunity to submit a proposed state protective action for the species in that state, including specification of the criteria for such action; and (2) provide guidance to the state regarding preparation of a proposed state protective action.  Allows the Secretary to add a population of a species to a list before the date it is submitted, but requires that the list include specification of the criteria for approval of the action.  Requires the Secretary to: (1) approve or disapprove a proposed list list if it meets the criteria for approval of the action, (2) provide guidance on how to modify the list after the action is completed, and (3) provide a final decision regarding the action.

This bill grants a passenger vessel of the United States having berth or stateroom accommodations for at least 50 passengers a certificate of inspection only if:   the vessel is constructed of fire-retardant materials; and  the vessel is operating engines, boilers, main electrical distribution panels, fuel tanks, oil tanks, and generators that meet current Coast Guard regulations, are operating boilers and main electrical generators that are contained within noncombustible enclosures equipped with fire suppression systems, and has multiple forms of egress off the vessel's bow and stern.  Before December 1, 2028, such requirements shall not apply to any passenger vessel in operation before January 1, 1968.  Upon a vessel exemption from the requirements, the owner or managing operator must notify the passengers and crew members of the vessel's deck and galleys prior to the sale of any ticket for boarding and to be affirmatively recognized by such passenger.  The bill exempts passenger vessels from the fire-retardant standards of this bill only if:   the vessel is operating engines, boilers, main electrical distribution panels, fuel tanks, oil tanks, and generators that meet current Coast Guard regulations; and  the vessel is operating

Health Care for Young Adults Act of 2005 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicaid (title XIX) coverage of individuals under the age of 23 in states with no more than 19 years of age. Provides for additional Medicaid allotments for such individuals in certain cases. Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide grants to states to expand Medicaid eligibility for such individuals.

Lower Colorado River Multi-Species Conservation Program Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to implement the LCR MSCP in accordance with the Program Documents. Authorizes the Secretary to enter into an agreement with the states providing for the use of water from the Lower Colorado River for habitat creation and maintenance in accordance with the Program Documents. Authorizes the Secretary to invest with the Secretary of the Treasury such portions of appropriations, and any non-Federal contributions made pursuant to the Program Documents, as are not, required to meet current expenditures. Makes the non-returnable and the non-reimbursable provisions of the Program inapplicable to the LCR MSCP. Prohibits future acts of Congress relating to Public Law 93-205 (16 U.S. C. 1531 et seq.) from modifying the Program Documents unless expressly made applicable to the LCR MSCP. States that any party to any agreement entered into with the United States or any agency under the LCR MSCP may commence a civil action in U.S. district court to enforce the agreement or to declare the rights and obligations of the parties under the Program Documents. Waives the sovereign immunity of the United States of claims for money damages,

Rocky Mountain Nation Park Wilderness Act of 1997 - Designates certain lands in Rocky Mountain National Park, Colorado, as wilderness and as part of the National Wilderness Preservation System, and together with such lands, shall be known as the Rocky Mountain National Park Wilderness. 
Makes the designation of such lands and the Wilderness Act as wilderness and the Rocky Mountain National Park Wilderness inapplicable to certain lands within the Indian Peaks Wilderness which were transferred to Rocky Mountain National Park by this Act. 
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to file a map and a boundary description of the area designated as wilderness by this Act with the Committee on Natural Resources of the United States House of Representatives and with the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the United States Senate. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) the reserve of a quantity of water sufficient to fulfill the purposes of the wilderness designation of such lands; and (2) the priority date of the water rights reserved in such designation.

Congenital Heart Futures Reauthorization Act of 2015 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to: (1) enhance and expand research and surveillance infrastructure to study and track the epidemiology of congenital heart disease (in this case, CHD); (2) plan and implement a public outreach and education campaign to improve understanding of the epidemiology of CHD across the lifespan; and (3) award grants to eligible entities to undertake the activities described in this Act and to implement them and report to Congress. The CDC may: (1) expand, intensify, and coordinate research and related activities with respect to congenital heart disease, which may include congenital heart disease research; and (2) develop research networks. The CDC must consider the application of such research and other activities to minority and medically underserved communities.

Small Business Lending to Entrepreneurs for Growth in Underserved Populations Act of 2011 or the Small Business Leg-Up Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to transfer all unobligated funds in the Small Business Lending Fund to the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund.

Amends the Small Business Jobs Act of 2010 to direct the Secretary to carry out a Small Business Capital Investment Program to increase credit availability for small businesses.

Interstate Transport Act of 2018 This bill provides that a person who is not otherwise prohibited by any federal law from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a knife shall be entitled to transport a knife for any lawful purpose from any place where the person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport the knife to any other place where the person may lawfully do so if: (1) in the case of transport by motor vehicle, the knife is not directly accessible from the passenger compartment or is contained in a locked container other than the glove compartment or console; and (2) in the case of transport by other means, including any transport over land or water, the knife is contained in a locked container.  A person may carry in the passenger compartment of a mode of transportation a knife or tool: (1) the blades of which consist only of a blunt tipped safety blade, a guarded blade, or both; and (2) that is specifically designed for enabling escape in an emergency by cutting safety belts.  A person may carry in the passenger compartment of a passenger aircraft subject to the rules and regulations of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). A person may not be arrested for violation of any law, rule, or regulation

Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to authorize the Secretary of the Interior to grant an easement or right-of-way on the outer Continental Shelf (OCS) or activities not otherwise authorized in such Act, the Deepwater Port Act of 1974, or the Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion Act of 1980 when such activities: (1) support exploration, development, production, transportation, or storage of oil, natural gas, or other minerals; (2) produce or support production, transportation, or transmission of energy from sources other than oil and gas; or (3) use facilities previously used for activities authorized under this Act.  Directs the Secretary to establish reasonable forms of annual or one-time payments for easements or rights-of-way granted on a competitive or non-competitive basis.  Directs the Secretary to prescribe any necessary regulations to ensure safety, protection of the environment, prevention of waste, and conservation of the natural resources of the OCS, protection of national security interests, and the protection of the correlation of rights therein.

Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to report to Congress on a focused, in-depth Independent Safety Assessment of the design, construction, maintenance, and operational safety performance of the systems at the Indian Point Energy Center, including a detailed explanation of the factual basis upon which the NRC and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) relied in approving the radiological emergency plan and making subsequent annual findings of reasonable assurance that the plan will adequately protect the public in the event of an emergency, beginning on July 25, 2003, and continuing to the present.
Requires the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Department of Homeland Security to report to Congress on a detailed response to each of the criticisms of the radiological emergency plan and a detailed explanation of what criteria the NRC and FEMA use in determining whether or not reasonable assurance can be provided that the radiological emergency plan is adequate to protect public health and safety, including what threshold figures of injuries and fatalities are acceptable or tolerable in the event of a nuclear accident.
Requires the NRC and FEMA to monitor the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's Independent Safety Assessment Team with 25 members, composed of: (1) unaffiliated nuclear power industry

Alaska Native Veterans Land Allotment Equity Act - Amends the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to allow any person who served on the land that was to become known as the Alaskan Indian Reservation, or who would otherwise have been eligible for an allotment under that Act, to receive an allotment under the Alaska Native Veterans Land Allotment Equity Act.  Allows a Native Corporation to select an alternative allotment from land within: (1) a right-of-way of the TransAlaska Pipeline, or (2) an inner or outer corridor of such a right-of-way.  Allows an Indian veteran who served between August 5, 1964, and May 7, 1975, to apply for and receive an allotment on behalf of the estate of his or her deceased surviving spouse or surviving child.  Directs the Secretary of the Interior to issue a certificate of allotment to any person or entity that has an interest in the land that is potentially adverse to the interest of the applicant.  Allows a person that selected an allotment to withdraw it and reselect land in accordance with this Act after enactment of this Act.

Clean Water Compliance and Ratepayer Affordability Act of 2015 This bill requires the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to carry out a pilot program to work with and facilitate the efforts of municipalities to develop and implement integrated plans to meet their wastewater and stormwater obligations under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act (commonly known as the Clean Water Act) in a cost-effective and flexible manner. The pilot program must be consistent with the Integrated Municipal Stormwater and Wastewater Approach Framework issued by EPA in May 2012. The EPA must select at least 15 municipalities to participate in the pilot program each fiscal year. A municipality is eligible to participate if it: (1) is a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permit holder or designee; or (2) is operating under an administrative order, administrative consent agreement, or judicial consent decree to comply with the requirements of the Clean Water Act. Priority in the pilot program is given to municipalities seeking to develop and implement approaches that adapt to changed or future uncertain circumstances.

Requires LEAs to conduct audits of expenditures under this Act to ensure that funds made available under it are used in accordance with ESEA requirements.

Indian Employment and Training Improvement Act of 1997 - Amends the Indian Employment, Training and Related Services Demonstration Act of 1992 to authorize a tribal government to use a percentage of funds under the Act to waive statutory requirements and to consider the disapproval of any waiver requested by the Indian tribe. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to assign Federal personnel and resources to Indian tribes in implementing the Act. 
Requires the head of each Federal agency that otherwise has jurisdiction over a program that is integrated under the Act to permit a tribal government to establish a consolidated advisory committee to carry out the duties of each advisory committee that would otherwise be required to carry out the programs. 
Requires each agency head to waive any statutory requirement, regulation, or policy requiring the establishment of an advisory committee (including any advisory commission or council) to carry out the duties of each advisory committee. 
Requires each regional consortium of Alaska Native villages or regional or village corporations to carry out a project under a plan that meets the requirements of this Act through a resolution adopted by the governing body of each such entity.

Junior Duck Stamp Conservation and Design Program Act of 1994 - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to carry out a Junior Duck Stamp Conservation and Design Program to:  (1) provide to school children environmental education opportunities relating to the conservation and management of migratory birds; and (2) increase the capacity for schools, States, and other educational programs to conduct conservation and education programs. 
Requires the Secretary to:  (1) take appropriate steps to conduct the Program in all of the States; and (2) annually report to the Congress on the status of the Program in each of the 50 States. 
Authorizes the Secretary to annually conduct a competition to:  (1) solicit the submission by students at elementary and secondary schools of designs relating to conservation of migratory birds; and (2) select winning designs from among those submissions for use for licensing and marketing. 
Authorizes the Secretary to use the proceeds from such a competition to fund the activities and expenses of the Program. 
Authorizes the Secretary to transfer to the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation the Cusano bequest.  Requires the Foundation to:  (1) require the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation to enter into an agreement to

Russian Weapons Embargo Act of 2014 - Prohibits the head of an executive agency from entering into a contract, subcontract, memorandum of understanding, or cooperative agreement with, or making a grant to, Rosoboronexport to: (1) enter into a contract, memorandum of understanding, or cooperative agreement with, or make a grant to, Rosoboronexport; (2) make a subcontract, memorandum of understanding, or cooperative agreement; or (3) make a subcontract, memorandum of agreement, cooperative agreement, loan, or loan agreement related to the design, manufacture, or sale of military equipment.  Terminates such prohibition upon the President certifying to the appropriate congressional committees that, to the best of the President's knowledge, Rosoboronexport has ceased the transfer of lethal military equipment to, and the maintenance of existing lethal military equipment for, the government of the Syrian Arab Republic, the armed forces of the Russian Federation, and agents of the Russian Federation are not taking active measures to destabilize the control of the government of the U.S. over eastern Ukraine, including through active support of efforts to unlawfully occupy facilities of the government

Transparency in Judgment Payments Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to publish electronically, in a manner consistent with applicable federal privacy law: (1) the agency responsible for the payment; (2) a citation to the provision of law under which the claim was made; (3) the amount to be paid; (4) the amount of any interest to be paid; (5) the amount of any attorney fees to be paid; and (6) for any case filed in a court to be included in the report.

Requires the Secretary to submit quarterly to Congress a report that contains: (1) any information published during the preceding quarter; and (2) a confidential appendix that includes for each case or claim, the plaintiff, counsel for the plaintiff, and defendant.

Directs the Secretary to report to Congress on: (1) civil actions filed or pending against the agency or any employee of the agency; and (2) settlements entered by or final judgments entered against the agency or any employee of the agency.

Building Bridges and Transforming Resentment and Unfairness to Support and Trust for Municipal Law Enforcement Act of 2014 or the Build TRUST Act of 2014 - Requires a local government which received a grant under the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 which does not reduce a subgrant award made to it to receive only 50% of the grant award that would have otherwise been awarded to it under such grant. Requires that any funds withheld from a direct grant award by the Attorney General to a unit of local government which does not reduce a subgrant award made to it receive only 50% of the grant award that would have otherwise been awarded to it under such grant.  States that any funds withheld from a direct grant award by the Attorney General to which the Attorney General has granted a waiver shall be reallocated in accordance with this Act.  Authorizes the Attorney General to grant a waiver to any local government for good cause shown, and to consider the following factors: (1) whether, resulting from allegations of excessive use of force, false arrests, improper searches and seizures, fails to discipline officers sufficiently
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2009, the duty on certain personal electronic devices.

Fort Sumner Project Title Conveyance Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the Fort Sumner Irrigation District, located in De Baca County, New Mexico, under the Memorandum of Agreement between the United States and the Fort Sumner Irrigation District Concerning Principles and Elements of Proposed Transfer of Title to Fort Sumner Irrigation District Facilities, including any amendments to such agreement.  Specifies the costs of such conveyance, including environmental compliance costs.  Requires the Secretary to assure compliance with all applicable requirements under: (1) the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969; (2) the Endangered Species Act of 1973; and (3) any other law applicable to the property conveyed.  Prohibits the United States from further conveying the property unless the Secretary has provided for such conveyance by two years after completion of the requirements.  Requires the United States to have no further interest in, and shall have no responsibility for operating or maintaining, the Project.  Requires the United States and the District to have no obligations under the Repayment Contract.  Terminates such repayment contract upon completion of the requirements.

Voluntary Adoption Protection Act - Amends the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978 to make involuntary removal of a child a child custody proceeding under the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978. 
Amends the Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978 to revise requirements for the determination of the jurisdiction of a child custody proceeding involving an Indian child. 
Revises requirements for the petition to invalidate a child custody proceeding. 
Revises requirements for the petition to return a child to his or her foster care. 
Revises requirements for the adoption of a child. 
Revises requirements for the adoption of an Indian child. 
Revises requirements for the adoption of an Indian child by voluntary removal.

Gila Bend Indian Reservation Lands Replacement Clarification Act - Amends the Gila Bend Indian Reservation Lands Replacement Act to allow gaming on lands located north of the 33.2-degree latitude line in exchange for a specified amount of land in the Tucson metropolitan area.

Prohibits gaming on such lands if they are located north of the line in Arizona or New Mexico.

Campus Fire Safety Right to Know Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require each eligible institution participating in any program under title IV (Student Assistance) to prepare, publish, and distribute to all current students and employees, and to any applicant for enrollment or employment upon request, an annual fire safety report which identifies: (1) each student housing facility; (2) whether or not each facility is equipped with a fire sprinkler system or another equally protective fire safety system; (3) statistics concerning the occurrence of fires and false alarms; (4) the presence of adequate fire escape planning or protocols; rules on portable electrical appliances; smoking and open flames; regular mandatory supervised fire drills; and planned and future improvement in fire safety; statistics on campus; and (5) information regarding fire alarms, smoke alarms, and the presence of adequate fire escape planning or protocols, rules on portable electrical appliances, smoking and open flames, regularmandatory supervised fire drills, and planned and future improvement in fire safety.
Amends Federal law to provide for continuing appropriations in the absence of regular appropriations for a fiscal year.

Amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to direct the Director of the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services to establish an emergency preparedness demonstration program to research and promote the capacity of disadvantaged communities to carry out programs to provide data, information, and awareness education by providing grants to, or executing contracts or cooperative agreements with, eligible nonprofit organizations to establish and conduct such programs.

Territorial Economic Growth and Recovery Act of 2016  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the limitation on the amount of the tax on the U.S. 15-year periodical gain from the sale of certain U.S. distilled spirits.  The bill also amends the Internal Revenue Code to require the Department of the Treasury to pay to the U.S. 15-year periodical gain from the sale of certain U.S. distilled spirits to the possessions of the United States and to the residents of the United States in a manner similar to a refund due from the credit allowed under such provisions.

Urban Recovery and Growth Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2010 the authority of the Internal Revenue Service to collect income tax from businesses located in certain economic development zones. Defines "economic development zone" as a 100-year extension of an economic development bond issued between 1995 and 2010.

National Spaceport Act - Establishes within the Department of Transportation a National Spaceport Office, with a staff consisting of a director, 4 regional supervisors, and no more than five additional support staff.  Requires the Office to:  (1) administer the application and assistance programs; and (2) establish appropriate procedures for the competitive awarding of grants, the use of excess Federal property, and excess Federal property by excess Federal employees for educational launches and the transfer of excess Federal property to spaceports. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to subject to tax-exempt requirements a spaceport (as defined by this Act) to treatment comparable to an airport. 
Requires the National Spaceport Office and of spaceports to submit annual reports to the Congress on their activities. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Delphi Pensions Restoration Act of 2012 - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 to reauthorize through FY2012 the Secretary of the Treasury's Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) to provide for the transfer of proceeds from the sale of Troubled Asset Relief (TAR) warrants and senior debt instruments acquired by the Secretary to the Delphi Retired Employees Fund.

Establishes the Delphi Retired Employees Fund to be used by the Secretary in making such payments.

Veterans Traumatic Brain Injury Treatment Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish a program to screen veterans for symptoms of traumatic brain injury (TBI) and recommend improving care and services.

Requires the Secretary to carry out such program in four geographically dispersed polytrauma network sites designated by the Secretary.

Directs the Secretary to establish and maintain a traumatic brain injury transition office at each Department polytrauma network site to coordinate the provision of health-care and services to veterans who suffer from moderate to severe TBI and are in need of such care.

Requires the Secretary to establish and maintain a traumatic brain injury registry, to be known as the Traumatic Brain Injury Veterans' Health Registry, to include information on: (1) service eligibility and disability status; and (2) relevant medical data relating to an individual's health status if the individual grants permission to include such information in the registry.

Energy Development Program Implementation Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to develop: (1) strategic plans for the energy development program consistent with title V of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Act of 1978 (NNPA); and (2) implementation plans for such program.

Allows federal employees serving in an exchange capacity in the program to be considered to be detailed.

Requires the Secretary to report annually to the appropriate congressional committees on the plans and to the appropriate congressional committees on the feasibility of expanding cooperative activities under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Act of 1978 into an international cooperative effort.

High School Data Transparency Act of 2011 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to collect, annually, from each coeducational secondary school that receives federal financial assistance that has aninterscholastic athletic program, certain information about that school, including: (1) the total number of male and female students that attended the school, disaggregated and cross-tabulated by gender and race or ethnicity; (2) a listing of the teams that competed in athletic competition and for each team the data included; (3) the teams' expenditures for the team, including the travel and equipment expenditures, the equipment expenditures, and the expenditures for facilities, including medical and other facilities; (4) the total number of trainers and medical personnel and for each trainer or medical personnel an identification; (5) the total number of coaches and the identification of such person's gender, employment status, and expenditures; and (6) the total number of competitive events scheduled and for each an indication of what day of the week and time the competition was scheduled. Requires the Secretary to: (1) ensure that all students at the school are informed of their right to request such information, and (2

Recapture Excess Profits and Invest in Roads (REPAIR) Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax of 25% on the windfall profit of a taxpayer who produces or distributes crude oil or refined oil products for a taxable year beginning during 2008 or 2009. Defines "windfall profit" as the excess of the adjusted taxable income of the taxpayer for the taxable year over the reasonably inflated average profit for such taxable year.

Medicare Fracture Prevention and Osteoporosis Testing Act of 2007 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a national minimum payment amount for CPT code 77080 (relating to dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry) and CPT code 77082 (relating to vertebral fracture assessment), and any successor to such codes as identified by HHS. Prohibits the Secretary from submitting to the Secretary or the Congress a report on the results of the study, unless the Secretary and the Congress have agreed to conduct a study.

This bill amends the federal criminal code to require states to establish and enforce laws that prohibit a person from operating a motor vehicle while the person is using a wireless communications device to compose, read, or send an electronic message when the vehicle is in motion or part of traffic.  A person who is subject to a penalty under this bill shall withhold for a fiscal year from apportionments of that state for FY2009.
Stop Illegal Reentry Act or Kate's Law - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to increase the criminal penalties for alien reentry into the United States.

Good Samaritan Charitable Physicians' Services Act of 2018  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a physician to provide medical services without expectation of reimbursement and to an individual enrolled under a state or child health plan a fee that is published on a publicly available website. The bill defines "qualified charity care" as physicians' services that are furnished without expectation of reimbursement and to an individual enrolled under a state or child health plan. The bill amends the Public Health Service Act to limit liability for harm caused by an act or omission of a physician if such act or omission occurs in the course of furnishing qualified charity care and was not grossly negligent.

Homebuyer Tax Credit Improvement Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow a taxpayer who is married (within the meaning of the term "married" to include a spouse under age 18) to apply for a first-time homebuyer tax credit without a tax return; and (2) require tax return preparers to file returns electronically unless they reasonably expect to file 100 or fewer individual income tax returns during a calendar year.

Fair International Labor Standards in Trade and Investment Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Labor to have the primary responsibility for advancing the policy objectives and goals set out in this Act and for coordinating all related U.S. activities.

Patient Access to Disposable Medical Technology Act of 2015 This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of certain medical equipment that is primarily and customarily used to serve a medical purpose, but that would otherwise be covered as durable medical equipment. Specifically, the bill provides for: (1) the special payment rule for such equipment, and (2) a single payment amount for such equipment and services.

Gulf Security and Iran Sanctions Enforcement Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to: (1) include in each lease issued after enactment of this Act that authorizes drilling for oil and gas on the Outer Continental Shelf a provision that requires the lessee to certify annually to the Secretary that the person does not engage in any activity for which sanctions may be imposed under the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996; and (2) disclose to the Secretary, upon such certification, any participation by the person in any energy-related joint venture, investment, or partnership located outside Iran that involves: (1) any person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to Executive Order 13224; (2) any person whose property and interests are blocked pursuant to Executive Order 13382; or (3) any entity listed on the Appendix A of the Iranian Transactions Regulations and authorizes the Secretary to cancel the lease if the person fails to make such a certification or makes such a certification that is false.

Authorizes the Secretary to waive such prohibition on a case-by-case basis if it is in the U.S. national interest.

Encroachment on Military Bases Prevention Act - Amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to prohibit the Secretary of the Interior from designating as a national marine sanctuary any area that the Secretary of Defense has designated for use for military readiness activities, including any area the use or navigation of which is prohibited under regulations issued by the Secretary of the Army under the first section of chapter XIX of the Act of July 9, 1918 (33 U.S.C. 3). States that such prohibition shall not apply to any designation of an area as, or addition of an area to, a national marine sanctuary that takes effect before the date of the enactment of this Act.

Statewide PTV Access Act of 2009 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to apply secondary transmission provisions to the secondary transmission of any noncommercial educational broadcast station outside the station's local market and not served by another noncommercial educational broadcast station located within that market area. Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to allow a satellite carrier to carry the signals of a network of three or more noncommercial educational broadcast stations outside the station's local market and not served by another noncommercial educational broadcast station located within that market area.

Highway Fairness and Reform Act of 2009 - Amends Federal highway law to direct the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to carry out a direct federal-aid highway program in accordance with the requirements of this Act. Requires the governor or chief executive officer of a state to have the state's consent to a state's participation in the program. Allows states to elect to have their roads managed by the federal-aid highway program. Requires the Secretary to accept an election under this Act if the state: (1) has an interstate maintenance program and agrees to maintain the interstate; (2) submits a plan to the Secretary describing the purposes, projects, and uses to which amounts will be put; and (3) agrees to obligate or expend amounts received under the program exclusively for projects that would be eligible for funding under the federal aid program. Makes a state that makes an election obligated to have its roads managed by the federal-aid highway program. Prohibits a state that makes an election obligated to have its roads managed by the federal-aid highway program in any fiscal year if the state are not participating in the program. Transfers to a state that makes an election obligated its program funds. Makes the

Third Higher Education Extension Act of 2007 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to extend the programs under title II (Student Assistance) of the Act through March 31, 2008.

Extends the authority of the Secretary of Education to make grants to states, political subdivisions, and other entities to enable them to provide student assistance to eligible low-income students. Authorizes the Secretary to award such a grant only if the state, political subdivision, authority, agency, instrumentality, or other entity is an eligible lender.

Prohibits a state, political subdivision, authority, agency, instrumentality, or other entity from being an eligible lender under title II (Student Assistance) if it is owned or controlled by a lender solely because it is an lender under title II, and if the lender holds the loan or income from the loan solely because it is the sole beneficial owner of the loan and the income from the loan.

Prohibits a state, political subdivision, authority, agency, instrumentality, or other entity from being an eligible lender under title III (Block Grants to States for Aid to Agriculture) if it is owned or controlled solely because it is an l

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2014 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require energy management requirements for federal buildings to include not only measures not implemented but also those not implemented in the performance contracts and utility energy service contracts for which a federal agency has been given responsibility. Requires each energy manager in a federally-owned building to provide an explanation regarding any life-cycle cost-effective measure (energy management measure) that has not been implemented.  Revises requirements for federal energy management contracts to require a federal agency to provide a justification for any energy management measure not implemented in a contract.  Revises requirements for the payment of energy savings contract costs. Requires federal agencies to provide energy savings contract and utility energy service contracts to the public for the first year after the contract is finalized.  Revises requirements for the use of energy in the performance contracts and utility energy service contracts to require each entity to provide a justification for any energy management measure not implemented in a contract.  Revises requirements for the payment of energy savings contract costs. Requires federal agencies to provide energy savings contract and utility energy service contracts to the public for the first year after the contract is finalized.

Childrens' Internet Protection Act - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to exclude universal service assistance for services for schools, libraries, and theaters that fail to provide the certification required by the Communications Commission for schools that fail to filter or block material deemed to be harmful to minors.

Amends Federal veterans' benefits provisions to permit a member of the Armed Forces with a combat-related disability who is entitled to monthly retired pay computed using a formula specified in the above provisions to elect a retired pay base equal to $2,917, which represents the average monthly salary for high school graduates in the United States, as determined by the Census Bureau for 2006.  Applies such provisions to members who retired or whose names were placed on the temporary disability retired list after September 11, 2001, except that any recomputation of the retired pay for a member on account of such amendments who retired or whose name was placed on the temporary disability retired list before the date of the enactment of this Act shall be effective only for months beginning after the enactment of this Act.

Autofill Act of 2015 This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to require the Department of the Treasury to establish a program under which taxpayers may download forms relating to the individual income tax returns that are populated with tax return information (e.g., wages, withholding, and self-employment income) reported to the Department of the Treasury. The program must include a deadline for making such information available.

Intergovernmental Law Enforcement Information Sharing Act of 2001 - Directs the Attorney General to carry out security clearance investigations for the persons identified in subsection (b) and grant appropriate security clearances to all such persons who qualify for clearances under the standards set forth in applicable laws and executive orders.

Directs the Attorney General to: (1) investigate and report to specified congressional committees on the security clearances of Governors, Territorial, and Local Governors, Chief Governors, and Officers of State and Local Police; and (2) ensure that such information systems: (1) permit efficient and effective sharing of information among appropriate Federal, State, and local officials and agencies; and (2) are configured to allow efficient and effective sharing of information among appropriate Federal, State, and local officials and agencies.

Mobile Workforce State Income Tax Fairness and Simplification Act - Prohibits state income tax withholding and reporting for wages or other remuneration earned in more than one state from exceeding state income tax withholding and reporting unless the employee is subject to income tax under this Act.

Defines "employee" to include a professional athlete, professional entertainer, or certain public figures.

SIG TARP Small Business Awareness Act of 2009 - Amends the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 (EESA) to direct the Special Inspector General for the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) to examine the effects of the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) on small financial institutions and small businesses. Directs the Special Inspector General to also examine the effects the provision of financial assistance under TARP has had on small businesses, including both positive and negative effects and the extent of such effects on small businesses generally and by type and region.

Requires the Special Inspector General to include in each quarterly report to Congress information on the activities of the Secretary and any financial institutions receiving TARP assistance to include and utilize minorities (as defined in the Financial Institutions Reform, Recovery, and Enforcement Act of 1989) and women (as defined in the Federal Home Loan Bank Act), and any other information on the activities of the Secretary and any financial institutions receiving TARP assistance to increase the participation of women, minorities , and women- and minority-owned businesses, including recommendations related to increasing such participation.

King Cove Road Land Exchange Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey to the state of Alaska 131 acres of federal land in the Refuge as depicted on the map entitled "Project Area Map" and dated September 2012.  Requires the federal land to be conveyed to the state for the purposes of: (1) designating a road corridor through the Refuge; and (2) constructing a single-lane gravel road along such corridor.  Limits the value of the federal land and the non-federal land to be exchanged under such exchange.  Requires the state to select an appraiser to conduct appraisals of the federal land and non-federal land.  Sets forth provisions regarding: (1) the equalization of the federal and non-federal land values, and (2) the route of the road to be constructed.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) reduce the estate and gift tax rates to 30 percent; (2) increase the exclusion from the gift tax to $50,000; and (3) increase the annual gift tax exclusion to $50,000.
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 1999, the duty on certain HIV drug substances.

.  Veterans Serving Veterans Act of 2018 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Veterans Serving Veterans Act of 2017 to require the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to maintain a single searchable database of military occupational specialties and qualified members of the Armed Forces.  The VA shall hire qualified members of the Armed Forces who apply for vacant positions listed in such database without regard to the provisions of this Act.  The VA may authorize a relocation bonus to a qualified member of the Armed Forces who has accepted a position in such database.  The VA shall implement a program to train and certify veterans to work as intermediate care technicians in the VA.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the exclusion from gross income for gain from certain small business stock purchases (qualified small business stock) to 75 percent of the gain from such purchases; (2) reduce the holding period for such stock purchases; (3) exclude from the gross income of a participating small business the gain from certain incentive stock options; and (4) allow an increased tax exclusion for the incentive stock option.

Highway Infrastructure Privatization Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to authorize the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to make up to 15% of the total amount of qualified highway infrastructure projects eligible for tax-exempt financing. Directs the Secretary to allocate such funds among eligible pilot projects.

National Telecommuting and Air Quality Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to make a grant to a nonprofit private entity that is knowledgeable on matters relating to air quality for the purpose of developing a design for the proposed pilot program that would: (1) include recommendations for carrying out the proposed pilot program in each of the following geographic areas: (2) the greater metropolitan region of the District of Columbia, (3) the greater metropolitan region of Los Angeles, (4) three additional areas to be selected, after consultation with the grantee; and (5) report to the Congress and to the Secretary the potential significance of the proposed pilot program as an incentive for expanding telecommuting and reducing VMTs in the geographic areas for which the design is developed and the extent to which the program would have positive effects on national, state, and local transportation and infrastructure policies, energy conservation, and consumption, national, State, and local air quality, and individual, family, and community quality of life.

Cyber Preparedness Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to expand the purposes of the National Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Center (NCCIC) to include: (1) access to timely technical assistance, risk management support, and incident response capabilities, including attribution, mitigation, and remediation; and (2) information and recommendations on security and resilience. (Sec. 3) NCCIC must assist, in coordination with NCCIC, fusion centers in using information related to cybersecurity risks to develop a comprehensive and accurate threat picture. (Sec. 4) The bill expands the scope of NCCIC to include state and major urban area fusion centers. (Sec. 5) NCCIC must work to share actionable information related to cyber threats in an unclassified form.

Veterans' Access to Child Care Act (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide child care assistance to an eligible veteran for any period the veteran: (1) receives covered VA health care services at a VA facility, and (2) is required to travel to and from such facility for the receipt of such services. Such assistance may include: (1) a stipend for the payment of child care offered by a VA-licensed child care center, (2) direct provision of child care at an on-site VA facility, and (3) a collaboration with a VA facility or program of another federal agency. Such assistance shall not be considered as the VA's "eligible veteran's medical assistance," as the VA shall provide to a primary caretaker of a child or children who receive such assistance. (Sec. 3) The VA shall reduce the amount of its existing Medicaid payment to a primary caretaker of a child or children receiving such assistance. (Sec. 4) The bill also extends the requirement for collection of fees for housing loans by nursing facilities.

Federal Agency Anti-Lobbying Act - Prohibits federal agencies from using funds made available to them by the appropriation for lobbying activities for purposes of establishing a civil prohibition on the expenditure of appropriated funds by such agencies for lobbying activities. Makes exceptions to such prohibition with respect to: (1) President and Vice President; (2) congressional communications; (3) public communications on views of the President for or against any pending legislative proposal; and (4) information or technical assistance by a federal agency. Authorizes the Comptroller General to obtain the assistance of the Inspector General of the Government Accounts for purposes of this Act.
Public Good IRA Rollover Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income distributions from individual retirement accounts for certain charitable purposes.

Solar Stimulus for Job Creation and Energy Independence Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make the tax credit for investment in solar energy property permanent; (2) allow a tax deduction for the installation of solar energy equipment; and (3) exempt from the tax deduction for investment in solar energy property any loans for solar energy investment.

Workforce Training Enhancement Act of 2016 This bill amends the Trade Act of 1974 to allow a state to use funds to reimburse a worker's costs before the worker is approved for training. A "state" is required to have a certification from the Department of Labor that the worker is eligible to apply for training.

Right of Passage Community Service Act - Amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to establish a Right of Passage Community Service Program to provide students with the opportunity to serve in their communities after-school and summer programs.

Health Care Liability Reform Act - Authorizes punitive damages for harm caused by a drug or device manufacturer or product seller in a civil action for product liability if the claimant establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the harm suffered was the result of conduct manifesting actual malice. Prohibits the amount of punitive damages that may be awarded for a claim in any civil action from exceeding three times the amount awarded to the claimant for the economic injury on which such claim is based, or $250,000, whichever is greater.

Workforce Enhancement for Technology Transfer Act - Directs the Secretary of Commerce, through the Director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology, to direct Regional Centers for the Transfer of Manufacturing Technology and, when established, Manufacturing Outreach Centers, to utilize, when appropriate, their expertise and capability to assist managers and other workers in U.S. manufacturing firms in effectively utilizing and operating advanced and modern technologies:  (1) by making available assessments of the needs of U.S. manufacturing firms for worker training in the effective utilization and operation of specific technologies the firms have adopted or are planning to adopt; (2) by making available to U.S. manufacturing firms information on commercially and publicly provided worker training services, including those provided by U.S. sources, in the effective utilization and operation of specific technologies the firms have adopted or are planning to adopt; and (3) by making available to U.S. manufacturing firms accessible and affordable training services for the effective utilization and operation of specific technologies the firms have adopted or are planning to adopt when such training is not available from commercially or other publicly provided training services. 
Directs the Secretary, through the Director and in consultation with appropriate Federal officials and with leaders of industry and labor, to assist managers and other workers in U.S. manufacturing

Securing Protections for the Injured from Limitations on Liability Act - Amends the Death on the High Seas Act to provide that the Death on the High Seas Act shall include recovery for loss of care, comfort, and companionship (except loss of care, comfort, or companionship) under the liability provisions of the Oil Pollution Act of 1990. Repeals the limitation on the liability of a claimant for wrongful death, personal injury, or property damage arising from an incident arising from an accident. Prohibits the trustee of a substantial estate from selling or leasing, other than in the usual course of business, significant property of the debtor unless: (1) creditors holding at least two-thirds of the claims not paid by the debtor consent to such sale or lease; or (2) the court finds sufficient property to remain in the estate.  Allows the debtor's anticipated future income to be sufficient for a claimant to be liable under the liability provisions of the Oil Pollution Act of 1990 if the debtor's anticipated future income will be sufficient.

Unemployment Assistance Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income distributions from tax-exempt retirement plans, health savings accounts, Roth individual retirement accounts, and qualified tuition programs.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax on imported crude oil and refined petroleum products. Defines "crude oil" to include crude oilcondensates and natural gasoline but does not include domestic crude oil.
