Psychological Kevlar Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to develop and implement a plan to incorporate evidence-based preventive and early-intervention measures, practices, or procedures that reduce the likelihood that personnel in combat will develop post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or other stress-related psychopathologies (including substance use conditions). Directs the Secretary to: (1) work with the Department of Veterans Affairs and the National Institutes of Health to research and implement best practices for information dissemination to enlisted personnel, officers, unit commanders, primary care providers, and other medical personnel, and families of members of the Armed Forces; and (2) establish a new Working Group to research and develop evidence-based preventive and early intervention measures, practices, or procedures that reduce the likelihood that such personnel will develop PTSD or other stress-related psychopathologies.

Amends the Agricultural Act of 1949 to permit the permitted hay and grazing of reduced acreage, acreage devoted to a conservation use, and acreage diverted from production under a land diversion program to be done: (1) in the five-month period established by the State committee for a State; or (2) during the five-month period thereafter established by the Secretary of Agriculture.

Artists' Contribution to American Heritage Act of 1999 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax deduction for the fair market value of certain literary, musical, artistic, or scholarly compositions, or similar property, created by the taxpayer and donated to him or her by an eligible donor.  Limits the amount of such deduction to the artistic adjusted gross income of the taxpayer.

Superfund Research, Development, and Demonstration Act of 1999 - Amends the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 to reauthorize appropriations for FY 2004 through 2006 for the Superfund Innovative Treatment and Evaluation (SITE) program.  Authorizes appropriations for each of FY 2000 through 2004 for the SITE program.  Requires each such project to be eligible for FY 2000 through 2004 if the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) determines that: (1) the Administrator intends to enter into agreements with persons, public entities (including the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, and other Federal agencies), and nonprofit private entities to arrange for the use of other sites appropriate for carrying out hazardous substances research, testing, evaluation, development, and demonstration projects; and (2) the Administrator, in order to reach FY 2004, has determined that the Administrator intends to enter into agreements with the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, and other Federal agencies to ensure the effective transfer to those

African Free Trade Initiative Act - Amends the African Growth and Opportunity Act to direct the President to develop a plan for negotiating and entering into one or more free trade agreements with all sub-Saharan African countries.

Diamond-Blackfan Anemia Research and Care Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to: (1) expand NIH research and related activities with regard to Diamond-Blackfan anemia; and (2) make grants to, or enter into contracts with, public or private entities to support a comprehensive research initiative to study, develop better treatments for, and ultimately find a cure for such anemia. Allows the Director to include research on: (1) the links of Diamond-Blackfan anemia to chronic diseases; (2) red cell differentiation; (3) the pathophysiology of such anemia; (4) the relationship between such anemia and predisposition to cancer; and (5) congenital anomalies in such anemia patients. Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director, to establish a comprehensive clinical care center for such anemia where a majority of the patients with the disease are examined, treated, and tracked through the registry, by experts in the disease.

Amends Federal law to: (1) make the prohibition against interment in national cemeteries inapplicable to persons convicted of committing capital crimes in military cemeteries; (2) prohibit the interment of a person convicted of a capital offense in a cemetery unless a good faith effort has been made to determine whether the person is a person convicted of a capital offense in military or otherwise ineligible for such interment or cemeteries; and (3) deny funeral honors to a person convicted of committing a heinous act for which a good faith effort has been made. Prohibits the Secretary of the Army from ensuring that funeral honors are provided to a person convicted of a capital offense in a cemetery unless a good faith effort has been made to determine whether such person is a person convicted of a capital offense in military or otherwise ineligible for such cemeteries. Directs the Secretary of the Army to remove the remains of Russell Wayne Wagner from Arlington National Cemetery.

Economic Fairness for Seniors Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to: (1) increase the monthly premium for 2009 Medicare part B (Supplementary Medical Insurance); (2) extend through 2010 the Medicare part B premium assistance; and (3) allow an individual who is entitled to Medicare or who is eligible for Medicare part B a special tax credit for certain government retirees.

Amends the American Recovery and Reinvestment Tax Act of 2009 to revise the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for 2010. Requires the Consumer Price Index to be adjusted for inflation using the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers (CPI-W) and if the elderly are being financially disadvantaged by the use of the CPI-W, to prepare a CPI-E.

Colombian Temporary Protected Status Act of 2002 - Expresses the sense of Congress that, in view of the recent escalation of the current civil war in Colombia, Colombia qualifies for designation under the Immigration and Nationality Act pursuant to which Colombian nationals would be eligible for temporary protected status in the United States. States that such designation shall continue for one year.

Authorizes the Chief of the National Guard to establish and operate up to five National Guard schools for the provision by the National Guard of training in drug interdiction and counter-drug activities, and drug demand reduction activities, to the personnel of specified agencies, states, and local law enforcement agencies.

Amends the Carl D. Perkins Vocational and Technical Education Act of 1998 to revise the definition of "Indian student count" for purposes of determining the enrollment of students in tribally controlled postsecondary vocational and technical institutions.
Veterans TRICARE Choice Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to permit a TRICARE-eligible individual to elect at any time to be ineligible to enroll in the TRICARE program.

American Worker Mobility Act of 2014 - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to grant a relocation subsidy to an individual who: (1) is totally unemployed and has exhausted all rights to regular compensation under the law of a state or under federal law for a job opportunity that provides a reasonable expectation of long-term duration in the applicant's current residence; (2) has exhausted all rights to regular compensation under the law of a state or under federal law for a job opportunity that provides a reasonable expectation of long-term duration in the applicant's current residence; (3) has not received a relocation subsidy in the 2-year period preceding such date of application; and (4) is able to work, available to work, and actively seeking work. Prohibits the Secretary from granting a relocation subsidy to an individual under this Act unless the Secretary determines that: (1) the individual will have to repay the loan or employer's regular compensation within a specified time frame, and (2) the individual has obtained a bona fide offer of suitable employment in the area in which the individual wishes to relocate.

Native American Commercial Driving Training and Technical Assistance Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Labor to make competitive grants to tribal colleges or universities and to private trucking firms or companies to support programs providing training and certificates leading to the licensing of Native Americans with respect to commercial vehicle driving.

Gives priority to grant applications that: (1) propose training that exceeds proposed minimum standards for training tractor-trailer drivers; (2) propose training that exceeds the entry level truck driver certification standards set by the Professional Truck Driver Institute; and (3) propose an education partnership with a private trucking firm, trucking association, or similar entity to ensure the effectiveness of the grant program.

Prescription Drug Labeling Promotion Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a working group to develop and promulgate guidance constituting best practices on access to prescription drug labeling for the visually impaired. Requires the working group to promulgate guidance on best practices for pharmacies to ensure that blind and visually impaired individuals have safe, consistent, reliable, and independent access to the information in the labeling of prescription drugs.

Directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review and report to Congress on the extent to which pharmacies are complying with best practices.

Religious Liberty and Charitable Donation Protection Act of 1997 - Amends Federal law to prohibit a trustee of a religious or charitable entity from considering a transfer of a charitable contribution to a qualified religious or charitable entity or organization covered by the Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993 as a transfer of a charitable contribution to a religious or charitable entity or organization which is not covered by such Act. 
Provides that a transfer of a charitable contribution to a qualified religious or charitable entity or organization shall not be considered to be a transfer covered under the Act if:  (1) the amount of the contribution does not exceed 15 percent of the debtor's gross annual income; or (2) the contribution made by a debtor exceeding the percentage amount of gross income does not exceed 15 percent of the debtor's income in which the transfer was made. 
Provides that a trustee of a religious or charitable entity shall not apply to a transfer of a charitable contribution that is not covered by the Act if:  (1) the amount of the contribution does not exceed 15 percent of the debtor's gross income; or (2) the contribution made by a debtor exceeding the percentage amount of gross income does

Federal Credit Cost Reduction Act of 1994 - Amends the Federal Credit Reform Act of 1990 and the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to provide that a separate listing of administrative costs for direct and loan guarantees computed on a cash accounting basis for any such loans and guarantees originating before enactment of this Act shall be included in the President's annual budget submission. 
Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to provide that a point of order in the House of Representatives or the Senate against consideration of any concurrent budget resolution that would allow the maximum permissible subsidy rate for any covered program to be breached shall be considered in the House of Representatives or the Senate. 
Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to provide that a budget resolution for any fiscal year that would allow maximum credit authority (that does not cause the maximum permissible subsidy rate) for any covered program to be breached shall be considered in the Senate budget resolution.

Amends the Trade Act of 1974 and the Trade Preference Act to require the President, in order to enter into negotiations with the Attorney General for the establishment of a trade agreement in the U.S. trade area of the Americas, to consider the following in the President's final decision:  (1) whether the trade agreement will benefit the U.S. economy; and (2) whether the U.S. government would be in a position to take such trade agreement into account in its own domestic development plan. 
Amends the Trade Preference Act to direct the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), in order to enter into negotiations with the U.S. Attorney General for the establishment of a trade agreement in the Caribbean Basin, to consider the following in the President's final decision:  (1) whether the trade agreement will benefit the U.S. economy; and (2) whether the U.S. government would be in a position to take such trade agreement into account in its own domestic development plan.

Syrian War Crimes Accountability Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of State to report to Congress on war crimes and crimes against humanity in Syria, including violations of internationally recognized human rights and crimes against humanity perpetrated during the civil war in Syria, including: (1) an account of the war crimes and crimes against humanity perpetrated by the regime of President Bashar al-Assad, (2) an account of the war crimes and crimes against humanity perpetrated by violent extremist groups and other combatants in the conflict, and (3) a description of efforts by the Department of State and the U.S. Agency for International Development to ensure accountability for violations of internationally recognized human rights and crimes against humanity perpetrated against the people of Syria by the regime of President Bashar al-Assad, violent extremist groups, and other combatants involved in the conflict, including: (1) a description of initiatives that the U.S. government has undertaken to train investigators in Syria on how to document, investigate, and develop findings of war crimes and crimes against humanity; (2) a description of the strategy and implementation efforts to ensure accountability for such crimes; and (3) an assessment of the impact of those initiatives. Veterans Life Insurance Opportunity Act of 1998 - Provides for a special period for certain veterans to convert to a Veterans' Group Life Insurance policy.
Mortgage Insurance Fairness Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow the deduction of premiums for mortgage insurance. Provides for the phaseout of such deduction in certain taxable years.

International Rule of Law and Antiterrorism Act of 2003 - Directs the President to: (1) direct the U.S. Permanent Representative to the United Nations (UN) to use the U.S. vote to establish negotiations with the United Nations and the United Nations member states to establish a professional United Nations civilian police corps; (2) direct the Secretary of State to request that the U.N. Secretariat prepare a report concerning the establishment of such a corps; and (3) direct the Secretary of State to work with the U.N. Secretariat and other UN member states to establish standards and training programs for international civilian police.

Expresses the sense of Congress that a professional U Nations civilian police corps should: (1) be composed of the appropriate number of law enforcement professionals recruited and employed by the United Nations (U.N.) and trained and equipped for civilian policing functions in U.N. international peace operations and available for rapid deployment to such international peace operations as needed; (2) be able to deploy not later than 15 days after a deployment is authorized pursuant to a U.N. Security Council resolution; (3) be managed by the U.N. Civilian Police Division, which shall be required to plan

Protecting Seniors' Medicare Advantage Financing Fund Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to eliminate the 2015 PACA enhanced Medicaid FMAP for prospective payors, purposes of the Medicare Advantage (MA) stabilization program.  (Currently, the 2015 FMAP is the same amount that is appropriated to the Treasury for the payment of reimbursement by the Secretary of Health and Human Services of the cost of the prospective payors' benefits under part B of title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act.)  The MA stabilization program is amended to require the Secretary to distribute, not later than December 31, 2014, to each eligible MA plan a PMPM stabilization funding amount.

Hygiene Assistance for Families of Infants and Toddlers Act of 2017 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to make grants to eligible entities to conduct demonstration projects to help families with eligible children address the diapering needs of such children.  HHS must report on the number of children and families receiving assistance under the projects and the methods used to distribute diapers and diaper supplies.

Block Access to North Korea Act of 2016 or BANK Act of 2016 This bill expresses the sense of Congress that:   providers of specialized financial messaging services are a critical link to the international financial system,   directly providing specialized financial messaging services to, or enabling or facilitating direct or indirect access to such messaging services for financial institution is inconsistent with the United Nations Security Council Resolution 2094, and   the United States reaffirms its commitment to allies in the region.   The President shall impose sanctions pursuant to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act with respect to a person who continues to knowingly and directly provide specialized financial messaging services to, or knowingly enable or facilitate direct or indirect access to, such messaging services for:   the Central Bank of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea,   a financial institution that facilitates any transaction or transactions or provides significant financial services for nuclear development or proliferation for or on behalf of North Korea, or   a person identified on the list of specially designated nides and blocked persons maintained by the Office of Foreign Assets Control of the Department of the Treasury by reason of assisting the nuclear development or proliferation efforts of North Korea. Name Matching for Enforcement and Security Act of 2001 - Requires the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, the Secretary of the Treasury, the Commissioner of Immigration and Naturalization, and the Director of Central Intelligence to develop and implement a unified electronic data system to provide current and immediate access to information in databases of U.S. law enforcement agencies and the intelligence community relevant to determine whether to issue a visa or to determine the admissibility of an alien to the United States. Requires the unified electronic database to: (1) have the capacity to match names even when those names are entered and stored in different fields within the different databases; (2) be searchable on a linguistically sensitive basis; (3) provide adequate user support; (4) be developed in consultation with private sector firms; and (5) utilize commercially available platforms. Requires the unified database to be developed and implemented for no more than 4 languages designated as high priorities by the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, and the Director of Central Intelligence. Requires the Director of Central Intelligence to report on progress in implementing this Act. Mary Jo Lawyer Spano Mesothelioma Patient Registry Act of 2015 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry to develop a patient registry to collect data on mesothelioma. The agency must use the registry to: (1) enhance and expand infrastructure and activities for tracking the epidemiology of mesothelioma patients; (2) collect, consolidate, and report on health information on mesothelioma patients; (3) describe the incidence and prevalence of mesothelioma in the United States; (4) facilitate research on mesothelioma; and (5) examine factors that may be associated with mesothelioma.

Amends Federal law to require that funds for such activities be available for the payment of costs incurred by the National Guard in conducting international military-to-civilian contacts, civilian-to-civilian contacts, and comparable activities for purposes as follows:  (1) to support the objectives of the commander of the combatant command in conducting such activities; (2) to build international civil-military partnerships and capacity; (3) to strengthen cooperation between the departments and agencies of the United States and foreign governments; and (4) to facilitate intergovernmental collaboration between the United States and foreign governments. 
Requires that funds for such activities be not available for the participation of a member of the National Guard in such contacts and activities in a foreign country unless jointly approved by the combatant command and the chief of mission concerned. 
Requires reimbursement of the Secretary of Defense for such costs. 
Requires the head of a Federal department or agency other than the Department of Defense (DOD) to reimburse the Secretary for the costs associated with the participation of personnel of the United States in such contacts and activities.

Family Farmer Bankruptcy Clarification Act of 2013 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to allow a governmental unit, upon filing a petition for a discharge from debt, to file a claim for a debtor's discharge claim that arises before the filing of the petition, or that arises after the petition, and before the debtor's discharge, if the estate of the debtor are liquidated in a case under chapter 7 of this Act.  Provides for the payment of a claimant for a discharge arising after the date on which the petition was filed.

Amends the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 to require the Secretary of Energy to complete a study on the impact of state and local performance benchmarking and disclosure policies, and any associated building efficiency policies, for commercial and multifamily buildings and the impact of programs and systems in which utilities provide aggregated information regarding whole building energy consumption and usage information to owners of multitenant commercial, residential, and mixed-use buildings. Requires the Secretary to submit a report on the results of the study to specified congressional committees. Requires the Secretary to report to such committees on the progress made in complying with this Act.

Encouraging Mortgage Modifications Act of 2008 - Amends the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act of 1974 to prescribe guidelines under which a servicer of a loan or a mortgage modification or workout plan must act to the best interests of all such investors and parties if the servicer agrees to or implements a qualified loan modification or workout plan for a qualified residential mortgage, or if, and only if, such efforts are unsuccessful or infeasible.

Defines "qualified loan modification or workout plan" as a contract, modification, or plan relating to a qualified residential mortgage loanconsummated on or after January 1, 2004, with respect to which: (1) payment default on the loan or loans has occurred, is imminent, or is reasonably foreseeable; (2) the dwelling securing the loan or loans is the primary residence of the owner; (3) the servicer reasonably believes that the anticipated recovery under the loan modification or workout plan will exceed the anticipated recovery through foreclosure, on a net present value basis; (4) the effective period runs for at least five years from the date of adoption of the plan, or until the borrower sells or refinances

District of Columbia College Access Improvement Act of 2002 - Amends the District of Columbia College Access Act of 1999 to: (1) increase the maximum amount of Federal funds appropriated for the District of Columbia public school and private school programs from $17,000,000 to $17 million; and (2) limit the aggregate amount of Federal funds for such programs to $17 million.

American Heroes Act - Allows a State to provide one statue of an individual representing that State which shall be displayed in the Capitol Visitor Center.  Requires the Architect of the Capitol to procure and install a statue honoring the passengers of United Airlines flight number 93 who died on September 11, 2001, for their heroic role in protecting Washington, D.C.  Authorizes appropriations.

Fair Wage Act - Amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to increase the federal minimum wage for employees to: (1) $8.00 an hour, beginning 30 days after the enactment of this Act or January 1, 2017, whichever date is earlier; (2) $9.00 an hour, beginning 1 year after such date; (3) 2 years after such date; and (4) the amount determined by the Secretary of Labor (based on the amount of the Consumer Price Index for urban wage and clerical worker jobs) for a year.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 6.2% of the wages paid by an employer who is found to be underutilizing an employer's existing employment and overutilizing employees.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for the hiring of a qualified mentor during the taxable year. Defines "qualified mentor" as an individual who has attained the age of 21, with respect to whom any agency certified by the State (including a private mentoring agency and governmental mentoring agency) has placed a qualifying mentored individual.

National Guard Investigations Transparency and Improvement Act of 2014 - Directs the Office of the Chief of the National Guard to undertake complex administrative investigations of matters relating to members of the National Guard when in state status, including investigations of sexual assault involving a member of the Guard in such status, upon the request of any of the following: (1) the Chief of the National Guard Bureau, (2) an adjutant general of a state or territory or the District of Columbia, (3) the governor of a state or territory, or (4) the commanding general of the National Guard of the District of Columbia. Requires the Chief to submit to the congressional leadership, upon the adoption of a final report on such investigation, a report that includes: (1) a summary description of the investigations undertaken during such year, including any trends in matters involving allegations of sexual assault involving a member of the Guard; (2) information, set forth by state and territory, on the investigations undertaken; and (3) information and matters on the investigations undertaken as the Chief considers appropriate. Requires the Chief to ensure that the Office maintains the necessary personnel and capabilities for the discharge of the duties of the Office.
Directs the Secretary of Commerce to convert certain entries of the United States Customs Service to Federal currency.

Home Health Care Planning Improvement Act of 2007 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, in the matter preceding it, to provide for the improvement of Medicare home health services.

This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the tax credit for production from advanced nuclear power facilities, to: (1) allocate such credit among a variety of eligible facilities; (2) treat such credit for purposes of the tax credit for the portion of a project's total national megawatt capacity limitation that is not covered by the credit; and (3) allow certain public entities (i.e., federal, state, or local governments, mutual or cooperative electric companies, or certain other entities) to transfer such credit to another entity for the purpose of receiving an application for a tax credit.

Strengthening Community Safety Act of 2010 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to authorize the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to make a grant to an eligible first responder agency for the additional costs incurred by the eligible first responder agency as a direct result of one or more employees of the agency or service who are reservists being placed on active duty. Defines "eligible first responder agency" as a law enforcement, fire service, or ambulance agency that is authorized or licensed by a state or local government, or that is designated by a state as a prehospital emergency medical response agency. Prohibits the Administrator from making a grant for costs relating to an employee being placed on active duty if federal funds are used, in whole or in part, for the pay or benefits of the employee.

Temporary IRA Distribution Suspension Act of 2008 - Suspends for calendar 2008-2010 the requirement that certain distributions from a defined contribution plan be made within the earlier of: (1) the calendar year 2008; or (2) the calendar year 2010, subject to specified requirements.

Makes this Act applicable to certain other plans as well.

Gas Pump Access Act of 2016 This bill prohibits the Department of Transportation (DOT) and the Department of Justice from approving the Department of Transportation's (DOT) plans for the American Gasoline Corporation (AGC) or the Department of Justice's (DOJ) gas station facilities in Florida, Florida, or Miami, Ohio, for failing to display a phone number to call for assistance on each self-service gas pump.  DOT and DOJ must make public the availability of fueling assistance to motor vehicle operators with a disability.

Provides for the appointment of U.S. Delegation representatives to meet jointly and at least annually and when Congress is not in session (except that this restriction shall not apply to meetings held in the United States) with representative parlimentary groups from other countries in the Americas for the purposes of:  (1) discussing common problems and interests in intellectual and industrial property; and (2) initiating and promoting national and multilateral measures as may further interests in such property. 
Establishes a schedule of U.S. Delegation appointments for each meeting of the Intellectual Property Assembly of the Americas. 
Requires the President pro tempore of the Senate from Members of the Senate (3 of whom, including the Vice Chairperson of the United States Delegation, shall be from the Committee on International Relations and 4 of whom shall be from the Committee on the Judiciary, unless the President pro tempore of the Senate, upon recommendations of the majority and minority leaders of the Senate, determines otherwise) to appoint a U.S. Delegation from Members of the House of Representatives (2 of whom, including the Vice Chairperson of the United States Delegation, shall be from the Committee on Foreign Relations and 4 of whom shall be from the

Federal Employees' Compensation Reform Act of 2011 - Amends federal law regarding retirement pay and benefits to provide for the transition to retirement of an employee who is a covered employee (i.e., an employee who is paid compensation under a retirement age limitation or a survivor annuity or both) and who is eligible for an annuity under chapter 83 or 84 (other than a survivor annuity).

 Directs the Secretary of Labor to provide notice to a covered employee, the employing agency of that covered employee, and the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) of the Social Security Administration (SSA) that the covered employee attains retirement age and is eligible for an annuity under chapter 83 or 84 (other than a survivor annuity). Requires the employing agency of that covered employee to file an application for an annuity with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) within one year of the termination of payments of compensation to such an employee.

 Directs the OPM to prescribe regulations to carry out this Act.

Caribbean National Forest Wild and Scenic Rivers Act of 2002 - Amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate specified segments of approximately 4.5 miles from its headwaters in the Bano de Oro Research Natural Area to the boundary of the Caribbean National Forest, Puerto Rico, as the Rio mameyes, from its headwaters in the Bano de Oro Research Natural Area to the crossing point of Trail No. 24/11 and the Rio de La Mina, from its headwaters in the Bano de Oro Research Natural Area to the access point of Trail No. 7 to the national forest boundary. 
Specifies that certain permitted activities within the boundaries of the segments added to the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System shall not be construed to prevent any of the following activities within the boundaries of such segments:  (1) Installation and maintenance of hydrologic, meteorological, climatological, or atmospheric data collection and transmission facilities when necessary to carry out Luquillo's experimental forest research; and (2) Construction and maintenance of nesting structures, observation blinds, and population monitoring platforms for threatened and endangered species.

Import Control and Safe Handling of Spent Nuclear Fuel Act of 1995 - Prohibits the importation of spent nuclear fuel from a country that:  (1) is not a country authorized to possess nuclear weapons; and (2) is known or suspected to be producing or developing nuclear weapons.  Allows the President to:  (1) require such countries to import unloaded fuel through a specified port; and (2) require unloaded fuel to be in compliance with such guidelines. 
Authorizes the establishment of reasonable guidelines to ensure that unloading, transfer, and shipment of such fuel at or through a specified port are conducted in a manner that protects the public health and safety and the environment at, and in the vicinity of, such marine port. 
Makes this Act applicable only to guidelines that are more protective of the public health and safety and the environment than other applicable requirements established under Federal, State, or local law.  Exempts such port authorities from the liability or indemnification provisions of other applicable Federal, State, or local laws. 
Specifies that nothing in this Act shall affect the liability or indemnification of the port in the handling of nuclear materials.

Colonias Improvement Act of 2014 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to issue a proposed rule that: (1) defines the term "covered program" (covered program) to the extent consistent with the requirements of this Act; (2) limits to a community that is located within 75 miles of the border between the United States and Mexico or has applied for or received funding under a covered program the grant it has awarded it; (3) reflects and preserves the historic, geographic, and cultural character of the communities served by the covered programs; and (4) may be used to determine whether an applicant qualifies for assistance under any covered program.  Directs the Administrator to establish and regularly update a website that: (1) serves as a clearinghouse for information relating to the covered programs, and (2) includes links to information specific to each state in which a covered program operates.  Directs the Administrator to: (1) establish a working group to review covered programs, (2) record information relating to each award that is and has been made under a covered program, (3) hold public hearings relating to covered programs, and (4) make recommendations to Congress

Health Care Consumer Protection Act of 1995 - Requires an insurer providing health insurance coverage under a health plan to provide annual notice to current enrollees regarding the extent of the coverage of the plan.  Requires such notice to be in writing and to include a copy of the contract between the insurer and enrollee, in addition to information regarding the terms and conditions of the policy and the rights and obligations of the parties including:  (1) covered and excluded services, equipment, and devices; (2) copayments, deductibles, and premiums; (3) enrollee satisfaction statistics; (4) financial responsibility of the enrollee; (5) utilization review requirements; and (6) a list of the usual, customary, and reasonable costs for procedures, tests, and examinations. 
Requires an insurer providing health insurance coverage under a health plan to, upon request, provide such an notice to each potential enrollee regarding the extent of the coverage of the plan. 
Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to promulgate regulations to ensure that an insurer providing health insurance coverage provide such notification to current and potential enrollees.

Small Business Reform Act of 2010 or the Not Too Small to Succeed in Business Act of 2010 - Amends the Small Business Act to make eligible for participation in the Small Business Administration (SBA) program any program under which a small business that has completed a nine-year period of participation in the program but is otherwise eligible for SBA program participation may participate during the two-year period beginning on enactment of this Act. Allows such program for a limited period of time for qualified program participants that are otherwise eligible but are still not so qualified as to be excluded from participation.

Education in Vocational Technology Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Education to make grants to States to improve the quality of instruction or training in, or training in, manufacturing and other occupational technologies. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Nuclear Policy and Posture Review Act of 2007 - Directs the President to conduct a nuclear policy review to consider a range of options on the role of nuclear weapons in U.S. security policy. Sets forth the scope of review and the elements of a recommended nuclear posture. Requires the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of Defense, the Director of National Intelligence, and the National Security Advisor to participate in the review. Requires the review to include contributions from outside experts and to include public meetings. Directs the Secretary to conduct the review in collaboration with the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of State, the Director of National Intelligence, and the National Security Advisor. Requires the review to include the following elements: (1) the role of nuclear forces in U.S. military strategy, planning, and programming, including the extent to which conventional forces can assume roles previously assumed by nuclear forces; (2) the policy requirements and objectives for the United States to maintain a safe, reliable, and credible nuclear deterrence posture; (3) the targeting strategy required to implement effectively the guidance provided by the nuclear policy review; (4) the levels and composition of the nuclear delivery systems that will be required for implementing the United States

Weekends Without Hunger Act - Amends the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a program to provide commodities, on a competitive basis, to eligible institutions to provide nutritious food to at-risk children on weekends and during extended school holidays during the school year.

Gives priority to institutions that: (1) have on-going programs and experience serving populations with significant proportions of at-risk school children; (2) have a good record of experience in food delivery and food safety systems; (3) maintain high quality control, accountability, and recordkeeping standards; and (4) provide children with readily consumable food of high nutrient content and quality.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) issue guidelines for projects receiving commodities; and (2) complete an interim evaluation of the pilot program.

Pharmaceutical Supply and Value Enhancement Act or the Pharmaceutical SAVE Act - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to authorize importation of a drug for a period of up to three years if: (1) the drug is a drug subject to specified provisions (including a prohibition against importation of a drug for use in a drug-shortage country); (2) the drug is authorized for use in one or more of the following drug categories (but only if the Secretary determines that the drug is not safe and effective, has been used in conjunction with a device for which there is no reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness, or the authorization to market the drug in one or more of the countries included in the list); (3) the manufacturer certifies to the Secretary that it intends to seek approval of the drug; and (4) an importer files with the Secretary information with respect to the drug the importer proposes to import, including the drug the importer claims has received approval from the Secretary and the manufacturer's agreement to import the drug.  Authorizes HHS to deny importation of a drug otherwise qualified for importation under this

Continuity of Electric Capacity Resources Act - Amends the Federal Power Act to require the Federal Power Administration (FPA) to submit to each transmission organization with a tariff on file a report that includes provisions addressing the procurement of electric capacity resources notice that the transmission organization is required to file a report with the FPA regarding the procurement of electric capacity resources notice that the transmission organization is required to file a report regarding the financial health, viability, and projected remaining years of service of the available electric capacity resources.

Requires the FPA to submit to the Commission a report that: (1) identifies electric capacity resources that are available to the FPA as of the date of the report; and (2) describes the fuel sources and operational characteristics of each electric capacity resource identified.

Requires the FPA to: (1) prior to the report submission date, have been made available to members of the transmission organization and to the public for comment; and (2) has been made available to the public for comment on the report.

Makes the objectives of the Act's "electric capacity resources" program (and related tariffs) inapplicable to certain electric power generation assets, including certain bulk-power assets, that are not subject to a production or distribution control system

Historic Rehabilitation Tax Credit Expansion Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a $25,000 offset for the rental real estate activities attributable to the rehabilitation credit.  Allows such offset for the portion of such credit attributable to the lesser of 25 percent of the tentative minimum tax or $50,000. 
Revises provisions relating to the rehabilitation investment tax credit to permit such credit to offset certain portion of such tax credit.

Amends Federal law to prohibit the Department of Defense (DOD) from procuring specified items of American origin from the Department of Agriculture (USDA).  Allows the purchase of specified articles from American sources.  Repeals the source provisions of the Department's appropriations Act, 1993 and the Department's appropriations law.

Preservation of Access tooporosis Testing for Medicare Beneficiary Act of 2011 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to extend the maximum payment for osteoporosis screening for Medicare beneficiaries from 2010 through 2013.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow individual taxpayers a tax credit for up to 50% of the cost of new motor vehicles sold in the United States.

Cameron Gulbransen Kids and Cars Safety Act of 2003 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to evaluate: (1) devices and technologies intended to reduce the incidence of child injury and death occurring outside of parked motor vehicles in nontraffic, noncrash events, including back-to-nature events, that are caused by such vehicles and determine which of those methods is the most effective; and (2) the currently available technology to prevent injury and death of children left unattended inside parked motor vehicles, including injury or death due to hyperthermia, power windows, or power sunroofs. Directs the Secretary to establish a database of (or modify an existing database to include) the numbers and types of injuries and deaths in non-traffic, noncrash events involving motor vehicles. Requires the Secretary to: (1) evaluate the available technologies for detecting and preventing collisions with individuals and objects behind motor vehicles; and (2) prescribe motor vehicle safety standards that require the installation of devices for detecting, and providing to operators of motor vehicles a warning of, individuals and objects behind the vehicle.

Amends the Civil Rights of Institutionalized Persons Act to provide that no claim with respect to prison conditions under the Revised statutes, or any other Federal law, by a prisoner confined in any jail, prison, or other correctional facility shall be adjudicated except for specified provisions under the Federal judicial code or the Civil Rights of Federal Institutions Act.  Amends the Federal judicial code to provide that a person who has not attained the age of 18 years may be adjudicated for, but only for a single instance of a child or juvenile.  Modifies the ban on multiple multifamily pauperis (i.e., a case in which at least one adult male and one female adult male and one child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child or child

Tackling Excessive Standardized Testing Act of 2015 or the TEST Act of 2015 Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to require that academic assessments be given in each of grades 4, 6, and 8 in lieu of the requirements of the test. Authorizes a public school to administer the academic assessments in each of grades 4 and 8 in lieu of the requirements of the test. Authorizes a public school or school whose students do not meet the academic achievement requirements of the test to administer the assessments in mathematics in accordance with the test, but only in the latter grade. Authorizes a public school or school whose students do not meet the academic achievement requirements of the test to administer the assessments in reading or language arts in accordance with the test, but only in the latter grade. Prohibits a state educational agency (SEA) from administering academic assessments in lieu of the requirements of the test in the first 12 months that a student is enrolled in a public elementary or secondary school.

DHS FOIA Efficiency Act of 2015 (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to finalize and issue regulations implementing the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) guidelines for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) with respect to the processing of requests made under FOIA.  The Chief FOIA Officer of DHS, in coordination with the Chief Financial Officer of DHS and the heads of each of the relevant components of DHS, shall identify the total annual cost to DHS of implementing FOIA guidelines and the cost guidance to the DHS employees processing requests.  The Chief FOIA Officer shall develop a plan to automate the DHS processing of requests to the DHS Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to the DHS Department.  The Chief FOIA Officer shall also provide the plan to DHS components and obtain DHS public disclosure requirements for the DHS public disclosure of information that may affect DHS employees.

Cocopah Lands Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to take certain land in Yuma County, Arizona, into trust for the Cocopah Indian Tribe of Arizona if the Tribe transfers title to the land to the Secretary and the Tribe transfers title to the SW\1/4, the NW\1/4, and the SE\1/4 of the Sec. 1, T. 10 S., R. 25 W., of the Gila and Salt River Base and Meridian, Yuma County, Arizona, except that the SW\1/4 and the NW\1/4 of the SE\1/4 lie south of the East Main Canal and Salinity Canal, respectively. Requires that such land be considered to be part of the Tribe's initial reservation.

Prohibits the use of such land for gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act.

Plan B for Plan B Act of 2005 - Requires the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, if the Commissioner of Food and Drugs (FDA) fails to approve or disapprove the application for Plan B, to publish in the Federal Register a determination, within 30 days after the enactment of this Act, that the application is approved or disapproved.

Uterine Fibroid Research and Education Act of 2003 - Requires the Director of the National Institutes of Health to expand, intensify, and coordinate programs for the conduct and support of uterine fibroids research.Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to develop and disseminate to the public information regarding uterine fibroids, including information on: (1) the incidence and prevalence of uterine fibroids; (2) the elevated risk for minority women; and (3) the availability of a range of treatment options for symptomatic uterine fibroids.

Requires each State to submit to the Attorney General a written report that specifies each location at which any law enforcement agency operating under State law stores or keeps explosive materials that have been shipped or transported in interstate or foreign commerce and the types and amounts of such materials. Directs the Attorney General to prescribe final regulations governing the storage and keeping by State and local law enforcement agencies of explosive materials that have been shipped or transported in interstate or foreign commerce. Sets forth the standards of public safety and security against theft which any place at which explosive materials that have been shipped or transported in interstate or foreign commerce are so stored or kept shall meet, and shall require any such place to be subject to video surveillance or to have in operation an alarm system capable of notifying the agency of unauthorized entry. Authorizes the Attorney General to enter during business hours any place where a State or local law enforcement agency stores or keeps explosive materials that have been transported in interstate or foreign commerce, for the purpose of inspecting the materials and determining whether they are being stored or kept in compliance with such regulations. Bond Transparency Act of 2014 - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require a broker, dealer, or municipal securities dealer that effects a riskless principal transaction to disclose, in writing, at or before completion of the transaction, the difference between the customer's purchase price and the broker's or dealer's purchase price, or the customer's sale price and the broker's or dealer's sale price.  Defines "riskless principal transaction" as: (1) a transaction in which a broker or dealer receives a customer order to buy or sell any specified debt securities and, after receiving the customer order, buys the specified debt securities from, or sells the specified debt securities to, another person, while acting as principal for its own account, to complete the customer order; and (2) any other transaction the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) identifies as a riskless principal transaction.  Requires a broker or dealer that effects such a riskless principal transaction to disclose, in writing, at or before completion of the transaction, the difference between the customer's purchase price and the broker's or dealer's purchase price, or the customer's sale price and the broker's or dealer's sale price

Equity in Public Education Act of 1996 - Directs the Secretary of Education to provide for the reimbursement of States for certain costs incurred in the reimbursement of educational costs for illegal aliens residing in such States.

Responsible Stem Cell Research Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a National Stem Cell Donor Bank to seek and preserve donations of qualifying human stem cells. Requires the Donor Bank to: (1) operate a registry of patients who are transplant candidates; (2) establish a system for finding donors who are unrelated to the patients and are suitably matched to them; and (3) carry out informational and educational activities.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow U.S. cruise industry income tax treatment as effectively connected with the conduct of a U.S. trade or business within the United States.

Incentives for our Nation's Veterans in Energy Sustainability Technologies or the INVEST Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a local agency that receives federal income tax payments to pay to a U.S. veteran the loss of a U.S. possession by reason of an amendment to the tax system in which the veteran is employed.  The Department of the Treasury must pay to each possession of the United States that does not have such a system the loss resulting from the amendment.

Global Nuclear Security Initiative Act of 2002 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Administrator for Nuclear Security, should develop a comprehensive program of activities to encourage all countries with nuclear materials to adhere to, or to adopt standards equivalent to, the International Atomic Energy Agency (INCIRC) standard on The Physical Protection of Nuclear Material and Nuclear Facilities, relating to the security of stockpiles of highly enriched uranium and plutonium.

Directs the Secretary to require the Office of International Materials Protection, Control, and Accounting of the Department of Energy to study and report to Congress on the feasibility and advisability of developing such a program.

Directs the Secretary to study and report to Congress on the feasibility and advisability of various actions to reduce the risks associated with terrorist attacks on nuclear power plants outside the United States.

Student Health Insurance Portability Protection Act of 1997 - Amends the Public Health Service Act, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, and the Internal Revenue Code to apply provisions of such Act, as well as provisions of the Public Health Service Act, to health insurance coverage offered in connection with a college-sponsored health plan.

Federal Bureau of Investigation First Amendment Protection Act of 1993 - Prohibits the Federal Bureau of Investigation (BIO) from initiating or conducting any investigation that may involve the collection of information about the exercise by a U.S. person of first amendment rights, other than in accordance with the limitations and requirements established by this Act. 
Requires the Attorney General to issue publicly available guidelines for investigations, including those that implement this Act. 
Prohibits the BIO from initiating an investigation unless the Director of the BIO, or the Director's designee, finds in writing that specific and articulable facts reasonably indicate that the subject of the investigation has engaged, is engaging, or is about to engage in a Federal criminal offense.  Allows employees of the BIO to initiate an investigation without a finding if exigent circumstances so require. 
Requires the BIO to:  (1) seek to gather only information relevant to Federal criminal offenses; (2) employ the least intrusive techniques available; and (3) follow procedures to minimize the acquisition, retention, or dissemination of any information relating to the exercise of first amendment rights or individual privacy.

Taxpayer Savings and Employee Notification Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to include life insurance investment gains in the gross income of nonqualified companies owned by an entity on one or more of its employees. Repeals the exclusion from such gross income for death benefits. Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to provide to each employee a written disclosure that shall contain: (1) a statement that the company plans to purchase such contract on the life of the employee; and (2) the identity of the insurance carrier with respect to such contract. Treats a violation of this Act as an unfair or deceptive act or practice under the Federal Trade Commission Act.

Local Food for Healthy Families Act of 2013 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to establish the Local Food for Healthy Families Program to make grants to certain entities to carry out projects to provide incentives to low-income families receiving supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits to purchase fruits and vegetables. Requires the Secretary to: (1) convene an advisory committee to advise the Secretary on the design of the program; (2) give priority to entities located in underserved communities, (3) provide for matching funds for qualifying projects, and (4) provide for an independent evaluation of each grant project.

Job Access and Work Incentives Act - Title I:  Preference for Policing Officers
 - Amends the Federal transportation code to provide preference for Federal employees to hire welfare recipients for jobs created to carry out a contract. 
Title II:  Job Access and Reversal Grants
 - Amends the Transportation Equity Act for the 21st Century to authorize the Secretary of Transportation to provide loan guarantees to States for specified periods to current or recent welfare recipients.

Recipients
 - Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide a loan guarantee to a recipient of assistance under a State program that provides a loan of up to $20,000 and a guarantee of interest at an annual rate of up to $5,000. 
Title IV:  Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services
 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to provide for the repeal of the authority of the Secretary of Health and Human Services to prescribe drug or alcohol treatment and recovery programs.

Brownfields Housing and Community Renewal Development Act - Amends the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to establish a program to make grants to assist in carrying out redevelopment activities for brownfield sites and abandoned, idled, and underused industrial, commercial or housing structures located in brownfield sites.

Stop Iran From Smuggling Weapons to Terrorists Act This bill authorizes the Department of Defense (DOD), with the concurrence of the Department of State, to provide training and equipment to Israel, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Qatar that have among their functional responsibilities maritime security missions. DOD may also provide training to ministry, agency, and headquarters level organizations.  DOD shall negotiate a cost-sharing agreement with a recipient country regarding the cost of such training. DOD shall credit a specified amount toward the provision of such training.

Business Checking Freedom Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Reserve Act to allow any depository institution to permit the owner of any deposit or account on which interest or dividends are paid to make up to 24 transfers per month (or such greater number as the Federal Reserve Board determines by rule or order) to another account of the owner in the same institution. Authorizes such transfers to be paid by the Federal reserve bank at least once each calendar quarter.

Requires the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to determine the appropriate payment of such interest on Federal reserve bank reserves for any purpose.

Taiwan Airpower Modernization Act of 2011 - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) a critical element to maintaining peace and stability in Asia in the face of China's two-decade-long military program of military modernization and expansion of military capabilities is ensuring a militarily strong and confident Taiwan; (2) a Taiwan that is confident in its ability to deter Chinese aggression will increase its ability to proceed in developing peaceful relations with China in areas of mutual interest; (3) the cross-Strait military balance between China and Taiwan has shifted in China's favor; (4) China's military expansion poses a clear and present danger to Taiwan; (5) Taiwan's air force continues to deteriorate, and this threat has very serious implications for U.S. security; (6) Taiwan's military aircraft continue to deteriorate; and (7) the United States must provide Taiwan with additional advanced multirole fighter aircraft and significant upgrades to Taiwan's existing fleet of multirole fighter aircraft. Directs the President to carry out the sale of no fewer than 66 F-16C/D multirole fighter aircraft to Taiwan.

Citizen Empowerment Act of 2015 This bill amends the federal criminal code to allow any executive agency employee conducting an in-person or telephonic interaction with an individual who is violating a federal statute or regulation to record that interaction at the individual's expense and with the individual's equipment. Any employee of an executive agency that is conducting such an interaction must notify the individual of the recording and provide the individual with a transcript or copy of the recording upon request.  Any employee who is permitted to represent before an agency or who is allowed to make an audio recording of an in-person or telephonic interaction must be granted the right to make such recordings.  Any employee who violates this bill and is subject to disciplinary action shall be subject to appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with federal or state law.

Hunt Unrestricted on National Treasures Act or the HUNT Act - Requires each head of a Federal public land management agency to make available to the public on the National Park Service, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the Forest Service, and the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) a list of the location and acreage of lands more than 640 acres in size under agency jurisdiction that have been determined to be of such a quality and that have potential for use for such purposes, including a plan developed by the agency that identifies how public access and egress could reasonably be provided to the legal boundaries of such lands. Requires the agency head to consider public access and egress to the legal boundaries of contiguous parcels of land equal to more than 640 acres in size under agency jurisdiction, including access and egress to specified roads or trails.  Requires the agency head to consider public access and egress to the legal boundaries of trails that provide the primary public access and egress to the legal boundaries of contiguous parcels of land equal to more than 640 acres in size under agency jurisdiction. Domestic Violence Courts Assistance Act - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to require the Attorney General to report to Congress on the implementation and effectiveness of the amendments made by this Act, including the effectiveness of grants made under such amendments in reducing the rates of domestic violence and shortening the period of judicial review in domestic violence cases.

Senior Citizens' Freedom to Work Act - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to increase the monthly amount of OASDI benefits for individuals who have attained retirement age (as defined by OASDI) before the close of the taxable year involved.  Increases such monthly amount after 2002. 
Directs the Managing Trustee of the Senior Citizens' Trust Fund to increase the rate of interest other than the mandatory interest rate applicable to individuals who have attained retirement age.

Environmental Protection Encouragement Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer to elect to expense the cost of any environmental improvement property (EIP) as an expense not chargeable to capital account.  Allows EIPs of a character which is subject to the allowance for depreciation provided under the Environmental Protection Act for one or more purposes:  (1) source reduction; (2) solid waste minimization; (3) waste conversion or recycling; (4) reduction of environmental hazards; (5) compliance with environmental permits, rules, and similar requirements; (6) prevention, containment, or control of unplanned releases; or (7) the manufacture, distribution, and sale of alternate fuels and blending stocks or fuel additives for reformulated fuels and the manufacture, distribution, and sale of alternative fuels for reformulated fuels.

Amends the Federal criminal code to provide that a person who is not prohibited by this Act from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a firearm or ammunition shall be entitled to transport a firearm for any lawful purpose from any place where the person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport the firearm to any other such place if, during the transportation, the firearm is unloaded and: (1) if the transportation is by motor vehicle, the firearm is not directly accessible from the passenger compartment; and (2) if the vehicle is without a compartment separate from the passenger compartment, the firearm is in a locked container other than the glove compartment or console, or is secured by a secure gun storage or safety device.

Provides that a person who is not prohibited by this Act from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a firearm or ammunition shall be entitled to transport ammunition, or any detachable magazine or feeding device for ammunition, for any lawful purpose from any place where the person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport the ammunition, magazine, or feeding device to any other such place if, during the transportation, the ammunition, magazine, or feeding device is not loaded into a firearm, and, if

Natural Disaster Mitigation Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual taxpayer a tax credit for 25% of the qualified natural disaster mitigation property expenditures made in connection with a principal residence of the taxpayer. Limits such credit to the excess of: (1) $5,000 over ($1 million for married individuals filing a separate return), over ($5 million for married individuals filing a separate return for nonresidents of the same residence), or (2) the credit allowable under this Act for all prior taxable years.

Defines "qualified natural disaster mitigation property expenditure" as an expenditure for property to improve the strength of a roof deck attachment, property to create a secondary water barrier to prevent water intrusion, property to improve the durability of a roof covering, property to brace gable-end walls, property to reinforce the connection between a roof and supporting wall, property to protect openings from penetration by windborne debris, property to protect exterior doors and garages, and property to improve the natural resiliency of the property.

Essential Oral Health Care Act of 2009 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to support volunteer dental projects to improve or improve the oral health care access of low-income individuals.

Requires the Secretary to award grants to states to purchase portable or mobile dental equipment and to pay for appropriate operational costs, including direct health care or service delivery costs, for the provision of free dental services to underserved populations that are delivered in a manner consistent with state licensing laws. Requires such grants to be used to: (1) enable states to make grants to individuals who have access to oral health care services equal to the population of the state; and (2) ensure that individuals covered by the plan have access to oral health care services to the same extent as such services are available to the state.

Nuclear Secrets Safety Act of 2000 - Directs the Administrator for Nuclear Security to: (1) conduct an inventory of each document or device at each national security laboratory that contains Restricted Data; and (2) report to the congressional defense committees on the results of that inventory. Requires the Administrator to ensure that, after October 1, 2002, each lock used by the Nuclear Security Administration (NSA) to secure any vault, safe, or other container used to store Restricted Data is an electronic lock that meets or exceeds the FF-L-2740A lock standard of the General Services Administration (GSA).

SCHIP Improvement Act of 1999 - Amends the National School Lunch Act to require the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a demonstration project in not more than 40 local agencies in not more than two States for the identification and enrollment of children in certain health programs for the purpose of identifying and enrolling such children in certain State plans and State child health plans. 
Directs the Secretary to make grants to States to carry out State plans to involve eligible entities in the identification of children eligible for benefits under, and enrollment of children in, specified health programs for the purpose of identifying and enrolling such children in certain State plans and State child health plans. 
Authorizes the Secretary to provide to the Secretary funds to carry out this Act.

Coastal Restoration Tax Credit Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for the qualified expenditures of the taxpayer for the taxable year for the expensing of qualified expenditures in order to restore and protect coastal lands.

Iranian Nuclear Trade Prohibition Act of 2005 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the countries of the world should choose between trading with state sponsors of terrorism or maintaining good trade relations with the United States.

Amends the Iran and Libya Sanctions Act of 1996 to prohibit the United States, or any entity of the United States, from purchasing nuclear fuel assemblies from any person or government entity that sells nuclear fuel assemblies to Iran.

Authorizes the President to waive such prohibition if he: (1) determines that such waiver is in the national security interest of the United States; and (2) notifies the required congressional committees of the President's intent to exercise such waiver.

Youth Opioid Use Treatment Help Act of 2017 or the YOUTH Act  This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to extend the authorization of appropriations for the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration's (SAMHRA) Youth Opioid Use Treatment program.  The SAMHRA program provides grants to states, Indian tribes, and other appropriate public or nonprofit institutions to establish demonstration programs to: (1) expand access to medication-assisted treatment for opioid use disorders among adolescents and young adults, (2) identify and test solutions for overcoming barriers to implementation of medication-assisted treatment for adolescents and young adults, or (3) create and distribute resources on medication-assisted treatment training and implementation for providers of health care to children, adolescents, and young adults.

Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to carry out major medical facility projects in FY2010 in: (1) construction of the Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Livermore, California; (2) a multi-specialty care facility in Winnipeg, Manitoba; (3) a new medical facility in Denver, Colorado; (4) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Louisville, Kentucky; (5) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Atlanta, Georgia; (6) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Bakersfield, California; (7) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Franklin, North Carolina; (8) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Kansas City, California; (9) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Loma Linda, California; (10) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Montgomery, Alabama; (11) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Montgomery, Florida; (12) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Loma Linda, California; and (13) a Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center in Loma Linda, Florida. Cut Taxes for the Middle Class Act of 2014 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) extend through 2014 the tax deduction for state and local general sales taxes, the deduction for qualified tuition and related expenses, and the work opportunity tax credit; (2) extend through 2014 the tax deduction for certain expenses of elementary and secondary school teachers; (3) extend through 2014 the tax deduction for certain expenses of business owners; and (4) extend through 2014 the tax deduction for certain new markets tax credit.

National Security Whistleblower Protection Act of 2016 This bill amends the federal criminal code to suspend or revoke access to classified information, and requires the Inspector General of the Department of Defense (DOD) to report to Congress the information that DOD receives regarding employees who have been suspended or revoked access to classified information. DOD must report to Congress on the number of allegations of such access, the number of such allegations that were closed by the Inspector General, the number of such allegations that were closed by the Inspector General, the number of such allegations that were closed by the Inspector General, the number of such allegations that were closed by the Inspector General, and the number of investigations of such allegations that were conducted.
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to promulgate regulations to protect the privacy of customers of telecommunications service.

Rocky Flats Environmental Technology Site Act of 2005 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to purchase essential mineral rights at Rocky Flats (a federal facility in Colorado known as the Rocky Flats Environmental Technology Site).

Prohibits the Secretary from purchasing an essential mineral right under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA) if the owner of the essential mineral right is a willing seller, the Secretary purchases the essential mineral right at fair market value, and the Trustees enter into a natural resources damage settlement providing that the purchase satisfies any existing or potential natural resource damage liability claim arising from releases of hazardous substances identified in the administrative record for the site.

Prohibits the Secretary from purchasing an essential mineral right under CERCLA unless: (1) the owner of the essential mineral right is a willing seller; (2) the Secretary purchases the essential mineral right at fair market value, and (3) the Trustees enter into a natural resources damage settlement providing that the purchase satisfies any existing or potential natural resource damage liability claim arising from releases of hazardous substances identified in the administrative record for the site.

Mortgage and Rental Disaster Relief Act of 2007 - Amends the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act to authorize the President to provide assistance on a temporary basis in the form of mortgage or rental payments to or on behalf of individuals and households who, as a result of financial hardship caused by a major disaster, have received written notice of dispossession or eviction from a residence by reason of a foreclosure of any mortgage or lien, cancellation of any contract of sale, or termination of any lease, entered into before such disaster. Allows such individuals and households to receive assistance if the adjusted gross income of that individual or household was not more than $75,000.

Allows such individuals and households to return the full amount of assistance to the government if they so wish.

Requires the Attorney General to select for participation in the program each incarceration facility that satisfies specified requirements, including that it is owned by the government of a local political subdivision and that it has submitted a request for such selection. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) the number of local political subdivisions to meet the standard in such clauses; and (2) the number of facilities to be included in the program. 
Directs the Attorney General to complete a study and report to the Congress on the logistical and technological feasibility of implementing such program.
