Wireless Microphone Users Interference Protection Act of 2013 - Directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to expand the scope of service for wireless microphone users to the owners of, and operators of, events and performances at: (1) amusement parks, (2) arenas, (3) concert centers, (4) educational facilities, (5) houses of worship, (6) lodging facilities, and (7) museums. Directs the FCC to establish two safe haven channels for exclusive use by wireless microphone users that are each 6 MHz in the spectrum ranging from 470 to 698 MHz, inclusive, other than frequencies identified as guard bands and the mid-band gap between the frequencies designated for uplink and downlink service in auctioned 600 MHz spectrum. Directs the FCC to: (1) authorize the owners and operators of wireless microphone users (and their appointed technical representatives) to have access to the TV bands databases for the purpose of protecting wireless microphone operations from interference; and (2) establish two safe haven channels for exclusive use by wireless microphone users that are each 6 MHz in the spectrum ranging from 470 to 69

Military Spouses Residency Relief Act - Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to: (1) provide that a person who is absent from a State because the person is accompanying the person's spouse who is absent from that same State in compliance with military or naval orders shall not, solely by reason of that absence: (2) provide that a servicemember who is absent from a State because the person is absent from a State, without regard to whether the person intends to return to that State, be deemed to have lost a residence or domicile in that State, without regard to whether the person intends to return to that State, be deemed to have acquired a residence or domicile in any other State, or be deemed to have become a resident in or a resident of any State; and (3) apply to absences from States that result from the removal from service of a servicemember who is absent from a State because the servicemember is absent from a State, regardless of the date of the military or naval order concerned. 
Amends the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act to provide that a spouse of a servicemember shall neither lose nor acquire a residence or domicile

Otay Mountain Wilderness Act of 1998 - Designates specified public lands in the California Desert District of the Bureau of Land Management as the Otay Mountain Wilderness. 
Recognizes that, because of the rugged mountain adjacent to the U.S.-Mexican border, the Wilderness Area is the most important component of the National Wilderness Preservation System. 
Designates the Otay Mountain Wilderness as a component of the Wilderness Preservation System. 
Requires the Wilderness Area to be administered in accordance with the requirements of the Wilderness Act, except that:  (1) any reference in such Act to the effective date of the Wilderness Act is deemed to be a reference to the effective date of this Act; and (2) any reference in such Act to the Secretary of Agriculture is deemed to be a reference to the Secretary of the Interior. 
Declares that any lands acquired after this Act's enactment shall become part of the Wilderness Area. 
Declares that the Wilderness Area is not intended to lead to the creation of protective buffer zones around the Wilderness.

Childcare Accountability and Responsibility Act of 2009 or the CARE for Kids Act of 2009 - Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to require a State and national criminal background check for a child care staff member of a child care provider to include: (1) a search of the National Sex Offender Registry; (2) a search of the National Crime Information Center; (3) a search of the State criminal registry or repository; (4) a search of State-based abuse and neglect registries and databases; and (5) a federal fingerprint identification system.

Requires a child care provider to submit a request for a State and national criminal background check to the appropriate State agency, including: (1) a criminal background check for each child care staff member prior to its submission; (2) each child care staff member for each prospective child care staff member before their first request for a background check; and (3) each child care staff member for each child care staff member after their first request for a background check for the child care staff member.

Limits a child care provider's eligibility for a State child care certificate to one request for a State and national criminal background

Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to implement a structured risk-benefit assessment framework in the new drug approval process to: (1) facilitate the balanced consideration of benefits and risks; and (2) develop and implement a consistent and systematic approach to the discussion of, regulatory decisionmaking regarding, and the communication of, the benefits and risks of new drugs. 
Requires the Secretary to: (1) establish and implement processes under which an entity seeking to develop patient experience data may submit to the Secretary initial research concepts for feedback, and with respect to patient experience data, draft guidance documents, completed data, and summaries and analyses of such data; (2) request such an entity to submit such documents, data, and summaries and analyses; and (3) submit patient experience data to be used to enhance the structured risk-benefit assessment framework. 
Requires the Secretary to: (1) publish guidance on the implementation of this Act within two years of this Act's enactment; and (2) issue draft guidance on the implementation within one year of this Act's enactment and once every six months for review by the Secretary.

Medicaid Fraud Recovery Act of 2008 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require local governments to provide for the following in their state plan: (1) recognition of unit; (2) local unit operation; (3) data sharing; (4) payment of bounty; and (5) state semiannual report submission.

Amends SSA title XIX to require local governments to provide for the following in their quarterly reports to the Secretary of Health and Human Services: (1) in the case of a local fraud investigation unit refuelling a claim, 10% of such refuelled funds are recouped; and (2) if a state refuses to prosecute a case referred to it by such unit, 10% of such funds are recouped.
Makes the surface estate of specified lands (including the mineral and geothermal leasing areas) treated as real property subject to the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949.

Accuracy in Medicare Physician Payment Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish and appoint an independent expert outside advisory panel to provide oversight of the processes relating to valuation of physicians' services, including the process of identifying, reviewing, and adjusting valuations for such services.  Authorizes the panel to establish screens and conduct surveys of suppliers of physicians' services and to conduct time and motion studies relating to such valuations.  Directs the Federal Advisory Committee to apply to the panel, except that the Secretary shall provide for the transfer of up to $10,000,000 for each fiscal year from the Federal Medical Supplementary Medical Insurance Trust Fund to the Center for Medicare & Medicaid Services Program Management Account to carry out this Act.

Head Start Assessment Act of 2003 - Prohibits the Secretary of Health and Human Services from proceeding with the full-scale implementation of the Head Start National Reporting System on Child Outcomes until the Secretary certifies to Congress that specified conditions have been met.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax deduction for qualified postsecondary education expenses.  Allows such deduction for a specified amount per taxpayer.  Limits such deduction to $10,000.

Purchase Card Waste Elimination Act of 2006 - Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to issue guidelines to assist the heads of executive agencies in improving the management of the use of the Governmentwide commercial purchase card for making micropurchases (i.e., purchases made in economical volumes).

Requires the Administrator of General Services to submit periodic reports on actions taken in each executive agency pursuant to such guidelines.

Directs the Director to submit to the congressional homeland security and governmental affairs committees a report summarizing progress made in improving the management of the use of the Governmentwide commercial purchase card for making micropurchases and achieving savings in micropurchases made with such card, expressed in terms of average savings achieved by each executive agency in the use of discount agreements.

Directs the Administrator to submit annually to such committees a report on all first class and business class travel by employees of each executive agency undertaken at the expense of the federal government.

Alisa's Law of 2014 - Amends the federal criminal code to require states to enact and enforce a law that requires a minimum of 180 days (of continuous breath samples) be provided to a person convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence (currently, continuous breath samples are required to be given every 210 miles). Requires states to withhold 1% of the amount required to be apportioned to a state if the state does not meet the requirements. Requires any funds withheld under this Act to be apportioned to the state in a fiscal year after the fiscal year in which the funds are authorized to be appropriated.

Foreign Investment Transparency and Security Act of 2006 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish limitations on foreign control of investments in certain U.S. critical infrastructure.

Authorizes a foreign government controlled entity to acquire, own, or otherwise control or manage U.S. critical infrastructure only through the establishment or operation of a foreign owned general business corporation that meets specified requirements.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to promulgate regulations to carry out this Act.

Bond Financing Renewal Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the cap on the amount of qualified small issue bonds that may be issued by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS); (2) increase the cap on the cost-of-living adjustment to the cap for such bonds; and (3) allow the IRS to acquire interest for small issue bonds used as a qualifying small business loan.

Freedom and Human Rights for the Enclaved People of Cyprus Act - Directs the President to take steps to inform the United Nations, foreign governments, and the appropriate departments and agencies of the United States Government to end restrictions on the freedom and human rights of the enclaved people of Cyprus, and to establish U.S. Government programs of assistance to the enclaved people of Cyprus, consistent with this Act. Directs the President to: (1) use funds allocated for a fiscal year to the government or ethnic community participating in the restrictions on the freedom and human rights of the enclaved people of Cyprus to assist such people, or (2) establish a foreign assistance program for the enclaved people of Cyprus to assist them, or to eliminate restrictions on the freedom and human rights of the enclaved. Directs the President to: (1) notify the heads of government of any foreign country that is participating in the restrictions on freedom and human rights of the enclaved people of Cyprus of the opposition by the United States to that government's participation in such restrictions; and (2) urge the U.S. government to cease participation in such restrictions and to work to eliminate such restrictions. Directs the Secretary of State to include a report on the enclaved people of Cyprus as part

Permissible revisions of budget resolutions by both Houses of the President may be considered as enforceable upon enactment or 15 days following the joint resolution on the budget for a fiscal year that has been enacted pursuant to this Act.  The joint resolution shall be considered as enforceable upon enactment or 15 days following presentment to the President, whichever occurs earlier.  The congressional procedures code is amended to permit automatic standing order upon veto of joint budget resolution.  The rules of the House of Representatives and the Senate to enforce joint budget resolutions are amended to permit joint budget resolution procedures.

Meat Promotion Act of 2005 - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a program of country of origin labeling for covered meat products.

Prohibits the Secretary from designating a covered meat product as having the United States as the country of origin unless the product is derived exclusively from an animal born, raised, and slaughtered in the United States, or from an animal born and raised in Alaska or Hawaii, transported for a period not to exceed 60 days outside of those States, and slaughtered in the United States.

Agricultural Credit Act of 2001 - Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to prohibit the Secretary of Agriculture from making or guaranteeing loans to a borrower who has received debt forgiveness on a loan made or guaranteed under such Act.  Authorizes the Secretary to make direct or guaranteed farm operating loans for paying annual farm or ranch operating expenses of a borrower who: (1) was restructured with a write-down or write-down during the lifetime of the borrower due to a financial problem relating to the natural disaster or a medical condition of the borrower or an immediate family member of the borrower; or (2) is currently on payments under a confirmed reorganization plan under the Federal Family Agriculture Loan program.  Authorizes the Secretary to make a direct or guaranteed farm operating loan for paying a borrower who: (1) was restructured with a write-down or write-down during the lifetime of the borrower due to a financial problem relating to the natural disaster or a medical condition of the borrower or an immediate family member of the borrower; or (2) is currently on payments under a confirmed reorganization plan under the Federal Family Agriculture Loan program.  Allows a borrower to reallocate funds for

PTSD/TBI Guaranteed Review For Heroes Act - Directs the Secretary of Defense to establish within the Office of the Secretary of Defense (DOD) a board of review to review the discharge or dismissal of a former member with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or traumatic brain injury (TBI) that is the result of a discharge or dismissal by a military personnel.  Requires the board to review the discharge or dismissal within 15 years of its receipt and to make changes if the discharge or dismissal is not honorable.  Directs the Secretary concerned to correct the military records of a former member in accordance with a change made by the board.  Provides that the Secretary shall: (1) refer a member for evaluation by a physical evaluation board if a physician, clinical psychologist, psychiatrist, or other appropriate health care professional determines that such member has PTSD or TBI, and (2) otherwise, if the board determines that the member is fit to perform the duties of the member's office, grade, rank, or rating because of such condition.

Amends Federal criminal law to require a person to license a person to hold a gun show to obtain a firearm.  Requires a person to submit to the Secretary of the Interior an application which:  (1) contains a certification by the applicant that the applicant meets certain requirements; and (2) is in such form as the Secretary shall establish to ensure that fees collected are sufficient to cover the costs of issuing licenses.  Authorizes the Secretary to issue a license to a firearm at a gun show only if the applicant receives a photographic or fingerprint of the issuing firearm and the applicant is in such form as the Secretary shall establish to ensure that fees collected are sufficient to cover the costs of issuing licenses.  Requires the Secretary to issue or deny an application to a firearm to compel the Secretary to so act.  Requires a firearm to be delivered to the Secretary by the holder of the gun show within 30 days after the end of the gun show.  Provides for criminal penalties for violations of this Act.

Obamacare Marriage Penalty Elimination Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the health insurance premium credit, to eliminate the marriage penalty.  The bill also amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to eliminate the limitation on the amount of the taxpayer's income that may be allocated to each spouse for purposes of determining the family size involved and household income with respect to each spouse.

Canyon Mountain Land Conveyance Act of 2013 - Requires the Secretary of the Interior to: (1) complete a survey of the boundary lines to establish the boundaries of the federal land taken into trust for the Cow Creek Band of Indians and the Coos Bay District, the Eugene District, the Medford District, the Roseburg District, the Salem District, and the Klamath Falls Resource Area of the Lakeview District; and (2) file a map and legal description of the federal land with specified congressional committees.  Requires the Secretary to identify any land owned by the Oregon and California Railroad that is conveyed under this Act.

Election Jamming Prevention Act of 2006 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the use of telecommunication devices, including telecommunications to communicate with an election-related information, to engage in the broadcast or exchange of election-related information (i.e., information about the endorsement, support, or opposition to any clearly identified candidate or slate of candidates for the office of President, Vice President, presidential elector, Member of the Senate, Member of the House of Representatives, or Delegate or Commissioner from a territory or possession) with the intent to annoy, abuse, threaten, or harass any person at the called number or who receives the communications.

Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to define "election-related information" as information related to: (1) the endorsement, support, promotion of, or opposition to any clearly identified candidate or slate of candidates for the office of President, Vice President, presidential elector, Member of the Senate, Member of the House of Representatives, or Delegate or Commissioner from a territory or possession; (2) the time, place, or manner for the election of such offices; or (3) the facilitation of transport to or from polling

Healthy Maternity and Obstetric Medicine Act or the Healthy MOM Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act and the Internal Revenue Code to require a group health plan to permit an employee who is eligible, but not enrolled, for coverage under the terms of a plan (or a dependent of such an employee if the dependent is eligible but not enrolled, for coverage under such terms) to enroll for coverage upon pregnancy, with the special enrollment period beginning on the date on which the pregnancy is reported to the plan. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services must issue regulations to ensure that pregnancy is considered a change in family status and a qualifying life event for an individual eligible to enroll, but is not enrolled, in a health benefit plan.

Continuity of Congress Act of 2003 - States that, in the event that one-fourth of the members of the House of Representatives are killed or incapacitated, the legislature of each State may enact such laws declaring who shall serve in the place of such members as the State determines necessary.

Earmark Reform and Federal Spending Transparency and Accountability Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit earmark beneficiaries from making contributions aggregating more than $5,000 to any requesting candidate with respect to such earmark beneficiary.

Defines "earmark beneficiary" as any person who specifically requests and benefits from a congressionally directed spending item, a limited tax benefit, or a limited tariff benefit that was enacted into law during the period beginning on January 1, 1971, and ending on December 31,  the next even-numbered year.

Requires an employee of the personal staff of a Member of Congress to not attend a political fund raiser held on behalf of the Member for whom they are employed.

Prohibits a Member of Congress from designating one employee who shall not be subject to the provisions of this Act.

Excepts from the definition of "earmark beneficiary" any person who requests and benefits from a congressionally directed spending item, a limited tax benefit, or a limited tariff benefit that was enacted into law during the period beginning on January 1, 1971, and

Supporting Emergency Responders Volunteer Efforts Act of 2009 or the SERVE Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow bona fide volunteer members of a qualified volunteer emergency response organization a refundable tax credit for up to $1,000 per year, up to 6 months in a taxable year, and up to 40 hours of such service during the taxable year. Defines "qualified volunteer emergency response organization" as a nonprofit organization with at least 6 months of experience providing emergency response services.

Fuel-Efficient Fleets Act of 2006 - Amends Federal transportation law to require each passenger automobile purchased by an executive agency after the enactment of this Act to achieve a minimum fuel economy of: (1) for vans (except minivans), not less than 15 miles per gallon; (2) for minivans, not less than 20 miles per gallon; (3) for pickup trucks, not less than 24 miles per gallon; and (4) for sport utility vehicles, not less than 36 miles per gallon.

Requires the Secretary of Energy to annually evaluate the fuel economy standards under this Act for new federal fleet vehicles. Authorizes the Secretary to award grants to assist states to purchase vans, trucks, sport utility vehicles, minivans, or passenger automobiles that meet the fuel economy requirements for new federal fleet vehicles as added by this Act. Requires such grants to be made available to states that comply with the minimum fuel economy standards.

Taxation of Minor Children Simplifcation Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the amount of the unearned income tax credit for minor children; (2) expand the parental election to claim such income; and (3) allow a parent to claim such income without the application of the tax credit.

(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the House on July 12, 2014.  Strengthening Child Welfare Response to Trafficking Act of 2014 - (Sec. 2) Amends the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act to include among the services that state child protective services systems may provide for identifying and assessing children who are sex trafficking victims, including provisions and procedures to identify and assess children who are victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons.  Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to report to Congress on the specific type and prevalence of severe forms of trafficking in persons to which children who are identified for services or intervention under the placement, care, or supervision of state, Indian tribe, or tribal organization child welfare agencies have been subjected as of the date of enactment of this Act.  Defines "severe form of trafficking in persons" to include the following: (1) children who are victims of trafficking; and (2) at risk of becoming victims of trafficking, including of children who are victims of severe forms of trafficking in persons.

Health Care COBRA Offset Tax Savings Act of 2005 or the Health Care COSTS Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a refundable tax credit for 50 percent of the amount of the premium (but for this Act, $30,000 increased by $10,000) which would be required to be paid by an individual who receives COBRA continuation coverage under a group health plan.

Enhanced Emergency and Enforcement Authority Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and the Securities Act of 1933 to make it an unlawful order for an investor, issuer, broker or dealer to conduct securities or comply with filing, reporting, delivery, or other obligations under the securities laws in a timely, orderly, or efficient manner, even if such order is made in response to a court order or a showing of cause.  Allows such an order to be issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) or by a depository institution (e.g., a bank or other financial institution).  Allows such an order to be served in any other district.  Amends the Investment Company Act of 1940 to make it unlawful for an investor, issuer, broker or dealer to conduct securities or comply with filing, reporting, delivery, or other obligations under the securities laws in a U.S. district court for any judicial district, subpoenas issued by or on behalf of such court to compel the attendance of witnesses or the production of documents or tangible things (or both) may be served in any other district.  Allows such an order

Safe Medications for the Elderly Act - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of pharmacological care services provided by a pharmacist who is legally authorized to furnish such services under State law.

(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on September 19, 2017.  This bill designates the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in Lexington, Kentucky, as the "Lexington VA Health Care System." (The VA is a nonprofit veterans' organization that provides medical, dental, vision, and other services to its members and employees.)  The VA shall designate the campus of the Troy Bowling Campus in Lexington as the "Troy Bowling Campus."  The campus shall be known and designated as the "Troy Bowling Campus."  The VA shall designate the health care facility of the VA at 1101 Veterans Drive in Lexington as the "Troy Bowling Campus."  The VA shall designate the campus of the Franklin R. Sousley Campus in Lexington as the "Troy Bowling Campus."

Elgin Stafford Mental Illness Information Disclosure Act of 2012 or Elgin's Law - Requires health care professionals to disclose to a parent of an individual who is being treated for mental illness by a health care professional, subject to specified exceptions, the information regarding the mental illness and treatment for mental illness that would be useful for the appropriate involvement of the parent with respect to the treatment. Exempts such information from HIPAA privacy regulations in exceptional circumstances.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to post information on the HIPAA privacy requirements on the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) websites as may be appropriate to inform the public and health care professionals.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 50% of the cost of the fuel (i.e., hydrogen) used to power a qualified hydrogen-powered vehicle refueling property. Defines "qualified hydrogen-powered vehicle refueling property" as property which: (1) is of a character subject to the allowable depreciation allowance; and (2) is for the production, storage, or dispensing of hydrogen fuel into the vehicle's fuel tank.

Excludes income from the sale of hydrogen fuel sold at retail for use in a hydrogen fuel cell vehicle from the gross income of the taxpayer. Terminates such exclusion after 2013.

Energy Savings Through Public-Private Partnerships Act of 2013 - Amends the National Energy Conservation Policy Act to require each federal agency to: (1) consider implementing any energy-saving or conservation measure life cycle cost-effective, and (2) bundling individual measures of varying paybacks together into combined projects (known as a "benchmarking system") to measure progress made toward such goal. Directs each federal agency to use energy savings performance contracts or utility energy service contracts to implement such measures. Requires the use of energy savings performance contracts or utility energy service contracts to measure progress made toward the goal of energy conservation.

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2015 This bill requires a state to enact and enforce a law that requires a minimum of 180 days of suspension for a driver's license if the driver is convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence. The Department of Transportation may withhold 1% of a state's apportionment of certain federal-aid highway funds if the state does not meet the requirements of this bill. The bill also requires the Department of Transportation to withhold 5% of a state's apportionment of certain federal-aid highway funds after a state meets the requirements of this bill. The bill also requires the Department of Justice to withhold 3% of a state's apportionment of certain federal-aid highway funds if the state does not meet the requirements of this bill. The bill also requires the Department of the Army to withhold 5% of a state's apportionment of certain federal-aid highway funds if the state does not meet the requirements of this bill.

Small Business Expansion and Job Creation Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) extend through 2010 the increased limitations on the expensing of certain business assets; (2) allow a special depreciation allowance for 2010 business assets; and (3) allow a taxpayer election to accelerate the rate of business capitalization through 2010.

Home-Assembled Firearms Restriction Act of 2015 This bill: (1) banning hazardous products (firearm receiver and receiver blank, for instance), (2) prohibiting the sale of any of the following:   a firearm receiver casting or firearm receiver blank that does not meet the definition of a firearm in the federal criminal code and that after purchase by a consumer, can be completed by the consumer to the point at which such casting or blank functions as a firearm frame or receiver for a semiautomatic assault weapon or machine gun; and (3) allowing the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) enforcement of this prohibition.   The bill also prohibits the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) from enforcing this prohibition in the same manner, by the same means, and with the same jurisdiction, powers, and duties as though all applicable terms and provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act were incorporated into and made a part of this Act.

Academic, Social, and Emotional Learning Act of 2011 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to include social and emotional learning (SEL) in the title II (Teacher Quality Enhancement) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965.

Requires that part A (Innovation for Teacher Quality) of title II include a teacher and principal training and recruiting fund and address the social and emotional development needs of students, including the need to improve student achievement, attainment, and behavior through addressing the social and emotional needs of students.

Requires that the term "social and emotional learning" (SEL) refer to the process through which children and adults acquire the knowledge, attitudes, and skills associated with the core areas of social and emotional competency, including self-awareness and self-management to achieve school and life success, such as identifying and recognizing strengths, needs, emotions, values, and self-efficacy, impulse control and stress management, self-motivation and discipline, and goal setting and organizational skills.

Extends the President' s term of service from two to one year.  Extends the period of probationary authority for a position that requires formal training, a license, or a license, certification, or other grant of permission to engage in a particular activity.  Requires an agency head to certify to the President that the probationary period applicable to a position is in the President' s best interest.  Extends the probationary period for a position that requires a license or a license, certification, or other grant of permission to operate from two to one year.  Extends the probationary period for a position that requires a license or a license, certification, or other grant of permission to operate from two to two years.

Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 and the Internal Revenue Code to provide that the concurrent resolution on the budget for FY 2006 or for any ensuing fiscal year shall be consistent with the spending limitation specified in the spending limitation on the budget for FY 2005 or 2006.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that the rate of tax imposed under this Act shall be reduced by the reduction percentage (the excess of the rate in effect over the rate for the reduction year, over the rate for the reduction year) if the OASDI rate ratio for the reduction year would have been 125 percent if the rate had been applicable and the rate during such year were twice such rate.

Defines "reduction year" as any year after the transition year in which the OASDI rate ratio exceeds 125 percent, and the excess of the reduction rate ratio for the transition year over the rate for the reduction year.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that the term "reduction percentage" for employer contributions to self-employed individuals and to the self-employed disability income is the same as the term for employer contributions to employer retirement accounts.

Great Lakes Navigation System Sustainability Act of 2013 - Directs the Secretary of the Army, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to manage and allocate funding for all of the individually authorized commercial and recreational navigation projects in the Great Lakes Navigation System (Great Lakes System) as components of a single, comprehensive system, recognizing the interdependence of the projects.  Directs the Secretary, acting through the Chief, to establish a program to fund eligible operations and maintenance projects of the Great Lakes System with the objective of maintaining such projects to their authorized depths and widths.  Authorizes appropriations for each of FY2014-FY2023 for such projects from the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund.  Requires the Secretary, acting through the Chief, to give a higher priority to projects than to projects in FY2014-FY2023.  Requires the Secretary, acting through the Chief, to give a higher priority to projects that are subject to the harbor maintenance fee and that are not subject to the harbor maintenance fee for which the non-federal sponsor provides a cost share of 50% or more.  Requires the Secretary, acting through the Chief, to give a higher priority to projects that are subject

Sweetgrass Hills Protection Act of 1995 - Establishes the Sweetgrass Hills Natural Area within the Bureau of Land Management's Sweetgrass Hills Area of Critical Environmental Concern as an administered natural area in Montana. 
Directs the Secretary of the Interior to acquire lands or interests within the Natural Area's boundaries by donation, purchase, or exchange. 
Prohibits the Secretary from issuing any lease under the mineral leasing or geothermal leasing laws of the United States for such lands. 
Prohibits any:  (1) mining or mining related activities within the Area from occurring except in accordance with requirements imposed by the Secretary; and (2) any surface disturbance of lands or waters within such Area, including disturbances through subsistence, from being permitted except in accordance with requirements imposed by the Secretary. 
Requires the Secretary to undertake and complete within three years after the enactment of this Act an expedited program to examine all unpatented mining claims, including those for which a patent application has been filed, within the Natural Area.  Provides for the determination of the Validity of a claim to be invalid. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Hiring Heroes Tax Incentive Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers a business tax credit for 15% of the wages of their employees who are either: (1) highly-qualified veterans who served on active duty in the Armed Forces of the United States; or (2) recently separated veterans who were separated from the Armed Forces under honorable conditions on active duty.

Prohibits the President from providing economic assistance, military assistance, or arms transfers to the government of Sudan unless the President certifies to the Congress that the government has taken appropriate action to eliminate chattel slavery in Sudan, including the enactment of antislavery laws, the enforcement of such laws, and the establishment of a slave trade control program.  Prohibits the Secretary of State from designating an individual to be responsible for monitoring slavery in Sudan when such diplomatic mission is reestablished. Directs the President to instruct the U.S. representative to each international financial institution to which the United States is a member to use the U.S. vote to oppose any assistance from such institution to Sudan until the government of Sudan has taken the necessary steps to eliminate chattel slavery.  Expresses the sense of the Congress that the President should work with foreign countries and appropriate international organizations to ensure that humanitarian assistance organizations have access to all parts of Sudan for the purpose of assisting individuals who have been enslaved to resettle in Sudan.

Medicare Established Provider Act of 2015 This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to implement a system to designate providers of services and suppliers who represent a low risk for submitting fraudulent claims for payment under Medicare. Under the system, providers and suppliers are required to: (1) submit annual updates on their status as having received payments for items and services furnished by such providers or suppliers, and (2) provide a method for payment or partial payment for such claims.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Treasury to strike and sell bronze duplicates.
Authorizes appropriations.

E-Mail User Protection Act - Prohibits a person from: (1) initiating the transmission of a unsolicited bulk electronic mail message that contains a false, fictitious, or misappropriated name of the sender, electronic mail return address, or name and phone number of a telephone contact person; (2) initiating the transmission of an unsolicited bulk electronic mail message to an interactive computer service with knowledge that such message falsifies an Internet domain, header information, date or time stamp, originating e-mail address, or other identifier; (3) initiating the transmission of an unsolicited bulk electronic mail message and to fail to comply with the request of the recipient of the message, delivered to the sender's electronic mail address, that the recipient does not wish to receive such messages; (4) using, creating, selling, or distributing any computer software that is primarily designed to create, on an electronic mail message, false Internet domain, header information, date or time stamp, originating e-mail address, or other identifier; (5) initiating the transmission of an unsolicited bulk electronic mail message and to fail to comply with such request, delivered to the sender's electronic mail address, that the recipient does not wish to receive such messages; (6)

Furthering Accountability and Individual Rights within the Military Act of 2014 or the Fair Military Act - Directs the Secretary of a military department to ensure that the written performance appraisals of each member of the Armed Forces under the jurisdiction of that Secretary include an assessment of the extent to which the member supports the sexual assault prevention and response program of the Armed Force concerned.  Requires the Secretary of each military department to ensure that the performance appraisals of each commanding officer under the Secretary's jurisdiction indicate the extent to which the commanding officer has or has not established a command climate in which: (1) allegations of sexual assault are properly managed and fairly evaluated; and (2) a victim can report criminal activity without fear of retaliation, including ostracism and group pressure from other members of the command.  Directs the Secretary of each military department concerned to ensure that the provisions of title XVII of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2014 and this Act apply to the United States Armed Forces. Directs the Secretary of each Department in which the Coast Guard is operating to ensure that such provisions of title XVII and this Act apply to the Coast Guard Academy. Amends Federal transportation law to grant to qualified motor vehicles a parking privilege for certain individuals with disabilities.  Provides that such privilege shall be extended to qualified motor vehicles designated under the laws of any State or political subdivision not in compliance with this Act.

Clean Up Earmarks Act of 2010 or the CUE Act of 2010 - Directs the Comptroller General to submit to Congress an audit of 5% of Senate earmarks for the current fiscal year chosen at random.

Amends the Standing rules of the Senate to require the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives to take necessary steps to improve the Web site earmarks.gov to: (1) make earmarks more easily searchable and to ensure that the site is user-friendly; and (2) ensure that the site does not include extraneous information.

Amends Rule XI of the Standing Rules to require the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives to take necessary steps to improve the Senator's earmarks.gov to: (1) make earmarks more easily searchable and to ensure that the site is user-friendly and does not include extraneous information; and (2) ensure that the site does not include extraneous information.

Amends the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995 to require the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives to report to Congress on the employment of a lobbyist who might directly

Securing the Cities Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to establish the Secure the Cities program to enhance DHS's ability to detect and prevent terrorist attacks and other high consequence events utilizing nuclear or other radiological materials that pose a high risk to homeland security in high-risk urban areas. (Sec. 3) DHS shall develop model exercises to test the preparedness of jurisdictions participating in the program. (Sec. 4) No additional funds are authorized to carry out this bill and the amendments made by this bill. Such requirements shall be carried out using amounts otherwise authorized.

Arapaho-Roosevelt National Forests Land Exchange Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to convey title to the lands owned by Grand Creek, LLC in Clear Creek County, Colorado, in order to exchange the non-federal lands for the federal lands.

Guaranteed Health Coverage for Pre-existing Conditions Act of 2014 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to prohibit a group health plan or health insurance issuer offering group health insurance coverage from imposing any preexisting condition exclusion with respect to such plan or coverage. Defines "preexisting condition exclusion" as a condition or exclusion relating to a condition that was present before the enrollment of the individual in the plan or for which the individual was either notified or recommended for enrollment.  Requires a health insurance issuer that offers coverage in the individual market to accept every employer and every individual in such market that applies for coverage.  Requires a health insurance issuer that offers coverage in the group market to establish special enrollment periods for qualifying events.  Requires the provisions of this Act to apply to coverage offered to individuals by a health insurance issuer in the individual market.  Prohibits PPACA repeal legislation from being enacted.

Workplace Integrity Act - Prohibits an employee from being granted official time in connection with any matter covered by this Act.

Authorizes the use of official time only for a purpose allowable under this Act, but only for a purpose allowable under specified federal law.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2013 the authority of the Secretary of the Treasury to finance alternative motor vehicle facilities.

Military Families Act - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security or the Attorney General to adjust the status of an alien who: (1) applies for such adjustment, (2) is admissible to the United States as an immigrant, (3) pays a fee in an amount determined by the Secretary for processing such application (unless such fee is waived by the Secretary), and (4) is physically present in the United States.

Preventing a Government Shutdown Act - Amends federal law to provide that any regular appropriations bill for a fiscal year (or, if applicable, for each fiscal year in a biennium, or a joint resolution making continuing appropriations is not in effect), if any regular appropriations bill does not become law before the beginning of such fiscal year, shall be at: (1) a specified rate of operations provided in the regular appropriation Act providing for such project or activity; or (2) in the absence of an Act, the rate of operations provided in such Act. Makes appropriations and funds made available, and authority granted, for a project or activity for any fiscal year pursuant to this Act at a rate of operations not in excess of the lower of: (1) the rate of operations provided in the regular appropriation Act providing for such project or activity; or (2) in the absence of such an Act, the last day of such fiscal year.

Senior Nutrition Act of 2002 - Amends the Agriculture and Consumer Protection Act of 1973 to provide for the eligibility of elderly persons under the community supplemental food program (CMPP) to participate in a CMPP program serving elderly persons.

Mortgage Disclosure Simplification Act of 2007 - Amends the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) to develop and prescribe standard written forms for statement of the essential terms of a federally related mortgage loan. Directs the Secretary to require that: (1) such forms are used in all transactions in the United States that involve federally related mortgage loans; and (2) in any such a transaction the forms are to be appropriately and accurately completed by the lender or mortgage broker or both, and the completed form to be provided to the borrower, together with the completed form to be provided by the lender or mortgage broker, or both, within three days after the application for the loan is made. Directs the standard written forms to be: (1) used in all transactions involving federally related mortgage loans, and (2) to be provided to the borrower, in a three-day after application, in accordance with such requirements as the Secretary shall by regulation.

Health Insurance Rate Review Act This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to declare that the requirements that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) review unreasonable premium increases in health care coverage do not prohibit a state from imposing additional rate requirements on health insurance issuers that are more protective of consumers. HHS or the relevant state insurance commissioner or state regulator must ensure that any excessive, unjustified, or unfairly discriminatory rates are corrected before, or as soon as possible after, implementation, including through mechanisms such as denying rates, modifying rates, or requiring rebates to consumers. HHS or the relevant state insurance commissioner or regulator must take corrective actions to ensure that any excessive, unjustified, or unfairly discriminatory rates are corrected, and HHS or the relevant state insurance commissioner or regulator must ensure that HHS or the relevant state insurance commissioner or regulator comply with the requirements of this bill.

Protecting Neighborhoods from Oil Pollution Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to require the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to: (1) issue final regulations requiring an owner or operator of an oil storage or processing facility to permanently close such facility if one or both of the following conditions apply: (1) the facility is located within 1 mile of 100 or more residential units, and 2 or more covered discharges occur at such facility within any 10-year period; (2) the facility is the source of groundwater contamination affecting 100 or more residential units; (3) the facility is the source of contamination affecting 100 or more residential units; (4) the facility is the source of contamination affecting 100 or more residential units within 10 years; or (5) the facility is the source of contamination affecting 100 or more residential units within 100 years.

Defines "permanent close" to include requirements that: (1) all liquid and sludge are removed from each container and connecting line associated with the facility within 10 years; (2) all connecting lines and piping associated

Veteran Employment Through Technology Education Courses Act or the VET TEC Act - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out a one-year pilot program of educational assistance to veterans who are eligible to enroll in high technology programs of education (HTE). Requires the Secretary to seek to enter into contracts with multiple qualified providers of HTE programs to provide eligible veterans with such assistance. Requires the Secretary to pay to each eligible veteran on a full-time basis a monthly housing stipend equal to the product of: (1) the amount of the veteran's basic allowance for a member with dependents in pay grade E-5 residing in the military housing area that encompass all or the majority portion of the ZIP code area in which is located the institution at which the individual is enrolled; or (2) the lesser of 1.0 or the number of course hours required for full-time pursuit of the program of education. Requires the Secretary to report annually to Congress on the pilot program.

Veterans' Burial Benefits Enhancement Act of 2003 - Amends Federal law to permit the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to lease to the Secretary specified unutilized or underutilized Federal property in a national cemetery under the National Cemetery Administration (NCA) for the burial of veterans who are veterans of any war. Sets forth provisions regarding the use of such property, including provisions regarding: (1) the lease of unutilized or underutilized Federal property in a national cemetery; and (2) the establishment of a national cemetery in each geographic area identified by the Secretary in order to ensure that veterans residing in such geographic areas reside at least 50 miles from an open national cemetery.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service, to establish an office, to be known as the Office for the Preservation of America's Main Street, to: (1) perform the functions of the Preservation Office; (2) support efforts of State and local public and private persons and entities to preserve Route 66; and (3) act as a clearinghouse for communication among Federal, State, and local agencies and private persons and entities interested in the preservation of Route 66.

Camera Accountability Maintenance and Transparency in Policing Act of 2017 or the CAM TIP Act of 2017 This bill amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to authorize the Department of Justice's Bureau of Justice Assistance to make grants to states, local governments, and Indian tribes for the acquisition, operation, and maintenance of body-worn cameras for law enforcement officers.  The bill requires grantees to use grant funds to: (1) establish policies and procedures for when law enforcement officers should wear, activate, and deactivate such cameras; (2) ensure the protection of civil liberties of members of the general public; (3) establish or propose guidelines for the collection and storage of recordings; (4) establish policies for the public's participation in and accountability for the use of such cameras; and (5) have guidelines and training courses for law enforcement officers.  The bill establishes the task force on community policing and body camera technology that shall provide recommendations on community policing. The Government Accountability Office must report on the Department of Defense Excess Personal Property Program.

Improving Corporate Governance Through Diversity Act of 2017 This bill requires executive agencies to submit to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) annual reports on diversity, including data submitted by: (1) the board of directors of a covered corporation, (2) the C-level executives of certain of its affiliates, and (3) the boards of directors and executive officials of certain of its subchapters.  The SEC must report on the racial, ethnic, and gender composition of the board and the C-level executives of the issuers of the annual reports. The SEC must also report on the affiliation of any member of the board or any C-level executive to a historically underrepresented group, including veterans of the Armed Forces and individuals with disabilities. The SEC must also report on any plan or strategy that exists on the submission of such data to improve diversity.
Medicaid Mammography Coverage Act of 1993 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to provide for coverage of screening mammography performed on women under 35 years of age.

Smart Water Management Conservation and Efficiency Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to establish and carry out a smart water management pilot program to award grants to utilities, municipalities, water districts, and other water authorities for demonstrating and deploying novel and innovative technology-based solutions that will: (1) increase the energy and water efficiency of drinking water, wastewater treatment, and water reuse systems; (2) improve those systems to help communities make significant progress in conserving water, saving energy, and reducing costs; and (3) support the implementation of innovative processes and the installation of advanced automated systems that provide real-time data on energy and water. Requires the Secretary to make competitive, merit-reviewed grants to no less than three but no more than five eligible entities. Requires the Secretary to annually evaluate each grant project and make best practices identified in the evaluations available to the public.

College Research Education and Teacher Excellence (CREATE) Opportunity Act of 2012 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to make permanent and increase the amount of the research tax credit for graduate students and postdoctoral fellowships.

Amends title IV (Student Assistance) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 to require the Secretary of Education to make annual payments to colleges and universities for the costs of conducting specified research. (Currently, such research is limited to the costs of conducting a one-year survey or an one-year internship.) Directs the Secretary to award a student's research project not more than two years after it is first awarded and in a program of instruction at the junior or community college for which the college awards an associate's degree or a certificate.

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to make permanent the requirement that certain student loan obligations be repaid in full within one academic year after the first loan is awarded.

Check the Box for Homeless Veterans Act of 2013 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) establish in the Treasury the Homeless Veterans Assistance Fund to provide services to homeless veterans; and (2) allow individual taxpayers to designate on their tax returns a portion (not less than $1) of any overpayment of tax or an additional contribution for the fund.

Stop Turning Out Prisoners Act - Amends the federal criminal code to provide that, in a civil action with respect to prison conditions, the court shall not grant or approve any prospective relief, except a relief that is narrowly drawn and the least intrusive means to remedy the violation of the Federal right. Prohibits the court, in determining the intrusiveness of the relief, from granting or approving any relief: (1) that is narrowly drawn and the least intrusive means to remedy the violation of the Federal right; or (2) that is immediately terminated.

Prohibits the court, in any civil action with respect to prison conditions, from granting or approving relief that was approved or granted in the absence of a finding by the court that prison conditions violated a Federal right. Requires a defendant or intervenor to be entitled to the immediate termination of any prospective relief, if such relief was approved or granted in the absence of a finding by the court that prison conditions violated a Federal right.

Directs the court, in any civil action in a federal court with respect to prison conditions, to promptly rule on any motion to modify or terminate prospective relief in a civil action with respect to prison conditions. Requires any prospective relief that

Marine Navigation Safety Improvement Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the Marine Navigation Safety Account, to be known as the "Marine Navigation Safety Fund," to be managed by the Secretary of Commerce.  Directs the Secretary to transfer to such Fund an amount not to exceed the sum of:  (1) 8 percent of the amount of taxes received in the Treasury under the Act for 1991 and 1992; and (2) interest on such amount for the calendar year 1991 and 1992, credited pursuant to the Act. 
Requires the Fund to be made available to the Secretary for the purposes of programs and activities related to commercial marine navigation. 
Amends the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 to authorize the Secretary to make the Fund available for the programs and activities related to commercial marine navigation.

Librarian Education and Development Act of 2003 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to extend to certain Federal student loan forgiveness and perkins loan forgiveness programs the prohibition against student loan forgiveness and perkins loan forgiveness programs for teachers who have: (1) employed for five consecutive complete school years in a school qualifying for such loan cancellation; or (2) taught a subject area relevant to the borrower's academic major as certified by the chief administrative officer of the public or nonprofit private secondary school.

Amends title IV (Student Assistance) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to provide for direct student loan forgiveness and perkins loan forgiveness for teachers who teach a subject area relevant to the borrower's academic major as certified by the chief administrative officer of the public or nonprofit private secondary school.

(Sec. 1) This bill suspends, until January 31, 2014, the authority of the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to provide supplemental agricultural assistance to eligible programs. (Under current law, USDA may only provide supplemental assistance if the supplemental program is provided through the agricultural marketing program.)  (Under the agricultural marketing program, USDA may only provide supplemental assistance to eligible programs if the program is provided through the commodity marketing program.)  (Sec. 2) The bill also suspends, until January 31, 2014, the authority of the Department to provide supplemental agricultural assistance to eligible programs that are related to the conservation stewardship program, farmland protection program, environmental quality incentives program, and wildlife habitat incentives program.  (Sec. 3) The bill also suspends, until January 31, 2014, the authority of the Department to provide supplemental agricultural assistance to eligible programs that are related to the conservation and agricultural marketing programs that are related to the conservation stewardship program, farmland protection program, environmental quality incentives program, and wildlife habitat programs.

Innovation Protection Act - Establishes in the Treasury the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Fund, which shall be available to the Director of the Office, until expended, for the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Enterprise Act of 1990 (the Act). Establishes in the Treasury the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Fees Fund, which shall be available to the Director of the Office, until expended, for the United States Patent and Trademark Office Public Fees Reserve Fund. Amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal the property subject to a liability tax.

Hazardous Materials Cooperative Research Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to establish a hazardous materials cooperative research program. Requires the DOT to establish an independent governing board to select projects and studies to be carried out under the program. Requires the board to select cooperative research studies that will yield results immediately applicable to risk analysis and mitigation or that will strengthen the ability of first responders to respond to incidents and accidents involving transportation of hazardous materials.
Requires the Quinault Business Committee to maintain separate accounts for the principal amount of the judgments and the investment income of the Quinault Indian Nation.

Trail of the Ancients National Heritage Area Study Act of 2005 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a study to assess the feasibility and suitability of designating the Highway 101 corridor in the Four Corners National Heritage Area as the Trail of the Ancients National Heritage Area.

Protecting Dissenting Viewpoints and Vests Act of 2017 This bill amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from revoking any license or other authorization of, or otherwise taking action against, any person on the basis, in whole or in part, of viewpoints taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content that is broadcast or otherwise disseminated by such person or any person affiliated with such person. The FCC may not place on any approval under the bill any condition regarding viewpoints to be taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content broadcast or otherwise disseminated by the person seeking such approval or decision, any successor of such person, or any person affiliated with such person. The bill prohibits the President from directing an agency to take any action against any person on the basis, in whole or in part, of viewpoints taken, or not taken, on issues of public importance in content that is broadcast or otherwise disseminated by the person seeking such approval or decision, any predecessor of such person, or any affiliate of such person.  The bill prohibits the President from directing an agency to place on any approval or other decision within the jurisdiction of the agency any

Skilled Workforce Enhancement Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited business credit for expenses incurred by highly skilled metalworking trades training employees.  Limits such credit to 80 percent of the training expenses paid or incurred by a taxpayer during the training period.  Requires a minimum of $100,000 per employee for training expenses and a maximum of 80 percent of such expenses for training employees of at least 18,000 hours of continuous hours of training.

Criminal Antitrust Anti-Retaliation Act - Amends the Antitrust Criminal Penalty Enhancement and Reform Act of 2004 to prohibit whistleblowers who provide or caused a violation of antitrust laws or any act or violation of antitrust laws from discriminating against a whistleblower in employment because: (1) the whistleblower provided or caused the violation; or (2) the whistleblower planned, initiated, or assisted an investigation or a proceeding filed or about to be filed relating to the violation.

Defines "whistleblower" as an employee, contractor, subcontractor, or agent protected from discrimination under this Act.

Authorizes an employee, contractor, subcontractor, or agent to seek relief by filing a complaint with the Secretary of Labor or by bringing an action for de novo review in the appropriate U.S. district court for an action that is against the employment practices of such employees.
Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to convey certain lands in New Mexico to one or more eligible buyers for the purpose of business and community development.

Great Lakes Pipeline Safety Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of Transportation (DOT) to study and report to the Department of the Interior on economic and environmental risks to the Great Lakes from a rupture, breakage, or other failure of onshore, underwater pipeline facilities within the Straits of Mackinac.  DOT shall conduct a supplemental study to evaluate the condition and structural integrity of onshore, underwater pipeline facilities in the Straits of Mackinac, taking certain criteria into consideration.

Grand Jury Reform Act of 1998 - Amends the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure to require the court to instruct and charge a grand jury on the rights, responsibilities, and duties of the grand jury, including the duty to inquire into criminal offenses that are alleged to have been committed within the jurisdiction, the right to call and interrogate witnesses, request production of a book, paper, document, or other object, the necessity of finding credible evidence of each material element of the crime charged, and the right to request that the attorney for the government draft indictments for charges other than those originally requested by that attorney. 
Requires a witness subpoena to be given adequate and reasonable notice of:  (1) his or her right to counsel; (2) his or her privilege against self-incrimination; (3) the subject matter of the grand jury investigation; (4) whether his or her own conduct is under investigation; (5) the criminal statute, the violation of which is under consideration by the grand jury, if such statute is known at the time of issuance of the subpoena; (6) his or her rights regarding immunity; and (7) any other rights and privileges which the court de

Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), to develop a plan for the purchase, storage, and rotation of a six-month supply of vaccines routinely recommended for children and adults and vaccines routinely recommended for children by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). Requires the Secretary to carry out: (1) a discussion of the considerations that formed the plan; and (2) the prioritization of the schedule for purchasing vaccines. Requires the Secretary to require manufacturers of vaccines included in such supply to provide at least one year notice of a discontinuance of the manufacture of a vaccine.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to pay a specified amount of compensation to those members of the Armed Forces and U.S. civilian employees who were captured by Japan and who were used as slave labor during World War II and who were prisoners of war during World War II.

Classroom Safety Act of 2000 - Amends the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) to authorize school personnel to discipline (including expel or suspend) a child with a disability who: (1) carries or possesses a weapon to or at a school, on school premises, or to or at a school function, under the jurisdiction of a State or local educational agency (LEA), or possesses or uses illegal drugs or sells or solicits the sale of a controlled substance while at a school; or (2) possesses or uses illegal drugs or sells or solicits the sale of a controlled substance while at a school. Declares that nothing in this Act shall be construed to prevent a child with a disability who is disciplined under the authority provided under this Act from asserting a defense that the carrying or possession of the weapon, or the possession of an illegal drug or sale or solicitation of the sale of a controlled substance was unintentional or innocent. Authorizes LEAs to choose to continue to provide educational services to a child with a disability who is expelled or suspended, if the LEA so chooses, and the location where the LEA provides the services shall be left to the discretion of the LEA

Duty Suspension Facilitation Act of 2010 - Requires the International Trade Commission (ITC) to submit to the Committee on Finance and the House Committee on Ways and Means of the Senate Committee on Agriculture and the Public Policy Committee on Finance and the House Committee on Agriculture and the Public Policy Committee on Commerce a proposed legislation which includes recommendations regarding: (1) amendments to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States extending existing temporary duty suspensions or existing duty reductions; (2) modifications to the Schedule to make technical corrections; and (3) the adjustment of duty to make technical changes.

Prohibits the ITC from recommending in the proposed legislation any suspension or reduction in duty of U.S. interest, if: (1) an interested federal agency determines such suspension or reduction is not in U.S. interest; (2) such suspension or reduction is objected to by a domestic producer who demonstrates that there is domestic production of the article for which suspension or reduction of duty is recommended in commercially available quantities; (3) the loss in revenue to the United States from such suspension or reduction of duty exceeds $500,000 annually; or (4) the suspension or reduction in duty is to be effective

National Park System New Area Studies Act - Amends the National Park System General Authorities Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to submit to the congressional research and development committees a list of areas which have been previously studied that contain primarily historical resources and a list of areas which have been previously studied that contain primarily natural resources.  Authorizes appropriations.
