DHS Paid Administrative Leave Accountability Act of 2015 (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to report to Congress on DHS employees on administrative leave who have been placed on administrative leave for certain personnel matters for a period of 6 consecutive months or longer.  The bill defines "personnel matters" as, with respect to an employee, any personnel investigation (including any investigation into misconduct and any national security or suitability investigation), any criminal matter, or any adverse action proposed or taken by DHS, including any action under the United States. DHS must implement a Department-wide policy in accordance with existing federal guidance specifically related to the use of administrative leave, or any other type of paid non-duty status without charge to leave, for personnel matters.  The policy shall include the responsibilities of DHS components for reporting information relating to administrative leave and such paid non-duty status to DHS, as required under the Act.  DHS must submit quarterly reports to Congress on DHS employees on administrative leave who have been placed on administrative leave for certain personnel matters for a period of 6 consecutive months

Work Made For Hire and Copyright Corrections Act of 2000 - Makes changes in the definition of "work made for hire" to: (1) include any sound recording of a work made for hire; and (2) exclude any legal significance or congressional approval or disapproval of any judicial determination that determines whether a work is eligible for copyright protection.

Prohibits the repeal of the prohibition against interpretation of a work made for hire provision as to whether it is eligible for copyright protection or whether it is interpreted to indicate congressional approval or disapproval of judicial determinations by the courts or the Copyright Office.

Tribal Colleges and Universities Faculty Loan Forgiveness Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to carry out a program through the holder of a loan, under the Federal Family Education Loan program, of assuming or canceling an obligation to repay a $15,000 federal student loan for a new student loan or loan replacement, who: (1) has been employed as a full-time faculty member at a Tribal College or University; and (2) is not in default on the loan.

Directs the Secretary to assume or cancel such obligation: (1) 15% of the amount of all federal student loans for the first or second year of a student's employment, (2) 20% of such total amount for the third or fourth year of such employment, and (3) 30% of such total amount for the fifth year of such employment. Prohibits such repayment of a federal student loan made for the first time after the first semester of a graduate program.

Amends the Public Health Service Act to provide for the double benefit of a nursing instructor and a nursing program at a tribally controlled college or university.

Taxpayers' Cancer Research Funding Act of 1996 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow taxpayers to designate on their tax returns a $5 contribution to the Breast and Prostate Cancer Research Fund.  Establishes in the Treasury the Breast and Prostate Cancer Research Fund.

Provide Access and Retain Continuity Act or the PARC Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to enter into agreements with States that submit an agreement that is approved or that is not approved by the Secretary to provide for States to conduct activities that are specified approved under this Act.  Allows a State to petition the Secretary for such an agreement.  Allows a State to amend and resubmit a petition that contains the terms of such an agreement.  Requires a State to provide to the requesting State a clear and comprehensive statement of the reasons why the petition was denied.  Allows a State to amend and resubmit the denied petition.  Requires a State to include a letter signed by the governor of the State submitting the petition addressed to the Secretary that contains a description of the eligible activities that the State seeks to conduct.  Allows a State to amend and resubmit the petition.  Requires a State to include a statement that the State shall indemnify and hold the U.S. harmless for any action of negligence or gross negligence on the part of the State while conducting an eligible activity.  Allows a State to amend and resubmit the petition.  Requires a State to include a letter that

Safe and Secure Border Infrastructure Act - Directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a grant program, administered by the Secretary of Transportation and the General Services Administration, to construct transportation and supporting infrastructure improvements at existing and new international border crossings to facilitate the safe, secure, and efficient movement of motor vehicles, non-motor vehicles, cargo, and individuals, including pedestrians, in order to facilitate the safe, secure, and efficient cross-border movement of motor vehicles, non-motor vehicles, cargo, and individuals, including pedestrians. Requires such projects to include: (1) highway or bridge projects eligible for such grants; (2) public transportation projects eligible for such grants; (3) demonstration and pilot projects related to innovative cross border systems management; and (4) passenger and freight rail transportation projects.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose an excise tax on the income of the personnel of a commercial passenger cruise vessel on the ground.  Establishes the Intermodal Infrastructure Trust Fund in the Treasury.

Country-of-Origin Labeling for Fuels Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy to study and report to Congress on methods and standards for requiring motor vehicle fuel suppliers and motor vehicle fuel retailers to disclose country-of-origin information with respect to motor vehicle fuel to the next person in the supply chain.

Requires the Secretary to prescribe regulations requiring such information disclosure.

King Holiday and Service Act of 1993 - Amends the Act entitled "An Act to Establish a Commission to assist in the first observance of the Federal legal holiday honoring Martin Luther King, Jr. FY 1994-1995" (Act) to require that the Commission:  (1) include service opportunities within its activities; and (2) make grants to eligible entities to pay the Federal share of the cost of planning and carrying out such service opportunities. 
Amends the National and Community Service Act of 1990 to authorize the Commission to make grants to eligible entities for the Federal share of the cost of planning and carrying out the activities described in this Act. 
Requires the Commission to make such grants, in cash or in kind, fairly evaluated, including facilities, equipment, or services. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Hass Avocado Quality Assurance Act of 2007 - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to issue final regulations to ensure that all Hass avocados sold to consumers in the United States meet the minimum maturity standards for sale to a consumer of California state law. Exempts such Hass avocados: (1) intended for consumption by charitable institutions; (2) intended for distribution by relief agencies; (3) intended for commercial processing into products; or (4) that the Secretary determines should not be subject to such subsection or such regulations.

Requires the Secretary to use inspectors that inspect avocados for compliance with the Agricultural Adjustment Act. Authorizes the Secretary to divert, export, or repack and reinspect any Hass avocados that do not meet the requirements of this Act or the regulations issued pursuant to this Act. Sets forth penalties for violations of this Act.
Help Organ Procurement Expand Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for organ donation.

Unemployment Compensation, Reemployment, and Fairness Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to require States to provide employment compensation to individuals who are participating in a qualified self-employment program.  Requires the State agency charged with the administration of the State law to provide an early review of such individuals' reemployment prospects.  Requires the State agency to provide job search and placement services, counseling, testing, occupational and labor market information, and referral to employers to such individuals.  Requires the State agency to provide technical and training program staff to assist with reemployment services.  Requires the Secretary of Labor to prescribe regulations to carry out this Act.

Responsible Debt Relief and Democracy Reform Act - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to authorize the President to cancel or reduce amounts owed to any foreign country by the United States if the government of that country: (1) ensures freedom of the press; (2) ensures freedom of association; (3) has established an independent and nondiscriminatory judicialiciary; (4) provides for the reduction or elimination of corruption relating to public officials; and (5) has an independent agency to audit and make all audits available to the appropriate administrative or judicial entities.

Requires the President to report to Congress that: (1) the requirements of this Act have been satisfied with respect to the foreign country involved; or (2) the requirement of this Act has been satisfied with respect to the foreign country involved.

21st Century Federal Pell Grant Plus Act - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to allow a student who is eligible for a Pell Grant (a Federal program of study designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary to succeed in a degree or certificate program) to receive the increased Pell Grant amount if the student: (1) completes the Pell Grant program within two years; or (2) enters a Pell Grant program after that time.

Veterans' Employment Transition Support Act of 2005 or the VETS Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for the hiring of qualified veterans as a combat zone or a hazardous duty area veteran.

United States Mariner and Vessel Protection Act of 2009 - Authorizes the use of maritime safety and security (MSS) and international maritime law (IML) to defend U.S. vessels against acts of piracy in international waters. Requires the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating to: (1) notify Congress when deploying a maritime safety and security team to deter, protect against, and rapidly respond to acts of piracy; and (2) notify the congressional defense committees when an individual is solely responsible for damages in an action brought under regulations under this Act. Provides that an individual's liability shall not be limited to the failure to use a firearm, but only the failure to use a firearm in a case in which the individual is solely responsible for damages.

States that a claimed process of making or using a machine, manufacture, or composition of matter is not infringed if the invention at the time it was made is a biotechnological process as defined under this Act.  States that a claimed process of making or using a machine, manufacture, or composition of matter is not infringed if the invention is a biotechnological material used in making a product if the invention is a biotechnological material used in making a product if the invention is a biotechnological material

Enhanced Savings Opportunities Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for the tax treatment of contributions to defined contribution plans.  Treats an annual contribution as not exceeding $40,000.  Treats an annuity contract as a defined contribution plan maintained by each employer with respect to which the employer has the control required under this Act.  Treats a deferred compensation plan of a State or local government and tax-exempt organization as a defined contribution plan.  Exempts from such limitations any pension plan for an individual for which the participant has the control required under this Act.
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2005, the duty on certain milling machines, extruders, and other milling equipment.

Directing Dollars to Disaster Relief Act of 2015 (Sec. 3) This bill directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to implement an integrated plan to control and reduce administrative costs for major disasters, which shall include: (1) steps the agency will take to reduce such costs; (2) timetables for implementation; and (3) a report on the plan that Congress must submit to Congress. FEMA shall: (1) submit an updated report for the previous fiscal year if it is determined to be feasible to track such data, and (2) submit an updated report for the previous five fiscal years if it is determined to be feasible.

Children First Act of 2010 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act (SSA) to exclude child care assistance from the determination of the child care assistance limit on the basis of the child's need for care.

Increases funding for child care. Reduces funding for child care for parents.

Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to transfer funds to an individual with custody who provides child care for a specified period (currently, limited to six months) if the individual provides child care for up to 6 months in a total year.

Requires the Secretary to report to the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) on the state of child care assistance in the United States for calendar quarters beginning on or after October 1, 2010.

Office of Biometric Identity Management Authorization Act of 2018 or the OBIM Authorization Act of 2018 This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish the Office of Biometric Identity Management within the Management Directorate of the Department of Homeland Security. The Office shall: (1) report to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) as the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) may direct, and (2) be administered by the Director of the Office. The Office shall: (1) have a significant professional management experience, as well as experience in the field of biometrics and identity management, lead DHS's biometric identity services, support anti-terrorism, counter-terrorism, border security, credentialing, national security, and public safety missions, and manage the operation of the Department's primary biometric repository and identification system, the primary biometric identification system, the primary federal, state, local, and tribal agencies, appropriate federal, state, local, and tribal agencies, appropriate foreign governments, and private sector entities; (2) enable operational missions across DHS, the Department, its components, appropriate federal, state, local,

National Trails System Willing Seller Act - Amends the National Trails System Act to: (1) prohibit the federal acquisition of land or interest in land outside the exterior boundaries of any federally administered area, except with the owner's consent, for the Oregon, Mormon Pioneer, Lewis and Clark, Iditarod, and Nez Perce National Historic Trails and the Continental Divide, North Country, Ice Age, and Potomac Heritage National Scenic Trails; and (2) provide that federal authority to acquire fee title shall be limited to an average of not more than one-quarter mile on either side of the Oregon, Mormon Pioneer, Continental Divide, Lewis and Clark, and Iditarod National Historic Trails and the Continental Divide National Scenic Trails.

Prohibits a prevailing rate employee, notwithstanding any other provision of law and except as otherwise provided in this Act, from being paid during the period beginning on January 1, 2014, and ending on the normal effective date of the applicable wage survey adjustment in FY2014, for: (1) the period beginning on January 1, 2014, and ending on the normal effective date of the applicable wage schedule in FY2014; and (2) the period beginning after the end of such period and ending on September 30, 2014, in an amount that exceeds the rate payable for the applicable grade and step of the applicable wage schedule in FY2014.

Prohibits a prevailing rate employee, notwithstanding any other provision of law and except as otherwise provided in this Act, from being paid during the periods beginning on January 1, 2014, and ending on the day after the end of the period and ending on September 30, 2014, in an amount that exceeds the rate payable by more than the sum of the percentage adjustment taking effect in FY2014 and the difference

Personal Exemption Fairness Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to require the Secretary of the Treasury to: (1) prescribe a multiplicative cost-of-living adjustment (COLDA) multiplier for each metropolitan statistical area in the United States, and (2) publish such COLDA index for that area.

Requires the President and the two-thirds majority of the Congress to report to the Congress on the progress made in implementing and executing the recommendations for closure or realignment of military installations.

Amends the Defense Base Closure and Realignment Act of 1990 to provide for a two-year post-2007 biennial review of the recommendations for closure or realignment of military installations.

Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection Advisory Board Enhancement Act - Amends the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 to require the Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to establish a Small Business Advisory Board to: (1) advise and consult with the CFPB in the exercise of its functions, and (2) provide information on emerging practices of small business concerns that provide eligible financial products or services, including regional trends, the effect that decisions by the CFPB have on rural areas, concerns, and other relevant information.

Requires the Director to appoint at least: (1) 15 members to the Board; and (2) at least 20 members to the Small Business Advisory Council.

Requires the Director to establish a Credit Union Advisory Council to advise and consult with the CFPB on consumer financial products or services that impact credit unions.

Declaration of Official Language Act of 1997 - Amends Federal law to require the English language proficiency standard for all U.S. citizens to be in English. 
Repeals provisions of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 which require bilingual election requirements.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to commence the redeployment of units and members of the Armed Forces deployed in Iraq as part of Operation Iraqi Freedom and contractors operating in Iraq as part of Iraq funded using amounts appropriated to the Department of Defense (DOD). Prohibits DOD funds from being obligated or expended to increase the number of members serving in Iraq as of January 1, 2007, unless the increase has been specifically authorized in advance by an Act of Congress. Authorizes DOD to retain in Iraq members of the Armed Forces for the purpose of providing security for the U.S. Embassy and other U.S. diplomatic missions in Iraq, protecting American citizens, serving in roles consistent with customary diplomatic positions, and training and equipping members of the Iraqi Security Forces. Prohibits DOD funds from being obligated or expended to further deploy units or members to Iraq, including through participation in any multinational force in Iraq except as provided under this Act or unless such deployment is specifically authorized in advance by an Act of Congress. Directs the President to transfer to the government of Iraq all rights in any military facility in Iraq that was constructed, repaired, or improved using amounts appropriated to DOD and occupied by a unit of the

Child Immunization Incentive Act of 1993 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to provide for the child care and immunization benefits of the TANF system for children under the age of six. 
Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act to require TANF providers to submit to parents of such children certificates signed by a physician who verifies that the child has been immunized. 
Directs the Surgeon General to issue, and revise from time to time, recommendations for the immunization of such children.

Home Energy Savings Incentives Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for the cost of qualified energy efficiency expenditures. Limits the credit to the excess of $5,000 over the aggregate credits allowed for such expenditures for all prior taxable years.

Federal Computer Security Act - Requires the Comptroller General to report to the Congress on the use of federal computer systems by agencies that operate a computer network that provides access to classified or personally identifiable information. Requires such reports to include: (1) a description of the logical access standards used to access such a system; (2) whether the agency is using multi-factor logical access controls to access such a system; (3) reasons for not using such access or multi-factor logical access controls; (4) data security management practices used to implement such access standards; and (5) the policies and procedures followed to conduct inventories of software, licenses, and associated data security controls and the reasons for not entering such controls or software. Requires the report to be made available upon request by any Member of Congress.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax exemption for certain individuals hired in 2010 who are qualified employers, including public institutions of higher education, for purposes of the employer tax exclusion.

Allows a business tax credit of 4% for the first year of a newly-hired employee's employment, with an increase to 10% for the following year.

Department of Homeland Security Data Framework Act of 2018 This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to develop a data framework to integrate existing DHS datasets and systems, as appropriate, for access by authorized personnel in a manner consistent with relevant legal authorities and privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties policies and protections.  DHS must ensure that the framework is accessible to employees of DHS who have an appropriate security clearance, are assigned to perform a function that requires access to information in the framework, and are trained in applicable standards for securing and using the information.  DHS may exclude information from the framework if it may jeopardize the protection of sources, methods, or activities, compromise a criminal or national security investigation, be inconsistent with other federal laws or regulations, or be duplicative or not serve an operational purpose if included in the framework. DHS must submit to Congress regular updates on the status of the framework.  The DHS government must notify Congress when the framework is fully operational.

Veterans Health Care Budget Reform and Transparency Act of 2009 - Amends the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Act to direct the Comptroller General (GAO) to study the adequacy and accuracy of the VHA medical care account projections for the fiscal year involved and the subsequent four fiscal years.

Native American Housing Enhancement Act of 2005 - Amends title V (Farm Housing) of the Housing Act of 1949 to require federally recognized Indian tribes and certain instrumentalities of the tribes to comply with title II (General Provisions) of the Indian Civil Rights Act when receiving assistance under title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (the Act) for housing assistance.

Amends the Cranston-Gonzales National Affordable Housing Act to exempt federally recognized Indian tribes, tribally designated housing entities, or other agencies primarily serving Indians from title II (General Provisions) when receiving assistance under title VI of the Act for housing assistance.

Black Hills National Forest and Rocky Mountain Research Station Improvement Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to sell or exchange specified land in South Dakota (including the Black Hills Meridian) for specified parcels of land in the state of South Dakota.  Subjects such sales or exchanges to laws (including regulations) applicable to the conveyance and acquisition of land for National Forest System purposes.  Allows the Secretary to accept cash equalization payments from any exchange.  Requires the Secretary to deposit such payments into a fund established by the Sisk Act and to be available for expenditure on the acquisition of land in the state of South Dakota and the construction of administrative improvements in connection with the Black Hills National Forest.  Authorizes appropriations.

Veterans Conservation Corps Authorization Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to establish a veterans conservation corps to: (1) provide training and employment to eligible veterans; (2) assist eligible veterans in transitioning from service in the Armed Forces to civilian life; and (3) assist the federal government in maintaining federal land and water.

State Health Care Flexibility Act of 2011 - Allows a qualifying state to opt out of the application of any or all of the PPACA (Supplemental Security Income) health insurance market reforms and immediate reforms provisions.

Senior$afe Act of 2015 This bill provides immunity from liability for disclosing the possible exploitation of a senior citizen to a covered agency if the individual: (1) served as a supervisor, compliance officer, or legal advisor for a covered financial institution; and (2) made the disclosure that the senior citizen was employed by the institution.  A covered financial institution shall not be liable, including in any civil or administrative proceeding, for disclosing the possible exploitation of a senior citizen to a covered agency if the individual: (1) served as a supervisor, compliance officer, or legal advisor for a covered financial institution; and (2) made the disclosure that the senior citizen was employed by the institution.  A covered financial institution may provide training regarding the identification and reporting of the suspected exploitation of a senior citizen to each officer or employee of the institution who: (1) is described in this bill; and (2) is authorized to review or approve the financial documents, records, or transactions of a senior citizen in connection with providing financial services to a senior citizen.

Manufacturing Advisory Council Establishment Act of 2004 - Establishes the President's Council of Advisors on Manufacturing to advise the President on policy matters affecting the domestic manufacturing sector.

Fair Trade in Grain Act of 1993 - Amends the Agricultural Trade Act of 1978 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to provide agricultural commodities or cash payments, or both, to promote the export of wheat to Mexico. 
Directs the administering authority to initiate a countervailing duty investigation and an antidumping duty investigation under the Tariff Act of 1930 with respect to the subsidies provided by Canada in connection with the exportation of wheat to the United States.

Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) and the Internal Revenue Code to permit the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (Pension Benefit Corporation) to accept from an employer a ratified collective bargaining agreement with respect to the multiemployer plan that provides for a reduction in the level of contributions made by a contributing employer and appropriate reduction in level of future benefit accruals for participants for a period of not more than five years provided that such Corporation determines that: (1) the contributing employer will be unable to pay its debts when due and will be unable to continue business without a reduction in its contribution rates; (2) the aggregate withdrawal liability of the contributing employer with respect to all multiemployer pension plans exceeds $750 million, or such lower amount as determined by the Pension Benefit Corporation; (3) there is substantial doubt as to the collectability of the withdrawal liability if the contributing employer were to withdraw from the plan; (4) the reduced contributions are not reasonably expected to have an adverse effect on the deficit of such Corporation; (5) other creditors, stakeholders, and other parties to which the contributing employer is obligated have accepted reductions that are comparable

Provides for specified conditions for the obligated 1992 Agreement to be effective until sixty days after the Secretary of the Interior certifies to the congressional financial committees that the Northern Mariana Islands are not in compliance with such conditions. 
Prohibits funds from being obligated for any project thereafter if the Secretary determines that the Northern Mariana Islands are not in compliance with such conditions.

Master Teacher Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Education to conduct a demonstration project to award competitive grants to local educational agencies (LEAs) to increase teacher salaries and employee benefits for teachers who enter into contracts with LEAs to serve as master teachers.
Tax Reduction and Economic Growth Act of 1995 - Provides for temporary tax reductions in the event of low growth.

Children's Products Safety Act of 2007 - Amends the Consumer Product Safety Act to require manufacturers of children's products to certify that they conform to consumer product safety rules before certifying their products to the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) for approval before entering the interstate stream of commerce. Requires the CPSC to issue a certificate which certifies that a product is not a banned hazardous product under such rules and specifies such product's safety standards or regulations.

Requires the CPSC to prescribe a rule for children's products that is not accompanied by a certificate from a third-party verification entity.

Choice in Welfare Tax Credit Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer to elect a credit (in lieu of a deduction otherwise available) of up to $100 ($200 for a joint return) for cash contributions to a qualifying charity whose primary activity is assistance to the poor.
Crop Risk Options Plan Act of 2013 - Amends the Federal Crop Insurance Act to provide additional supplemental crop insurance options.

Flat Alternative Individual Return Tax Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to subject to the FAIR taxable income of an individual a tax equal to 20 percent of such income.  Increases such income by an amount determined by the Secretary of the Treasury equal to:  (1) the cost of living adjustment for the calendar year; and (2) the Consumer Price Index.  Requires an individual's taxable income to include the taxpayer's adjusted gross income and the cost-of-living adjustment for the calendar year.  Requires an individual's dependent child to have no liability for tax imposed by this Act with respect to such income and to not be required to file a tax return. 
Prohibits a bill that includes provisions that:  (1) increase the FAIR tax rate; (2) create an additional FAIR income tax rate; or (3) reduce the rate. 
Makes it out of order in the House of Representatives or the Senate to consider any legislation that:  (1) increases the FAIR tax rate; (2) creates any additional FAIR income tax rate; or (3) reduces such rate. 
Provides for a waiver or suspension of this prohibition.

National Whale Conservation Fund Act of 1998 - Amends the National Fish and Wildlife Establishment Act to authorize the Foundation to establish a national whale conservation endowment fund. 
Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce to transfer to the Foundation for deposit in the endowment fund any amount received by the Secretary under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972 or the Endangered Species Act of 1973, or any amount received by the Secretary as a settlement or award for damages in a civil action or other legal proceeding relating to damage of natural resources. 
Expresses the intent of the Congress that in making expenditures from the endowment fund, the Foundation should give priority to funding projects that address the conservation of populations of whales that are:  (1) the most endangered (including the northern right whale Eubaleana glacialis); or (2) most warrant, and are most likely to benefit from, research managment, or educational activities that may be funded with amounts made available from the fund.

Justice for Public Safety Officers Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to impose a fine and/or prison term of up to 10 years for killing a federally funded or federal law enforcement officer while that officer is engaged in official duties, or on account of the performance of official duties, or kills a former federally protected safety officer on account of the past performance of official duties.  Defines "federally protected safety officer" as an individual serving a public agency in an official capacity, as a judicial officer, as a law enforcement officer, as a firefighter, as achaplain, or as a member of a rescue squad or ambulance crew.  Provides for a fine and/or prison term of up to 10 years for killing a law enforcement officer while that officer is engaged in official duties, or on account of the performance of official duties, or kills a former law enforcement officer on account of the past performance of official duties.

Secure Fence Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to take all actions the Secretary determines necessary and appropriate to achieve and maintain operational control over the entire international land and maritime borders of the United States, including: (1) systematic surveillance of such borders; and (2) physical infrastructure enhancement to prevent unlawful entry by aliens into the United States and facilitate access to such borders by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), such as additional checkpoints, all weather access roads, and vehicle barriers.

Requires the Secretary to report to Congress on progress made toward achieving such operational control and on the progress made in carrying out such control.

Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to require the Secretary to provide for least 2 layers of reinforced fencing along the port of entry and along the border between the United States and specified areas.

Directs the Secretary to conduct a study on the feasibility of a state of-the-art infrastructure security system along the northern international land and maritime border of the United States and to evaluate the authority of CBP personnel to stop vehicles that enter the United States illegally and refuse to stop when ordered to do so by

Directs the Under Secretary for Science and Technology in the Department of Homeland Security to conduct an independent study of the effects on human health caused by the use of backscatter x-ray machines (x-rays) at airline checkpoints operated by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). Requires the laboratory to use: (1) calibration testing equipment to determine the placement of testing equipment so that radiation emission readings during the testing of such machines are as accurate as possible and how best to measure the dose emitted per scan; (2) the dismantling and evaluating of one or more backscatter x-ray machine used at airline checkpoints; (3) the assessment of fail-safe mechanisms of such machines; (4) the collection of peer review of any tests performed; and (5) the development of a report that contains the preliminary findings of the study and evaluation and the result and result of the study and evaluation. Requires TSA to ensure that large, easily readable signs or electronic displays are placed at the front of airline passenger check point queues where backscatter advanced imaging technology machines are used for screening to inform airline passengers, particularly passengers who may be sensitive to radiation exposure, that they may request alternative screening procedures instead of passing through a backsc

Federal Railroad Safety Authorization Act of 1994 - Amends Federal transportation law to authorize the Secretary of Transportation to make pilot projects to demonstrate the possible benefits of implementing alternatives to the strict application of requirements regarding railroad safety pilot projects.  Authorizes the Secretary to waive compliance with such requirements for a period of no more than two years, if the Secretary determines that such waiver of compliance is in the public interest and consistent with railroad safety. 
Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to report to the Congress on pilot projects and other related matters. 
Requires the Secretary to submit to the Congress a biennial report on any action taken on railroad bridge displacement detection systems. 
Requires the Secretary to consider whether or not to prescribe regulations and issue orders concerning:  (1) inspection procedures to identify internal rail defects, before they reach imminent failure size, in rail that has significant shelling; and (2) any specific actions that should be taken when a rail surface condition, such as shelling, prevents the identification of internal defects.

Emergency Unemployment Compensation Amendments of 1993 - Amends the Emergency Unemployment Compensation Act of 1991 to extend the termination of benefits for new claimants for regular unemployment compensation (including new claimants under each State unemployment compensation law which is approved under the Federal Unemployment Tax Act and new claimants under Federal unemployment benefit and allowance programs administered by the State under agreements with the Secretary of Labor).  Directs the Secretary of Labor to establish a program for encouraging the adoption and implementation by all States of a system of profiling all new claimants for regular unemployment compensation (including new claimants under each State unemployment compensation law which is approved under the Federal Unemployment Tax Act and new claimants under Federal unemployment benefit and allowance programs administered by the State under agreements with the Secretary of Labor).  Directs the Secretary of Labor to provide technical assistance and advice to the States in the development of model profiling systems and the procedures for such systems. 
Requires the Secretary to report to the Congress on the operation and effectiveness of the profiling systems adopted by the States, and the Secretary's recommendation for continuing the systems and any appropriate legislation. 
Authorizes appropriations for nonrepayable advances

Prohibits the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) from collecting a guarantee fee in connection with a loan of not more than $150,000 made to a veteran or spouse of a veteran on or after October 1 of the first fiscal year beginning after the date of enactment of this Act. Excepts from such requirement any loans made during the upcoming fiscal year.

Ban Poisonous Additives Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require that, if it is a food intended for children 3 years of age or younger, the container of which is composed, in whole or in part, of bisphenol A (BPA). Requires that the BPA-free container of infant formula containment containers be composed of such bPA-free material.

Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require that, if it is a food intended for children 3 years of age or younger, the container of which is composed of such material be composed of bisphenol A. Requires that the BPA-free material of infant formula containment containers be composed of such material.

Trade Promotion Authority Extension and Enhancement Act of 2007 - Amends the Bipartisan Trade Promotion Authority Act of 2002 to extend through July 1, 2016, and through July 1 of each fifth year thereafter, the authority of the Trade and Trade Coordinating Council to make trade promotion and trade reform recommendations to Congress. Extends through July 1, 2016, and through July 1 of each fifth year thereafter, the authority of the International Trade Commission (ITC) to report to Congress on the progress made in negotiations to achieve the objectives of this Act. Prohibits the ITC from extending for the succeeding five years any trade authorities procedures that it has so extended. Directs the ITC to report to Congress, not later than June 1, 2011, and not later than June 1 of each fifth year thereafter, a written report that contains: (1) an economic analysis of the impact of the five-year extension of such procedures on U.S. trade, and (2) a statement of views regarding whether the procedures should be extended for the succeeding five years.

Family Farmer Bankruptcy Clarification Act of 2017 This bill allows a bankruptcy case that arises after the date on which the petition was filed to be treated as a federal bankruptcy case under the bankruptcy code.  The bill provides for the payment of a claim by the holder of a debtor's discharge that arises after the discharge from the debtor's custody.

Commit to Opioid Medical Prescriber Accountability and Safety for Seniors Act or the COMPASS Act - Amends part D (Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program) of title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to provide, subject to specified requirements, an annual opioid notification to a prescriber who is an outlier prescriber of opioids. Requires the Secretary to use National Provider Identifiers (NPIDs) on claims for covered part D (Voluntary Prescription Drug Program) drugs for part D eligible individuals enrolled in Medicare or Medicare Advantage-Prescription Drug (MA-PD) plans based on the threshold established under this Act.

Desert Community Lands Act  This bill directs the Department of the Interior to convey to the town of Apple Valley, California, without consideration, all U.S. rights and interests to certain federal land in the proposed conveyance area of the approximately 4,630 acres of land generally depicted as "Proposed Conveyance Area," which shall be designated as the "Apple Valley Off-Highway Vehicle Recreation Area."   Interior may use such conveyed land for any public purpose, consistent with the Recreation and Public Purposes Act.   The purposes of the conveyance are to allow the town to use the conveyed land to provide a suitable location for the establishment of a centralized off-road vehicle recreation park, the public with opportunities for off-road vehicle recreation, and a designated area and facilities that would discourage unauthorized use of off-highway vehicles in areas that have been identified by the federal government, the state of California, or San Bernardino County as containing environmentally sensitive land.   The land conveyed may not be disposed of by the town without the approval of the Department of the Interior.   Conveyance to Twentynine Palms, California, is prohibited without the city's approval.   Conveyance to Barstow, California,

Alcohol Advertising Accountability Act of 1996 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report annually to the Congress on alcohol advertising, its profile, and its effects. 
Requires the Secretary to establish a panel made up of such individuals to review alcohol advertising in all media, including broadcast and cable television, other electronic means, and print and outdoor advertising and review promotional activities undertaken to promote the sale of alcoholic beverages. 
Requires the Secretary to convene at least two public hearings before the panel each year and to have the panel conduct a hearing in each of the regional offices of the Department of Health and Human Services over the five-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act. 
Requires the report to be developed on the basis of the work conducted and to include a determination of the extent to which young people are exposed to alcohol advertising and promotions of alcoholic beverages.

Mortgage Cancellation Relief Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income for certain indebtedness discharged in the case of an individual an individual who has suffered from an indebtedness for which the taxpayer has made an election to discharge.

Local Zoning Decisions Protection Act of 2017 This bill declares that the final rule of the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) affirmatively furthers the Fair Housing Act by notifying the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) that the rules and notices concerning the Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing Assessment Tool are no force or effect. HUD must jointly consult with state and local officials to develop recommendations to further the purposes and policies of the Fair Housing Act.

Honorable Stephanie Tubbs Jones College Fire Prevention Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to establish a demonstration program to award grants for the installation of fire sprinkler systems, or other fire suppression or prevention technologies, in student housing and dormitories owned or controlled by an eligible entity (an institution of higher education, the active membership of which consists primarily of students in attendance at such institution, the social fraternity or sorority exempt from taxation, and membership in the active membership of such institution) that are eligible for assistance under the Higher Education Act of 1965 (HEA) to apply for grants. Requires the Secretary to develop a plan to inform eligible entities of the availability of such grants and the amount of such assistance. Prohibits the Secretary from awarding such grants to entities that are not sufficiently competitive or that are not using appropriate amounts of assistance. Requires the Secretary to make such grants available to other eligible entities. Prohibits any grant from being expended for administrative expenses with respect to the grant. Requires the Secretary to provide to Congress a report that includes: (1) the number and types of entities receiving assistance, (2) the amounts of such assistance, (3) the sources and sources of

Food Sharing Act of 2017 This bill amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to authorize the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to make grants to public food programs and private nonprofit organizations to establish and carry out gleaning projects.  The USDA may also provide assistance to an eligible entity to develop new resources and strategies to reduce food insecurity and prevent food insecurity in low-income communities that are the subject of such projects.  The bill defines "gleaning project" as a project in which an entity collects edible, surplus food that would be thrown away and distributes the food to agencies or nonprofit organizations that feed the hungry, or that harvests for free distribution to the needy, an agricultural crop that has been donated by the owner of the crop, or that has been donated by the owner of the crop.  The USDA may also provide assistance to an eligible entity to develop new resources and strategies to reduce food insecurity and prevent food insecurity in low-income communities that are the subject of such projects by: (1) developing creative food resources, or (2) coordinating food services with park and recreation programs, and other community-based activities, to reduce barriers to access to food.

Social Security COLA Limitation Act of 1994 - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to provide for the continued application of the current OASDI cost-of-living adjustment.

HOPE VI Green Building and Technical Assistance Act of 2007 - Amends the United States Housing Act of 1937 to prohibit the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) from making grants to an applicant unless the revitalization plan of the applicant to be carried out with such grant amounts complies with the following requirements: (1) the green communities criteria checklist; and (2) the LEED-NC 2.2 green building rating system for new construction and rehabilitation. Requires the Secretary to verify, or provide for verification, sufficient to ensure that each revitalization plan carried out with amounts from a grant complies with the requirements and plan. Directs the Secretary to establish procedures to ensure such compliance. Directs the Secretary to use not less than two% for grants in such fiscal year to potential HUD grant applicants and recipients to assist such entities in developing and planning revitalization programs under this Act or to recipients in obtaining technical assistance in carrying out such programs.

State Temporary Economic Priority (STEP) Act - Authorizes a State to transfer or consolidate funds made available to it under certain transportation, education, and job training programs after the United States experiences economic growth at an annual rate of less than one percent for two calendar quarters.  Treats such transferred or consolidated funds as transportation funds.  Permits the use of such funds for the improvement of basic transportation programs, the enhancement of education programs, the prevention and intervention programs for children and youth who are Neglected, Delinquent, or At-Risk, and the improvement of academic achievement.

Drunk Driving Repeat Offender Prevention Act of 2009 - Amends the federal criminal code to require states to enact and enforce a law that requires the installation of an ignition interlock device for a minimum of 180 days on each motor vehicle operated by an individual who is convicted of driving while intoxicated or driving under the influence (i.e., driving while intoxicated).

Requires a state to withhold specified percentages of apportioned funds from apportionment to a state for FY2014-FY2015 if the state does not meet the requirements of this Act.

Opioid Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to five-year pilot projects to develop a standardized peer review process and methodology to evaluate prescription drug monitoring programs in states receiving such grants.  Authorizes the Secretary to award grants to states to develop continuing education criteria and review processes that allow state health profession boards or agencies to certify appropriate education and training for informed and safe prescribing of opioids and other drugs listed on schedule II or III (S-2) under the Controlled Substances Act.  Directs the Secretary, acting through the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, to conduct a review of naloxone to consider whether naloxone should cease to be subject to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA) and be available as an over-the-counter drug, according to FFDCA requirements.  Directs the Secretary, acting through the Commissioner, to convene or coordinate with an existing entity an interagency working group to encourage states and local governments to increase opportunities for disposal of opiates, such as frequent take-back programs and fixed medicine disposal sites at law enforcement public buildings. Kids 2000 Act - Directs the Attorney General to make grants to the Boys and Girls Clubs of America for the purpose of funding effective after-school technology programs, such as PowerUp, in order to provide: (1) constructive technology-focussed activities that are part of a comprehensive program to provide access to technology and technology training to youth during after-school hours,eks days, and school vacations; (2) supervised activities in safe environments for youth; and (3) full-time staffing with teachers, tutors, and other qualified personnel. 
Requires the Boys and Girls Clubs to make subawards to local boys and girls clubs authorizing expenditures associated with providing technology programs such as PowerUp, including the hiring of teachers and other personnel, procurement of goods and services, and other specified purposes.

Joe Testaverde Adult Stem Cell Research Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to expand, intensify, and coordinate NIH activities regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Requires the Director to award grants and contracts to public or nonprofit private entities to pay costs of planning, establishing, improving, and providing basic operating support for centers of excellence regarding qualifying adult stem cell research.

Requires each center to conduct basic and clinical research on qualifying adult stem cells.

Requires each center to establish, provide to the subjects of research, referrals for health and other services, and the patient care costs of research to the subjects to be made available for such research.

Requires the Director to provide for a program under which samples of tissues and genetic materials that are of use in qualifying adult stem cell research are donated, collected, preserved, and made available for such research.

Solar Fuels Innovation Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Energy Policy Act of 2005 to require the Department of Energy (DOE) to carry out a research initiative, to be known as the Solar Fuels Basic Research Initiative, to expand theoretical and fundamental knowledge of photochemistry, electrochemistry, biochemistry, and materials science useful for the practical development of experimental systems to convert solar energy to chemical energy.  DOE must leverage expertise and resources from the National Laboratories, universities, and the private sector to carry out the initiative.  The initiative shall include multidisciplinary teams leveraging expertise from the National Laboratories, universities, and the private sector to achieve goals.  The initiative shall also support research needed to bridge scientific barriers and discover knowledge relevant to artificial photosynthetic systems.  The initiative shall be carried out through Energy Frontier Research Centers, Energy Innovation Hubs, or other organizational structures.  DOE may organize additional activities through Energy Frontier Research Centers, Energy Innovation Hubs, or other organizational structures. Requires the Director of National Intelligence to make publicly available on an Internet website captured documents are not to be: (1) made publicly available for review after the date of enactment of this Act; or (2) reviewed for review before the date of enactment of this Act.

Requires the Director to submit to specified congressional committees a report on captured documents that: (1) is to be made publicly available for review after the date of enactment of this Act; or (2) is not made publicly available after such date.

Requires the Director to report to such committees on progress made in making captured documents publicly available.

Iran Sanctions Enhancement Act of 2007 - Amends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to require the President to impose two or more of the following sanctions upon a person: (1) an investment of $20 million or more (or any combination of investments of at least $5 million each) for a specified period that directly and significantly contributed to the enhancement of Iran's ability to develop petroleum resources of Iran; or (2) an activity that could contribute to Iran's ability to import refined petroleum resources. Directs the President to report to Congress on any person who has provided Iran with refined petroleum resources or any activity that could contribute to Iran's ability to import refined petroleum resources.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Cultural Resource Programs, to: (1) facilitate the development of guidelines and a program of technical assistance and grants that will set priorities for the preservation of the Route 66 corridor; and (2) designate officials of the National Park Service stationed at locations convenient to the States to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) support efforts of State and local public and private persons, nonprofit Route 66 preservation entities, Indian tribes, State Historic Preservation Offices, and entities in the States for the preservation of the Route 66 corridor by providing technical assistance, participating in cost-sharing programs, and making grants; (2) act as a clearinghouse for communication among Federal, State, and local agencies, nonprofit Route 66 preservation entities, Indian tribes, State historic preservation offices, and private persons and entities interested in the preservation of the Route 66 corridor; and (3) assist the States in determining the appropriate form of and establishing and supporting a non-Federal entity or entities to perform the functions of the Cultural Resource Programs after those programs are terminated.

Taking Account of Institutions with Low Operation Risk Act of 2015 or the TAILOR Act of 2015 This bill requires the Federal financial institutions regulatory agencies to: (1) tailor their regulatory actions so as to limit the regulatory compliance impact, cost, liability risk, and other burdens of such actions; and (2) report to Congress on the specific actions taken to do so. The agencies must also report to Congress on the extent to which such actions result in differential regulation of similarly-sorted institutions of diverse charter types with respect to comparable regulations.

Holding Salaries in Escrow  (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of the Treasury to: (1) make an annual determination of whether the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and the President are in compliance with certain statutory requirements for submission of the President's budget to Congress, and (2) notify the chairpersons of the congressional budget committees of any such determination.  No funds may be appropriated or otherwise made available from the U.S. Treasury for the Director of OMB, Deputy Director of OMB, and the Deputy Director for Management of OMB during any period of noncompliance determined by the Inspector General of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM).  The OMB Deputy Director and the Deputy Director for Management of OMB may not receive pay for any period of noncompliance determined by the Inspector General of OPM.

Technological Resource to Assist Criminal Enforcement (TRACE) Act - Amends the Federal criminal code to require a licensed manufacturer or importer of firearms to: (1) test fire manufactured or imported firearms as specified by the Attorney General; (2) prepare ballistics images of the fired bullet and cartridge casings; (3) make the records available to the Attorney General for entry into a computerized database; and (4) store the fired bullet and cartridge casings.Directs the Attorney General to assist firearm manufacturers and importers in complying with this Act by: (1) acquiring, installing, and upgrading ballistics equipment and bullet and cartridge casing recovery equipment; (2) hiring or designating sufficient personnel to develop and maintain a ballistics database; (3) providing education about the role of ballistics; (4) providing for the coordination among law enforcement and regulatory agencies and the firearm industry to curb firearm-related crime and illegal firearm trafficking; and (5) taking other necessary steps to make ballistics testing effective.Directs the Attorney General to: (1) establish a computer system through which State and local law enforcement agencies can promptly access the ballistics records stored under this Act; and (

Buy America Update Act - Amends Federal procurement law to direct the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to review regulations found in certain Federal Procurement Act requirements regarding the procurement of rolling stock and determine whether manufactured products other than steel and iron should be considered domestic content preferences.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) initiate a rulemaking to develop audit procedures for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) for the agency to review offeror and recipient compliance with domestic content provisions; and (2) issue guidance on best practices for pre-award and post-delivery audits by FAA recipients.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) initiate a rulemaking to further develop standards under the Federal Aviation Act for measuring the percentage value of a component relative to the entire procurement; and (2) initiate a rulemaking to further develop standards under the Federal Merchant Marine Act for measuring the percentage value of a component relative to the entire procurement. Directs the Secretary to: (1) consult with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) before seeking a waiver request for a component component, material, or subcomponent; and (2) publish a summary of the Scouting report along with the waiver request. Directs the Secretary of Education to discharge or cancel the federal student loan indebtedness of: (1) an eligible spouse of a student who died (or died) or who became (or become) permanently and totally disabled due to injuries suffered in the terrorist attack on September 11, 2001; (2) an eligible spouse of an eligible victim who became (or become) permanently and totally disabled due to injuries suffered in the terrorist attack on September 11, 2001; or (3) an eligible parent who became (or become) permanently and totally disabled due to injuries suffered in the terrorist attack on September 11, 2001.

Eating Healthy at School Act of 2010 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to study and report to Congress on: (1) the effectiveness and efficiency of administrative review systems to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act, including the provisions with respect to nutrition, eligibility, meal counts, and claims for reimbursement; (2) design and test alternative processes and procedures that may improve the effectiveness and efficiency of the administrative review systems; and (3) identify any alternative processes and procedures for establishing a more effective and efficient administrative review system which reflects the results of tests of alternative processes and procedures conducted pursuant to this Act and considers the practicality of implementing such processes, including the cost and burden of implementation that would be imposed on local school food authorities, local educational agencies, and state educational agencies.

Heavy Truck, Tractor, and Trailer Retail Federal Excise Tax Repeal Act of 2017  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the excise tax on certain new heavy trucks, tractors, and trailers, to: (1) repeal the excise tax on certain motor vehicles used exclusively on mobile machinery, (2) exclude from the definition of "tires of the type used on highway vehicles" certain tires of a type used exclusively on motor vehicles with a chassis that has been specially designed to serve only as a mobile carriage and mount (and a power source, where applicable) for the particular machinery or equipment involved, whether or not such machinery or equipment is in operation, and (3) allow the use of certain tires of a type used exclusively on mobile machinery for the purpose of transporting a load other than that particular machinery or equipment.

Rape Survivor Child Custody Act - Directs the Attorney General to make grants to states that have in place a law that allows a mother of any child that was conceived through rape to seek court-ordered termination of the parental rights of her therapist with regard to that child.

Requires a state receiving such a grant to submit an application to the Attorney General in such manner, including information about the law.

Authorizes appropriations.

Women and Alcohol Research Equity Act of 1996 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the Institute of Health and Human Services to obligate at least $43,997,080 for the purpose of carrying out specified projects concerning research on alcohol abuse and alcoholism among women.  Authorizes appropriations for such projects for FY 1997 and 1998.

Airline Passenger Fairness Act - Amends Federal air transportation law to prohibit a certificated air carrier from advertising an unfair or deceptive practice in its passenger airline advertisements, or from providing a consumer full access to all fares for that carrier, regardless of the technology the consumer uses to access the fares if such information is requested by that consumer.

HSA Accessibility and Portability Act of 2006 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to allow a health insurance issuer to elect, with respect to any small employer, to meet the requirements of the guaranteed issue of guaranteed health insurance coverage (Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act of 1985) instead of complying with the Guaranteed Issue Requirement of the Unguaranteed Issue Act of 1986.

Greater Sage Grouse Protection and Recovery Act of 2016 This bill prohibits the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture (USDA) from making a finding in a state with a state management plan that September 30, 2026, indicates the Greater Sage Grouse (Urocercus urophasianus) is endangered or threatened until the state has made a determination within three years after the notification.  The bill also prohibits the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture (USDA) from making a finding in a state that provides a federal resource management plan that affects the Grouse in a manner inconsistent with the state management plan for a period, to be specified by the governor.  The bill also prohibits the two federal agencies from making a finding in a state that: (1) provides a federal resource management plan that affects the Grouse in a manner inconsistent with the state management plan for a period, to be specified by the governor, or (2) is modified by a federal resource management plan that is inconsistent with the state management plan.

Safe, Convenient, Reliable, Efficient, Effective, Next-Generation, Functional, and Secure TSA Act of 2016 or the SCREEN FAST Act This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) of the Department of Transportation (DOT) to establish a three-abandoned or decommissioned airport security system at three airports in the Marshall Islands, Micronesia, and Palau.  The TSA must: (1) select an airport from among airports classified by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) as category X, that is able to begin reconfiguration and installation of security systems expeditiously; and (2) give priority to an airport that submits a proposal seeking federal funding for reconfiguration and that has the space needed to reduce vulnerabilities and reconfigure the existing security systems and is able to enter into a cost-sharing arrangement with TSA.  The TSA must carry out the pilot programs established under this Act using amounts from the airport security system.

Fort Stanton and Rio Bonito Corridor Vegetation Management Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the Bureau of Land Management, to solicit competitive bids for and enter into vegetation sales contracts to use livestock grazing as a vegetation management tool.  Provides for the consistency with which such contracts are ratified under the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976. 
Directs the Secretary, in managing land within Fort Stanton and the Rio Bonito Corridor that is under the jurisdiction of the Secretary, to solicit competitive bids for and enter into vegetation sales contracts for the purpose of using livestock grazing to manage such land.  Requires 12 and 1/2 percent of the proceeds of vegetation sales contracts to be paid to the State of New Mexico for distribution to Lincoln County, New Mexico, to be used for purposes authorized under the Act of June 28, 1934.  12 and 1/2 percent shall be deposited in the general fund of the Treasury, and 75 percent shall be deposited in a special account in the Treasury. Pay Accountability Act - Requires the White House Office to: (1) withhold from payroll payments for compensation of the President or Vice President an amount equal to the product of a specified annual rate of pay or salary and the number of 24-hour periods during which the government shutdown is in effect or the public debt limit is reached (as the case may be); and (2) deposit such amounts in an escrow account withheld from payroll for the President or Vice President. Requires the White House Office to transfer to the Secretary of the Treasury any amounts remaining in any escrow account under this Act on the last day of the Congress involved. Sets forth the role of the Secretary of the Treasury in this Act.

Agricultural Credit Expansion Act - Amends the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act to: (1) make the limited liability companies (LV companies) of the Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the Department of the Interior eligible for farm loans; (2) allow certain limited liability companies to operate and operate more than 50 percent of their land; (3) allow certain LV companies to operate and operate more than 50 percent of their land in the case of an operator having a direct ownership interest in more than 50 percent of the land; and (4) make such limited liability companies eligible for certain farm loans.

Breast Cancer Patient Education Act of 2012 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to provide for the planning and implementation of an education campaign to inform breast cancer patients anticipating surgery regarding the availability and coverage of breast reconstruction, prostheses, and other options.

Requires such campaign to include dissemination of certain information, including information regarding: (1) breast reconstruction is possible at the time of breast cancer surgery, or in a delayed fashion; and (2) prostheses or breast forms may be available.

Requires such campaign to also include dissemination of such other information (whether developed by the Secretary or by other entities) as the Secretary determines relevant.

Judicial Transparency and Ethics Enhancement Act of 2006 - Amends the federal judicial code to establish the Office of Inspector General for the Judicial Branch of the U.S. Government, which shall: (1) conduct investigations of matters pertaining to the Judicial Branch; (2) conduct and supervise audits and investigations; (3) prevent and detect waste, fraud, and abuse; and (4) recommend changes in laws or regulations governing the Judicial Branch.

Requires the Inspector General to: (1) make investigations and reports; (2) obtain information or assistance from any federal, state, or local governmental agency, or other entity, including all information kept in the course of business by the Judicial Conference of the United States, the judicial councils of circuits, the Administrative Office of the United States Courts, and the U.S. Sentencing Commission; (3) require attendance and testimony by witnesses; (4) administer to specified public agencies and to the extent and in such amounts as may be provided in advance by appropriations Acts; (5) enter into contracts and other arrangements for audits, studies, analyses, and other services with public agencies and private persons; and (6) make such

Cormorant Management and Natural Resources Protection Act - Amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to delegate authority to the Secretary of the Interior with respect to cormorants in a State to the governor of that State effective on the date that the Secretary approves a management plan submitted by the governor.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) approve or disapprove a management plan submitted by the governor if it is in accordance with U.S. obligations under treaties and federal law; and (2) review every five years each management plan approved for a State under this Act and the State governor's exercise of authority delegated under this Act.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) review every five years each management plan approved for a State under this Act and the state governor's exercise of authority delegated under this Act; and (2) revoke such approval and delegation if it is not in accordance with this Act.

Tax Relief for Victims of Disasters Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make permanent the tax deduction for income attributable to a federally declared disaster; and (2) allow a tax deduction for housing displaced displaced individuals if such individual was provided housing free of charge by the taxpayer in the principal residence of the taxpayer for a period of 60 consecutive days which ends in such taxable year.

Hospice Evaluation and Legitimate Payment Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act (SSA) to revise hospice care eligibility requirements. (Currently, hospice care is limited to the provision of home care services to eligible beneficiaries.) Revises the Medicare Hospice Payment Reform demonstration program to: (1) establish a Medicare Hospice Payment Reform demonstration program to test the proposed revisions, and (2) require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to conduct an evaluation of the program.  Requires the Secretary to ensure that any revisions in payment implemented as part of the demonstration program result in the same estimated amount of aggregate payments that would have been made if the hospice programs had not participated in the demonstration program.

National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to: (1) enhance and expand infrastructure and activities to track the epidemiology of neurological diseases, including multiple sclerosis and Parkinson's disease; and (2) incorporate information obtained through those activities into a national, statistical-safe, evidence-based surveillance system.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), acting through the Director, to: (1) provide for the collection and storage of information on neurological diseases in the United States; (2) ensure that the National Neurological Diseases Surveillance System is designed to facilitate further research on neurological diseases; (3) provide for the collection and storage of other available information on neurological diseases, including information concerning demographics, risk factors, and diagnosis and progression markers; (4) provide for the collection and storage of information relevant to analysis on neurological diseases; and (5) address issues identified during the consultation process.

Amends the Food Security Act of 1985 to require the Secretary of Agriculture to: (1) make payments to a person or legal entity for a period not less than five years, or permanently, to the person or legal entity's estate; and (2) deny any income verification and enforcement procedures the entity may have received while the entity was ineligible.

Requires the Secretary to request the Administrator of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to verify the average adjusted gross income, average adjusted gross farm income, and average adjusted gross nonfarm income of the entity's person or legal entity for each of specified periods.

Authorizes the Secretary to request the Administrator to deny the issuance of applicable payments and benefits to the entity's person or legal entity, under similar terms and conditions as described in this Act.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for a specified amount of long-term care needs.

Chickasaw National Recreation Area Land Exchange Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to convey certain federal lands in Sulphur Springs National Recreation Area, Oklahoma, to the Chickasaw Nation, in exchange for certain land within the Park.

Requires the values of the federal and non-federal lands to be determined by an appraisal that is acceptable to the Secretary and the Chickasaw Nation.

Immigration Anti-Discrimination Improvement Act of 1993 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Comptroller General to report annually to the Congress on:  (1) the pervasiveness of unfair immigration-related employment practices; and (2) enforcement with respect to such practices. 
Directs the Attorney General to report semiannually to the Congress on unfair immigration-related employment practices and enforcement with respect to such practices. 
Requires the Special Counsel for Immigration-Related Unfair Employment Practices to provide for agreements with Federal and State agencies involved with enforcement of laws relating to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of national origin under which such agencies would receive charges respecting unfair immigration-related employment practices and promptly forward such charges to the Special Counsel. 
Directs the Attorney General to establish a national, toll-free telephone service to receive charges of unfair immigration-related employment practices and to provide for outreach efforts to educate the public concerning such provisions. 
Directs the Attorney General to establish a monitoring panel to monitor application of the anti-discrimination provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act and to report annually to the Attorney General and the Congress respecting such implementation.
