Requires a satellite carrier, upon a challenge by a network station regarding whether a subscriber is an unserved household within the predicted grade B contour of the station, to inform the subscriber from the network station in writing that the network station has challenged the subscriber's receipt of the signal of the same network from the satellite carrier, and offer the subscriber the option of conducting a measurement of the signal intensity to determine whether the household is an unserved household. Provides for the cost of such a measurement, and a statement of the costs, to be included in a subscriber's notice to subscribers no later than 60 days after the enactment of this Act.  Requires the subscriber, if the satellite carrier conducts a signal intensity measurement and the measurement indicates that the household is not an unserved household, to reimburse the satellite carrier for the costs of the measurement, or the household is an unserved household.  Requires the subscriber, if the subscriber requests the satellite carrier to conduct a signal intensity measurement, to reimburse the satellite carrier for the costs of the measurement.  Provides for arbitration of the terms and conditions of such measurement upon satisfaction of such terms and conditions.

Ronald Reagan Memorial Act of 2000 - Authorizes the Ronald Reagan Memorial Commission to: (1) establish the Ronald Reagan Memorial in accordance with this Act on Federal lands administered by the National Park Service in the District of Columbia; and (2) begin the process of recommending a location and selecting a design for the memorial no later than six months after enactment of this Act. Requires the Commission to: (1) erect a suitable marker to be installed by the Secretary of the Interior no later than three months after enactment of this Act; and (2) be chaired by one of its members, to be designated jointly by the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the majority leader of the Senate, and to be exempt from the Federal Advisory Committee Act.

This bill directs the Department of the Interior to offer for sale to qualified entities, for fair market value, the remaining right, title, and interest of the United States in and to certain covered land (including the U.S. right to use the surface for mineral purposes) within the boundaries of Mohave County, Arizona.  Interior shall determine fair market value for such land.  The bill terminates Interior's authority to sell such land 10 years after the enactment of this bill.

Bodegas as Catalysts for Healthy Living Act - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to carry out a program under which the Administrator makes grants to any of the following: (1) a local redevelopment agency that is chartered, established, or otherwise sanctioned by a state or local government; (2) a local redevelopment agency that is involved in the expansion of a small business's inventory to include one or more of the following products; (3) a community-based organization working in collaboration with one or more of the community-based organizations in expanding that inventory; or (4) a community-based organization working in collaboration with one or more small business concerns in expanding those products. Limits the maximum grant amount to $100,000. Authorizes appropriations.

Border Enforcement Security Task Force Reauthorization Act of 2017 This bill amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to modify the BEST unit's requirements for the establishment of BEST units. Specifically, the bill modifies the requirement that the Coast Guard Investigative Service (CGIS) and the geographically responsible Coast Guard Section of the Geographical Suspension Enforcement (GSE) Nexus report to the Department of State on each unit's performance in: (1) enhancing border security, disrupting and dismantling transnational criminal organizations, and reducing drug trafficking, arms smuggling, child exploitation, illegal alien trafficking, and smuggling, violence, and kidnapping along and across U.S. borders; (2) improving information sharing among federal, state, local, tribal, and foreign law enforcement agencies; (3) addressing intelligence coordination gaps; and (4) addressing information-sharing intelligence needs in advancing Department of Justice's homeland and border security priorities. Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a Clean Energy Technology Manufacturing and Export Assistance Program to promote policies to reduce production costs and encourage innovation, investment, and productivity among businesses in the United States that produce or export clean energy technologies or related services.

Requires the Under Secretary to provide information and other assistance to businesses in the United States, including analyzing and making recommendations with respect to policies to reduce production costs and encourage innovation, investment, and productivity among businesses in the United States that produce or export clean energy technologies or related services.

Directs the Under Secretary to report to Congress on how the program will be used to: (1) encourage the production and exportation of clean energy technologies and related services in the United States; (2) encourage the creation and maintenance of clean energy technology jobs in the United States; and (3) benefit small- and medium-sized businesses.

Medicare Certified Registered Nurse First Assistant Direct Reimbursement Act of 2001 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, as amended by the Medicare, Medicaid, and SCHIP Benefits Improvement and Protection Act of 2000, to provide for the coverage of surgical first assisting services furnished by a certified registered nurse first assistant.

Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to suspend, through December 31, 2007, the requirement for a prescription drug plan (PDP) to include an initial enrollment period of 12 months and a final enrollment period of 2006-2007.

Waco Mammoth National Monument Establishment Act of 2011 - Establishes in Texas, as a unit of the National Park System, the Waco Mammoth National Monument.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire by donation from the city any land or interest in land owned by the city within the proposed boundary of the Monument.

Directs the Secretary to complete a general management plan for the Monument.

Terminates the designation of the Monument as a unit of the National Park System if federal funds are required to operate and maintain it.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) hold a public hearing before the expiration of the 90-day period beginning on the date of the petition; and (2) review the marketing practices of air carriers that may inhibit the availability of quality, affordable air transportation services to commercial service airports.

Jason's Law - Directs the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to implement a pilot program to address the shortage of long-term parking for commercial motor vehicles on the National Highway System (NHS). Requires the Secretary to allocate funds among states, metropolitan planning organizations, and local governments. Requires funds to be used for projects: (1) that serve the NHS, and (2) that may include construction of safety rest areas and parking facilities adjacent to commercial truck stops and travel plazas. Requires projects to have a severe shortage of commercial motor vehicle parking capacity in the corridor to be addressed and have consulted with affected state and local governments, community groups, private providers of commercial motor vehicle parking, and motorist and truck organizations, and motorist and truck organizations.

Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide for a program of training to provide eligible veterans with skills relevant to the job market.  Requires the program to provide for payments to employers who provide for eligible veterans a program of apprenticeship or on-the-job training if: (1) such program is approved by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs; (2) the rate of pay for veterans participating in the program is not less than the rate of pay for nonveterans in similar jobs; and (3) the Secretary reasonably expects that the veterans will be qualified for employment in that field upon completion of training.  Requires the Secretary to enter into contracts with employers to provide programs of apprenticeship or on-the-job training that meet the requirements of this Act.  Allows such payments to be made on a quarterly basis.  Requires the Secretary to include a description of activities carried out under this Act in the annual report to be submitted to the Secretary.

Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to contract with a non-VA provider if the VA determines that VA facilities are not capable of: (1) economically furnishing covered health services to such veteran because of geographical inaccessibility, or (2) furnishing such services to such veteran because the VA has the necessary personnel, resources, or ability.

Post-Deployment Health Assessment Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Defense to issue guidance for the provision of in-person mental health screenings for each member of the Armed Forces who is deployed in connection with a contingency operation to: (1) at a time during the period beginning 180 days before the date of deployment in connection with the operation and ending 90 days before the date of deployment in connection with the operation; and (2) at a time during the period beginning 90 days after the date of deployment in connection with the operation.

Directs the Secretary to share with the Secretary of Veterans Affairs specified information on members of the Armed Forces who is under such screenings as the Secretary and the Secretary of Veterans Affairs jointly consider appropriate to ensure continuity of mental health care and treatment during their transition from health care and treatment provided by the Department of Defense (DOD) to health care and treatment provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

Drinking Water Affordability Act of 2016 This bill amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to revise requirements for national primary drinking water regulations. The bill revises requirements regarding: (1) the national primary drinking water regulation, including requirements for national primary source water protection areas; (2) the administration of state loan funds for such areas; (3) the administration of source water protection area (SPSA) programs; and (4) the requirement for state participation in source water protection area (SPSA) improvement programs.

Consumer Credit Card Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to prohibit a consumer from using adverse information concerning any consumer, including any information in any consumer report, in any consumer credit card account under an open end consumer credit plan or any consumer report that is not disclosed in a consumer statement required under the Act.

Amends the Truth in Lending Act to prohibit an increase in any interest rate applicable to any outstanding balance of a consumer credit card account under an open end consumer credit plan or any consumer report that is not disclosed in a consumer statement required under the Act.

American Textile Technology Innovation and Research for Exportation (ATTIRE) Act - Directs the Secretary of Commerce to establish a competitive grant program to fund textile research and innovation and to promote increased textile exports.

Veterans Benefits Network Act - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make grants to an eligible entity to establish a regional technology system to provide an active database and enrollment system that can be used by a coordinated network of private, public, and nonprofit entities to assist veterans and their family members in applying for benefits and services offered by such entities that participate in the network. Requires such entities to: (1) be eligible for the grant; (2) submit to the Secretary an application containing a description of the credentialing system the entity intends to use to determine which service providers will be eligible for inclusion in the network; and (3) use the grant to establish a coordinated network of private, public, and nonprofit services that can be used by such entities to assist veterans and their family members in applying for benefits and services offered by such entities.

Counseling in Shelters Act of 2002 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Assistant Secretary for the Administration on Children, Youth, and Families, to make grants to eligible entities for providing on site mental health and substance abuse counseling and referral services to individuals who have been subjected to domestic or sexual violence.

Social Security Protection and Tax Relief Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to impose a 12 percent tax on an individual's adjusted gross income for income tax, social security, and employer taxes.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow tax-free distributions from an individual retirement account (IRA) for the purchase or acquisition of a principal residence. Defines "qualified acquisition costs" as the costs of acquiring, constructing, or reconstructing a principal residence.

Lamprey Wild and Scenic River Act - Amends the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate specified segments of the Lamprey River in New Hampshire as recreational rivers and components of the National Wild and Scenic Rivers System. 
Directs the Secretary of the Interior to coordinate the management responsibilities of the Secretary with respect to such designated segments. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) zoning ordinances; (2) acquisition of lands; and (3) the authority of the Secretary to acquire lands.

STEM Network Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make matching grants to eligible networks to expand STEM education. Requires networks to use grant funds to: (1) test, validate, share, and scale up STEM education research, promising practices, and exemplary programs among members of the network and with other eligible networks; (2) identify points of weakness and strength among state STEM education efforts, the needs of English language learners and special education students, and the need to increase scientific literacy of prekindergarten through grade 12 students; (3) assist in the implementation of rigorous common content standards in STEM education for grades prekindergarten through grade 12 that reflect common elements between disciplines and take into consideration the Next Generation Science Standards and the Common Core State Standards Initiative; (4) promote STEM career pathways that reflect the projected STEM workforce needs of the 21st century that may include mentoring programs and STEM professional outreach; and (5) develop STEM-related workforce education and training programs in secondary schools and institutions of higher education to enhance the skills of workers to meet the needs of business and industry. Supporting Education for Returning Veterans Act of 2008 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants to institutions of higher education to establish programs that support veterans by providing and coordinating services that address their academic, financial, physical, and social needs. Requires such programs to include: (1) establishing a center of excellence for veteran's success on the campus of the institution; (2) a support team for veterans who are students at the institution; (3) outreach to, and recruitment of, veterans; (4) supportive instructional services for veterans; (5) activities designed to ease the transition of veterans to life on the campus of the institution; (6) support for veteran student organizations and veteran student support groups on campus; and (7) coordination of academic advising and admissions counseling with military bases and National Guard and Reserve units in the area.

Export Enhancement Act of 1999 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to revise the duties of the Foreign Assistance Board of Directors of the Corporation. 
Directs the Board to vote in favor of any action proposed to be taken by the Corporation that is likely to have significant adverse environmental impacts that are sensitive, diverse, or unprecedented, unless for at least 60 days before the vote:  (1) an environmental impact assessment or initial environmental audit; and (2) such assessment has been completed by the project applicant and made available to the public. 
Requires the Board to hold a public hearing in order to afford an opportunity for any person to present views regarding the activities of the Corporation. 
Sets forth provisions regarding the duties of the United States Trade Representative. 
Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to extend the authority of the Trade and Development Agency to make specified determinations as to whether or not certain Federal export promotion activities are likely to have significant adverse environmental impacts. 
Requires the Trade Promotion Coordinating Committee to report to the Secretary of Commerce on the actions taken or efforts currently underway to eliminate the areas of overlap and duplication among Federal export promotion activities

Great Falls Preservation and Redevelopment Act of 1993 - Establishes the Great Falls Historic District in Paterson, New Jersey. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to make grants to, and enter into cooperative agreements with, nonprofit entities for:  (1) the purchase of property or easements; (2) emergency stabilization; and (3) the establishment of a coordinated fund. 
Requires the Secretary to enter into cooperative agreements with the owners of properties within the District of historic or cultural significance for the preservation and interpretation of such properties. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Requires the Township to install the Lens in the Lighthouse for the purpose of operating the Lens and Lighthouse.  Provides for the conveyance of such Lens and personal property.

Katie Sepich Enhanced DNA Collection Act of 2010 - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to require the maximum amount of funds that would otherwise be allocated to a state under the Montgomery GI Bill to be increased by 5% for such state in order to implement a minimum DNA collection process and use such process for the year 2011.

Increases the amount of funds that would otherwise be allocated to a state under the Montgomery GI Bill to be increased by 10% for such state in order to implement an enhanced DNA collection process and use such process for the year 2011.

Hardship Outlays to protect Mortgagee Equity (HOME) Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the tax on early distributions from the tax on principal residence mortgage payments distributions for mortgage principal residence mortgages.

Custodial Interrogation Recording Act - Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to direct the Attorney General to make grants to States and local governments to take whatever steps the Attorney General determines to be necessary to achieve the complete and accurate recording, by both audio and video means, of every custodial interrogation occurring within the State or local government. Limits the portion of the costs of a program funded by such a grant to 75 percent.

Amends the Community-Based Overweight and Obesity Prevention Program of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to direct the Secretary of HHS to establish a community-based overweight and obesity prevention program, which shall award grants to, or enter into contracts with, eligible entities to: (1) plan evidence-based programs for the prevention of overweight and obesity among children and their families; or (2) implement such programs. Requires the Secretary to award grants to, or enter into contracts with, entities that have a history of working within and serving the communities in which they serve.
Tax Equity Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide regional cost-of-living adjustments in individual income tax rates.

Emergency Mortgage Loan Modification Act of 2008 - Makes a servicer of a residential mortgage loan that acts in a manner consistent with the duty to maximize the total proceeds from the loan agreement or for which payment default would be imminent or reasonably foreseeable.

Declares that a servicer that acts in a manner consistent with the duty to maximize the total proceeds from the loan agreement or for which payment default would be infeasible, engages in other loss mitigation, including acceptance of a short payment or partial discharge of principal, to the extent that such actions will maximize the net present value to be realized on the loan, including over that which would be realized through foreclosure.

Declares that this Act shall not be construed to limit a servicer's ability to enter into loan modifications or workout plans other than qualified loan modifications.

International Commerce Enhancement Act - Amends the Arms Export Control Act to revise and extend through FY 2012 the authority of the President to issue, and to suspend, import and export quotas for: (1) weapons and equipment; and (2) non-farm defense and non-fuel defense (NFD) provisions.

Allows funds apportioned to a state under this Act to be used for regional collaboration and coordination activities that lead to regional traffic incident management policies, programs, plans, procedures, and agreements; purchase or lease of telecommunications equipment for first responders as part of the development of a regional traffic incident management program; purchase or lease of equipment to support the clearance of traffic incidents; transportation management system payments to contractors for towing and recovery services as part of a regional traffic incident management program; rental of vehicle storage or staging areas immediately adjacent to roadways as part of a regional traffic incident management program; traffic service patrols as part of a regional traffic incident management program; enhanced hazardous materials incident response; traffic management systems in support of traffic incident management; traffic incident management training; crash investigation equipment; other activities under a regional traffic incident management plan; and statewide incident reporting systems.

Colorectal Cancer Detection Act of 2018  This bill amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to allow Medicare coverage for the screening of colorectal cancer in the year following the date of the enactment of this bill.

Infertility Research Centers Act of 2002 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development to make grants to, and enter into contracts with, public or nonprofit private entities for the development and operation of infertility prevention centers.

Federal Reserve Accountability Act of 2009 - Authorizes the Comptroller General to conduct reviews of the credit facilities of the Federal Reserve System (the System). Authorizes the Comptroller General to make and retain copies of certain books, accounts, and other records established by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the Board) and any credit facility (as specified) that is established by an agency (as specified) at any reasonable time. Requires the Comptroller General to have access to the officers, employees, contractors, and other agents and representatives of any single and specific partnership or corporation (as specified) or any credit facility (as specified) at any reasonable time, as the Comptroller General may request. Requires the Comptroller General to provide to any such partnership, corporation, or credit facility a current list of officers and employees to whom information made available under this Act may be made available, and who may make notes or copies necessary to carry out a review or examination. Requires the Board to place a link entitled "Audit" on its website.

Cures Can Be Found Act of 2005 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited credit, through 2007, for: (1) qualified stem cell research and storage contribution; and (2) $2,000 for each qualified umbilical cord blood donation made by the taxpayer during a taxable year.

Regulatory Integrity Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill requires each executive agency to publish in a searchable format information regarding pending agency regulatory actions that are not in the public interest and that are not puffery.  Each agency must publish a list of each pending agency regulatory action and with regard to each such action: (1) the date on which the agency first began to develop or consider the action, (2) the status of the action, (3) an estimate of the date of the action, (4) a list of agency regulatory actions issued by the agency, or (5) a copy of an approved or revised copy of an agency rulemaking.  The information must specify whether the agency is considering alternatives, including alternatives that may conflict with the intent, objective, or methodology of the action.  The information must also specify whether the agency is accepting or will be accepting comments.  The information must also describe the content of the information and the methods and a copy of the original communication.  The information must also indicate the number of public communications issued by the agency for each such action. Amends the Public Health Service Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and issue public service announcements that advertise and promote the pharmacist profession, highlight the advantages and rewards of being a pharmacist, and encourage individuals to enter the profession. 
Requires the Secretary to award grants to entities to support State and local advertising campaigns through appropriate media outlets to promote the profession, highlight its advantages and rewards, and encourage individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds to enter the profession. 
Directs the Secretary to establish a demonstration project to enhance the participation of individuals who are pharmacists in the National Health Service Corps Loan Repayment Program. 
Authorizes appropriations.

Knife Owners' Protection Act of 2017 This bill applies to any person who is not otherwise prohibited by federal law from possessing, transporting, shipping, or receiving a knife or knives from any place where such person may lawfully possess, carry, or transport such a knife or knives.  Any person who is transporting a knife or tools designed for enabling escape in an emergency incorporating a blunt tipped safety blade, a protected blade, or a separate blade for cutting safety belts may be carried in the passenger compartment and need not be secured in a locked container, glove compartment, or console. This bill shall not apply to the transport of a knife or tools in the passenger cabin of aircraft whose passengers are subject to airport screening procedures of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA). A person who is transporting a knife or tools in compliance with this bill may not be arrested or otherwise detained for violation of any law or any rule or regulation of a state or any political subdivision related to the possession, transportation, or carrying of knives, unless there is probable cause to believe that the person is not in compliance with at least one of the requirements of this Act.  A person may assert this bill as a claim or defense in any action

Child Modeling Exploitation Prevention Act - Amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to prohibit employers from employing child models in exploitive child modeling.  Defines "exploitive child modeling" as modeling involving the use of a child under 17 years old for financial gain without the purpose of marketing a product or service other than the image of the child.  Exempts from such prohibition any such use, regardless of whether the employment relationship of the child is direct or indirect, or contractual or noncontractual, or is termed that of an independent contractor.  Makes such prohibition inapplicable to an image which, taken as a whole, has serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value.  Makes such prohibition inapplicable to an image which, taken as a whole, has serious literary, artistic, political, or scientific value, except in cases in which the intent is to make a financial gain thereby, or to convey a message which is opposed to the prevailing commercial opinion of the time. Presidential Transition Act of 2000 - Amends the Presidential Transition Act of 1963 to include within the President-elect's budget the President's transition costs for briefings, workshops, or other activities to acquaint key prospective presidential appointees with the problems and challenges that most typically confront new political appointees when they make the transition from campaign and other prior activities to assuming the responsibility for governance after inauguration. Requires the Office of Government Ethics to study and report on improvements to the financial disclosure process for presidential nominees.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to transfer certain land in the Standing Rock Indian Reservation, North Dakota, to the Secretary of the Interior for the Oahe Dam and Reservoir Project.  Provides that nothing in this Act deprives any person of any easement, leasehold, or other right of interest that the person may have in the land to be transferred.  Requires the Secretary to prepare a map of the land transferred.

International Remittance Services Enhancement and Protection Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Credit Union Act to require the appropriate Federal banking agencies, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to jointly prescribe disclosure requirements for any money transmitting business initiating an international money transfer on behalf of a consumer (whether or not the consumer maintains an account at such institution or business) to provide to the consumer: (1) any fees to be charged to the recipient, including any exchange rate or currency conversion fees; and (2) a final itemization of all costs to the consumer, which would include all fees charged, for the remittance.

Animal Agriculture Environmental Incentives Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a limited credit for the purchase of equipment for the milking of dairy cows or the raising of livestock or poultry (including egg production) for commercial sale.

Prohibits a health care provider from being considered to be in noncompliance with the applicable requirements of this Act before October 16, 2003, with respect to: (1) electronic transactions in connection with a health care claims or equivalent encounter information transaction, (2) health care payments or remittances or health care claim status transactions, and (3) enrollment and disenrollment in a health plan transaction. Deems such a provider to be noncompliance with such requirements until October 16, 2003, with respect to: (1) the April 14, 2003, date of compliance with the requirements of this Act; or (2) whether the transmission meets any standard formats required by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) of the Code of Federal Regulations.

Protection from Sexual Predators Act of 1997 - Expresses the sense of the Congress that States should more seriously consider the relatively high recidivism rate of sexual offenders when deciding whether to plea bargain with a first-time sexual offender and whether to grant parole to sexual offenders. 
Amends the Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act of 1994 to provide that a State is not eligible for a grant unless it has provided assurances to the Attorney General that such State has in effect laws which allow the court to impose a sentence of life in prison without parole on a defendant in a criminal case who is convicted of a State offense for conduct that:  (1) is an offense under the Federal criminal code or under U.S. maritime law; or (2) would have been an offense under either of such Acts if the offense had occurred in the special maritime or territorial jurisdiction of the United States. 
Requires the National Institute of Justice to carry out a study of persistent sexual predators.  Requires the Institute to report to the Congress and the President on such study.

Meat and Poultry Products Traceability and Safety Act of 2003 - Amends the Federal Meat Inspection Act and the Poultry Products Inspection Act to require that in order to trace the history, use, and location of an article through a recordkeeping and audit system or registered identification, specified criteria be met.

Veterans Timely Access to Health Care Act - Amends federal veterans' benefits provisions to require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to prescribe an appropriate standard for access to care, for a veteran seeking primary care from the VA, for a waiting period at a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) health-care facility. Directs the Secretary to periodically review such standards and report on VA experience with regard to such waiting periods.

Historically Women's Public Colleges or Universities Historic Building Restoration and Preservation Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to make matching grants to historically women's public colleges or universities for the preservation and restoration of historic buildings and structures on their campuses.

Global Investments in America's Cities Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require that at least 3,000 of the visas made available under such Act be reserved for qualifying immigrants seeking to invest in a new commercial enterprise which will create employment in an economically distressed urban area and with respect to which such alien or relative has invested or is actively in the process of investing.

Defines "economically distressed urban area" as, at the time a petition for classification under such Act is filed, a city that has an average unemployment rate of at least 150% of the national average rate for the preceding year.

Requires the Comptroller General to report to Congress on the EB-5 (Entry, Board, and Passport to Immigration) Visa Program.

Small Business Expansion and Hiring Act of 2011 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a business-related tax credit for the retention of certain individuals who are newly hired by an employer. Defines "retained worker" as an individual who was employed for 40 hours or more during the 12-month period before the credit was introduced.

Making Education Affordable Act This bill amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Department of Education to award grants to institutions of higher education (IHEs) that carry out dual or concurrent enrollment programs or early college high school programs that enable students to earn college credits while in high school.  The IHEs must use grant funds to: (1) provide teachers, principals, and other school leaders with professional development activities that enhance or enable the provision of postsecondary coursework through such programs, and (2) support activities that help students meet eligibility criteria for such programs.  IHEs that receive a grant may use grant funds for costs associated with carrying out such transition programs, including the costs of: (1) tuition and fees, books, and required instructional materials for such program so that students will not be required to pay tuition or fees for postsecondary courses, and (2) transportation to and from such program.

Helping Responsible Homeowners Act - Requires the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) to provide for the refinancing of mortgage owned by the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac).

Women's Human Rights Protection Act of 1993 - Expresses the sense of the Congress that the State Department should designate a special assistant to the Assistant Secretary of State to promote international women's human rights within the overall human rights policy of the United States Government.  States that the purpose of assigning a special assistant is not to segregate such issues, but to assure that they are considered along with other human rights issues in the development of U.S. foreign policy.  Declares that a specifically designated assistant is necessary because within the human rights field and the foreign policy establishment, the issues of gender-based discrimination and violence against women have long been ignored or made invisible.  Declares that the Assistant Secretary should seek to assure that such issues are a factor in determining appropriate recipients for U.S. bilateral assistance as well as U.S. votes at the multilateral development banks.  Declares that the Assistant Secretary should seek to assure that the protection of women's human rights, including womens participation in U.S. political process, women's right to freedom of association and expression, and freedom from discrimination, would be addressed in the context of U.S. funded programs in the area of democracy including, but not limited to, democracy programs at the

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a taxpayer to exclude from gross income certain noncorporate income, including oil and gas production, that is used, sold, or exchanged for publicly traded infrastructure property. Defines "infrastructure property" as property which is part of any of the following: (1) roads and related improvements; (2) train tracks and related improvements; (3) airports; (4) dumps and waste; and (5) facilities for the transmission and distribution of electricity. Makes such property eligible for the tax deduction for domestic production activities in the case of publicly traded partnerships.

Independent Pharmacy Protection Act of 2006 - Amends part D (Voluntary Prescription Drug Benefit Program) of title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a Medicare Advantage organization to include in a prescription drug plan (PDP) contract for a prescription drug that provides for the payment of direct deposit (D) and increased dispensing fees for generic drugs.

Return of Talent Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to permit eligible aliens to return to their country of citizenship if the country is engaged in post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction activities, for a period not exceeding 24 months, without an exception granted under specified provisions to certain non-citizen aliens.

Allows such aliens to return to their country of citizenship with the alien and reenter the United States with the alien.

Extends the 24-month period for such aliens to meet the continuous residency requirements in that period.

Allows such aliens to meet the requirements for the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) for post-conflict or natural disaster reconstruction efforts.

Makes eligible for such aliens permanent the citizens of a country in which armed forces of the United States are engaged or have engaged in the 10 years preceding such determination.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to: (1) monitor and enforce the requirements of this Act; and (2) report to Congress.

Lifelong Improvements in Food and Exercise (LIFE) Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to carry out a national program to conduct and support activities regarding individuals who are overweight or obese in order to make progress toward the goal of significantly reducing the number of cases of obesity among individuals in the United States.

SOAR to Health and Wellness Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish a pilot program to provide training to health care providers and other related providers on human trafficking. The pilot program shall train health care providers and other related providers to: (1) identify potential human trafficking victims, (2) implement proper protocols and procedures for working with law enforcement to report and facilitate communication with such victims, (3) refer victims to social or victims service agencies or organizations, (4) provide such victims with coordinated care tailored to their circumstances, (5) include gender responsive and comprehensive training, and (6) consider the potential for integrating the training with existing training programs for victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, child abuse, child neglect, child maltreatment, and child sexual exploitation. HHS shall collect and report on data on the number of facilities operating under the pilot program, the number of health care providers and other related providers trained through the pilot program, and the total number of facilities operating under the pilot program.

Seniors Financial Fraud Prevention Act of 2010 - Directs the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to establish a separate office within the TCC to: (1) monitor the market for mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud targeting seniors; (2) coordinate with other relevant agencies regarding the requirements of this Act; (3) provide information to seniors and families and caregivers of seniors on mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud targeting seniors; (4) disseminate to seniors and families and caregivers of seniors general information on mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud targeting seniors; (5) provide publicly available information on any record of civil or criminal law enforcement action for mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud against particular entities or individuals; and (6) maintain a website to serve as a resource for seniors and families and caregivers of seniors regarding mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud targeting seniors.

Directs the FTC to: (1) log and acknowledge the receipt of mail, telemarketing, television, and Internet fraud complaints by individuals who certify that they have a reasonable belief that they have been the victim of fraud in connection with the conduct of mail, tele

Community Health Center Volunteer Provider Protection Act of 2005 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Comptroller General to study the adequacy of liability coverage through the program under which funds are provided for the coverage of public or nonprofit private entities, and volunteer practitioners, serving as public or nonprofit private health centers.

Dru Sjodin National Sex Offender Public Database Act of 2004 - Directs the Attorney General to make publicly available in the National Sex Offender Registry, via the Internet, all information described in the Jacob Wetterling Crimes Against Children and Sexually Violent Offender Registration Act regarding sexually violent predators and persons convicted of a sexually violent offense or criminal offense against a minor.

Requires the public registry to: (1) provide the name and any known aliases of the persons convicted of a sexually violent offense or a criminal offense against a minor; (2) provide the date of release, with a physical description and photograph, of the persons convicted of a sexually violent offense or a criminal offense against a minor; (3) consider whether or not to institute a civil commitment proceeding or any equivalent proceeding required under State law; and (4) intensively monitor, for at least one year, any persons who have been unconditionally released by the State and who have not been civilly committed.

Gerardo Hernandez Airport Security Act of 2014 - Directs the Assistant Secretary of Homeland Security (Transportation Security) to provide to all airports in the United States at which the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) performs, or oversees the implementation and performance of, security measures, and provide technical assistance as necessary, to verify that such airports have in place individualized working plans for responding to security incidents inside the perimeter of the airport, including active shooters, acts of terrorism, and incidents that target passenger-screening checkpoints.  Specifies types of plans, including one for establishing a unified command, a schedule for regular testing of communications equipment, an evaluation of how emergency calls will reach airport police, and a practiced method and plan to communicate with travelers and all other persons inside the perimeter of the airport.  Directs the Assistant Secretary to: (1) identify best practices that exist across airports for security incident planning, management, and training; and (2) establish a mechanism through which to share such best practices with other airport operators nationwide. Directs the Assistant Secretary to: (1) certify to Congress that all screening personnel have participated in practical training exercises for active shooter scenarios, and (2) provide to such committees

Stock Option Accounting Reform Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to require all publicly traded publicly traded companies to file annual reports with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on their stock options.  Prohibits the expensing of all options to purchase the stock of an issuer if the issuer: (1) has annual revenues of less than $25 million; (2) is organized under the laws of the United States or Canada; (3) is not an investment company; (4) the aggregate value of the outstanding voting and non-voting common equity securities held by non-affiliated parties is less than $25 million; and (5) the parent of the issuer meets certain requirements regarding the expensing of stock options.  Prohibits the SEC from recognizing as generally accepted any accounting principle establishing a standard setting body relating to the expensing of stock options unless it: (1) complies with the requirements of this Act; and (2) the economic impact study required by the Stock Option Accounting Reform Act of 2003 has been completed. Directs the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary of Labor to conduct and complete a joint study on the

Livestock Concentration Report Act - Establishes a Commission on Concentration in the Livestock Industry to:  (1) determine whether the study of concentration in the red meat packing industry adequately examined and identified procurement markets for slaughter cattle in the continental United States, analyzed the effects that slaughter cattle procurement practices, and concentration in the procurement of slaughter cattle have on the purchasing and pricing of slaughter cattle by beef packers; (2) requested the Attorney General to report on the application of antitrust laws and operation of other Federal laws applicable with respect to concentration and vertical integration in the procurement and pricing of slaughter cattle and of slaughter hogs by meat packers; (3) review laws and regulations relating to the operation of the meat packing industry regarding the concentration, vertical integration, and vertical coordination in the industry; (4) review the farm-to-retail price spread for livestock during the period beginning on January 1, 1993, and ending on the date the report is submitted; (5) make recommendations regarding the adequacy of price data obtained by the Department of Agriculture under the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946; (6) make recommendations regarding the adequacy of price discovery in the livestock industry for animals held for market; and (7

Law Enforcement Protection Act of 1997 - Amends the Federal criminal code to exempt qualified current and former law enforcement officers carrying appropriate written identification from State and local laws prohibiting the carrying of a concealed firearm. 
Authorizes the consent of Congress to enter into interstate or foreign commerce agreements for the enabling of individuals to carry concealed weapons.

Art-in-Architecture Act of 1993 - Requires the General Services Administration (GSA) to make art projects for the building available for commissioning. 
Authorizes the Administrator of the General Services Administration to increase the amount of funds available for new construction, building purchase, acquisition, or prospectus-level repair and alteration projects to include artworks for the building if the Federal Government has given the artist written permission to fabricate actual size reproductions. 
Requires the GSA to commission works of art by living American artists to be placed in federal buildings. 
Authorizes the GSA to decrease the amount of commission for a project, specifying reasons for decreasing amounts, for a project warranting less art work. 
Directs the GSA to:  (1) commission works of art by living American artists to be placed in federal buildings; and (2) provide for necessary services to maintain and preserve the works of art in a state of high quality.

Promoting Self-Reliance for the World's Poorest Act of 2002 - Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 to include within the Micentor PRISEA program grants for development of microenterprises and poverty measurement methods.

Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge Act - Establishes the Northern Yukon-Arctic International Wildlife Refuge in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge System, Canada, to be known as the Northern Yukon-Arctic Refuge.

Bright Idea Act of 2007 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to initiate a project to establish technical standards for general service lamps.

Requires the Secretary to consult with interested parties and consult with the EPA regarding whether such standards should be changed.

Traveler Redress Improvement Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to ensure the availability of DHS Traveler Redress Inquiry Program (DHS TRIP) redress process to adjudicate inquiries for individuals who are:   citizens of the United States or aliens lawfully admitted for permanent residence,  filed an inquiry with DHS TRIP after receiving enhanced screening at an airport passenger security checkpoint more than 3 times in any 60-day period, and  believed they were wrongly identified as being a threat to aviation security.  The TSA shall: (1) report to Congress on the implementation of the redress process, and (2) review and update the Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) for the Secure Flight programs. (Sec. 3) DHS shall: (1) conduct a comprehensive review of the DHS TRIP intelligence-based screening rules, and (2) notify specified entities of any such change, update, implementation, or suspension of the rules.  (Sec. 4) The Government Accountability Office shall: (1) report to Congress on the TSA
Amends the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States to suspend, through December 31, 2007, the duty on: (1) certain organic chemicals; and (2) certain alcohols.

Teacher Tax Credit Act of 2007 - Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to allow a tax credit for 50% of expenses for kindergarten, elementary, and secondary school teachers, instructors, counselors, aides, and principals in an eligible elementary or secondary school for an academic year ending during a taxable year. Defines "eligible teacher" as an individual who is a kindergarten through grade 12 classroom teacher, instructor, counselor, aide, or principal in an elementary or secondary school on a full-time basis for an academic year ending during a taxable year.

Denies such a tax credit for expenses for which a deduction was made under this Act.

This bill requires the United States to take all necessary and appropriate steps to ensure the safety of the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya, Iraq. The bill also requires the United States to provide assistance to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees to process applications by Camp Liberty/Hurriya residents for refugee status and to secure their orderly resettlement in safe locations outside of Iraq, including in the United States for any such residents who express such a desire. The United States must: (1) take all necessary and appropriate steps to ensure the safety of the residents of Camp Liberty/Hurriya, and (2) report to Congress on steps taken to guard the safety of Camp Liberty/Hurriya and secure their orderly resettlement.

(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on March 1, 2004. The summary of that version is repeated here.)(Sec. 2) Amends the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act of 1996 to extend through December 1, 2004, the basic pilot program. Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to expand the operation of such program to all 50 States by December 1, 2004. Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to report to the congressional homeland security committees on the progress of the basic pilot program. Authorizes the Secretary of Homeland Security to give priority to petitions for classification under the basic pilot program for regional centers to promote economic growth. Authorizes the Secretary of Commerce, Justice, and State to give priority to petitions for immigration-related economic development projects.  Directs the General Accounting Office to report to Congress on the immigrant investor program.

Enhancing Nutrition in Medical Education Act of 2004 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to make grants to accredited schools of medicine to integrate innovative curricula on nutrition into medical education. Directs the Secretary to ensure that such curricula focus on preventive health measures, including education on the causes, treatment, and prevention of obesity, the office education and counseling to ensure appropriate diet for mostly healthy people, and the prevention and treatment of common nutritional deficiencies. Directs the Secretary to establish a multidisciplinary planning committee to develop the curricula. Sets forth grant requirements.

Dismemberment Abortion Ban Act of 2015 This bill prohibits a physician knowingly performing a dismemberment abortion and thereby killing an unborn child from being dissected or from performing an abortion on a woman who is a victim of rape or incest. A woman who is a victim of rape or incest may file a civil action against any person who has performed a dismemberment abortion. A woman who is a victim of a violation of the prohibition against dismemberment abortion may not be prosecuted under this bill.

No Entry for Supporters of the Iranian Regime Act of 2010 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make aliens who engage in certain activities with respect to Iran inadmissible to the United States. Authorizes the Secretary of State to waive the prohibition and to notify an alien of the reasons for inadmissibility.

Amends the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to require a state regulatory authority (regulatory entity) to: (1) establish proceedings to examine the degree to which distributed resources contribute ancillary services; and (2) prescribe appropriate measures to ensure adequate ancillary services so that grid interconnection for distributed resources is safe, reliable, and efficient. 
Requires each state regulatory authority and each nonregulated electric utility to: (1) begin the consideration required under those provisions; or (2) make the determination necessary to the standard established by those provisions.  Deems to be a reference to the date of enactment of those provisions any delay in the implementation of those provisions, or any failure to comply with those provisions.

Synthetics Trafficking and Overdose Prevention Act of 2016 or the STOP Act of 2016 This bill amends the Tariff Act of 1930 to revise the requirements for the shipment of certain non-letter class mail to the United States. The bill requires the Postmaster General to provide the appropriate documentation or information to the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) or a U.S. Postal Union (USPOU) if such mail is imported into the United States for export. The bill also requires the USPS or USPOU to provide the Postmaster General with an electronic entry for such mail. The bill also requires the Postmaster General to provide the appropriate notification to the USPS or USPOU of any such mail that is arriving in the United States. The bill also requires the USPS or USPOU to provide the Postmaster General with a specified amount of additional information to the USPS for any non-letter class mail. The bill also requires the USPS or USPOU to provide the Postmaster General with a specified amount of additional information to the USPOU for any non-letter class mail.
