Ports-to-Forts Act of 2012 - Authorizes the Maritime Administrator (MHA) of the Department of the Navy to make grants to states or ports to assist them in repairing or constructing commercial strategic seaports.

Accessing Medicare Therapies Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for the inclusion of negotiated price of drugs provided under certain compassionate Medicare (CMS) programs, including those administered by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) or the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) pharmacies. Defines "negotiated price" for a covered drug part D drug, with respect to an individual enrolled in a CMS plan, as the average negotiated price for such drug in the zip code of the enrollee.

Criminal Terrorism Improvements Act of 2006 - Amends the federal criminal code to: (1) impose a death penalty for any person who commits a terrorist offense; (2) increase the penalties for such offenses; (3) provide for a three-year increase in the prison sentence for terrorists who violate the terms of their sentences; and (4) deny federal benefits to terrorists.

Defines "terrorist offense" as a felony offense that is: (1) a federal crime of terrorism; (2) any offense under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 or the Atomic Energy Act of 1949; or (3) a federal offense that is an attempt or conspiracy to commit such an offense.

Declares that any individual convicted of a federal crime of terrorism shall, as provided by the court on motion of the government, be ineligible for any or all federal benefits for any term of years or for life.

Agricultural Water Conservation Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 30 percent of the water conservation system expenses for the purchase and installation of a water conservation system but only if: (1) the land served by the water is wholly in an area of extreme drought severity on the Palmer Drought Severity Index published by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA); (2) the taxpayer has a water conservation system which has been reviewed and approved by the Service and Bureau of Reclamation and has been reviewed and approved by the President and the Congress; and (3) there is an irrigation water savings of at least 5 percent attributable to such system.

Dollar Bill Act of 2013 - Directs the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to designate a specific week (the Target Week) starting no earlier than 90 days from the enactment of this Act and ending no later than 120 days from the enactment of this Act.  Directs the Board to use open market operations to maintain and promote stable and effective financial markets during and after the transition to a defined value for the U.S. dollar.  Requires all entities that depreciate capital assets for tax purposes to be entitled to 100% expensing of all capital investment for tax purposes in the year that the investment is made.  Requires the Congressional Budget Office (CBO), in addition to the scoring CBO will do of the tax changes provided in this Act, to calculate the impact on federal revenues on a present value basis.  Amends the Federal Reserve Act to remove federal reserve bank authority to pay earnings on reserves.

Dairy Promotion Fairness Act - Amends the Dairy Production Stabilization Act of 1983 to require the Secretary of Agriculture to appoint at least two members to the National Dairy Promotion and Research Board. Directs the Secretary to appoint National Dairy Promotion and Research Customs (NCRRC) members. Requires the NCRRC to provide an assessment to the Board in the manner prescribed by the order.

Pesticide Maintenance Fees Reauthorization Act - Amends the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act to extend through FY 2006 the authority of the Secretary of Agriculture to issue registration fees for registered pesticides. Extends through FY 2006 the authority of the Secretary to issue additional registration fees. Extends through FY 2006 the authority of the Secretary to issue pesticide tolerance processing fees.

Hippocratic Oath and Patient Protection Act of 1996 - Prohibits a health care carrier from:  (1) preventing or limiting a health care provider's protected communication to a patient or the public; or (2) disclose to a health care provider and an enrollee a list of all services and benefits offered under the health plan, including any service or benefit maximum, limitation, or exclusion, or an indemnification clause as under a health care plan. 
Sets forth provisions regarding:  (1) a protected communication, and for purposes of such provisions, prohibited indemnification clauses; and (2) enforcement. 
Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to impose a civil money penalty upon a health carrier who violates this Act. 
Requires the Secretary to report to the Congress on the impact of this Act on health carriers, health care providers, and enrollees.

SuperPAC Elimination Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to eliminate certain limitations on the contribution election by citizens and lawful permanent residents to the candidates in federal elections.  The bill requires a political committee of a candidate or of a committee of a candidate to notify a principal campaign committee in writing of any excess contributions the candidate received during a calendar year. A principal campaign committee must submit an additional notification within 24 hours after the aggregate amount of contributions received exceeds $200.

Buy America 2.0 Act This bill amends the federal transportation infrastructure project (FTMIP) program to prohibit federal agencies from obligating for a transportation or infrastructure project any steel, iron, and manufactured goods used for the project unless the steel, iron, and manufactured goods used for the project are produced in the United States.  The bill also prohibits the use of public transportation fuels (i.e., methanol) for the production of steel or the use of certain FTMIP components for the production of steel or the use of certain components for FY2021.

Terrorism Elimination Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the Counter-Terrorism Trust Fund to provide funds to the Department of the Treasury to make expenditures for counter-terrorism efforts by the United States. Provides for the issuance of Freedom Bonds to raise funds to assist in the recovery operations following the terrorist acts of September 11, 2001.

Federal Facility Accountability Act of 2013 - Amends the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA) to require federal agencies, departments, and instrumentalities to submit, annually and in the same manner and to have been, at facilities owned or operated by such entities, or by the same entity in the same manner and to have been, at any facilities they operate, to the United States any remedial actions at such facilities.  Requires the United States to waive any federal immunity otherwise applicable to any state substantive or procedural requirement with respect to the enforcement of any injunctive relief under CERCLA, civil penalties, or federal fines.  Provides for civil penalties and civil remedies for federal employees and property for federal violations of CERCLA.  Authorizes the President to issue, issue, issue, issue, issue, issue, and issue, until the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) directs, actions taken, or regulations promulgated pursuant to such delegation or assignment.

Ensuring Full Use of Federal Health Care Funding Act of 2014 - Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to determine the recoupment amount for each state and the amounts that will be made available for grants to qualified entities in each state.  Directs the Secretary to recoup any funds awarded to a state under this Act to the extent that such funds are not obligated by the state for expenditure before April 1, 2014.  Allows the Secretary to decide not to recoup the funds of a state that has submitted a plan for spending such funds in a timely manner.  Requires the Secretary to use all such funds to make grants to qualified entities to carry out activities in the state consistent with this Act.  Directs the Secretary to establish standards for qualified entities to engage in outreach, education, and enrollment activities, and to avoid conflicts of interest.  Requires grants to be used for: (1) non-navigator assistance personnel; (2) outreach; and (3) marketing and campaign materials.

Department of Homeland Security Component Privacy Officer Act of 2008 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate a full-time privacy official, who shall report directly to the senior official appointed under this Act, who shall have primary responsibility for the component in implementing the privacy policy for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Requires such component to have primary responsibility for its component component in implementing the privacy policy for DHS.

Requires such components to report directly to both the head of the component and the senior official, who shall have the primary responsibility for the component in implementing the polices and directives of such senior official.

Requires such components to report directly to both the head of the component and the senior official appointed under this Act, who shall have the primary responsibility for the component in implementing the polices and directives of the President, the Vice President, the President's successor, the President's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor's successor

Medicare Prescription Drug Lifeline Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a process under which an applicable individual may terminate enrollment in either the Medicare prescription drug or MA-PD plans in which they are enrolled and enroll in any prescription drug plan or MA-PD plan that provides some coverage of covered part D drugs (as defined in title XVIII of the Social Security Act) after the individual has reached the initial coverage limit but has not reached the annual out-of-pocket threshold.

Directs the Secretary to notify, or require sponsors of prescription drug plans and organizations offering MA-PD plans to notify, applicable individuals of the option to change plans under such process. Requires such notice to be provided to an applicant individual within 30 days of meeting the definition of such individual.

Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on the costs to the Medicare program of eliminating the initial coverage limit under the Medicare prescription drug and MA-PD plans.

Political Broadcasting Access Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require that each broadcast station license issued under such Act annually make available free broadcast time for political advertising.  Requires the Federal Communications Commission to make such free broadcast time available allot free broadcast time annually to:  (1) the national organization of each qualified political party; and (2) the State organization of each qualified political party of the State within which the preponderance of the station's audience resides.  Requires allot free broadcast time to each qualified political party in accordance with the following standards:  (1) such party shall allot an equal amount, but not less than two hours, of free broadcast time annually to the national organization of each qualified political party and the State organization of each qualified political party of the State within which the preponderance of the station's audience resides; (2) the two or more hours of free broadcast time allotted to any organization be composed of units of varying lengths of not more than five minutes or less than 10 seconds; and (3) the broadcast time allotted by any such political party be allotted so that:  (1) at least one-half of the total

Enhancing Employment and Training Through Education Act of 2013 - Amends the Food and Nutrition Act of 2008 to direct the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to carry out, under such terms and conditions as the Secretary considers appropriate, pilot projects to identify best practices for employment and training programs to raise the number of work registrants who obtain unsubsidized employment, increase their earned income, and reduce their reliance on public assistance, including but not limited to the supplemental nutrition assistance program (SNAP, formerly known as the food stamp program). Requires pilot projects to be selected based on criteria that shall include: (1) enhancing existing employment and training programs in the state; (2) agreeing to participate in the evaluation; (3) collaborating with the state workforce board and other job training programs in the state and local area; (4) the extent to which the pilot project's components can be easily replicated by other states or political subdivisions; and (5) such additional criteria that ensure that the pilot projects: (1) target a variety of populations of work registrants, including childless adults, parents, and individuals with low skills or limited work experience; (2) are selected from a range of existing

Veterans Access to Care Accountability Act - Directs the Comptroller General to conduct random, periodic audits of Department of Veterans Affairs medical facilities and the Veterans Integrated Service Networks to assess whether such facilities and Networks are complying with all standards imposed by law or by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs with respect to the timely access of veterans, medical services, and other health care from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). Directs the Secretary to: (1) notify such eligible veteran of the status of the appointment of such eligible veteran for such care or services; and (2) make every effort possible to schedule an appointment for such eligible veteran for such care or services at a VA medical facility or through a non-VA health care provider on a date that is not later than seven days after the receipt of such report. Directs the Inspector General of the VA to report any such failure to the director of a VA medical facility or other official responsible for activities at such facility to the appropriate congressional committees. Prohibits the Secretary from paying a bonus or award to any director or other official of the VA, including a performance award, for the misrepresentation of patient records or other data to conceal a VA performance award. Directs the Inspector General to

Bounty Hunter Accountability and Quality Assistance Act of 1998 - Directs the Attorney General to develop model guidelines for the State control and regulation of persons employed or applying for employment as bounty hunters. 
Requires the guidelines to include recommendations of the Attorney General regarding:  (1) whether a person seeking employment as a bounty hunter should be required to submit to a fingerprint-based criminal background check prior to entering into the performance of duties; and (2) the availability of liability insurance for actions taken in the course of performing duties. 
Prohibits the guidelines from being construed to authorize the promulgation of any Federal regulations relating to bounty hunters, bounty hunter employers, or bail bond agents. 
Directs the Attorney General to publish model guidelines developed pursuant to this Act in the Federal Register.

Reinstatement of Enrollment for Medicaid Eligibility of Disadvantaged Youth (REMEDY) Act - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid program to suspend, rather than terminate, enrollment for individuals who are: (1) under the state plan for medical assistance under title XIX (Medicaid) until they become eligible for Medicaid enrollment after release; or (2) enrolled for Medicaid enrollment until the individual is no longer eligible to be so enrolled.

Amateur Radio Parity Act of 2016 (Sec. 3) This bill directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to amend its rules concerning private land use restrictions to prohibit the application to amateur stations of any private land use restriction, including a restrictive covenant, that fails to reasonably accommodate amateur service communications or that does not constitute the minimum practicable restriction on such communications to accomplish the lawful purposes of a community association seeking to enforce the restriction.  The FCC must also amend its rules by requiring any licensee in an amateur radio service to notify and obtain prior approval from a community association concerning the installation of an outdoor antenna.  The FCC may not change the requirements of this Act.

Dorothy Buell Memorial Visitor Center Lease Act - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the Porter County Convention, Recreation and Visitor Commission to establish a joint partnership with respect to the management of the Porter County Convention, Recreation and Visitor Center.

Authorizes the Secretary to lease space in the Center for use as a visitor center for the Lakeshore.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) identify the overall goals and purposes of the Center; (2) describe the allocation of management and operational duties between the Secretary and the Commission; (3) identify how activities of the Center will be funded; (4) establish procedures for changing or dissolving the joint partnership; and (5) address any other issues determined to be appropriate by the Secretary or the Commission.

Authorizes appropriations.

Title II - Public Land Technical Amendments Act of 2006 - Amends the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2005 to authorize appropriations for the Porter County Convention, Recreation and Visitor Center.

Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to authorize the issuance of a debenture purchased by the Federal Financing Bank and guaranteed by the Administration of the Small Business Administration.  Allows such Bank to prepay the debenture by paying the Federal Financing Bank the repurchase premium and the interest rate on the debenture.  Requires the Federal Financing Bank to pay the difference between the repurchase premium and the interest rate to the Bank.  Requires the Bank to pay the difference to the Federal Financing Bank the repurchase premium and the interest rate.  Requires the Federal Financing Bank to pay the difference to the Bank the same interest rate as it would have received if the Bank had not received such interest.  Requires the Federal Financing Bank to repay the debenture to the Bank within 10 years after the date of the prepayment.

Authorizes the Departments of Veterans Affairs and Housing and the Urban Development and Water Resources Management and the Environmental Protection Agency to apply for a commercial space station license.

Working Families' Access to Health Innovations Act of 2013 - Amends the Small Business Act to authorize the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to guarantee up to 90% of the loan made to a qualified eligible professional for the acquisition of health information technology for use in such professional's medical practice and for the costs associated with the installation of such technology. Limits the maximum amount of such loan principal to $350,000 and $2,000,000 with a single qualified professional and a single group of affiliated qualified professional lenders.  Authorizes the Administrator to impose a guarantee fee on the borrower of such a loan.  Requires the loan applicant to be a qualified eligible professional whose practice: (1) is a small business concern; and (2) serves individuals at least 50% of whom are entitled to benefits or enrolled under title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act, or (3) serves an area that consists predominantly of low-income families.  Limits the maximum loan principal to: (1) $350,000 with respect to any single qualified professional; and (2) $2

EMTALA Regulatory Improvement Act of 2003 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a procedure to notify hospitals and physicians when an investigation is closed of the presence of a EMTALA (Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act) investigation.

Directs the Secretary to establish a Technical Advisory Group to review issues related to the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) and its implementation.

Vision Zero Act of 2017 This bill authorizes the Department of Transportation to award grants to eligible entities to develop a transportation-related death and serious injury plan to eliminate transportation-related fatalities and serious injuries in the jurisdiction of such entity within a specified timeframe, not to exceed 20 years.  The grant program is available to eligible entities that serve a jurisdiction with a population of under 200,000. The federal share of project costs may not exceed 80%.

Small Business Hardship Relief Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for a hardship exemption for an employer who employed an average of not more than 100 full-time employees on business days during the preceding calendar year.

Amends Federal law to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to notify the Secretary whenever any State, county, municipality, or other jurisdiction is subject to a heat emergency which threatens the health of its residents. 
Requires the Secretary to:  (1) research and report to Congress on the amount of funds needed to fully compensate public utilities for the delivery of energy necessary to sufficiently cool the residencies of a LIHEAP recipient in a manner that will alleviate the likelihood of heat-related illness and prevent the worsening of existing acute conditions; and (2) take into account specified factors when determining the amount of money necessary to fund the "Emergency Cooling Fund." 
Directs the Secretary to direct the Governors of each State in which an emergency was declared that a portion funds designated by the Secretary shall be designated by the State for the use of providing energy to cool the residencies of current LIHEAP recipients, augmented by this Act. 
Requires the Administrator of the General Services Administration to receive notification of any declaration of a heat emergency as reflected in this Act. 
Directs the Administrator to initiate expedited procedures to distribute property to States and municipalities affected by the heat emergency, and to social service agencies and

Rail-Highway Grade Crossing Safety Act of 1994 - Amends Federal transportation law to authorize States, after adopting a policy requiring the review of the need for all new public at-grade rail-highway crossings, to use the funds authorized under this Act to provide an incentive payment to a local jurisdiction upon the permanent closing by the jurisdiction of a public at-grade crossing.  Authorizes the Secretary of Transportation to set aside $500,000 of such funds for the surface transportation program for FY 1856 through 2002 to carry out a public information and education program to help prevent and reduce motor vehicle accidents, injuries, and fatalities. 
Requires the Secretary to establish a grade crossing corridor safety incentive program. 
Requires the Secretary to carry out a program to provide additional financial incentives to States that review and implement grade crossing safety improvements on a corridor basis.

Fairness and Accountability in Reorganizations Act of 2006 - Repeals the prohibition against the payment of a performance, incentive, or other bonus or other compensation enhancement unless the court finds reasonable that such enhancements are essential to the survival of the business or are necessary to the organization's survival.

Requires the court, in determining whether a proposed tax credit or pension benefit plan provides for those necessary modifications in employee benefits and protections that are necessary to permit the reorganization of the debtor and assures that all creditors, the debtor, and all affected parties are treated fairly and equitably, the court shall take into account the ongoing impact on the debtor of the debtor's relationship with all subsidiaries and affiliates, regardless of whether any such subsidiary or affiliate is domestic or nondomestic or whether any such subsidiary or affiliate is a debtor entity.

Frank Buckles World War I Memorial Act This bill authorizes the World War I Memorial Foundation to establish a memorial to honor the soldiers who served in World War I and to ensure that future generations of Americans will know the complete history of World War I.

Satisfying Energy Needs and Saving the Environment Act or the SENSE Act.  Requires the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to authorize the operator of a coal refuse electric utility steam generating unit to comply with either: (1) an emissions standard for emissions of hydrogen chloride or sulfur dioxide that meets EPA requirements; or (2) an emission standard for emissions of hydrogen chloride and sulfur dioxide that meet EPA requirements but that are not more stringent than those for hydrogen chloride or sulfur dioxide. Prohibits the Administrator from requiring that such unit comply with both such standards.  Requires the Administrator to require an operator of a coal refuse unit to comply with no more than one of such emission standards. Prohibits the Administrator from requiring that such unit comply with both such standards.  Requires the Administrator to require an operator of a coal refuse unit to comply with no more than one of such emission standards, no more than one of such standards, or no more than one of such standards, for at least 30 boiler operating days.

Nutria Eradication and Control Act of 2009 - Establishes a nutria eradication program under which the Secretary of the Interior may, subject to the availability of appropriations, provide financial assistance to the states of Maryland, Louisiana, Delaware, Oregon, Virginia, and Washington to implement measures to: (1) eradicate or control nutria; and (2) restore wetland damaged by nutria.

Directs the Secretary to require that the program consist of management, research, and public education activities carried out in accordance with the document published by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service entitled "Eradication Strategies for Nutria in the Chesapeake and Delaware Bay Watersheds." Limits the federal share of the program to 75%.

Consumer and Community Choice in Access Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to authorize the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to require cable operators that provide interconnection, using cable system facilities, with the Internet to offer such interconnection on terms and conditions that are fair, reasonable, and nondiscriminatory. 
Requires cable operators to provide direct or indirect interconnection with the facilities and equipment of any Internet service provider on terms and conditions that are functionally and economically equivalent to the interconnection provided to any other Internet service provider, whether or not affiliated with the cable operator. 
Provides for the leasing of over-the-road cable service from a cable system operator to a cable operator's agent. 
Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require cable operators providing interconnection with the Internet to offer such interconnection on terms and conditions that are fair, reasonable, and nondiscriminatory. 
Provides for the limitation on the authority of a State or francising authority, or for civil action on the date of enactment of this Act.

Expresses the sense of Congress that the Department of Defense should undertake appropriate actions to ensure that family members of members of the National Guard and reserve who are mobilized have full access to mental health care during the periods of mobilization, deployment, and demobilization of such members of the Guard and reserve.

Directs the Secretary of Defense to: (1) undertake a nationwide initiative to increase access to mental health care for family members of members of the Guard and reserve who are deployed; and (2) reimbursement for such mental health care shall be provided under the TRICARE program for any family member's mental health care that is provided to a member of the Guard or reserve during the period of deployment.

Strengthening Local Transportation Security Capabilities Act of 2018 (Sec. 3) This bill directs the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to prioritize the assignment of officers and intelligence analysts from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and from the Office of Intelligence and Analysis of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to locations with participating state, local, and regional fusion centers in jurisdictions with a high-risk surface transportation asset in order to enhance DHS's security. TSA officers and intelligence analysts must work with state, local, and regional fusion centers to: (1) identify terrorist and other threats to surface transportation assets, (2) promote more consistent and timely sharing of threat information among jurisdictions, and (3) enhance DHS's situational awareness of such threats. (Sec. 4) DHS must make available to appropriate owners and operators of surface transportation assets and any other person that DHS determines appropriate to foster greater sharing of classified information relating to terrorist and other threats to surface transportation assets. NEPA Reciprocity Act - Allows states to use state laws and procedures to conduct reviews and make approvals in lieu of federal environmental laws and regulations, consistent with the provisions of this Act.

Witness Security and Protection Grant Program Act of 2011 - Directs the Attorney General to make competitive grants to state, tribal, and local governments to establish or maintain witness protection programs in: (1) court proceedings involving homicide, or involving a serious violent felony or serious drug offense as defined in the federal criminal code; and (2) court proceedings involving gangs or organized crime.

Requires the Attorney General to evaluate grant applications based on certain criteria, including: (1) the extent to which the applicant has a lack of infrastructure to support a witness assistance program; (2) the extent to which witness intimidation is present with respect to the applicant; (3) the level of cases not prosecuted by the applicant due to witness intimidation; (4) the number of homicides or serious violent felonies or serious drug offenses per capita in the jurisdiction of the applicant; (5) the number of serious violent felonies or serious drug offenses, as defined in the federal criminal code, per capita committed in the jurisdiction of the applicant; and (6) the extent to which organized crime is present in the jurisdiction of the applicant.

Oil Industry Merger Antitrust Enforcement Act - Amends the Clayton Act to require the Federal Trade Commission and the Antitrust Division of the Department of Justice to review and revise all enforcement guidelines and policies concerning mergers and acquisitions in oil companies and among companies involved in the production, refining, distribution, or marketing of oil, gasoline, natural gas, heating oil, or other petroleum-related products. 
Requires the Federal Trade Commission and the Antitrust Division to jointly review and revise all enforcement guidelines and policies regarding the application of the horizontal merger guidelines and the non-horizontal merger guidelines developed by the Horizontal Merger Guidelines issued April 2, 1992, and revised June 14, 1984. 
Requires the Federal Trade Commission and the Antitrust Division to report to specified congressional committees regarding such review and revision.

Amends the Clean Air Act to define "renewable biomass" as: (1) materials, pre-commercial thinnings, or invasive species from National Forest System land and public lands that are byproducts of preventive treatments that are removed to reduce hazardous fuels, reduce or contain disease or insect infestation, or restore ecosystem health; would not otherwise be used for higher-value products; and are harvested in accordance with specified requirements for old-growth forest restoration and management and large tree restoration and management.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (ESEA) to require each local educational agency (LEA) receiving assistance under ESEA to provide, upon a request made by a military recruiter or institution of higher education, access to the name, address, and telephone listing of each secondary school student served by the LEA, unless the parent of such student has submitted the prior consent request.  Prohibits a parent from submitting a written request, to the LEA, that the student's name, address, and telephone listing not be released for purposes of such request without the prior written consent of the parent.  Requires each LEA to notify parents of the students served by the LEA of the option to make a request, including the prior consent request.  Requires each LEA to: (1) provide, upon a request made by a military recruiter for military recruiting purposes, access to the name, address, and telephone listing of each secondary school student served by the LEA, notwithstanding ESEA provisions that deny recruiting access to a military recruiter; and (2) notify parents of the student's option to make such a request without prior written parental consent. American Freedom Agenda Act of 2007 - Repeals the Military Commissions Act of 2006 and the President's authority to establish military commissions for the trial of war crimes only in places of active hostilities against the United States where an immediate trial is necessary to preserve fresh evidence or to prevent local anarchy.

Prohibits any civilian or military tribunal of the United States from admitting as evidence statements extracted from the defendant by torture or coercion.

Prohibits any federal agency from gathering foreign intelligence in violation of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.

Prohibits a U.S. officer or agent from kidnapping, imprisoning, or tortureting any person abroad based solely on the President's belief that the subject of the kidnapping, imprisonment, or torture is a criminal or enemy combatant.

Prohibits a U.S. journalist from publishing information received from the executive branch unless the publication would cause direct, immediate, and irreparable harm to U.S. national security.

Creating Opportunities for Military Members to Use Transportation Efficiently Act of 2014 or the COMMUTE Act of 2014 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD) to establish a Military Community Infrastructure Program to provide grants to eligible entities (state or local governments, owners or operators of public transportation, or a metropolitan or regional planning organization) for the construction of: (1) roads; (2) mass transit and parking facilities; (3) pedestrian access and bicycle access; and (4) public transportation systems. Defines "eligible entity" to mean: (1) a state or political subdivision, (2) an owner or operator of public transportation, (3) a local governmental authority, (4) a metropolitan or regional planning organization, or (5) a regional transportation planning organization.

Amends the San Luis Rey Indian Water Rights Settlement Act to require the Secretary of the Interior to arrange for the development of at least 16,000 acre-feet of supplemental water from public lands within the boundaries of the State of California outside the service area of the Central Valley Project and to obtain at least 16,000 acre-feet of either from water conserved by the works authorized in title II of such Act or through contract with the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California.  Subjects such right to the provisions of such Act and of the settlement agreement governing the use and disposition of supplemental water.  Authorizes appropriations for such work. 
Authorizes the use of Federal funds for such work.  Prohibits the use of Federal funds for construction of such works.  Requires the water identified in the above Act to be made available, subject to the approval requirement established in the settlement agreements, for consumptive use by California Contractors within their service areas according to their priority under the Seven Party Agreement. Broadband Internet Regulatory Relief Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require an incumbent local exchange carrier (ICE) to file a petition with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) with respect to its provision of advanced service, in any State in which 70 percent of the ICE's DSL-capable loop in its service territory are ICE-capable.  Prohibits such a carrier from subjecting such services to FCC regulation if the FCC determines that services are being offered by an unaffiliated ICE provider in the manner established by this Act.  Requires the FCC to approve any petition for such treatment if it is determined that services are being offered by an unaffiliated provider in the manner established by this Act.  Provides that if the FCC determines that services are being offered by an unaffiliated provider in the manner established by this Act, it shall approve the ICE petition unconditionally.

Protecting Domestic Violence and Stalking Victims Act - Expands the definition of "intimidate partner" and "misdemeanor crime of stalking" to include: (1) an individual who is a dating partner or former dating partner of a victim; and (2) a firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition firearm or ammunition

Insider Trading Prohibition Act - Amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 to make it unlawful for any person to purchase, sell, or enter into, or cause the purchase or sale of, any security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement while in possession of material, nonpublic information relating to such security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement, or relating to the market for such security, security-based swap, or security-based swap agreement, if such person knows, or recklessly disregards, that such information has been obtained wrongfully or that such purchase, sale, or entry would constitute a wrongful use of such information. Makes such prohibition inapplicable to any person who controls or employs a person who has violated this Act. Exempts securities or transactions from this prohibition if the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) determines that such action is inconsistent with its purposes.

Desalination Energy Consumption Reduction Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of Energy to make incentive payments to the owners of qualified desalination facilities to encourage the utilization of the best available technology to reduce the consumption of electrical energy in the desalination process. Authorizes the Secretary to make such payments no later than FY2018.

Customs Training Enhancement Act - Directs the Commissioner of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to establish and carry out educational seminars at U.S. ports of entry to improve the ability of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) personnel to classify and appraise articles imported into the United States in accordance with the customs laws of the United States, including to improve the ability of CBP personnel to identify and prevent the mislabeling and transshipment of articles. Authorizes the Commissioner and interested parties to provide instruction and related instructional materials at each seminar. Requires the Commissioner to pay the costs of each seminar and the expenses of each such seminar to the cost to establish and carry out such seminars.

Seeds for the Future Act - Amends the Competitive, Special, and Facilities Research Grant Act to require the Secretary of Agriculture (Secretary) to ensure that at least $50,000,000 for each fiscal year is used for competitive research grants that support the development of public cultivars.

Requires the Secretary to appoint a Research, Education, and Extension Coordinator within the Research, Education, and Extension Office that reports to the Coordinator about research activities funded by the Department relating to the breeding of public cultivars.

Requires the Under Secretary to appoint a Coordinator within the Office that reports to the Under Secretary about research activities and coordination functions relating to public cultivar research.

Patient Access to Durable Medical Equipment Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to publish on its website the results of the monitoring of access to durable medical equipment (DME) and of health outcomes on its website, and of federal Medicaid reimbursement to states for DME to Medicare payments.

Organic Farmer and Consumer Protection Act of 2017 This bill amends the Organic Foods Production Act of 1990 to authorize appropriations to carry out activities under the national organic program.  The bill authorizes appropriations for the program through FY2022.  The Department of Agriculture (USDA) must modernize its international trade tracking and data collection systems to carry out activities under the program.  USDA may provide funds for FY2019 for: (1) carrying out this bill, and (2) maintaining the database and technology upgrades previously carried out.  USDA must also provide for the sharing of confidential business information with federal and state agency officers and employees. USDA may also issue regulations to limit the type of operations that are excluded from certification under this bill.

Survivor Benefits Improvement Act of 2013 - Amends federal veterans' benefits provisions to: (1) extend the initial period for increasing the proportion of a surviving spouse of a veteran with disabilities (including spina bifida) under the Servicemembers' Health Insurance Program (SIP) and the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) pension plan to five years; (2) authorize the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to provide to a child of a veteran who is suffering from spina bifida the health care, vocational training, and rehabilitation and monetary allowance required to be paid to a child of a Vietnam veteran who is suffering from spina bifida under SIP provisions; and (3) authorize the Secretary to provide to a child of a veteran who is suffering from spina bifida the health care, vocational training, and monetary allowance required to be paid to a child of a Vietnam veteran who is suffering from spina bifida under SHA veterans' active duty pension plan provisions. Authorizes the Secretary to provide to a surviving spouse of a veteran who is suffering from spina bifida the health care, vocational training, and monetary allowance required to be paid to a child of a Vietnam veteran who is suffering from spina

Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund Act of 1998 - Establishes in the Treasury the Veterans Tobacco Trust Fund, consisting of such amounts as may be appropriated, credited, or donated to such Fund.  Requires that the Fund be furnished with the necessary equipment and supplies to conduct programs to reduce the use of tobacco products by minors and to conduct research relating to prevention and treatment of, and rehabilitation from, tobacco addiction and diseases associated with tobacco use.

Medicaid Directory of Caregivers Act or the Medicaid DOC Act - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require states to publish on their public State website a directory of providers providing medical assistance on a fee-for-service basis or through a primary and specialty care case-management system. Requires providers to register with the state Medicaid administration and provide information regarding: (1) whether the provider is accepting as new patients individuals who receive medical assistance, and (2) the provider's cultural and linguistic capabilities.

Fluke Fairness Act of 2013 - Directs the Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission (Commission) to submit to the Secretary of Commerce and the Secretary may approve, within one year after enactment of this Act, a modified fishery management plan for the commercial and recreational management of summer flounder under the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act or an amendment to such plan that: (1) is based on the best scientific information available, (2) reflects changes in the distribution, abundance, and location of summer flounder in establishing distribution of the commercial and recreational catch quotas, (3) considers regional, coastwide, or other management measures for summer flounder that comply with the National Standards, and (4) prohibits the allocation of commercial or recreational catch quotas for summer flounder on a state-by-state basis using historical landings data that does not reflect the status of the summer flounder stock, based on the most recent scientific information.  Requires the Comptroller General (GAO) to submit to Congress and the Secretary, within one year after the approval of such modified plan, an assessment of whether it complies with the National Standards.

Ending Maternal Mortality Act of 2018 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop and submit to Congress a national plan to reduce maternal mortality over the next 10 years. The plan must include:  a list of objectives for meeting the goals, and a strategy for implementing the plan across the agencies and offices of HHS and other departments and services; specific issues to address, including increasing public understanding of maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity, improving data collection, including state-level reporting, identifying at-risk populations, and improving health and treatment services for expectant mothers struggling with substance use and mental health disorders; and  a plan for making each plan publicly accessible on the HHS website.

Backcountry Landing Strip Access Act - Prohibits the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture from taking any action that would permanently close, restrict, or render or declare unserviceable any aircraft landing strip located on federal land under their respective jurisdictions unless: (1) the action has been approved by the head of the aviation department of the state in which the aircraft landing strip is located; (2) the Secretary publishes notice of the proposed action in the Federal Register, including notice that the action would permanently close, restrict, or render or declare unserviceable the aircraft landing strip; (3) the Secretary provides for a 90-day public comment period on the action's proposed action; and (4) the Secretary and the head of the aviation department of the state in which the affected aircraft landing strip is located have taken into consideration any comments received.

Requires the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to: (1) establish a national policy for governing backcountry aviation issues related to the management of federal land under their jurisdiction; and (2) require officials with jurisdiction over such land to adhere to such policy.

Medicare and Medicaid Hospital Self-Referral Amendments of 1996 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a discharge plan to:  (1) specify the qualified provider that may provide post-hospital care, and identify (in a form and manner specified by the Secretary) any provider (to whom the individual is referred) in which the hospital has a disclosable financial interest (as specified by the Secretary) or which has such an interest in the hospital; and (2) identify any provider (to whom the individual is referred) in which the hospital has a disclosable financial interest or which has such an interest in the hospital in the same manner as such requirements apply to individuals entitled to benefits under title XVIII (Medicare) in the same manner as such requirements apply to individuals entitled to benefits under title XVIII (Medicare) with respect to discharge planning processes. 
Requires the Secretary to make public certain information disclosed to the Secretary pursuant to this Act.
