Veterans Acquiring Community Care Expect Safe Services Act of 2017 or the Veterans ACCESS Act (Sec. 2) This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to deny or revoke the eligibility of a health care provider to provide non-VA health care services to veterans if the VA determines that the health care provider: (1) was removed from employment with the VA due to conduct that violates a policy of the VA relating to the delivery of safe and appropriate health care; (2) violated certain requirements related to a medical license; (3) had a VA credential revoked and the grounds for such revocation impacts the VA's ability to deliver safe and appropriate health care; or (4) violated a law for which a term of imprisonment of more than one year may be imposed.  The VA may deny, revoke, or suspend such eligibility if necessary to protect the health, safety, or welfare of veterans and the VA shall report on the implementation by the VA of this Act.  The Government Accountability Office shall report on the VA's review of the status of health care providers in the Department and the history of VA employment with the VA.

Scenic Columbia Gorge Restoration Act of 2017 This bill directs the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to begin proposing response activities for lands within the National Scenic Area (NSA) adversely impacted by a catastrophic event to address conditions caused or exacerbated by the event.  USDA shall allow 30 days for public scoping and comment regarding a NSA response activity, 15 days for filing an objection, and 15 days for the agency response to the objection.  USDA shall implement an environmental assessment for a NSA response activity and a categorical exclusion for a response activity that does not exceed 10,000 acres within the NSA and includes lands that are visible from key viewing areas.  USDA consultations with affected species and designated critical habitat shall not be required if the USDA determines that a response activity is not likely to adversely affect listed species or designated critical habitat.  The bill prohibits restraining orders, preliminary injunctions, and injunctions pending appeal from being issued in the U.S. Court of the Court of the President. Amounts in the special fund established pursuant to the Act of June 9, 1930, shall be available to USDA for response activities.  USDA shall

Treatment of Indian Tribal Natural Resource Income Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt from the Federal income tax income derived from a natural resources-related activity by a member of an Indian tribe, or from a qualified Indian entity, any income earned by that tribe directly or indirectly from a natural resources-related activity by a qualified Indian entity.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish a five-year selection commission to recommend individuals to the President for appointment as Commissioner of Revenue.

Government Audit Reform Act of 2010 - Directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to monitor the risk, cost-benefit, efficiency, and effectiveness of the implementation by federal agencies of this Act by: (1) evaluating such implementation governmentwide; and (2) identifying additional guidance and resources necessary to improve such implementation.

Requires the Director to submit to the House Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the Senate Comptroller General a report that includes the findings of such an evaluation.

Directs the Director to designate an office in the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) or another federal entity to act on behalf of the Director to: (1) oversee the implementation of the single audit and the program-specific audit under the OMB audit provisions of this Act, to identify simplified alternatives for achieving the purposes of the Single Audit Act of 1984 and the Single Audit Act Amendments of 1996; and (2) report to Congress on the results of the evaluation.

Directs the Director to evaluate the implementation of the recommendations made to OMB by the President's Council on Integrity and Efficiency in the OMB report to Congress.
Andrew Prior Act - Amends the Truth in Lending Act to discharge private educational loans in the event of the death of the borrower.

Critical Infrastructure Protection Act or CIPA - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to: (1) include in national planning scenarios the threat of electromagnetic pulses caused by intentional means, including acts of terrorism; and (2) conduct outreach to educate owners and operators of critical infrastructure, emergency planners, and emergency responders at all levels of government of the threat of such events.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Under Secretary for Science and Technology, and in consultation with other relevant agencies and departments of the federal government and relevant owners and operators of critical infrastructure, to conduct research and development to mitigate the consequences of such events.

Directs the Secretary, acting through the Under Secretary for Science and Technology, to conduct research and development to: (1) include an objective scientific analysis of the risks to critical infrastructures from a range of EMP events; (2) determine the critical national security assets and vital civic utilities and infrastructures at risk from such events; (3) an evaluation of emergency planning and response technologies that would address the findings and recommendations of experts; and (4) an analysis of technology options that are available to improve the resiliency of critical infrastructure

Professional's Access To Health Workforce Integration Act of 2015 This bill authorizes the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to award grants to eligible entities to carry out activities related to providing health services to internationally- educated health professionals, including training, education, and the provision of resources and support.

Veterans Benefits Administration Improvement Act of 2001 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit to the congressional veterans' committees a comprehensive plan for the improvement of the processing of veterans' compensation claims.

Healthy Schools Partnerships Act of 2010 - Amends the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to direct the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a demonstration project to make grants to local academic experts, registered dietitians, or other nutrition professionals, community partners, and local schools to test and evaluate innovative models to improve nutrition education, student decision making, and healthy school environments.

Gives grant priority to entities that demonstrate: (1) a severe need to improve the school environment; (2) commitment to make in-kind or cash contributions; and (3) ability to measure results.

Small Business Investment Improvement Act of 1999 - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to provide for the Small Business Administration (SBA) Program of Small Business Administration (SBA) funds to be used for the investment of small businesses.

Pro-Growth Budgeting Act of 2012 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 (CBA) to require the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to prepare for each major legislation report of the Congress, including the budgetary effects of bills or resolutions, in a supplement to estimates prepared under this Act.

Requires such analysis to describe the potential economic impact of the applicable major bill or resolution on major economic variables, including real gross domestic product, business investment, the capital stock, employment, interest rates, and labor supply.

Requires such analysis to describe the potential fiscal effects of the bill or resolution on revenue feedback, changes in revenue resulting from changes in economic growth, and revenue and debt effects from changes in economic growth.

Requires the CBO to submit to the congressional budget committees a supplemental projection, assuming extension of current tax policy for the fiscal year beginning on October 1 of that year with a projected extension of current tax policy.

Federal Land Freedom Act of 2015 This bill authorizes a state that has established a leasing, permitting, and regulatory program to: (1) transfer responsibility for leasing, permitting, and regulating oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy development to the state, and (2) seek to transfer responsibility for leasing, permitting, and regulating oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy development to the state to the federal government.  States may lease, permit, and regulate the exploration and development of oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy on federal land in lieu of the federal government.  States may also seek to transfer responsibility for leasing, permitting, and regulating oil, natural gas, and other forms of energy development to the federal government to the state.  States may collect royalties or other revenues in an amount equal to the amount of royalties or revenues that would have been collected if the lease or permit had been issued by the federal government.  States must deposit revenues collected from leases or permits in the same federal account in which revenues would have been deposited if the lease or permit had been issued by the federal government.

Pink Tax Repeal Act - Makes it unlawful for any person to sell or offer for sale in interstate commerce any two consumer products from the same manufacturer that are substantially similar if such products are priced differently based on the gender of the individuals for whose use the products are intended or marketed.

Provides for enforcement, including by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), by the same means as though all applicable terms and provisions of the Federal Trade Commission Act were incorporated into this Act.

Declares this Act inapplicable to certain actions brought by a state attorney general against a defendant named in a complaint of the FTC for violation of this Act.

Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act - Allows Forest Service employees, the Bureau of Land Management of the Department of the Interior, the National Park Service, the Fish and Wildlife Service, the Bureau of Indian Affairs, and the Bureau of Reclamation of the Department of the Interior to compete for a permanent appointment in the competitive service under their merit promotion procedures if: (1) such individual was appointed initially under open, competitive examination to the time-limited appointment; (2) the employee has served under 1 or more time-limited appointments before receiving an intervening break of two or more years; and (3) the employee's performance has been at an acceptable level of performance throughout the period or periods (as the case may be) referred to in clause (2).

Allows such employees to choose to become career-conditional or non-course-conditional employees upon their completion of their service requirements for career tenure.

Amends the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act of 1986 to require the owner or operator of a facility to notify the emergency response and community response compartments of the following entities: (1) the facility operator, if established pursuant to the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980 (CERCLA); and (2) the state emergency response commission or a state agency authorized to receive notification of a release under the Clean Water Act from a facility. Requires notification within 1 hour of having such knowledge.

Amends CERCLA to extend the requirement for notification to the National Response Center (NRC) of a release under the Clean Water Act from a facility. Requires notification within 1 hour of having such knowledge.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide that, if a common trust fund transfers substantially all of its assets to one or more regulated investment companies in exchange for stock in such company or companies to which such assets are transferred, and such stock is distributed by such fund to participants in such fund in exchange solely for their interests in such fund, no gain or loss shall be recognized by any participant in such fund by reason of such transfer or distribution, and no gain or loss shall be recognized by any participant by reason of such exchange.

Nuclear Power Plant Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 to direct the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to initiate a proceeding to revise its regulations to ensure that each utilization facility licensed under the Act can withstand and adequately respond to: (1) an earthquake, tsunami, strong storm, or other event that threatens a major impact to the facility; (2) a loss of the primary operating power source for at least 14 days; and (3) a loss of the primary backup power source for at least 72 hours.

Requires the NRC to provide for: (1) a requirement that each licensed utilization facility, including any onsite spent nuclear fuel facilities, be equipped with resilient containment, safety, and diagnostic systems sufficient to withstand the circumstances described in this Act; (2) a requirement that licensees have at least 14 days worth of emergency power system fuel onsite with which to power the licensed facility in the event of a loss of the primary operating power source; (3) a requirement that licensees develop and obtain approved plan approval for sufficient additional fuel or batteries in the event of a long duration loss of operating power or total station blackout; (

Peer Support Communities of Recovery Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to allow a national nonprofit entity, through FY2023, to award grants to recovery community organizations to establish regional technical assistance centers to provide regional technical assistance for: (1) building blocks for substance use disorder recovery; and (2) recovery community organizations serving prevention, treatment, recovery, payor, faith-based, and criminal justice stakeholders in the implementation of local addiction and recovery initiatives.  Eligible entities may award grants to recovery community organizations in the following circumstances: (1) for services and allow such organizations to use grant funds to establish regional technical assistance centers; and (2) in connection with the establishment of regional technical assistance centers, for purposes of establishing regional technical assistance for the development of regional addiction recovery services.  Eligible entities may also award grants to recovery community organizations to establish recovery community centers to provide recovery community organizations with regional technical assistance for: (1) implementation of regionally driven, peer-delivered addiction recovery support services, or (2) establishment of recovery community organizations.

Child Care Criminal Background Check Act of 2009 - Amends the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to require a child care provider who is licensed by the state or receives funds under the Child Care and Development Block Grant Program to obtain a comprehensive criminal background check of each employee who provides child care services, each applicant for employment to provide such services, and each family child care provider who provides or applies to provide such services.

Requires the State to make the results of such check available to such provider and to such employee or applicant.

Volunteer Emergency Services Recruitment and Retention Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) allow bona fide volunteers a deferred compensation plan (a plan paid by volunteers to compensate for services performed by such volunteers); and (2) exclude from the definition of "eligible deferred compensation plan" a plan paying solely length of service awards to a volunteer volunteer.

Medicaid Reform and Personal Responsibility Act of 2017 This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require states to apply work requirements for able-bodied adults without dependents to a state Medicaid program to provide services for such adults without dependents. Able-bodied adult without dependents shall not receive medical assistance under Medicaid if the able-bodied adult without dependents: (1) refuse to register as employed or as unemployed, (2) refuse to accept an offer of employment, (3) refuse to use a paid-upomerential or other employment arrangement, (4) refuse to satisfy an application requirement to work beyond 12 consecutive months in a manner prescribed by the state, (5) refuse to accept an offer of employment, and (6) refuse to provide the state with sufficient information to determine the adult's employment status or the job availability.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Commerce to develop and implement a comprehensive program for fish screens, fish passage devices, and other measures agreed to by local interests and relevant federal agencies for water diversions by local governmental entities in Oregon, Washington, Montana, and Idaho that provide water supplies.

Randy Barrett Act - Amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to direct the Commissioner of Social Security, in any case in which an individual is terminally ill and is not entitled to benefits based on disability, to waive the application of the waiting period and, notwithstanding the waiting period of a terminally ill individual, to be entitled to OASDI benefits for each month during which the individual is under a disability.

DMZ War Veterans Recognition Act of 2006 - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service, to place a plaque at the Korean War Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., to commemorate the sacrifices of those soldiers who served, were wounded, or were killed from 1953 until the present in defense of the Republic of Korea.

Hydrographic Services Improvement Act Amendments of 2008 - (Sec. 3) Amends the Hydrographic Services Improvement Act of 1998 to: (1) authorize the Administrator of the U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey to acquire, maintain, and operate a Joint Hydrographic Institute; (2) authorize appropriations for the Administrator to create, support, and maintain a Joint Hydrographic Institute; (3) authorize appropriations for the Administrator to contract for hydrographic surveys, including leasing or time chartering of vessels, and operate such surveys; (4) authorize the Administrator to operate a geodetic survey vessel owned by the United States and operated by the Administration to carry out hydrographic functions; (5) authorize the Administrator to operate a short title to the Coast and Geodetic Survey Act to exist; and (6) add a title to the Act that is not currently applicable to the Coast and Geodetic Survey of the United States.

Community Gardening and Nutrition Act of 2014 - Amends the Domestic Volunteer Service Act of 1973 to direct the Director of the Department of the Interior to establish a Community Garden Pilot Program to carry out the work described in the Act's title I (Community Gardens for Health and Nutritional Benefits) part A (Fruits and Vegetables) (Farm and Garden) program. Requires the Director to give priority to: (1) volunteers with experience in health, nutrition, and gardening; (2) projects located in varied geographic regions; and (3) selecting a balance of urban and rural projects.  Authorizes appropriations for the Program through FY2014.

Federal Internship Improvement Act - Directs the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to: (1) make publicly available on the Internet the names, contact information, and relevant skills of individuals who have completed or are nearing completion of an internship program; and (2) conduct an exit interview with each agency employee who completes an internship program. Directs OPM to: (1) annually submit to OPM a report assessing such program; and (2) annually submit to Congress a report summarizing the information submitted.

Concussion Treatment and Care Tools Act of 2010 or the ConTACT Act of 2010 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to establish: (1) concussion management guidelines that address the prevention, identification, treatment, and management of concussions in school-aged children, including standards for such children to return to play after experiencing such a concussion; and (2) a grant to states for the collection by target entities of information on the incidence and prevalence of concussions among school-aged children attending or participating in entities and the implementation of the guidelines, the implementation by target entities of the guidelines, and the funding implementation by target entities of the guidelines.

Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to states for: (1) providing for the collection by target entities of information on the incidence and prevalence of concussions among school-aged children attending or participating in entities; (2) adopting, disseminating, and ensuring the implementation by target entities of the guidelines; and (3) funding implementation by target entities of the guidelines. Requires states receiving such grants to utilize, to the extent practicable, applicable expertise and services offered by high school sports associations, youth sports associations, athletic

Hunter and Farmer Protection Act of 2015 This bill amends the Migratory Bird Treaty Act to prohibit the Department of the Interior from allowing any person to take any migratory game bird by baiting or on or over any area on which salt, grain, or other feed has been placed, exposed, deposited, or distributed, if the person knows or reasonably should know that the area is a baited area.  The bill defines "normal agricultural practice" as any practice in one annual growing season that: (1) is carried out in order to produce a marketable crop, including planting, harvest, post-harvest, or soil conservation practices; and (2) is recommended for the successful harvest of a given crop by the applicable state department of fish and wildlife.

International Money Transfer Disclosure Act - Directs the appropriate federal agencies to jointly prescribe regulations that require any financial institution or money transmitting business initiating an international money transfer to: (1) disclose fees charged to the recipient, including exchange rate or currency conversion fees; and (2) provide good faith efforts to resolve any related issues.

Requires such disclosures to be in English and in the same language, if other than English, as the language principally used by the financial institution or money transmitting business to advertise, solicit, or negotiate at the office of the institution or business at which the international money transfer is initiated.

Defines "appropriate federal agency" for the purpose of this Act to include the appropriate federal banking agency, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC).

Mental Health First Act of 2013 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Administrator of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to award grants to states, political subdivisions, Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and nonprofit private entities to initiate and sustain mental health first aid training programs.  Requires such programs to be designed to: (1) train individuals in the categories of emergency services personnel and other first responders, police officers and other law enforcement personnel, teachers and school administrators, human resources professionals, and faith community leaders; (2) include a core live training course for such individuals on the skills, resources, and knowledge to assist such individuals in crisis to connect with appropriate local mental health care services; (3) train on mental health resources, including the location of community mental health centers and the availability of trained teachers and school administrators; and (4) include continuing education and updated training for individuals in the categories listed above.  Requires such programs to be designed to: (1) train individuals in the categories listed in the previous section; and (2) include a core live training course for such individuals on the skills, resources, and knowledge to assist such individuals in crisis to connect with

Mandate Prevention Act of 2010 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to make any bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report that would increase the direct costs of federal private sector mandates by an amount that causes the specified thresholds (defined as the amount appropriated for each fiscal year for such mandates included in the bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report) to be exceeded, unless: (1) the bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report provides new budget authority or new entitlement authority in the House of Representatives or direct spending authority in the Senate for each fiscal year for such mandates included in the bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report; or (2) the bill, joint resolution, amendment, motion, or conference report includes an authorization for appropriations in an amount equal to or exceeding such threshold and identifies a specific dollar amount of the direct costs of such mandate for each year up to 10 years during which such mandate is in effect.

Requires the responsible federal agency to determine whether there are insufficient appropriations for that fiscal year to provide for the direct costs of such mandate and to notify Congress of such determination and submit a statement

Free File Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of the Treasury to continue operating the IRS Free File Program as established by the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and published in the Federal Register on November 4, 2002.  The IRS Free File Program shall continue to provide free commercial-type online individual income tax preparation and electronic filing services to the lowest 70% of taxpayers by income. The program shall continue to make available to all taxpayers a basic, online electronic fillable forms utility. The program shall continue to work cooperatively with the private sector to provide the free individual income tax preparation and electronic filing services described in this bill. The IRS Free File Program shall continue to make available to all taxpayers (without regard to income) a basic, online electronic fillable forms utility. The program shall continue to work cooperatively with the private sector to enhance and expand the use of the program to provide needed benefits to the taxpayer while reducing the cost of processing returns. Nothing in this bill is intended to impact the continuity of services provided under Taxpayer Assistance Centers, Tax Counseling for the Elderly, and Volunteer Income Tax Assistance programs.

Presidential Library Donation Reform Act of 2016 (Sec. 2) This bill requires presidential archival fundraising organizations to submit quarterly reports to the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) no later than 15 days after the end of the requirement period.  The Archivist of the United States must publish such information on the National Archives website within 30 days after each quarterly filing, with the information subject to a fee or other access charge in a downloadable database.  The bill also prohibits the inclusion of any information submitted that is false or willfully exclude material that is not monetary or in-kind.  The bill also prohibits contributors from: (1) submitting false material information, or (2) omitting material information that is false or willfully exclude material from inclusion in the National Archives.  The Archivist must: (1) publish such information on the National Archives website within 30 days after each quarterly filing, with the information subject to a fee or other access charge in a downloadable database, and (2) promulgate regulations to carry out this bill.

Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Promotion Act of 1998 - Amends the Migratory Bird Hunting and Conservation Stamp Act to: (1) authorize the Secretary of the Interior to use from receipts from the sale of migratory bird hunting and conservation stamps an amount not to exceed $1 million for each of FY 1999 through 2003 for the promotion of additional stamp sales; (2) include in each annual report to the Secretary of the Interior the statement of all expenditures; and (3) provide a copy to the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission, the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate, and the Committee on Resources of the House of Representatives.

Renewable Energy Investment Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to extend through 2015: (1) the tax credit for investment in renewable energy; (2) the tax credit for investment in alternative fuels; (3) the tax credit for investment in energy property; (4) the tax credit for investment in advanced biofuels research; and (5) the tax credit for investment in biofuels development and demonstration.

National Reconstruction Study Area Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the National Park Service, to complete a study of the National Park System (NPS) unit of the National Park System (NPS) to assess the suitability and feasibility of designating the NPS unit as a unit of the National Park System.

Directs the Attorney General to provide, in accordance with this Act, for the granting of posthumous citizenship to a person who died as a result of an injury incurred in one or more of the events described in the preceding clauses, on September 10, 2001, the hijacking of American Airlines flight 11, the hijacking of U.S. 77, and the hijacking of American Airlines flight 93 on September 11, 2001. Provides that any person who died as a result of an injury incurred while assisting in the emergency response to an event shall be considered to have died as a result of an injury incurred in such event. Waives the requirement that a person demonstrate an understanding of the English language or a knowledge and understanding of the principles and form of government in order to be naturalized, unless otherwise provided by this Act.

Strengthening Background Checks Act of 2013 - Amends the NICS Improvement Amendments Act of 2007 to increase mandatory minimum penalties for states that do not make certain data available to the national instant criminal background check system.  Directs the Attorney General to withhold 10% of mandatory penalty amounts from a state that fail to comply with the requirements of this Act or provide less than 90% of the records required under the Act. Allows the Attorney General to waive such requirements for one year if the state provides substantial evidence that it is making a reasonable effort to comply.  Requires the Attorney General to withhold 5% of the amount that would otherwise be allocated to a state under the Act for each such one-year period. Requires the Attorney General to withhold 10% of the amount that would otherwise be allocated to a state for each such one-year period if the state provides evidence that it is making a reasonable effort to comply. Requires the Attorney General to withhold 5% of the amount that would otherwise be allocated to a state for each such one-year period if the state provides evidence that it is making a reasonable effort to comply.

Freedom to Fish Act - Amends the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act to prohibit any fishery management plan prepared by a Regional Fishery Management Council or the Secretary of Commerce from establishing areas closed to recreational fishing unless: (1) there is a clear indication that recreational fishermen are the cause of a specific conservation problem and that less severe conservation measures will not adequately provide for conservation and management of the affected stocks of fish; (2) the closed area regulation includes specific measurable criteria to determine the conservation benefit of the closed area on such fish and provides a timetable for periodic review of the continued need for the closed area; (3) the closed area is no larger than that which is supported by the best available scientific information; or (4) provision is made to reopen the closed area to recreational fishing whenever any such condition that was the basis of the closure no longer exists.

State Court Interpreter Grant Program Act - Directs the Administrator of the Office of Justice Programs of the Department of Justice to make grants to States to develop and implement programs to assist individuals with limited English proficiency to access and understand State court proceedings in which they are a party.

Social Security Caregiver Credit Act of 2018 This bill amends title II (Old Age, Survivors and Disability Insurance) (OASDI) of the Social Security Act to allow an individual who is a dependent relative of a deceased individual to be paid a wage for providing OASDI support during the month in which the individual was engaged for at least 80 hours in providing care to a dependent relative without monetary compensation for up to five years of such service. The bill defines "dependent relative" as a child, grandchild, niece, or nephew of an individual who: (1) is a child, grandchild, niece, or nephew of the individual who is either a child to which the individual or the individual's spouse or domestic partner is standing inloco, who is under the age of 12, or a child, grandchild, niece, or nephew of the individual who is a parent, aunt, or uncle; or (2) is a child, grandchild, niece, or nephew of the individual who is a child to which the individual is either a child to which the individual's spouse or domestic partner is standing inloco, a

Sexual Assault Prosecution Act of 2002 - Amends the federal criminal code to: (1) limit the categories of sexual offenses to those committed in violation of the prohibition against discrimination in favor of women in the Armed Forces; and (2) require the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation to develop a plan to grant voluntary awards to States to facilitate DNA analysis of all casework evidence of unsolved crimes.

Over-the-Counter Hearing Aid Act of 2017 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to regulate over-the-counter hearing aids. Currently, FDA regulation of hearing aids is limited to the use of air conduction hearing aids. This bill expands the hearing aids category to include hearing aids that are intended to be used by adults over the age of 18. The FDA must promulgate regulations to establish a category of hearing aids that meets specified safety and efficacy requirements and to make certain disclosures to consumers.

Red Cliffs Desert Reserve Completion Act - Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to pay James Doyle, out of money not otherwise appropriated, a sum of money representing the amount to which James Doyle may be entitled in order to make James Doyle whole for any damages and losses sustained by James Doyle by reason of the Federal Government's taking of approximately 2,000 acres of his land located in the St. George area of Utah, now designated as the Red Cliffs Desert Reserve.

Teaching Children to Save Lives Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Education to carry out a program under which the Secretary is authorized to award grants to eligible local educational agencies or targeted schools for implementing nationally recognized CPR and AED training courses. Allows grantees to use such grants to obtain: (1) training individuals in CPR and AED skills and instruction; (2) obtaining printed informational or instructional materials; (3) obtaining manikins; (4) obtaining AED training devices; and (5) obtaining other equipment as determined appropriate by the Secretary.

Comprehensive Problem Gambling Act of 2011 - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Administrator of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to establish and implement programs for the prevention, treatment, and research of pathological and other problem gambling.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Administrator, to carry out a national campaign to increase knowledge and raise awareness within the general public with respect to problem gambling issues.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Administrator, to carry out activities that include augmenting and supporting existing national campaigns and producing and placing public service announcements.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Administrator, to: (1) coordinate the voluntary donation of, and administer, resources to assist in the implementation of new programs and the augmentation and support of existing national campaigns to provide national strategies for dissemination of information to prevent problem gambling; (2) encourage media outlets to provide information about the prevention of problem gambling; and (3) target radio and television audiences of events including sporting and gambling events.

Requires the Secretary, acting through the Administrator, to consider the recommendations of the National Gambling Impact Study Commission for a

Welfare Improvement Act of 1997 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to prohibit a State from using TANF assistance for a minor child born to a recipient or a person who received such assistance at any time during the ten-month period ending with the birth of the child.  Prohibits a State from providing cash benefits for a minor child born to a family with no other children.  Prohibits a State from:  (1) requiring a child to be given up to work in order to receive TANF benefits; or (2) requiring a State to provide a child with a work-related certificate if the child refuses to engage in work required in accordance with TANF assistance. 
Prohibits a State from:  (1) reducing the amount of TANF assistance otherwise payable to the family; or (2) terminating TANF assistance for any individual who refuses to engage in work required in accordance with TANF assistance. 
Prohibits a State from providing TANF payments to a State unless the State:  (1) establishes and maintains a reasonable program for randomly testing an individual in

Requires the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation to establish and maintain a national clearinghouse for information on incidents of crime and terrorism: (1) committed against or directed at any animal enterprise; (2) committed against or directed at any commercial activity because of the perceived impact or effect of such activity on the environment; or (3) committed against or directed at any person because of such connection with or support of any enterprise or activity described in clause 1.
Requires the clearinghouse to: (1) accept, collect, and maintain information on such incidents; (2) collate and index such information for purposes of cross-referencing; and (3) provide information to assist in the investigation of such incidents.
Requires the Director to carry out the Director's responsibilities under this Act in cooperation with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms.

Gun Victim Compensation Act - Amends the Gun Victim Compensation Act to provide that any person who sells, delivers, or otherwise transfers a firearm or a handgun to a person who the transferor knows or has reasonable cause to believe is a juvenile shall be liable for damages caused by a discharge of the transferred firearm by the transferee.

Provides that nothing in this Act shall be construed to limit or have any other effect on any other cause of action available to any person.

Small Business Relief and Job Creation Act  This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an employer who employs: (1) a qualified small business candidate who is eligible for the unemployment compensation program to treat such candidate as a member of a targeted group for purposes of the employer's general employment tax credit for 2018 and 2019, and (2) a qualified unemployed individual who begins work for such employer in 2019 or 2020, subject to the employer's modified employment with such individual.  The bill defines "eligible small business" as any person who: (1) is a qualified small business candidate who is eligible for the unemployment compensation program for 2018 and 2019, and (2) employs not more than 100 full-time employees during the 1-year period beginning with the day the individual begins work.  The bill defines "eligible unemployed individual" as any individual who is a qualified unemployed individual who: (1) is a qualified individual who is not employed for a 35-hour period, and (2) is not currently employed and is not currently in the targeted group for which the employer pays unemployment compensation.

Stop the Sale of Murderabilia Act of 2013 - Amends the federal criminal code to impose a fine and/or imprisonment for any person who knowingly deposits for mailing or delivery, or knowingly causes to be delivered by mail, any property, article, or object, with intent that such property, article, or object be placed in interstate or foreign commerce.  Sets forth a six-month waiting period before any other term of imprisonment may be imposed.  Sets forth civil and criminal forfeiture penalties for the forfeiture of real or personal property used or intended to be used to commit, facilitate, or promote the commission of an offense punishable by imprisonment for a criminal offense.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to implement a process to provide eligible organizations and individuals expedited access to federal lands to conduct good Samaritan search-and-recovery missions.

MMA Territorial Equity for Low-Income Individuals Act of 2004 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for the equitable treatment of the residents of territories under the Medicare prescription drug program (PDP-3).

Amends the Medicare Prescription Drug, Improvement, and Modernization Act of 2003 to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to request the Institute of Medicine of the National Academy of Sciences to undertake a study that examines the access of Medicare beneficiaries in such territories to prescription drugs during each of three periods: (1) before mma; (2) discount card and transitional assistance; and (3) implementation of the PDP-3 program.

Volunteer First Responder Housing Act - Requires a qualified volunteer first responder who: (1) is a bona fide volunteer performing qualified services for an eligible employer; (2) has volunteered for at least two continuous years for an eligible employer; and (3) during each of the two years has met the minimum requirements for active membership and has volunteered for at least 200 hours, and has certified as a firefighter or other responder in the state, unit, or Indian tribe in which the individual is serving as volunteer.

Requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to amend: (1) the relevant federal regulations to provide that a qualified volunteer first responder qualifies as a firefighter or emergency medical technician for purposes of the Good Neighbor Next Door Sales Program; and (2) the relevant state, local, and tribal housing and urban planning regulations to provide that a qualified volunteer first responder shall submit to the Secretary a verification letter from the head of the eligible employer for which the qualified volunteer first responder volunteers, which shall include the date on which the responder joined the employer as a volunteer and attest to the Secretary that the responder continuously served as a volunteer for the 2-year period

Requires the Secretary of Transportation to publish a supplement to the major rehabilitation report for the Herbert Hoover Dike system, approved by the Chief of Engineers in November 2000.

Directs the Secretary, in May 2007, to: (1) extend the deadline for the designation of a major project for navigation, Saco River, Maine, authorized by the Act of June 3, 1896; and (2) publish a report on the identification of additional risks associated with flood events at the system.

Includes the section 107 minor rehabilitation report of the Illinois Waterway project in the South Fork of the South Branch of the Chicago River.
