(2) Thence north 1 degree, 32 minutes, 31 seconds west, bearing based on the Illinois State Plane Coordinate System, NAD 83 east zone, along the west line

Forest Roads-Community Right-To-Know Act - Requires the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture (USDA) to discuss progress on implementing the Forest Roads-Community Right-To-Know Act, which requires the Department of the Interior and the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to develop and implement plans for the potential permanent closure of forest roads on federal lands that are either in or adjacent to federal lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) or that are within units of the National Forest System (NFS). Requires such plans to include project proposals that will result in the permanent closure of such roads. Requires such plans to also provide information regarding: (1) the state and local government officials involved; (2) the road closures and associated traffic patterns and volumes; and (3) the public notice and comment requirements of this Act. Prohibits the implementation of such plans, except for plans implemented during the fiscal year in which this Act is enacted, unless the Secretary and the appropriate state and local government officials have met to discuss the implementation of the Act.

Estate and Gift Tax Phase-Out Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to phase out the estate and gift tax credit. 
Repeals the Federal transfer tax credit. 
Repeals the Federal gift tax credit.

Common Sense Campaign Reform Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 100 percent of the portion of a congressional campaign contribution that does not exceed $25.  Reduces the ceiling on contributions to candidates by multiplicity of political parties. 
Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit a multicandidate political committee (CIPC) from establishing, maintaining, financing, or controlling a political committee other than the principal political committee of the candidate. 
Requires each CIPC to include in its report the name and mailing address of the person making the contribution, the occupation and the name of the employer of the individual, and the name of the entity that establishes the fund. 
Requires any separate segregated fund under the Act that is a multicandidate political committee to include in its name the name of the entity that establishes the fund.

Developing Resources Immediately and Long-Term through Leases on Our Nation's Offshore Waters Act of 2009 or the DRILL NOW Act of 2009 - Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to: (1) authorize the President to withdraw any lands of the outer Continental Shelf from disposition for exploration, development, or production of oil and gas, except as the President determines necessary for national security purposes; and (2) authorize the Secretary of the Interior to issue leases authorizing the conduct of oil and natural gas exploration and extraction activities in any area within 50 miles of the state's coastline and within the lateral seaward boundaries of the state extended.

Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to deposit 30% of the qualified revenues in a separate account in the Treasury, which shall be known as the Clean and Alternative Energy Fund and be available to the Secretary of Energy for making grants for research and development of clean and alternative energy. Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to pay to each such state a portion of such amount that is proportional to the portion of the lease tract that is so located with respect to the state, and that have enacted a statute that establishes a plan for expenditure of

Federal Reserve Board Civil Rights Compliance Act of 1999 - Requires the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to post and keep posted in conspicuous places upon its premises where such notices to employees and applicants for employment are customarily posted and at such other places as the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission may determine, a notice to be prepared or approved by the Commission setting forth: (1) quotations from or summaries of the pertinent provisions of title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and (2) information pertinent to the rights and procedures applicable to employees of, and applicants for employment by, the Board.

Neighborhood Security Act of 2003 - Authorizes the Attorney General to award one or more grants to nonprofit organizations and professional associations to develop and improve Neighborhood Watches throughout the Nation. Requires such grants to be used to: (1) complete a survey of Neighborhood Watches that identifies such programs by zip code; (2) establish a national registry of Neighborhood Watch leaders, with appropriate contact information, and a model program for educating community members about the prevention of terrorism and crime, responding to terrorism and crime, and achieving broad community involvement in activities; (3) use the best practices identified in the Neighborhood Watches to create a manual for communities seeking to establish a new Neighborhood Watch or improve an existing Neighborhood Watch; and (4) engage in outreach and respond to inquiries in order to disseminate information about the benefits of effective Neighborhood Watches, the means to establish new Neighborhood Watches, and the means to improve existing Neighborhood Watches.

Education Savings Account and School Excellence Act of 1999 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) increase the amount of qualified educational expenses for which the tax-free and exclusionary provisions of the tax deduction apply; (2) allow a tax deduction for the expenses of attending elementary and secondary school; and (3) allow a tax exclusion for the expenses of attending a public, private, or religious school.

Restoring the Partnership for County Health Care Costs Act of 2015 This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to modify the requirements for eligibility for Medicaid, Medicare, SSI, and CHIP. Specifically, the bill requires a county to provide to eligible individuals in custody a monetary benefit of up to $1,250 for any offense under the criminal code that results in a charge of a mental illness. Additionally, the bill requires the inmate of a public institution to provide to eligible individuals in custody a monetary benefit of up to $1,250 for any offense under the criminal code that results in a charge of a mental illness.

Telephone Call Privacy Act of 1999 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to revise the requirements relating to the use and disclosure of customer proprietary network information relating to a telecommunications carrier. 
Authorizes a telecommunications carrier that receives or obtains customer proprietary network information by virtue of its provision of a telecommunications service to use, disclose, or permit access to customer proprietary network information that identifies a customer as follows:  (1) in the provision of the service from which such information is derived and services necessary to the provision of such service, including the publishing of directories; and (2) in the case of the use of such information by the carrier for the provision of another of its products or services to the customer, only if the carrier provides the customer a clear and conspicuous notice meeting the requirements of this Act with respect to such information and the customer's written notice approving the use, disclosure, or access of such information. 
Requires a telecommunications carrier that receives or obtains such information by the same manner and in the same manner and in the same manner and in the same manner and in the same manner and in the same manner and in the same manner and in the same manner and in the same manner and in the

Internet of Things Consumer Tips to Improve Personal Security Act of 2017 or the IOT Consumer TIPS Act of 2017 This bill requires the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to develop voluntary educational cybersecurity resources for consumers relating to the practices of consumers with respect to the protection and use of consumer devices, including citing evidence of consumer attitudes and expectations. The resources must be technology-neutral and include guidance, best practices, and advice for consumers to protect against, mitigate, and recover from cybersecurity threats or security vulnerabilities. The FTC must ensure that the resources developed are available to and readily accessible by the public on its website. The FTC must review and update the resources in collaboration with industry stakeholders to address changes in cybersecurity threats or security vulnerabilities.

Indian Tribal Development Corporation Feasibility Study Act of 2004 - Amends the Native American Business Development, Trade Promotion, and Tourism Act of 2000 to require the Secretary of Commerce to establish the Tribal Development Corporation Feasibility Study Group (the Group). Sets forth the Group's duties, including to study the feasibility of establishing an Indian Tribal Development Corporation and to submit a report to the congressional tribal and resource committees.

Railroad Hours of Service Act of 2010 - Makes rail employees covered under the Railroad Hours of Service Act of 2010 in effect as of January 1, 2011, and specifies the hours of service for such employees, including those required to work with the same equipment, operate the same engines, and operate the same schedules.

Revises the definition of "yardmaster employee" to: (1) include all work where there is a potential to interact or otherwise come into contact with safety-critical devices or circuits, and (2) include all work where there is a potential to interact or otherwise come into contact with safety-critical devices or circuits as a hazardous work.

Requires the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to prescribe regulations to require all deadhead transportation in excess of a specific number of hours to be counted as time on duty and reset the calendar day clock.

Federal Entrepreneur-in-Residence Act of 2012 - Directs the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to establish a federal entrepreneur-in-residence program to appoint entrepreneurs in the agency of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to carry out the duties of the Office.

Requires the Director of OPM to: (1) give priority to placing entrepreneurs-in-residence across the federal government at separate agencies, and (2) to the extent practicable, not appointing more than 2 entrepreneurs-in-residence to positions in the same agency during the same year.

Requires the Director to: (1) give priority to assisting federal agencies in improving outreach to small business concerns and entrepreneurs, (2) provide recommendations to the head of the agency employing the entrepreneur-in-residence on inefficient or duplicative programs, (3) facilitate meetings and forums to educate small business concerns and entrepreneurs on programs or initiatives of the agency, and (4) provide technical assistance or mentorship to small business concerns and entrepreneurs in accessing agency programs.

Makes an entrepreneur-in-residence subject to specified compensation and basic pay terms.

School-Based Asthma Management Program Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to provide preference to a State that: (1) permits trained personnel of the school to administer epinephrine and asthma-related rescue medications; and (2) maintains a supply of epinephrine in a secure location that is easily accessible to trained personnel of the school for administration of any student of the school reasonably believed to have an asthma diagnosis.

Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to give additional preference to a State that: (1) allows trained personnel of the school to administer epinephrine to any student of the school reasonably believed to have an asthma diagnosis; (2) maintains a supply of epinephrine in a secure location that is easily accessible to trained personnel of the school for administration to any student of the school reasonably believed to have an asthma diagnosis; (3) has in place a plan for having on the premises a school nurse or one or more other individuals who are trained personnel of the school; and (4) has in place a comprehensive school-based asthma management program that includes an asthma education program and a school nurse management system.

Directs the Assistant Secretary for Educational Research and Improvement to submit to the congressional committees a spending plan for activities funded through the Office of Educational Research and Improvement for each fiscal year, prior to the obligational requirement of any funds for the fiscal year.  Requires such plans to be made available to a State, local educational agency (LEA), or private or parochial school, upon the request of the State, LEA, or school, and the use of such tests to establish and implement voluntary national tests for 4th grade English reading and 8th grade mathematics.  Directs the Board to: (1) ensure that the content and standards for the tests are the same as the National Assessment; (2) exercise exclusive authority over any expert panel or advisory committee that will be or is established with respect to the tests; (3) ensure that the tests are linked to the National Assessment to the maximum degree possible; (4) develop test objectives, test specifications, and test methodology; (5) develop policies for test administration; (6) develop procedures for reporting test results; (7) have final authority over the appropriateness of all test items; (8) ensure that all items selected for use on the tests are free from racial, cultural

Tobacco Program Administrative Reform Act of 1998 - Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to estimate the costs to be incurred by the Department of Agriculture (USDA) during the next fiscal year by administering the tobacco quota program under the Agricultural Adjustment Act of 1938, the tobacco price support program, and the crop insurance programs for tobacco and tobacco products.  Requires the Secretary to determine the market share of each tobacco product manufacturer and tobacco product importer during the most recent calendar year and the amount of the assessment payable by each manufacturer or importer for that year.  Establishes the Tobacco Assessment Fund in the Treasury.  Allows the use of such assessments to change the crop insurance premiums assessed to tobacco producers under the Federal Crop Insurance Act relative to other crops.

This bill amends the Delaware and Lehigh National Heritage Corridor Act of 1988 to reauthorize and update the Delaware and Lehigh National Heritage Corridor Act of 1988.  The bill revises the definition of "corridor" for purposes of the Act, including by expanding the definition to include the entirety of the Delaware and Lehigh National Heritage Corridor.  The bill also reauthorizes the National Park Service's (NPS's) Corridor Program through FY2019.

Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area Act of 2015  This bill establishes the Hurricane Sand Dunes National Recreation Area in Utah to provide for: (1) the enhancement of recreational uses, and (2) the use of off-highway vehicles.  The Bureau of Land Management shall: (1) administer the Recreation Area and the proposed exchange parcel, and (2) only allow uses of the Recreation Area that are consistent with the purposes described in this bill.  The exchange authorized under this bill shall be subject to valid existing rights. The value of the federal and non-federal lands to be exchanged shall be determined by appraisals.  The value of the federal and non-federal lands to be exchanged shall be equalized by reducing the acreage of the land to be conveyed or adding additional state land to the non-federal land to be conveyed.  The value of the federal and non-federal lands to be exchanged shall be equalized by reducing the acreage of the non-federal land to be conveyed or adding additional state land to the non-federal land.

Arsenic-Treated Wood Mandatory Labeling Act - Amends the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 to require that each U.S. piece of arsenic-treated wood offered for sale has a specified affixation statement affixed to it, including: (1) "This piece of wood has been treated with arsenic;" (2) "Arsenic exposure through the mishandling of this wood can cause cancer, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea;" (3) "Never burn this wood; doing so will release arsenic into the air;" (4) "To avoid the health risks associated with mishandling arsenic-treated wood, you must wear gloves, goggles, coveralls, and face masks when working with it;" (5) "Wash exposed body areas thoroughly with soap and water after working with arsenic-treated wood;" and (6) "Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after working with arsenic-treated wood." 
Requires the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to submit to Congress an update on the status of any ongoing review of the health risks associated with arsenic exposure.

Broadband Conduit Deployment Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of Transportation (DOT) to require states to evaluate the need for broadband conduit (a type of fiber-optic cable used to connect multiple broadband providers) in certain highway construction projects. If the evaluation identifies an anticipated need in the next 15 years for broadband conduit under the hard surfaces to be constructed project, the conduit shall be installed. DOT must ensure that: (1) an appropriate number of broadband conduits are installed along such highway to accommodate multiple broadband providers, with consideration given to the availability of existing conduits; (2) the size of each conduit is consistent with industry best practices; and (3) hand holes and manholes for fiber-optic cable and a pull tape are placed at a depth consistent with industry best practices. DOT may waive the application of this bill if it determines that such waiver is appropriate with respect to a covered highway construction project based upon: (1) a showing of undue burden; (2) a determination that the installation of broadband conduit beneath hard surfaces to be constructed as part of a covered highway construction project is not necessary based on the

Housing Assistance Authorization Act of 2007 - Authorizes the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to make grants to the Housing Assistance Council for use by such Council to develop the ability and capacity of community-based housing development organizations to undertake community development and affordable housing projects and programs in rural areas. Authorizes such use of such funds to be used by the Housing Assistance Council for: (1) technical and financial assistance to local non-profit organizations to undertake community development and affordable housing projects and programs serving low- and moderate-income households, particularly through organizations located in neighborhoods with substantial populations of Hispanic origin; and (2) such other activities as may be determined by the Secretary and the organizations. Authorizes such use of such funds to provide such other activities as may be determined by the Secretary and the organizations. Authorizes the Secretary to make grants to the Housing Partnership Network to create, sustain, and improve access to affordable housing and community facilities that benefit very low- and moderate-income households and communities. Authorizes such use of such funds to be used by the Network to: (1) make investments, loans, and grants to its member nonprofits that demonstrate expertise in using such funds to leverage additional private capital to build, operate, finance, and sustain affordable housing and related community

Emergency Unemployment Compensation Act of 2003 - Amends the Temporary Extended Unemployment Compensation Act of 2002 to extend the additional weeks of unemployment compensation for individuals who exhausted all other available TEUC amounts before the date of enactment of this Act.

Personal Health Investment Today Act of 2009 or the PHIT Act of 2009 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a medical care tax deduction for up to $1,000 ($2,000 for a joint return or a head of household) of qualified sports and fitness expenses. Defines "qualified sports and fitness expenses" as amounts paid for fitness facility memberships, physical exercise programs, and equipment for a physical exercise or activity program.

Southern New Mexico and El Paso, Texas, Veterans Traumatic Brain Injury Care Improvement Act of 2011 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) to report to Congress on the feasibility and advisability of establishing a polytrauma rehabilitation center or polytrauma network site within a reasonable driving distance of Fort Bayard Medical Center in Grant County, New Mexico, and Holloman Air Force Base.

Directs the Secretary to consider and evaluate various locations for the potential location of a new polytrauma rehabilitation center or polytrauma network site.

Service Dogs for Veterans Act of 2009 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to begin a three-year pilot program to assess the benefits, feasibility, and advisability of using service dogs for the treatment or rehabilitation of veterans with physical or mental injuries or disabilities, including post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Requires the Secretary to provide a service dog to a number of veterans with such injuries or disabilities that is greater than or equal to 200% of the participants required to produce scientifically valid results with respect to assessing the benefits and costs of the use of such dogs for such treatment or rehabilitation.

Upper Mississippi Conservation and River Protection Act of 2012 or the Upper Mississippi CARP Act - Directs the Secretary of the Army, acting through the Chief of Engineers, to study the feasibility of temporarily closing the lock at the Upper St. Anthony Falls Lock and Dam to manage the threat of Asian carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) traveling up the Mississippi River in Minnesota.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) assess the potential impacts, including environmental and economic impacts; (2) conduct a study on the feasibility of implementing control measures at the Dam; (3) study the types of control measures and the potential impacts of nonimaging closure; and (4) conduct a study on the possible consequences of nonimaging closure.

Authorizes the Secretary to close the Dam at the Upper St. Anthony Falls Lock and Dam if the Secretary determines in writing that closure is justified as a method to manage the threat of Asian carp traveling upstream of the Dam.

Requires the Council on Environmental Quality to incorporate the Upper Mississippi River and tributaries, the Minnesota River, and the St. Croix River into the Asian Carp Control Strategy Framework of the Council.

Coordinating Assistance for TANF Recipients Act - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to make grants to states to conduct demonstration projects designed to implement and evaluate strategies to provide coordinated case management to help individuals receiving TANF assistance under state programs receive their full employment and self-sufficiency.

Veterans Comprehensive Hepatitis C Health Care Act - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide a blood test for the Hepatitis C virus to: (1) each veteran who served in the Vietnam era, and is enrolled to receive care under the Hepatitis C virus (HCV) testing program; and (2) any other veteran who requests such test. Requires the Secretary to provide a liver biopsy upon request.  Requires the Secretary to provide a Hepatitis C virus genotype test before beginning treatment of such veterans.  Requires the Secretary to provide increased training options to Department health care personnel.  Requires the Secretary to allocate funds to Department Hepatitis C detection and treatment programs.  Directs the Secretary to develop and implement a standardized Hepatitis C virus testing policy.  Requires the Secretary to establish at least one and no more than three Hepatitis C centers of excellence.

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a program to encourage and assist producers, processors, and other handlers of agricultural commodities to donate such commodities to selected food banks, soup kitchens, and homeless shelters in the United States to assist the homeless and poor.  Authorizes the Secretary to enter into agreements with producers, processors, and other handlers of agricultural commodities who offer to make such commodities available for donation.  Allows local governments to nominate food banks, soup kitchens, and homeless shelters for such program.  Requires the Secretary to review submitted plans and to select food banks, soup kitchens, and homeless shelters based on the nomination.  Requires the Secretary to enter into contracts with persons to collect, store, and distribute agricultural commodities made available for donation under this Act.  Requires the Secretary to use funds available for the purposes of the Act to be used for the program.

Hire Now Tax Cut Act of 2010 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exempt a qualified employer from the employer tax credit for wages paid in 2010. Defines "qualified employer" as an employer other than the United States, any state, local government, or instrumentality of the foregoing. Allows a qualified employer to elect to have this credit not apply.

Quit Smoking Incentive and Opportunity Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a refundable tax credit for tobacco use cessation expenses. Limits such credit to amounts equal to the qualified tobacco use cessation expenses paid for the benefit of the taxpayer, the taxpayer's spouse, or any dependent.

Community Pharmacy Fairness Act of 2007 - Makes any independent pharmacies that are engaged in negotiations with a health plan regarding contract terms under which the pharmacies provide health care items or services for which plan benefits are provided, subject to the same antitrust laws as the antitrust laws applicable to negotiations between independent pharmacies and health plans.

Declares that actions taken in good faith under this Act shall not be the subject under the antitrust laws of criminal sanctions, civil damages, fees, or penalties beyond actual damages incurred.

Exempts from the application of such antitrust laws any agreement or otherwise unlawful conspiracy that excludes, limits the participation or reimbursement of, or otherwise limits the scope of services to be provided by any independent pharmacy or group of independent pharmacies with respect to the performance of services that are within their scope of practice as defined or permitted by relevant law or regulation.

Declares that this Act applies only to independent pharmacies excluded from the National Labor Relations Act.

Copper Valley Native Allotment Resolution Act of 2007 - Grants rights-of-way across the Native allotments for an electric transmission line to the Copper Valley Electric Association for an electric transmission line.

Declares that this Act does not apply to land owned by Ahtna, Inc. and any prior or current right-of-way agreements that may exist between Ahtna, Inc. and the Copper Valley Electric Association or Alaska.

Provides for compensation for the rights-of-way granted, with specified locations, to the owners of such Native allotments.

Influenza Vaccine Emergency Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require a manufacturer or distributor of influenza vaccine to include in the contract with respect to the sale of the vaccine a provision in writing expressly stating: (1) the policy that the sale will be subject to specified conditions; and (2) the compensation the manufacturer or distributor will receive for the quantity of vaccine involved.  Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to pay the manufacturer or distributor the same amount as, under the contract, the manufacturer or distributor received or would have received for the quantity of vaccine involved.  Provides for the use of the authority provided for emergency sales contracts with respect to any contract with respect to which the Secretary has not published a determination that the extent of compliance with such guidelines has not been sufficient to constitute an adequate response to the emergency.

Water System Adaptation Partnerships Act of 2009 - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to make grants to community water systems to assist in planning, designing, constructing, implementing, or maintaining any program, strategy, or infrastructure improvement: (1) to conserve water or increase water use efficiency; (2) to carry out water metering to measure water efficiency effectiveness of a water efficiency program; (3) to preserve or improve water quality; (4) to enhance water management by increasing source water preservation and protection, or natural or engineered green infrastructure in the management, conveyance, or treatment of water, wastewater, or stormwater; (5) to increase energy efficiency or the use and generation of renewable energy in the management, conveyance, or treatment of water, wastewater, or stormwater; (6) to support the adoption and use of advanced water treatment, water supply management, or water demand management technologies or processes that maintain or increase water supply or improve water quality; (7) to complete studies or assessments to project how climate change may impact the future operations and sustainability of the water system; or (8) to carry out any other activity or project to address any ongoing or forecasted, based on the best available

Health Care for Veterans of Project 112/Project SHAD Act of 2003 - Amends Federal provisions concerning the Department of Defense (DOD) Department of Defense (DOD) testifying before the House Committee on Armed Services and Government Accountability and Review Committee on Veterans Affairs to provide that a veteran who participated in a test conducted by DOD under the SHAD program in 1962 and who participated in a program for chemical and biological warfare testing in 1973 is eligible for hospital care, medical services, and nursing home care for any illness, notwithstanding that there is insufficient medical evidence to conclude that such illness is attributable to such testing. Provides that such veterans who participated in a SHAD test and in a VA test who do not have baccalaureate degrees shall not be denied a promotion on that basis. Provides additional pay for the next grade for addition of additional health care workers in the Veterans Health Administration.Provides for additional pay for the next service discharge for the service of a veteran who has completed a service of service in the Veterans Administration.Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to establish, and provide for the issuance of, permittificates for the appointment of additional health

Safe, Efficient, Coordinated, Unified, Revitalized, Enhanced Visa Waiver Act - Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to establish an electronic system through which an alien seeking to enter the United States without a visa under the visa waiver program shall: (1) be required to submit biographical information before embarkingation; and (2) be provided with a method for an electronic determination of eligibility, and a deployment fee, in 90 seconds or less.

Amends the Enhanced Border Security and Visa Entry Reform Act to direct the Secretary to install at all ports of entry into the United States equipment and software to allow biometric comparison and authentication of all U.S. visas and other travel and entry documents issued to aliens.

Amends the Act to authorize the Secretary to grant up to two extensions for a country, and its nationals, of specified deadlines.

Pro-Growth Budgeting Act of 2014 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to prepare for each major bill or resolution reported by any congressional committee a macroeconomic impact analysis of the budgetary effects of such legislation for the ten fiscal-year period beginning with the first fiscal year for which an estimate was prepared and each of the next three ten fiscal-year periods. Requires the analysis to describe the potential economic impact of the applicable major bill or resolution on major economic variables, including real gross domestic product, business investment, the capital stock, employment, interest rates, and labor supply.  Requires the analysis to describe the potential fiscal effects of the bill or resolution, including any estimates of revenue increases or decreases resulting from changes in gross domestic product.  Directs the CBO to report on the accuracy of the original macroeconomic impact analysis of such enacted legislation and submit these reports to the congressional budget committees.

Repeals the concurrent resolution on the budget for FY2002, with respect to the surplus or deficit, public debt, debt held by the public, net interest (900), and allowances (920).

Requires the chairman of the House Committee on Appropriations to make necessary conforming changes in total new budget authority, total budget outlays, the surplus or deficit, public debt, debt held by the public, net interest (900), and allowances (920).

Requires the chairman of the Senate Committee on the Budget to make the appropriate adjustments in the congressional record concerning the budget for FY2002.

Amends the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985 (Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act) to: (1) increase the maximum amount of appropriations authorized for FY2002 from $683.2 million to $702.8 million; and (2) reduce the amount of appropriations authorized for FY2002 for the period beginning FY2001 and ending FY2002.

Amends the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act

Preserving Data in Government Act of 2017 This bill requires any open government data that is made available to the public for 90 consecutive days to remain machine-readable, available in an open format, and part of the worldwide public domain or, if necessary, published with an open license.  It shall not be a violation to alter the contents of the open government data or the contents of the open government data format.  It shall not be a violation to remove any open government data from public availability if: (1) the data is too costly to maintain or (2) the data does not provide sufficient value to the public.

Small Business Review Panel Technical Amendments Act of 1999 - Amends Federal environmental law to require the head of an environmental protection agency (EPA) agency to:  (1) notify the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Small Business Administration (SBA) in writing before the publication of an initial regulatory flexibility analysis that a covered agency is required to conduct under the Federal Trade Commission Act of 1934 provisions regarding the potential impacts of a proposed rule on small entities and the type of small entities that might be affected; and (2) identify affected small entity representatives and transmit information to the identified representatives for obtaining advice and recommendations about the potential impacts of the draft proposed rule. 
Requires the head of an environmental protection agency to convene a review panel to report to the SBA Chief Counsel on:  (1) the comments received from the small entity representatives; and (2) its findings regarding issues related to such proposed rule and any such issues regarding the draft proposed rule. 
Requires the SBA to modify the draft proposed rule, the initial regulatory flexibility analysis for the draft proposed rule, or the decision on whether an initial regulatory flexibility analysis is required for the draft proposed rule.

Trade and Environment Enforcement Act or Green 301 Act - Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to direct the Trade Representative (TRA) to identify those foreign country trade practices that cause negative environmental impacts on the protection of human, animal, or plant life or health or the conservation of exhaustible natural resources in the United States, the foreign country, a third country, or internationally.

Requires the TRA to: (1) take into account all relevant factors, including the strength of the connection between trade and the negative environmental impact; (2) provide the opportunity for input by and consultation with interested persons; and (3) provide the TRA with an opportunity to submit a report on foreign country trade practices that may in the future warrant inclusion in the report as foreign country trade practices that negatively affect the environment.

Improving Security for Investors and Providing Closure Act of 2013 or the Improved SIPC Act of 2013 - Amends the Securities Investor Protection Act of 1970 to allow one-time payments to a one-time customer of the debtor's SIPC Fund from which customers can elect to receive one-time payments from the SIPC Fund. Defines "debtor" as the broker or dealer that is the subject of the action brought under this Act.

Civil Rights Amendments Act of 1993 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the the Civil Rights Act of 1968 to make changes in the definition of "affectional or sexual orientation" with respect to housing, real estate, and brokerage. 
Amends the Federal criminal code to make it a crime to:  (1) interpose an interception of the sound of a gun in a building, place, or vehicle, or to use a firearm in a threatening or criminal manner; or (2) make a false statement or act of terrorism in a public place, or in a vehicle, or in a building, place, or vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a building, place, or vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a vehicle, or in a

Promoting Affordable Childcare for Everyone Act or the PACE Act  Amends the Internal Revenue Code, with respect to the child and dependent care tax credit, to: (1) increase the amount of such credit for the first $50 of a taxpayer's income; (2) allow an inflation adjustment to such credit amount after 2016; and (3) increase the exclusion for employer-provided dependent care assistance.

Absentee Ballot Track, Receive, and Confirm Act - Amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to direct the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to make a payment to a state to reimburse it for the costs incurred in establishing an absentee ballot tracking program with respect to elections for federal office held in the state (including costs incurred prior to enactment of this Act). Requires the FCC to make such payments to a state if it so chooses.

Requires the FCC to certify to the FCC, in order to receive a payment, that it has established an absentee ballot tracking program with respect to elections for federal office held in the state. Limits such payment to the number of jurisdictions in the state that are responsible for operating such program and $3,000.

Homeowner Empowerment Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income certain distributions made in any month to the extent that such distribution when added to all other distributions made in such month which are taken into account under the Federal Family Income (FFI) tax code is less than $5,000 in any individual's lifetime. Excludes such distributions from the definition of "qualified mortgage distribution" for purposes of this Act.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to require the taxpayer to repay any distributions exceeding $5,000 within 12 years.

Civil Rights Amendments Act of 2003 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the the Civil Rights Act of 1968 to make changes in the definition of "affectional or sexual orientation" with respect to housing, real estate, and brokerage.

Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1968 to make it a crime to favor or avoid discrimination on the basis of affectional or sexual orientation.

Birthparent Assistance Act of 2008 - Authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide certain services for birthparents who have placed a child for adoption, either directly or by grant to or contract with state or local governmental entities or public or private agencies or organizations, including licensed child welfare or adoption agencies or adoptive family groups and faith-based organizations.

Specifies such services for birthparents as: (1) post-legal adoption services; (2) individual, group, and family counseling; (3) establishment and operation of a nationally-available hotline to provide such counseling and related services; and (4) training of staff at hospitals and other appropriate birth care facilities relating to their interaction with birthparents and adoptive families.

Animal Drug Amendments of 1994 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to exempt certain animals from the requirements for the safe use of certain medications if the drug is by or on the lawful order of a licensed veterinarian within the context of a veterinary-client-patient relationship.  Provides for the safe use of certain animal drugs by or on the lawful order of a licensed veterinarian if the use is by or on the lawful order of a veterinarian who has provided the animal with food and water, has given the animal a treat, and has given the animal a place to rest.  Provides for the safe use of certain animal drugs by or on the lawful order of a veterinarian who has provided the animal with food and water, has given the animal a treat, and has given the animal a place to rest.

Requires the Secretary to carry out a demonstration program under which the Secretary establishes a four-year, residential, military style academy that offers at-risk youth secondary school coursework and vocational training, and that may offer precollegiate coursework.

Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) to authorize a state public entity health benefits pool to apply for and pass through funding under PPACA for health care benefits through January 1, 2014.  Directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to approve any application if the Secretary determines that the health care benefits provided through the pool: (1) will provide coverage that is at least as comprehensive as the coverage provided by PPACA; (2) will provide coverage and cost sharing protections against excessive out-of-pocket spending that are at least as affordable as the PPACA provisions; and (3) will result in cost savings to the federal government because the cost of providing health care benefits to individuals through the pool will be less than the PPACA costs.  Directs the Secretary to provide for an alternative means by which an aggregate amount determined under PPACA shall be paid to the pool for such purposes.

Common Sense Nutrition Disclosure Act of 2012 - Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require that the information disclosed in a food labeling claim concerning a food item be within the scope of the food item, the number of servings and information per serving, or the common unit division of the product. Allows the use of other methods for determining the content of food items.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to direct the Attorney General to ensure that numerical limitation computation accurately reflects the number of h-1b nonimmigrants employed.

Directs the Attorney General to promulgate regulations establishing the precise durations of the periods of time that are allowed for cancellations of visas and authorizations for nonimmigrant status.

Cell Phone Theft Prevention Act of 2012 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit a provider of commercial mobile or commercial mobile data service from providing service on a mobile electronic device that has been reported to such provider as stolen: (1) by the person who holds the account with respect to such service, if such person submits to such service a copy of a report made to a law enforcement agency regarding the theft; or (2) by another service provider on a mobile electronic device if the person submits to such service a copy of a report by another service provider.

Requires service providers to inform all other service providers of such service of: (1) the capability of deleting from a remote location all information that was placed on a mobile electronic device after its manufacture; and (2) the ability of a service provider on a mobile electronic device to make available the remote deletion capability required by this Act.

Requires service providers to make available to the account holders the capability of deleting, from a remote location, all information that was placed on a mobile electronic device after its manufacture.

American Elections Act of 2010 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to revise the foreign national limitation on corporate contributions and expenditures in connection with a federal, state, or local election.

Requires a corporation, prior to carrying out any activity related to the making or administration of a political committee, to certify that it is in compliance with this Act.

Requires a corporation to certify that it is in compliance with disclosure requirements under the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971.

Requires a corporation to include in a clearly spoken manner its current and prior voting stock, if the person who paid for a communication is a corporation that has such stock.

Small Business Health Relief Act of 2011 - Makes coverage (including health savings accounts) affordable for individuals and small businesses. Allows individuals to keep coverage they like it if they like it.

Amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to repeal the restriction on over-the-counter (OTC) medicines and the annual cap on coverage for individuals under the age of 65.

Repeals the requirement that health plans cover individuals who are covered by a group health plan or coverage in which an individual is enrolled on or after March 23, 2010, but before any plan year beginning not later than one year after the enactment of this Act. Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to promulgate regulations to clarify such application.

Requires the amendments made by this Act to take effect as if included in the enactment of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act.

Genetic Fairness Act of 1996 - Prohibits an insurer offering a health plan from:  (1) terminating, restricting, limiting, or otherwise applying conditions to coverage of an individual or family member under the plan; (2) canceling or refusing to renew the coverage of such an individual or family member; (3) denying coverage or excluding such an individual or family member from coverage; (4) imposing a rider that excludes coverage for certain benefits and services; (5) establishing differentials in premium rates or cost sharing for coverage; or (6) otherwise discriminating against an individual or family member in the provision of health care. 
Requires insurers offering health plans to provide enrollees with a written statement disclosing the rights of the enrollee under this Act. 
Sets forth enforcement requirements.

Amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 to authorize the Secretary of Education to award grants to local educational agencies (LEAs) that have made certain improvements in their teacher quality programs to award grants to LEAs that have taken steps to improve student achievement.

Education Modernization Fund Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to make low interest, long-term loans to States for the purpose of constructing and modernizing elementary schools and secondary schools.  Establishes the Education Modernization Fund to be made available for such loans.  Requires the Secretary to determine a formula for allocating such funds to States for such loans.

Derivatives and Hedge Fund Regulatory Improvement Act of 2008 - Directs the appropriate federal banking agencies (in coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), after consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) for the implementation of their coordinated rulemaking regarding entities under their respective jurisdictions) to initiate a coordinated rulemaking regarding the entities under their respective jurisdictions that engage in transactions involving unregistered hedge funds or over-the-counterderivatives to: (1) extend requirements of regulations relating to the safety and soundness of the financial system applicable to mutual funds under the Investment Company Act of 1940 to unregistered hedge funds, including to require the fund to disclose its policies on borrowing money and to require a shareholder vote to change such policy; (2) provide for the regulation of over-the-counterderivatives, including credit default swaps, interest rate swaps, currency swaps, mortgage-backed securities, asset-backed securities, collateralized debt obligations, and otherderives that are not traded on a national securities exchange or by a registered securities association, in the public interest and for the protection of investors, the stability of the

Marriage Penalty Relief Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) eliminate the marriage penalty in standard deduction income; (2) increase the married income tax rate to 200 percent; (3) increase the earned income credit to $3,000; and (4) allow a earned income credit for inflation adjustments to the $3,000 amount in the 15 percent bracket.

Repatriate Our Patriots Act - Prohibits a special veteran from being removed from the United States. Requires a special veteran, in the case of a special veteran residing abroad, to be naturalized as a U.S. citizen upon the filing of the appropriate application, paying the appropriate fees, and taking and subscribing to a certificate of citizenship. Allows the Secretary of Homeland Security to waive taking of the oath of allegiance if the veteran is unable to understand or communicate the meaning of his or her removal. Directs the Attorney General to rescind any outstanding order of removal and any finding that the veteran is subject to removal or is inadmissible. Directs the Secretary to establish a program and application procedure to permit such veterans removed from the United States before enactment of this Act to enter the United States as lawfully admitted aliens. Requires the Secretary to: (1) identify immigration cases involving special veterans by inquiring of every alien processed prior to initiating removal proceedings, and (2) keep records of such veterans for an opportunity to track their outcomes.

Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians Recognition Act - Extends Federal recognition to the Mowa Band of Choctaw Indians of Alabama.  Restores Federal rights and privileges abrogated by earlier laws. 
Approves and ratifies the cession of lands to the United States by the Tribe.  Makes all historical tribal lands abrogated or diminished before this Act's enactment. 
Requires the Tribe to transfer to the United States any interest in lands held by the Tribe on this Act's enactment date.  Requires the Secretary of the Interior to accept any deed or other instrument used to make a conveyance under this Act. Makes the lands held in trust for the use and benefit of the Tribe in trust for the benefit of the Tribe. 
Entitles the Tribe to all services and benefits provided by the Federal Government to Indians because of their status as federally recognized Indians. Makes the services and benefits provided by the Government to the Tribe inqualified. 
Requires the Tribe to submit to the Secretary any bylaws or other constitutions adopted by the Tribe.

Know Before You Fly Act - Amends Federal transportation law to require air carriers to disclose, in an internetfare quotation, whether or not they will: (1) provide for additional fees for checked baggage and carry-on baggage; (2) arrange for ground transportation; (3) provide meal vouchers; (4) arrange for air transportation on another air carrier or foreign air carrier to the passenger's destination; and (5) provide for sleeping facilities, food, and water inside the airport terminal.

Requires a covered air carrier to: (1) publish a clear statement indicating whether or not it, with respect to a passenger of the air carrier whose travel is interrupted as a result of a widespread disruption, will: (1) provide for hotel accommodations; (2) arrange for ground transportation; (3) provide meal vouchers; (4) arrange for air transportation on another air carrier or foreign air carrier to the passenger's destination; and (5) provide for sleeping facilities, food, and water inside the airport terminal.

Directs the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to: (1) designate an office of the FAA to receive and analyze FumeQueriesAirquarantinedReporting Office reports

Sport Fish Restoration and Recreational Boating Safety Act of 2011 - Amends the Federal Aid in Fish Restoration Act to: (1) extend through FY2017 the prohibition against the transfer to the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating funds for the Department of the Interior for the purpose of implementing recreational boating safety measures; and (2) exclude from the annual appropriation for FY2012, for FY2013 and thereafter, amounts that are set aside for such purposes.

Extends through FY2017 the prohibition against the transfer to the Secretary of the Interior any amount that is set aside for boating safety purposes of: (1) $6.5 million for FY2012; (2) $200,000 to fund the National Boating Safety Advisory Council; and (3) not less than $6 million for national boating safety activities of national nonprofit public service organizations.

Extends through FY2017 the prohibition against the transfer to the Secretary of the Interior any amount that is set aside for boating safety purposes of amounts that are set aside for national boating safety activities of national nonprofit public service organizations

Disaster-Affected Homeowners Notification Act of 2013 - Requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) to notify mortgagees and servicers of their recommendations or guidelines for assistance with respect to any mortgage or servicer of any kind that makes available forbearance relief with respect to any mortgage or servicer of any agency head or enterprise issues with respect to any mortgage or servicer of any such agency.  Requires the applicable agency heads to: (1) provide such notification to mortgagees or servicers, and (2) provide such notification to areas subject to the disaster declaration.  Directs the agencies to issue guidelines to provide notice and awareness of any such forbearance relief in connection with a major disaster throughout the areas subject to the disaster declaration.

Help Extend Auditory Relief (HEAR) Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to provide for Medicare coverage of hearing aids as durable medical equipment. Defines "hearing aid" to include: (1) aural rehabilitation services, in the case of an individual who has a hearing loss; (2) a comprehensive audiologic assessment to determine if a hearing aid is appropriate and to determine the need for other diagnostic medical or audiologic testing; and (3) a threshold test to determine audio acuity. Excludes hearing aids furnished by a physician or qualified audiologist, who is legally authorized to supply such hearing aid under the state law, from coverage.

Forest Service Financial Accountability Restoration Act of 1999 - Prohibits the use of Forest Service discretionary programs and activities for a fiscal year in which the Forest Service is no longer an agency at high risk of waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement due to weaknesses in its accounting and financial reporting systems, as determined under this Act.  Terminates the Forest Service's high risk status upon the earlier of:  (1) the date on which the Forest Service is no longer an agency at high risk of waste, fraud, abuse, and mismanagement due to weaknesses in its accounting and financial reporting systems; or (2) the end of the fifth fiscal year subject to such limitations.  Authorizes the Forest Service to make such certification only if:  (1) the Forest Service receives two consecutive unqualified audit opinions from the Inspector General of the Department of Agriculture; and (2) the Forest Service corrects the material weaknesses identified in the audit reports of the Inspector General regarding the Forest Service's fiscal year 1995 financial statements and all subsequent audit reports of the Inspector General regarding the Forest Service's financial statements published before the enactment of this Act.  Directs the Forest Service to maintain or increase

Distributed Power Hybrid Energy Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy to develop and transmit to the Congress a distributed power hybrid systems strategy showing: (1) opportunities and priorities that might best be met with distributed power hybrid systems configurations; (2) what barriers exist to the use of distributed power hybrid systems; (3) what technology gaps need to be closed; and (4) what system integration tools are needed to plan, design, build, and operate distributed power hybrid systems for maximum benefits.

Directs the Secretary to implement the strategy and report to the Congress annually on the use of, and experience with, distributed power hybrid systems.

National Urban Watershed Model Restoration Act - Directs the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to develop and carry out a pilot program to serve as a national model for the restoration of urban watersheds and community environments.  Requires such program to be carried out in the Anacostia River watershed, District of Columbia and Maryland. 
Requires the Administrator to:  (1) integrate on a community or geographic basis the regulatory and nonregulatory programs of the Environmental Protection Agency with other Federal, State, and local government programs and provide effective coordination among such programs; (2) support baseline monitoring efforts of State and local governments to determine key trends in ambient environmental conditions for the purpose of filling gaps in critical data about the environmental condition of the watershed; (3) develop and maintain environmental indicators in conjunction with interested public entities and ensure regular public reporting of such indicators; (4) provide grants to local community groups and nonprofit organizations to foster community involvement in the decision making process, environmental educational goals, and restoration strategies; (5) assist in the establishment of measurable goals for the restoration of the watershed; (6) maintain a biennial work plan for the Anacostia River watershed; and (7) demonstrate new technologies and approaches which are applicable

Social Security Disability Amendments Act of 1994 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to provide for a limited exclusion from self-identification under the program for individuals determined to be self-sufficient by the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of eligibility for Federal assistance under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (DL) program. 
Requires plans for achieving self-support to meet certain criteria, including a completed plan for achieving self-support which is not disapproved by the Secretary within 60 days after the submission of the plan. 
Amends the Federal Family Education Loan (FFEL) program to provide for a limited exclusion from self-identification under the program for individuals determined to be self-sufficient by the Secretary for purposes of eligibility for Federal assistance under the William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan (DL) program. 
Requires plans for achieving self-support to meet certain criteria, including a completed plan for achieving self-support which is not disapproved by the Secretary within 60 days after the submission of the plan. 
Amends the Federal Aid to Education Loan (FEL) program to provide for a limited exclusion from self-identification

Truth in Video Game Rating Act - Directs the Federal Trade Commission to prescribe rules under which the following criteria shall be used to prohibit the rating of any video games: (1) withholding of content from sale or distribution in interstate commerce; (2) in any other manner disclosing code or method of accessing hidden content; (3) providing a rating that is grossly mischaracterized by the content of the video or computer game; and (4) requiring a rating organization to provide a code or method of accessing hidden content.

Directs the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, to act as the lead federal agency for coordinating and disseminating information on existing federal programs and assistance that may be used to help initiate, develop, and finance energy efficiency, renewable energy, and energy retrofitting projects for schools.

Nonprofit Energy Efficiency Act - Directs the Secretary of Energy (DOE) to establish a pilot program to award grants for the purpose of retrofitting nonprofit buildings with energy-efficiency improvements. Defines "energy-efficiency improvement" as an installed measure (including a product, equipment, system, service, or practice) that results in a reduction in demand for energy or fuel supplied from outside the nonprofit building. Includes a hospital, youth center, school, social welfare program facility, house of worship, and other nonresidential and noncommercial structures eligible for such a grant. Authorizes the Secretary to award such a grant if an applicant submits a grant application form, in such form, and containing such information as the Secretary may prescribe. Limits each grant award to: (1) an amount equal to 50% of the energy-efficiency improvement, and (2) $200,000. Amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to increase the amount of funds authorized for such grants for FY2013-FY2016.

Amends the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (ERISA) and the Internal Revenue Code to require an individual account plan to include with the plan statement a notice that the plan may be overinvested in employer securities and employer real property, subject to a penalty for failure to provide such notice to participants and beneficiaries. Excludes from such penalty amounts: (1) any determination under the plan that the account may be invested in such securities and real property; and (2) any determination that the plan administrator has not provided such a penalty. Sets forth a civil penalty against an account administrator who fails to provide such a penalty.

Medicare HMO Protection Act of 1998 - Amends part A (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) (TANF) of title IV of the Social Security Act to authorize the Secretary of Health and Human Services to delay the effectiveness of a TANF initial contract period by up to three years if an adequate provider network has been established. 
Authorizes the Secretary and the Medicare+Choice organization terminating coverage to negotiate for a new contract which will enable the organization to continue coverage.  Requires the Medicare+Choice organization to provide and pay for written notice at least 120 days before the contract's termination, as well as a description of alternatives for obtaining TANF benefits.
Focus on Children Act - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to direct the Director of the Office of the Comptroller General to study and report annually to Congress on spending on children.

Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund Act of 1997 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish the Intercity Passenger Rail Trust Fund to finance qualified expenses of:  (1) the National Railroad Passenger Corporation; and (2) each non-Amtrak State to the extent such taxes are not attributable to the Highway Trust Fund financing rate. 
Provides for the transfer of amounts equivalent to certain Federal taxes imposed under this Act to the Fund.

Guam War Claims Review Commission Act - Establishes the Guam War Claims Review Commission to examine the facts and circumstances surrounding the implementation and administration of the Guam Meritorious Claims Act and the effectiveness of such Act in addressing the war claims of American nationals residing on Guam between December 8, 1941, and July 21, 1944.  Directs the Commission to: (1) review the facts and circumstances surrounding the implementation and administration of the Act; (2) review all relevant Federal and Guam territorial laws, records of oral testimony previously taken, and documents in Guam and the Archives of the Federal Government regarding Federal payments of war claims in Guam; (3) receive oral testimony of persons who personally experienced the taking and occupation of Guam by Japanese military forces, noting especially the effects of infliction of death, personal injury, forced labor, forced march, and internment; (4) determine whether parity of war claims paid to residents of Guam under the Guam Meritorious Claims Act as compared with awards made to other similarly affected U.S. citizens or nationals in territory occupied by the Imperial Japanese military forces during World War II; (5

Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Secretary of Education to carry out a program to provide low-income, minority, or disadvantaged college students with the information, preparation, and financial assistance to gain access to and complete law school study.  Authorizes the Secretary to contract with, or make a grant to, the Council on Legal Education Opportunity to provide for the delivery of specified services, including: (1) prelaw information resource centers, summer institutes, midyear seminars, and other educational activities; and (2) services for law school study and preparation.

Federal Public Safety Officer Surviving Spouse Protection Act of 2005 - Amends Federal law regarding the retirement annuities of Federal employees to provide for termination of survivor annuities of Federal public safety officers killed in the line of duty if the widow, widower, or former spouse was a Federal public safety officer who was killed in the line of duty.

Drug Rebate Equalization Act of 2009 - Amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to extend through 2016 the requirement for certain Medicaid-eligible outpatient drug discounts to enroll applicants in Medicaid managed care organizations (MSO's).
Grants a Federal charter to the 29th Division Association, Incorporated.

Improving Department of State Oversight Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of State to certify to Congress that it has made reasonable efforts to ensure the integrity and independence of the Office of the Inspector General Information Technology systems. The bill amends the Foreign Service Act of 1980 to require the Inspector General of the Department to report to the Inspector General on any allegations of waste, fraud, or abuse in the Department program or operation, criminal misconduct on the part of a Department employee, or serious, noncriminal misconduct on the part of any individual authorized to carry a weapon, make arrests, or conduct searches. The Inspector General may investigate matters covered by clause (i) if the Inspector General has first reported the allegations to the Inspector General. The Inspector General may, if the Inspector General has cooperated fully with the Inspector General, investigate matters covered by clause (iii) only if the Inspector General has first reported the allegations to the Inspector General. The Inspector General may prescribe general rules under which any requirement of clause (iii) or clause (iv) may be dispensed with. The Inspector General shall report to Congress on the Inspector

Partnering to Detect and Defeat Tunnels Act This bill requires the Department of Defense (DOD), in coordination with the Department of State and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), to seek to enter into an agreement with Israel to partner and coordinate in developing and deploying technologies to detect and counter tunnels.  DOD shall designate a military department or other element of DOD to carry out this bill.  The Secretary of Defense shall designate a senior intelligence officer to manage the collection and analysis of intelligence regarding the tactical use of tunnels.  The DOD shall submit to Congress an annual report that includes: (1) instances of tunnels being used to attack installations of the United States or allies; (2) trends or developments in tunnel attacks throughout the world; (3) key technologies used and challenges faced by potential adversaries of the United States with respect to using tunnels; and (4) the capabilities of DOD for defending fixed or forward locations from tunnel attacks.  DOD must report to Congress on: (1) the use of sensors and electronic survivability in connection with tunnels; (2) the physical security program of the Combating Terrorism Technical Support Office; and (3) the Joint Improvised Explosion
Public Pension Parity Act of 1995 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to exclude from gross income certain amounts received by an individual as a governmental pension under a public retirement system.

Directs the Secretaries of the Interior and Agriculture to jointly establish a broad-based advisory group composed of representatives from the nonbroadcast communications industry and the two agencies to review recommendations on acceptable criteria for determining fair market values and next best alternative use.  Requires the group to report its findings to specified congressional committees.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to implement a program for administering and enforcing the restrictions on the importation of steel products from certain foreign countries.  Requires the Secretary to establish and implement a steel import notification and monitoring program.  Requires such notification to include a determination that a steel importation is notified.  Requires the Secretary to compile and publish on a weekly basis information regarding such steel imported products.

Protecting Employees and Retirees in Municipal Bankruptcies Act of 2014 - Amends federal bankruptcy law to: (1) eliminate the exemption from mandatory minimum bankruptcy filings for certain nonbankruptcy employees and retirees of entities that are employees or retirees of a federal, state, or municipal government; and (2) require the appropriate court, in the case of a plan that modifies a collective bargaining agreement or retiree benefit, to have jurisdiction of an appeal of a determination made by a bankruptcy court, except in the case of a plan that is not reviewed by a court of appeals, to have jurisdiction of a direct appeal to the court of appeal.  Directs the court, in the case of a plan that modifies a collective bargaining agreement or a retiree benefit, to consider and determine the appeal on an expedited basis.  Prohibits the authorized representative of such individuals from serving as the representative if: (1) the labor organization elects not to serve as the representative, or (2) the court, upon a motion by a party in interest, determines that different representation is appropriate.
