Health Care Fraud and Abuse Advisory Opinion Act of 1994 - Amends title XI (General Provisions) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to issue advisory opinions as provided for under provisions relating to the prohibition against discrimination in health care under title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act. 
Directs the Secretary to issue advisory opinions on whether an arrangement or proposed arrangement will result in a prohibited referral within the meaning of provisions relating to Medicare.

Alternative Minimum Tax Repeal Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to phase out the alternative minimum tax (AMT) on individual taxpayers beginning in 2011. Reduces the maximum amount of the AMT for taxpayers other than corporations.

Great Lakes Ecology Protection Act of 2000 - Amends the Nonindigenous Aquatic Nuisance Prevention and Control Act of 1990 to direct the Secretary of Transportation to issue regulations to: (1) prevent the introduction and spread of aquatic nuisance species within the Great Lakes; and (2) require all vessels, their crew, and passengers to: (1) carry out any discharge or exchange of ballast water before entering the Lakes; or (2) carry out any discharge or exchange of ballast water within the Lakes only in compliance with such regulations. Requires the Secretary to maximize public participation in the issuance of such regulations.

Ethanol Stimulus Act of 2006 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to establish a two-two ethanol production facility credit for producers of high-conversion ethanol in certain states (eligible for such credit if the production of high-conversion ethanol from renewable resources begins after August 8, 2005, and ends on the last day of the fourth taxable year following such date).

Amends Federal law to require that the Federal Government's recordkeeping and compliance programs be made available in electronic form and in indexable form by December 31, 1999. 
Requires the Federal Government's recordkeeping and compliance programs to be made available by December 31, 1999, for the following agencies:  (1) the Federal Communications Commission (FCC); (2) the Department of Transportation (DOT); (3) the Department of Homeland Security (DHS); (4) the Department of Justice (DOJ); (5) the Department of the Army; and (6) the Department of the Navy. 
Requires the FCC's annual report to the Congress on or before such date, including the number of cases arising, the exemption from the prohibition, and the disposition of such cases, to include a description of the agency's efforts to encourage compliance.

Amends the Export-Import Bank Act of 1945 to prohibit the Bank from guaranteeing, insuring, extending credit, or participating in the extension of credit to an entity with respect to the export of any good or service destined for China if the Board of Directors of the Bank determines that such entity has established and is adhering to the code of conduct set forth in this Act.  Directs the Bank to withdraw any guarantee, insurance, or credit that it has provided, and to withdraw from any participation in an extension of credit, to an entity with respect to the export of any good or service destined for China if the Bank Board determines that the entity is not adhering to such code.  Directs the Bank to: (1) withdraw any guarantee, insurance, or credit that it has provided, and to withdraw from any participation in an extension of credit, to an entity with respect to the export of any good or service destined for China if the Bank Board determines that the entity is not non-aggressively prohibiting the adoption of foreign-brand products or services; (2) require the same behavior by all partners, suppliers, and subcontractors under terms of contracts as is required by the Small Business Act; and (

Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to convey, without consideration, to the State of Colorado all U.S. rights of interest of the United States in and to a parcel of real property, including improvements, other than Kit Carson Chapel, consisting of approximately 512 acres and comprising the location of the Ft. Lyon Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, to permit the State to utilize the property for purposes of a correctional facility.  Prohibits the Secretary from making such conveyance, within three health care facilities, and within a nursing home care facility in Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 19, unless the State agrees to provide appropriate public access to such property and the cemetery located on the property.  Authorizes the Secretary to convey, without consideration, to the State any furniture, fixtures, equipment, and other personal property associated with the property conveyed.  Requires the Secretary to pay the State, or any private nursing home care facility, for costs incurred in providing nursing home care to any veteran who is relocated from the Ft. Lyon Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center.  Requires the Secretary to provide extended care services to such veterans.

Genetic Privacy and Nondiscrimination Act of 2003 - Amends the Public Health Service Act and the Public Health Service Act to prohibit a group health plan or health insurance issuer offering group health insurance coverage from adjusting premiums or premium contribution amounts for a group on the basis of predictive genetic information concerning an individual (including a dependent) or a family member (including information about a request for or receipt of genetic services).

Victims of Abuse Access to Health Insurance Act - Prohibits any insurer from: (1) engaging in a practice that has the effect of denying, canceling, or limiting health insurance coverage or health benefits to, or establishing, increasing, or varying the premium charged for such coverage to, or for an individual on the basis that the individual is, has been, or may be the victim of domestic violence; or (2) considering a condition or injury that occurred as a result of such violence as a pre-existing condition.  Specifies conditions and injuries which may have caused or contributed to the victim's condition.  Prohibits an individual aggrieved by reason of such conduct from commencing a civil action for relief.  Authorizes the court to award appropriate relief, including temporary, preliminary, or permanent injunctive relief and compensatory and punitive damages, as well as the costs of suit and reasonable fees for plaintiffs attorneys and expert witnesses.  Directs the aggrieved party to choose either: (1) an appropriate attorney or witness for each of the following actions; or (2) a qualified qualified attorney or witness for each of the following actions.  Authorizes the court to award appropriate relief, including temporary, preliminary, or permanent inj

Army Arsenal Strategic Workload Enhancement Act of 2012 - Directs the Secretary of Defense (DOD) to develop and promulgate measurable and enforceable guidelines for the DOD, defense agencies, and the military services to have supplies, components, end items, parts, assemblies, and sub-assemblies made infactories or arsenals owned by the United States, to the extent those factories or arsenals can make those supplies, components, end items, parts, assemblies, and sub-assemblies on an economical basis while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to mobilization, national defense contingency situations, and other emergency requirements.

Directs the Secretary of the Army to assign government-owned and government-operated Department of the Army factories and arsenals sufficient workload to ensure cost efficiency and technical competence in peacetime, while preserving the ability to provide an effective and timely response to mobilizations, national defense contingency situations, and other emergency requirements.

Requires the Secretary to submit to Congress a report for the Army identifying: (1) the core arsenal manufacturing capability; (2) the workload required to cost-effectively support the arsenals and the manufacturing capability inherent in these installations; (

Janey Ensminger Act of 2016 This bill amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry to review and publish in the Federal Register and on its website not fewer than three times every three years the scientific literature relevant to the relationship between the employment or residence of individuals at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, for at least 30 days during the period beginning on August 1, 1953, and ending on December 21, 1987, and specific illnesses or conditions incurred by such individuals.  The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) must also publish a list of illnesses or conditions for which there is evidence that exposure to a toxic substance at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, during the period specified may be a cause of the illness or condition.  Eligibility for health care from the Department of Veterans Affairs is specified for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) under the Medicare program.

Veterans Equal Treatment Act - States that the funding allocation formula for the Department of Veterans Affairs medical care system known as the Veterans Resource Allocation system, established pursuant to the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) pursuant to the Departments of Veterans Affairs and Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and Independent Agencies Appropriations Act, 1997, has been discontinued by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) effective at the end of the fiscal year during which this Act is enacted.  Directs the Secretary to develop a new formula for the allocation of funds appropriated to the VA for Medical Care to the national service regions, known as Veterans Integrated Service Networks, of the VA. Requires the Secretary to implement such formula in accordance with specified requirements.  Authorizes appropriations for the VA for FY 2004, $10 million for development and implementation of a replacement funding allocation formula.  Authorizes appropriations for the VA for FY 2004, $100 million for "Medical Care" for the VA, and such amount is in addition to any other amount authorized to be appropriated to the VA for FY 2004.

Safe and Affordable Drugs from Canada Act of 2015 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to direct the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to promulgate regulations permitting individuals to safely import into the United States a prescription drug purchased from an approved Canadian pharmacy that:   is dispensed by a pharmacist licensed in Canada;  is purchased for personal use in quantities not greater than a 90-day supply; is filled using a valid prescription issued by a physician licensed to practice in the United States; and has the same active ingredient or ingredients, route of administration, dosage form, and strength as a prescription drug approved under the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).   The FDA must publish a list of approved Canadian pharmacies, including their website address, from which individuals may purchase prescription drugs.

Off-Reservation Land Acquisition Guidance Act - Directs the Secretary of the Interior to evaluate, before taking off-reservation land into trust for the benefit of an Indian tribe, the anticipated benefits to the off-reservation land and any concerns raised by applicable State and local governments relating to the acquisition of the land.  Requires the Secretary to prepare a report that includes an assessment of:  (1) the impacts of taking the off-reservation land into trust on the on-reservation unemployment rate, the impacts of taking the off-reservation land into trust on reservation life and tribal membership, the specific on-reservation benefits of taking the off-reservation land, and whether the transfer of jurisdiction to the Indian tribe over the parcel is likely to disrupt established local governmental operations, the potential impacts on real property taxes and adjacent land and property, and the compatibility of the anticipated use of the land with the zoning and land use requirements of the applicable State and local governments; and (2) whether the transfer of jurisdiction to the Indian tribe will affect the tribal government's ability to efficiently implement governmental and regulatory responsibilities and the compatibility of the anticipated use of the land with the applicable zoning and land use requirements. Save Our Seas Act of 2017 or the SOS Act of 2017 This bill amends the Marine Debris Act to extend and authorize appropriations for: (1) the work with the Department of State and other federal agencies to develop outreach and education strategies to address both land- and sea-based sources of marine debris; and (2) the Marine Debris Program at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).  The bill authorizes: (1) the work with the state of Alaska and the Department of the Interior to develop outreach and education strategies to address both land- and sea-based sources of marine debris; and (2) the Marine Debris Program at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

Great Lakes Federal Effectiveness Act - Establishes the Great Lakes Research Council, which shall: (1) advise and promote coordination of Federal research activities to avoid unnecessary duplication and ensure greater effectiveness in achieving ecosystem protection of the Great Lakes through the goals of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement; (2) identify topics for and participate in meetings, workshops, symposia, and conferences on Great Lakes research issues; (3) make recommendations for the uniform collection of data for enhancing research and management protocols relating to the Great Lakes ecosystem; (4) advise and cooperate in the establishment of a comprehensive, multi-media data base for the Great Lakes ecosystem; and (5) ensure that the results, findings, and information regarding Great Lakes research programs conducted or sponsored by the Federal Government be disseminated in a timely manner, and in useful forms, to interested persons, using as much as possible existing mechanisms, such as the Great Lakes Research Inventory prepared by the International Joint Commission.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a tax deduction for political contributions made by him or her within the taxable year.  Limits the amount of such deduction to $100 ($200) for a joint return.  Allows the deduction only if the individual publicly announces before the close of the calendar year, and meets certain qualifications, that he or she is a candidate for election to such office.  Allows the deduction only if the individual meets the qualifications prescribed by law. 
Requires the State and national political party rules for allowances of political contributions to be prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury.

Cuba Sanctions Reform Act of 2004 - Prohibits the imposition of additional sanctions for one year after enactment of this Act unless renewed pursuant to specified provisions of the Relations with Cuba Act of 1997.

Magistrate Judge Improvement Act of 2000 - Amends the Federal criminal code to set forth the magistrate judge's power to exercise contempt authority as set forth in this Act. 
Authorizes a magistrate judge to punish by fine or imprisonment any person who commits a misdemeanor or who commits a class A or B misdemeanor in a petty offense case involving a juvenile. 
Authorizes the magistrate judge, in a petty offense case involving a juvenile, to exercise all powers granted under this Act, including the power to enter a sentence for a petty offense and the power to enter a sentence for a class A or B misdemeanor in a case in which the parties have consented.

Community Investment and Empowerment Act - Amends the Small Business Investment Act of 1958 to direct the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to make competitive grants to communities for: (1) the creation of a grant and/or revolving loan fund program that helps develop financing packages for Class 1 commercial investment; (2) lowering of real estate property tax rates; (3) conducting community-wide market analysis to help recruit and/or retain Class 1 commercial investment; (4) creating employment training programs for Class 1 business customer service, sales, and managerial positions; (5) retail marketing strategies to solicit new Class 1 commercial investment starts in the community; (6) program allowances for activities such as the publication of marketing materials, development of economic development web pages, and educational outreach activities with retail trade associations; and (7) hiring business recruitment specialists.

Directs the Secretary of Commerce to: (1) assess the U.S. economy to determine what goods it currently produces, where it is produced, in which manufacturing sector the United States is most competitive, and what policies are necessary to maintain or increase the competitiveness of U.S. manufacturing in the global economy; and (2) develop a national manufacturing strategy. Requires the Secretary to: (1) establish targets for the growth of U.S. manufacturing, including targets for job creation, for each of FY2012-FY2016; and (2) conduct a survey of all federal agencies that provide support to U.S. manufacturers, including the Department of Commerce, the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, the Department of the Treasury, the Small Business Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of Science and Technology Policy, the Office of the United States Trade Representative, and other federal agencies as appropriate. Directs the Secretary to: (1) hold not fewer than two hearing sessions that include witnesses from manufacturing sectors that the Secretary considers important; and (2) report to Congress on progress and trends in U.S. manufacturing since the Secretary's 2004 report, "Manufacturing in America:

Local Farm Vehicle Flexibility Act - Prohibits the Secretary of Transportation from terminating, reducing, limiting, or otherwise interfering with the amount or timing of State highway grants that a State is otherwise eligible to receive under any minimum standard or exemption provided by the State for a covered farm vehicle or the driver of such vehicle that is less stringent than the requirements for commercial motor vehicles and drivers established under Federal regulations, including those pertaining to: (1) controlled substances and alcohol use and testing; (2) commercial driver's licensing; (3) driver qualifications; (4) medical certifications; (5) driving and operating commercial vehicles; (6) parts and accessories for the safe operation of commercial vehicles; (7) the maximum hours of service of drivers; (8) vehicle inspection repair and maintenance; (9) employee safety and health standards; and (10) recordkeeping related to compliance with such standards.

True Understanding of the Economy and Safety Act or the TRUE Safety Act This bill requires the Comptroller General to assess the methodology followed by the Secretary of Transportation in carrying out the efficacy of the 34-hour restart rule published on December 27, 2011, entitled "Hours of Service of Drivers." The bill specifies that the bill's purpose is to assess the methodology and data used by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration in its Regulatory Impact Analysis. The bill also specifies that the GAO assessment shall be: (1) to conduct an analysis of the methodology and data used by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration in its Regulatory Impact Analysis, (2) to evaluate the validity and representativeness of the driver data used to evaluate the operational and economic impacts of the new 34-hour restart rule applicable to operators of commercial motor vehicles, (3) to conduct an analysis of the data and methodology used to develop the proposed safety and health benefits of the new 34-hour restart rule applicable to operators of commercial motor vehicles, (4) to review the safety, health, cost, and operational implications of the new 34-hour restart rule, and (5) to review the research used in developing and justified the

Women's Autoimmune Diseases Research and Prevention Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to require the Director of the Office on Women's Health in the Department of Health and Human Services to expand, intensify, and coordinate research and related activities on autoimmune diseases in women. Requires the Director to conduct or support research to expand the understanding of the causes of, and develop methods for preventing, autoimmune diseases in women.

Redundant Remapping Reform Act of 2011 - Prohibits the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) from updating or publishing a National Flood Insurance Program rate map for an area that is being developed for a levee for which the Army Corps of Engineers has entered into a cost-sharing agreement with the Administrator. Prohibits the Administrator from updating or publishing a National Flood Insurance Program rate map for an area that is being developed for a levee not being used for which the Army Corps of Engineers has entered into a cost-sharing agreement.

Prohibits the Administrator from updating or publishing a National Flood Insurance Program rate map for an area that is being developed for a levee that is being planned, constructed, or rehabilitated, if the scheduled completion date for the planning, construction, or rehabilitation of the plan is determined to be uncertain. Sets forth exceptions to such prohibition, including for levees that will experience an indefinite delay.

Requires the Administrator to publish a notice to be used by owners of qualified levees to inform affected persons of the possible dangers of living in an area affected by the qualified levees without flood insurance coverage, the availability of flood insurance coverage,

Amends the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006 (NDAA FY 2006) to increase the number of aliens admitted and eligible for special immigrant status for purposes of the Refugee Assistance Eligibility Act of 1994.

Requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to report to Congress whenever the Secretary increases, as specified, the numerical limitation on such alien's special immigrant status.

Provides for: (1) the inclusion of an alien in special immigrant status for purposes of the Refugee Assistance Eligibility Act of 1994; and (2) refugee refugee eligibility for any alien provided special immigrant status under such Act.

Provides for: (1) the special immigrant eligibility of certain refugees eligible for special immigrant status under the Refugee Assistance Eligibility Act of 1994; and (2) the special immigrant eligibility of certain permanent resident aliens eligible for special immigrant status under the Refugee Assistance Eligibility Act of 1994.

Transparency in Energy Production Act of 2016 This bill directs the Department of the Interior to make available to the public: (1) information that describes for all covered operations the aggregate amount of each fossil fuel, by type and by state, produced under federal leases and for gas reported, the portion and source of such amount that was released by each of venting, flaring, and fugitive release; (2) information that accurately describes the estimated amounts of existing fossil fuel resources on federal lands under lease for the production of renewable energy; and (3) information that describes the amount and sources of energy, in megawatts, produced from operating solar, wind, and geothermal projects on federal lands under lease for the production of renewable energy.  Interior shall initiate a process under the Federal Oil and Gas Royalty Management Act of 1982 to require accurate measuring and reporting by each holder of a lease for the production of fossil fuels on federal lands of the actual amount of methane gas produced under such lease, including all such gas not sold by or on behalf of the lessee.  Every two years, Interior shall submit a report that includes: (1) efforts underway by the Department of the Interior to decrease greenhouse gas emissions from covered

Requires the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate to make arrangements for the award of a congressional gold medal in honor of the American soldiers who were prisoners of war at Bataan/Corregidor/Luzon, collectively, in recognition of their personal sacrifice and service to their country. Expresses the sense of the Congress that the Smithsonian Institution should make the gold medal received available for display at other locations, particularly locations associated with those who fought in defense of Bataan and the prisoners of war.

Government Shutdown Accountability and Economic Report Act of 2017 (Sec. 2) This bill requires the Director of the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to submit to Congress on a regular basis a report estimating: (1) the economic output lost on that day as the result of a government shutdown; (2) any decrease in gross domestic product for the quarter that will occur as the result of such a shutdown; (3) the value of any assistance, including loans, grants, and contracts, that the Small Business Administration was unable to provide as the result of such a shutdown; and (4) the amount of any revenue lost on that day because of the effects of the shutdown on tourism and travel to and within the United States, including travel by foreign tourists.

Small Business Banking Regulatory Relief Act of 1999 - Amends Federal law to authorize any depository institution to permit the owner of any deposit or account on which interest or dividends are paid to make up to 24 transfers per month, for any purpose, to another account of the owner in the same institution. 
Amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act to prohibit the payment of interest on demand deposits. 
Amends the Federal Reserve Act to prohibit any payment of interest on the reserves at Federal Reserve banks. 
Amends the Federal Reserve System to provide for the payment of interest on reserves at Federal reserve banks.

Border Security and Elimination of Sanctuary for Illegal Aliens Act of 2007 - Expresses the sense of Congress that the worsening crisis of illegal immigration must be solved.

Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to: (1) increase incentives to recruit individuals to become border patrol agents to full-time employees within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS); and (2) develop incentives to retain experienced border patrol agents through the establishment of a retention program.

Directs the Secretary to: (1) make a priority construction of the border fencing required by this Act; and (2) report to Congress on the progress and expected completion date of such construction.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to: (1) provide for criminal penalties for an alien who is arrested for any offense by a state or local law enforcement agency for unlawful presence in the United States; and (2) include an alien arrested for an aggregate period of more than one year in the Immigration and Nationality Act as an eligible alien for such a penalty.

Drug-Induced Rape Prevention and Punishment Act of 1996 - Amends the Controlled Substances Act to impose a fine and/or 30-meter stick (with a maximum length of 100mm) imprisonment for distribution of controlled substances without the individual's knowledge, and for distribution of controlled substances to an individual who is unaware that a substance with the ability to alter that individual's ability to appraise conduct or to decline participation in or communicate unwillingness to participate in conduct is administered to the individual.  Imposes a fine and/or 30-meter stick (with a maximum length of 100mm) imprisonment for distribution of flunitrazepam (with a maximum length of 1 gram) to any person convicted for the possession of flunitrazepam exceeding the maximum length of the drug. 
Directs the Administrator of the Drug Enforcement Administration to study and report to specified congressional committees on the appropriateness and feasibility of rescheduling flunitrazepam as a Schedule I controlled substance under the Controlled Substances Act. 
Authorizes the Attorney General to create educational materials regarding the use of controlled substances in the furtherance of rapes and sexual assaults.

Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Amendments of 1993 - Amends the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to require the Commission to request the head of a federal agency, department, or unit to explain the reasons for the failure to submit the plan and to present any objections to any requirement of the Commission with respect to such plan.  Requires the Commission to order an agency or any officer or employee of such agency, department, or unit to submit the plan before the end of the period as determined to be reasonable.  Provides that the Commission may initiate a proceeding to determine:  (1) who is the officer or employee responsible for the failure of the agency, department, or unit to comply with the order; and (2) whether any disciplinary action is warranted against such officer or employee for such failure to comply.  Requires the Commission to submit its findings and recommendations to the administrative head of the agency, department, or unit in which such officer or employee is employed.  Provides that the Commission may issue an order that:  (1) any officer or employee of the agency charged with complying with the order or any officer or employee of the United States determined to be responsible for the failure of the agency to

Chacoan Outliers Protection Act of 1993 - Designates 310/80,033-B (historically significant) Acaco Culture Archaeological Protection Sites in the Chaco Culture Archeological Protection Sites National Park in New Mexico and the Chaco Culture Archaeological Protection Sites in Puerto Rico as Chaco Culture Archaeological Protection Sites.  Designates 14,372 acres of specified National Park Service land as Chaco Culture Archaeological Protection Sites. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to assist the Navajo Nation in the protection and management of such Sites through a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement. 
Authorizes the Secretary to assist the Navajo Nation in site planning, resource protection, interpretation, resource management actions, and such other purposes as may be identified in a grant, contract, or cooperative agreement.

(Sec. 2) HHS shall convey to the Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation in Dillingham, Alaska, all interest of the United States in and to certain property included in the Dental Annex Subdivision (including all land, improvements, and appurtenances) containing 1.474 acres more or less.  (Sec. 3) HHS shall convey to the Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation, as soon as practicable, all interest of the United States in and to certain property included in the Dental Annex Subdivision (including all land, improvements, and appurtenances) containing 1.474 acres more or less. Dental and Optometric Care Access Act or the DOC Access Act - Amends the Public Health Service Act to provide for the improvement of health care coverage under a group health plan or an individual or health insurance coverage offered through an individual or health insurance coverage offering limited scope dental or vision benefits.

Earmark Transparency Act of 2010 - Amends the Congressional Budget Act of 1974 to require the Clerk of the House of Representatives and the Secretary of the Senate to jointly establish a searchable website, which shall be comprised of a database including: (1) the fiscal year in which the item would be funded; (2) the number of the bill or joint resolution for which the request is made; (3) the amount of the initial request made by the Member of Congress; (4) the amount approved by the committee of jurisdiction; (5) the amount carried in the bill or joint resolution and accompanying report as passed by the House, as passed by the Senate, and as transmitted to the President; (6) the name and address of the intended recipient; (7) the type of organization (public, private nonprofit, or private for profit entity) of the intended recipient; (8) the project name, description, and estimated completion date; and (9) a justification of the benefit to taxpayers.

Less Imprecision in Species Treatment Act of 2018 or the LIST Act of 2018 This bill amends the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to direct the Department of the Interior to initiate the recovery process for any species that is listed as endangered or threatened under the Act if the Department has produced or received substantial scientific or commercial information demonstrating that the species is recovered or that recovery goals have been met. The Department must remove a species from a list published under this Act if it has produced or received substantial scientific or commercial information demonstrating that the species is recovered or that recovery goals have not been developed. In the case of a species removed, the publication and notice of the removal must be solely of a notice of the removal.  Interior must promptly publish notice of any negative finding or negative finding that a person submitted a petition that is the subject of a positive finding. If Interior finds that a person submitted a petition that is the subject of a positive finding, then the person must not be considered an interested person for purposes of the petition for purposes of any review of that petition.

Amends the Federal criminal code to make a U.S. national eligible for, and eligible for, advanced training in the Senior Reserve Officers' Training Corps (SCREC).  Makes a U.S. national eligible also for, and eligible for, financial assistance as a member of, the SCREC.

Veterans' Housing Benefits Enhancement Act of 2007 - Authorizes the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to furnish improvements and structural alterations to a member of the Armed Forces who has a total disability (including a severe burn injury) permanent in nature, or aggravated by a severe burn injury, if such member is likely to be discharged or released from the Armed Forces for such disability.

Requires the Secretary to report to the congressional veterans' committees on the adequacy of the authorities available to the Secretary to assist disabled veterans in acquiring suitable housing units, adapting to their residences, or obtaining necessary land and other appropriate property.

Amends the Veterans' Protection and Assistance Act to provide for the temporary furnishing of veterans' housing units with special fixtures or movable facilities to accommodate severe burn injuries.

Directs the Secretary to report to specified congressional veterans' committees on the advisability of providing assistance to veterans and members of the Armed Forces who reside with family members on a permanent basis.

Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals Reorganization Act of 2000 - Divides the current U.S. Court of Appeals for the ninth circuit into: (1) the ninth circuit, composed of Arizona, California, Nevada, and Oregon; and (2) the twelfth circuit, composed of Alaska, Guam, Hawaii, Idaho, Montana, Northern Mariana Islands, Oregon, and Washington.

Main Street Survival Act - Expresses the sense of the Congress that the President, acting through the Secretary of the Treasury, should encourage financial institutions that have received federal financial support to maintain historic levels of lending to small and medium-sized businesses.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) establish the Main Street Revolving Loan Fund to provide temporary loans to businesses that meet the size requirement under the Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP) of the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008; and (2) transfer and credit $1 billion to the fund.

Directs the Secretary to use the funds to finance the cost of operations, including the purchase and operation of equipment, paying salaries, and building expenses.

Prohibits the use of funds to significantly expand operations.

Requires a total maximum of $1 million in loans to a particular business in any fiscal year.

Authorizes the use of such loans to support businesses that have suffered a significant decrease in sales or have suffered a significant decrease in revenue.

Dairy Promotion Equity Act - Amends the Dairy Production Stabilization Act of 1983 to require the Secretary of Agriculture to establish a minimum membership of 36 in the National Dairy Promotion and Research Board. 
Requires the Secretary to appoint a Board member from nominations submitted by importers of imported dairy products. 
Requires the Board to provide that each importer of imported dairy products shall pay an assessment to the Board. 
Requires the Secretary to conduct a referendum on the approval of the Dairy Promotion Equity Act.

Balanced Trade Act of 2006 - Amends the Trade Act of 1974 to direct the President, whenever there is a U.S. current account deficit that exceeds 2% of the gross domestic product, to declare a temporary import surcharge in the form of duties in addition to those already imposed if any.  Requires the President, within 30 days after making such determination, to proclaim a surcharge in the form of duties in the form of duties in addition to those already imposed if any.  Provides for surcharges of up to 20% in any surcharge declared.

Iran Intelligence Oversight Act - Requires the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress an updated National Intelligence Estimate on Iran and to report to Congress on: (1) the reasons why such Estimate cannot be submitted by the date specified; and (2) an estimated date for the submittal of such Estimate.

Requires the National Intelligence Estimate to be submitted in classified form. Requires the Director of National Intelligence to report to Congress on: (1) the reasons why the Estimate cannot be submitted by the date specified; and (2) an estimated date for the submittal of such Estimate.

Instructs the President to report to Congress on: (1) U.S. policy objectives and U.S. U.S. strategy regarding Iran; and (2) the role of diplomacy, incentives, sanctions, other punitive measures, and other programs and activities relating to Iran for which funds are provided by Congress.

Financial Accounting for Intangibles Reexamination (FAIR) Act - Expresses the sense of the Congress that, prior to changing existing rules of accounting for business combinations, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Financial Accounting Standards Board should undertake a comprehensive reexamination of the appropriate methods of accounting for purchased and internally generated intangibles, including goodwill, and should await the results of related studies. 
Establishes the Commission on Financial Accounting for Intangibles to:  (1) consider the general usefulness of financial statements prepared under generally accepted accounting principles in light of recent trends in the securities markets; (2) consider the impact that shortcomings in generally accepted accounting principles have on securities market volatility, capital allocation, and the investment of retirement fund assets, both individual and institutional; (3) consider the general question surrounding the role of intangible assets in financial reporting in the economy; and (4) consider the economic impact that would result if the pooling of interests method of accounting for business combinations were eliminated. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) consider the general usefulness of financial statements prepared under generally accepted accounting principles in light of recent trends in the securities markets; (2) consider the impact that short

Immigration Backlog Reduction Act of 2011 - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to remove specified illegal aliens from the United States who are: (1) arriving in the United States for the four years preceding such date, or (2) arriving in the United States for the four years preceding such date and have not been physically present in the United States for the four years preceding such date.

Defines "inadmissible" to mean that an alien is: (1) inadmissible under specified grounds (including a criminal alien), (2) physically present in the United States for less than one year, and (3) presenting a significant risk to national security.

Directs the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to refer an alien for an interview by an asylum officer if the alien has been physically present in the United States for less than one year. Authorizes the Secretary to also determine the deportability of an alien if he or she was convicted of a criminal offense and is deeming that the alien is physically present in the United States for the four years preceding such date.

Mortgage E-Verify Act of 2010 - Amends the Federal National Mortgage Association Charter Act to prohibit the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) from: (1) refinancing, restructuring, or modifying any single-family housing mortgage held by or that backs any security issued by the corporation, or (2) purchasing, or issuing any security that is backed by, any single-family housing mortgage made for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of the mortgagor's previous single-family housing mortgage on the same property, unless the identity and work eligibility of the mortgagor has been confirmed by an inquiry under this Act.

Prohibits the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) from authorizing or entering into any agreement for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of any single-family housing mortgage that is insured by the HUD Secretary under this Act, or from insuring any single-family housing mortgage made for the refinancing, restructuring, or modification of the mortgagor's previous single-family housing mortgage on the same property, unless the identity and work eligibility of the mortgagor has been

Cure for AIDS Act of 2012 - Requires the Secretary of Defense, acting through the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program, to establish and support an accelerated research program dedicated to the discovery of a cure for HIV/AIDS.

Requires the Secretary to ensure that research conducted under this Act is highly targeted to address: (1) how HIV persists despite antiretroviral therapy; (2) where HIV persists beyond the reach of antiretroviral therapy; (3) whether ongoing attempts of the immune system to clear the infection actually hinders the ability of the medical community to cure infected individuals; (4) why the immune system reduces but does not eliminate levels of the virus; (5) how to measure ultra-low levels of the virus in the body; and (6) identifying and testing interventions, such as drugs, that may eliminate the virus from infected individuals.

Requires the Secretary to coordinate with at least one eligible nonprofit entity whose primary mission is ending the AIDS epidemic through innovative research and that has experience carrying out programs dedicated to AIDS cure research.

Acid Deposition and Ozone Control Act of 1997 - Amends the Clean Air Act to direct the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency to add any State to the single ozone transport region that contributed 4 parts per billion or more to ozone via aerial transport to the ozone level of any noncompliant area in the single ozone transport region for any 1 of the second through tenth worst ozone days that occurred during the previous 10 years. 
Requires the Administrator to promulgate regulations requiring reductions in the emissions of nitrogen oxide and sulfur dioxide in any State added to the single ozone transport region to 1/3 of the 1990 levels by the year 2003. 
Authorizes the Administrator to establish an allowance trading program to carry out this Act.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a 20-year recovery period for the depreciation of certain residential property, including heating, air conditioning, and commercial refrigeration systems.

Financial Institution Customer Protection Act of 2014 - Prohibits a federal banking agency from suggesting, requesting, or ordering a depository institution to terminate a customer account unless: (1) the agency has a material reason to do so, (2) such reason is not based solely on reputation risk, and (3) such reason is not being taken into account by any banking institution.  Requires an appropriate federal banking agency to: (1) provide such a suggestion, request, or order to the institution in writing, and (2) accompany such a request with a justification for why the termination is needed.  Prohibits a federal banking agency from suggesting, requesting, or ordering a depository institution to inform the customer of the justification for the customer's account termination if the agency believes the customer poses a threat to national security. Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to render aliens convicted of an aggravated felony or a firearm offenses inadmissible to the United States.  Prohibits the President, the U.S. Attorney General, or the Governor of any of the States from granting a waiver to an alien who is present in the United States after the expiration of the period of stay authorized by the Attorney General or the governor for a criminal conviction for a misdemeanor offense. 
Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to render aliens convicted of a criminal offense inadmissible to the United States.  Prohibits the President, the U.S. Attorney General, or the governor of any of the States from granting a waiver to an alien who is present in the United States, upon a warrant issued by the Attorney General, an alien who is accused of a misdemeanor crime of a firearm or a destructive device, or who is convicted of a misdemeanor crime of a criminal offense, if the Attorney General alleges that the alien:  (1) (1) has sought to procure or has procured a visa, other documentation, or admission into the United States for himself, himself

Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve Boundary Adjustment Act of 2004 - Amends the National Parks and Recreation Act of 1978 to adjust the boundary of the Barataria Preserve Unit of Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve in Louisiana.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire any land, water, and interests in land and water within the boundary of the Unit by donation, purchase, transfer, or exchange, with limitations.

Authorizes the Secretary to acquire, acquire, and acquire oil and gas rights in the area identified on the map.

Directs the Secretary to preserve and protect: (1) fresh water drainage patterns; (2) vegetative cover; (3) the integrity of ecological and biological systems; and (4) water and air quality.

Requires any reference in a law (including regulations, maps, documents, paper, or other record of the United States) to the Unit to be considered to be a reference to the Unit.

Authorized Rural Water Projects Completion Act - Establishes in the Treasury the Reclamation Rural Water Construction Fund, consisting of: (1) amounts deposited in the Fund under this Act; and (2) any interest earned on investment of amounts in the Fund.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to deposit in such Fund $80 million of revenues that would otherwise be deposited for the fiscal year in the reclamation fund established by the first section of the Act of June 17, 1902.

Authorizes the Secretary to expend from the Fund not more than the sum of: (1) $80 million for the fiscal year in which the expenditures are made, or (2) the amount of interest accrued in the Fund for the fiscal year in which the expenditures are made.

Prohibits the Secretary from using Fund amounts to complete construction of rural water projects: (1) authorized to be carried out by the Secretary on or before the date of enactment of this Act; or (2) for which the Secretary has completed a feasibility report that recommends the construction of a rural water project.

Prohibits the Secretary from using Fund amounts to pay for any operation and maintenance costs of an authorized rural water project.
