Iran Nuclear Nonproliferation Act - Expresses the sense of Congress that: (1) full diplomatic, political, and economic relations between the United States and Iran cannot be normalized unless and until enforceable safeguards are put in place to prevent weaponization of Iran's nuclear program and the government of Iran ends its support for international terrorist groups; and (2) no congressional authorization for the use of military force in any Act of Congress enacted before enactment of this Act constitutes, either implicitly or explicitly, an authorization for the use of military force against Iran or its nuclear program.

Amends the Small Business Administration Act to authorize the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA) to award a grant to one or more eligible associations for use in accordance with the requirements of this Act.  Requires an eligible association to submit to the SBA an application in such form and containing information as the SBA may require.  Allows an eligible association that has received a grant to apply for one or more additional grants, as may be necessary to carry out the SBIR and STTR program.  Permits an eligible association that has received a grant to reimburse a qualified mentoring organization for expenses incurred in order to advise and guide such an organization through the SBIR and STTR program.  Requires an employee of such an organization, while carrying out activities under the program, to be deemed to be a Federal employee.  Requires the Administrator of the SBA to submit to the House and Senate Small Business Committees recommendations regarding any change in the maximum grant amount under this Act.

Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to subject to criminal penalties: (1) aliens who remain in the United States for any period of time after a visa or status under which the alien is lawfully present (vISA) has expired; and (2) persons who violate such prohibition.
Authorizes the Secretary of State to apply for an alien visa overstay or deny entry if the Secretary determines that the alien violated specified grounds, including medical necessity. Provides for the revocation of such an alien's visa under specified circumstances.
Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to require the Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) to provide a foreign government with a copy of any Department of State or U.S. diplomatic or consular records pertaining to the issuance or refusal of visas or permits to enter the United States, or any information contained therein, if the Secretary determines that such record is in the national interests of the United States.

Outer Continental Shelf Enhanced Exploration and Deep Water Incentives Act - Amends the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act to revise the incentives program for exploration and development on producing or producing marginal or unused resources on producing or producing leases.  Revises the definition of "frontier area" for purposes of such incentives program.

TPS Reform Act of 2016 This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to extend the initial designation of a foreign state that is subject to specified requirements, including an estimate of the number of nationals of the foreign state who are, or within the effective period of designation, likely to become, eligible for temporary protected status.
Military Call-Up Relief Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to waive the ten percent penalty on early withdrawals from retirement plans for certain individuals.

Fair Credit Reporting Act Amendments of 2000 - Amends the Fair Credit Reporting Act to require consumer reporting agencies to make all disclosures under the Act without charge to a consumer, within one year after the consumer's request, without charge to any consumer reporting agency that: (1) the consumer has already received information from any consumer reporting agency; or (2) the consumer's request for a consumer report relates to the consumer from the agency. Makes consumer reporting agencies required to provide an annual credit report that includes information concerning credit scores or other risk scores or predictors, including information regarding credit scores or other risk scores or predictors, the factors taken into account in deriving a score or predictor, the relative weight of each factor, and the manner and extent to which such factors raise or lower the score or predictor. Makes consumer reporting agencies required to: (1) review and monitor the extent to which consumer reporting agencies and their furnishers are complying with the procedures, time lines, and requirements under the Fair Credit Reporting Act for the prompt investigation of the disputed accuracy of any consumer information and the prompt correction or deletion of any inaccurate or incomplete information or information that cannot be verified; and (2) report to Congress on the results of such review

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) make permanent the small business expensing allowance (expundable expenses in the low income tax bracket); (2) allow an additional $500,000 in small business expensing allowances for computer software; and (3) allow an additional $1,000,000 in tax deductions for individuals for the purchase of privately manufactured automobiles.

State Veterans Home Nurse Recruitment Act of 2004 - Directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to make payments to States for assistance in hiring and retaining nurses. Sets forth eligibility requirements for such recipients.

Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a small manufacturers' computer hardware and software credit for the cost of qualified computer hardware and software property for use in any small manufacturer located in the United States. Defines "qualified computer hardware" to include disk drives, integrated circuits, display screens, cables, modems, speakers, and printers. Terminates such credit after 2011.

Residential and Commuter Toll Fairness Act of 2009 - Authorizes states, counties, municipalities, and multi-jurisdictional transportation authorities (TAs) that operate or manage roads, highways, bridges, railroads, busses, ferries, or other transportation systems to establish programs that offer discounted transportation tolls, user fees, or fares for residents of specific geographic areas in order to reduce or alleviate toll burdens imposed upon such residents.

Taxpayer's Right to View Act of 1993 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to prohibit a cable operator from assessing or collecting any separate charges for any video programming of a sporting, theatrical, or other entertainment event if such event is performed at a facility constructed, renovated, or maintained with tax revenues or by an organization that receives public financial support. 
Authorizes the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and local franchising authorities to make determinations concerning the applicability of such prohibition.

Consumer Learning through Electronic Accessible and Reasonable Cost Information Act of 2013 or the CLEAR Cost Information Act of 2013 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to require a Medicare payment report to include information on the percentage that charity care makes up of the total care furnished by hospitals and critical access hospitals. Requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to post such information on a publicly accessible and searchable website.  Requires the Secretary to report on the percentage that hospitals and critical access hospitals make of the total care furnished by such hospitals.  Requires the Secretary to include a link on the hospital's website or critical access hospital's home Internet website, on the hospital's website, or on the hospital's website, and on the home Internet website of the hospital.  Requires the Secretary to post the hospital's hospital data on a publicly accessible and searchable website.  Requires the Secretary to report on the percentage that charity care makes up of the total care furnished by hospitals and critical access hospitals.

Communities Committed to College Tax Credit Act of 2008 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for 50% of designated qualified college scholarship funding contributions made by the taxpayer. Defines "qualified scholarship funding trust" as a U.S. tax-exempt charitable organization established to provide scholarships to children of tax-exempt qualified scholarship funding agencies.

Clinical Trials Modernization Act of 2015 This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to establish a framework through which: (1) sponsors of drugs, biological products, or devices may submit proposals for the incorporation of adaptive trial designs, Bayesian methods, or other alternative statistical methods into proposed clinical protocols and marketing applications for drugs, biological products, or devices; and (2) the FDA shall include in approved drugs and biological products the inclusion of such techniques in the development and regulatory review and approval, licensure, or clearance of drugs, biological products, and devices. The FDA must: (1) update and finalize draft guidance addressing the use of adaptive trial designs and Bayesian methods in clinical trials, and (2) issue draft guidance on the use of such techniques in the development and regulatory review and approval, licensure, or clearance of drugs, biological products, and devices. The bill requires the FDA to: (1) publish the final guidance required by this bill within 6 months after the public meeting, and (2) review and, as appropriate, revise the guidance documents to reflect developments in statistical methods that could be appropriate for use in clinical trials.

Medicare Home Health Equity Act of 1998 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to provide interim payment for home health services. 
Requires the Director of the Congressional Budget Office to estimate the amount of savings resulting from the interim payment system for home health services.

Ensuring the Taxpayer a Fair Return for Federal Onshore Oil and Gas Resources Act of 2015 Amends the Mineral Leasing Act to: (1) increase the maximum amount of federal oil and gas royalties paid by a company to 40% for each acre of federal land it leases, (2) allow the Secretary of the Interior to adjust the federal oil and gas royalty rate for inflation, and (3) increase the percentage of acreage covered by the federal oil and gas royalties that may be sold or rentals of the public lands in Alaska.

Kake Tribal Corporation Land Exchange Act - Directs the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (commonly known as the Alaska Native Claims Act) to convey to the corporation specified 2,427 acres of Federal land in the Copper River Meridian and to convey to the United States, no later than 90 days after the effective date of this Act, as shown on the map dated ____ and labeled Attachment A. Specifies the land to be conveyed by Kake Tribal Corporation to the United States, no later than 90 days after the effective date of this Act, as shown on the map dated ____ and labeled Attachment B. States that the land to be conveyed shallremain in effect for five years after the date of enactment of this Act.

Caring Family Act of 2003 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual taxpayer who is the spouse of, or a dependent of, the taxpayer (or a member of the taxpayer's household) with a long-term care needs to claim an exemption from the tax deduction for such needs for taxable years beginning after 2003.

Serving Everyone with Reliable, Vital Internet, Communications, and Education Act of 2007 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to continue in effect the Lifeline Assistance Program and the Link Up Program, which provide low-income consumers with one of several types of broadband services, including: (1) wire or wireless telephone service; (2) Internet access service; (3) wireless broadband service; and (4) any evolving technology the FCC deems consistent with the purposes of the Lifeline Assistance Program.

Requires the FCC to expand the program by allowing low-income consumers to choose to use the Lifeline Assistance Program or the Link Up Program for any one of the following: (1) wire or wireless telephone service; (2) Internet access service; and (3) wireless broadband service.

Directs the FCC to expand the program by allowing low-income consumers to participate in the Lifeline Assistance Program and the Link Up Program, including by doing so, through the Lifeline Assistance Program and the Link Up Program.

Requires the FCC to study and report to Congress on the necessary benefit level, projected projections, industry requirements, and policy proposals for a

Business Relief and Incentives for Small Entrepreneurs Act of 2007 or the Business RAISE Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow for the recovery of depreciation for certain improvements to retail space and for qualified new retailer property.  Expands the definition of qualified retail improvement property to include any improvement to an interior portion of a building which is nonresidential real property if: (1) such portion is open to the general public and is used in the trade or business of selling tangible personal property or services to the general public; and (2) such improvement is placed in service more than three years after the date the building was first placed in service.  Requires the definition of "qualified retail improvement property" to include any improvement for which the expenditure is attributable to: (1) the enlargement of the building, (2) any elevator or escalator, or (3) the internal structural framework of the building.  Requires the Secretary of Labor to: (1) publicize the expansion of the work opportunity tax credit and to provide technical assistance to employers seeking to take advantage of such credit; and (2) authorize appropriations for FY2008-FY2012.

Directs the Secretary of Agriculture to conduct a study and report to Congress regarding the safety of food products derived from cloned animals, including an evaluation and measurement of the potential health effects and costs attributable to milk from cloned animals in the food supply.

On-the-Job Training Tax Credit Act of 2015  Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow employers who employ not more than 500 full-time employees during the taxable year a business-related tax credit for 50% of the job training program expenses. Defines "job training program expenses" as amounts paid or incurred by an employer for expenses incurred for participation in a qualified training program. Terminates such credit after 2017.

National Parks Capital Improvements Act of 1996 - Authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to enter into a memorandum of agreement with an entity to act as an authorized fund raising organization for the benefit of the Grand Canyon National Park and any other national park designated by the Secretary that has an approved general management plan with capital needs in excess of $5 million.  Requires the organization to issue taxable bonds in return for the Park surcharge collected.  Requires the United States to not be liable for the security of any bonds issued by the organization, except that if the surcharge is not imposed for any reason or if such surcharge is reduced or eliminated, the full faith and credit of the United States is pledged to the payment of such bonds and the interest accruing on such bonds. 
Authorizes the Secretary to authorize the Superintendent of the park to charge and collect, in addition to the entrance fee, a surcharge of up to $2 for each individual charged the entrance fee.  Requires bond proceeds to be used to amortize the bond issue, provide for the reasonable costs of administration, and maintain a sufficient reserve consistent with industry standards. 
Allows bond proceeds to be used for a park facility project that does

Campaign Information Improvement Act - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to: (1) make nonpolicymaking stations prohibited from preempting the use of broadcast stations by a candidate for public office who has purchased and paid for such use pursuant to the provisions of this Act; (2) subject station licensees to the free broadcast time obligations of the Act; (3) require each station licensee to make available free broadcast time for policy debates; (4) allot free broadcast time for policy debates in accordance with the requirements of this Act; (5) allot time allotted to candidates for the House of Representatives and the Senate for policy debates to be allotted so that the candidates appear at the forum of the discussion on political issues or the Senate and the House on the same day; and (6) allot time allotted to candidates for the presidential election to the Senate and the House of Representatives for policy debates to be allotted to the same extent, to the same candidates, and subject to the same conditions as free broadcast time is required to be provided by broadcast station licensees under this Act.

SAFE Transitional License Act This bill amends the Housing and Economic Recovery Act of 2008 to allow a loan originator to establish a state-licensed mortgage company in the United States to establish a residence in a state that is not the application state during the 30-day period preceding the date of the application. A state-licensed mortgage company shall meet certain requirements, including that it: (1) meets certain minimum licensing requirements; (2) is employed by a state-licensed mortgage company in the application state; and (3) was licensed in the United States during the 30-day period preceding the date of the application. A state-licensed mortgage company shall also meet certain requirements for state-licensed loan originators that: (1) meet certain minimum requirements for a loan originator to be a loan originator in the United States, and (2) engage in residential mortgage loan origination and processing activities.

Crime Victims' Bill of Rights Act - Amends the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure to extend the prohibition against the imposition of a sentence for the commission of a crime to include the imposition of a sentence for the imposition of a sentence for the imposition of a crime against a victim of a person who is present at the sentencing hearing of such person. 
Amends the Victims of Crime Act of 1984 to authorize the court to hear a statement by a victim of a crime against an individual who is present at the sentencing hearing of such individual. 
Amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968 to require a State to notify a victim of crime of the availability of visual and physical separation from an alleged perpetrator of such crime while waiting in a judicial facility for a courtroom appearance. 
Amends the Federal criminal code to require Federal prosecutors and law enforcement officials to provide an effective system of notice to crime victims of the existence of compensation and other programs to assist victims of crime in which those victims might be eligible to participate.

Secure Online Communication Enforcement Act of 2000 - Amends the Federal criminal code to prohibit a governmental entity from requiring a service provider to disclose to a subscriber or customer of such service or site a copy of a warrant issued under the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure or equivalent State warrant, or a grand jury or trial subpoena, before or at the same time such warrant is served on the subscriber or customer before or at the same time such warrant is served on the provider.  Authorizes such service or site to be provided to any subscriber or customer of such service or site, including Internet Web site providers. 
Requires such service or site to be made available to the public on the Internet as is, or an operator of an Internet Web site (including an agent of such operator) or other third party, for the user's convenience. 
Prohibits a provider of such services or sites from terminating the service or access to such services to an individual who refuses to consent to such disclosure.

Strengthening Homeland Security, Intelligence, and Essential Law Enforcement Departments Act of 2011 or SHIELD Act of 2011 - Requires the payment of the debt limit necessary for the military pay and allowances of the members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard, including reserve components, who perform active service during a period of lapsed appropriations.

Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to make available to the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Homeland Security in the case of the Coast Guard, during a period of lapsed appropriations, the amounts necessary to continue to provide pay and allowances (without interruption) to members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard, including reserve components, who perform active service during such period.

Requires any product which is manufactured in the United States and which is assembled, in whole or in part, from parts that are the product of a foreign country to: (1) disclose the country of origin of such part; and (2) state the proportion of the cost of such product which is accounted for by such parts.  Sets forth similar requirements with respect to the labeling of products with foreign parts.

District of Columbia Land Use Notification Act of 1993 - Amends the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 to prohibit the Administrator of the Federal Property and Administrative Services (FAPSA) from carrying out any activity affecting real property located in the District of Columbia unless:  (1) the Administrator provides a notice to the District of Columbia Mayor, the Chair of the Council of the District of Columbia, and the Chair of the Advisory Neighborhood Commission (the Council) in whose neighborhood the property is located; and (2) the Administrator provides the individuals with the opportunity to present oral or written comments before carrying out the activity. 
Prohibits a covered agency (any of the Architects of the Capitol, the National Park Service, or the Smithsonian Institution) from carrying out any activity that affects real property located in the District unless:  (1) the Administrator provides such an explanation and justification to the individuals; and (2) the Administrator provides such an opportunity to present comments to a representative of the agency before carrying out the activity. 
Provides exceptions for emergencies.

Security Enhancement and Jobs Act of 2011 - Amends federal transportation law to direct the Secretary of Transportation (DOT) to approve or deny an application to the air carrier operator for the Airport Security Administration (ASA) screening program.

Directs the Secretary to provide to the airport operator a written report that sets forth: (1) the findings that served as the basis for the denial; (2) the results of any cost or security analysis conducted in considering the application; and (3) recommendations on how the ASA can address the reasons for the denial.

Authorizes the Secretary to carry out this Act through the Assistant Secretary of Homeland Security (TSA) through the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

Fair American Corporate Tax Act or FACT Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to: (1) reduce the top marginal tax rate for certain noncorporate taxpayers; (2) increase the tax deduction for certain personal service corporations; and (3) limit the treatment of treaty benefits for certain deductions for certain noncorporate payments.

Alaska Natural Gas Pipeline Improvement Act of 2011 - Amends the Alaska Natural Gas Pipeline Act of 2004 to define "Alaska natural gas transportation project" as: (1) any natural gas pipeline system that carries Alaska natural gas to the border between Alaska and Canada (including related facilities subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission); or (2) any pipeline segment that the Commission finds could feasibly be incorporated into and serve as an integrated segment of the natural gas pipeline system.

Directs the Attorney General to establish the National Task Force on Violence against Women to develop a uniform Federal, State, and local law enforcement strategy to protect women against violent crime, punishing persons who commit such crimes, and enhancing the rights of victims of such crimes.

Authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to transfer to the Government of the Dominican Republic:  (1) the THOMASTON class dock landing ships ALAMO (LSD 33) and HERMITAGE (LSD 34); and (2) the GARCIA class frigate BRADLEY (FF 1041) and DAVIDSON (FF 1045) if such vessels are available. 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to transfer to the Government of China the "THOMASTON class dock landing ships CHINESE (LST 1195) and SHINING (LST 1183) and the "KNOX class frigate CLARK (LST 1179) and the "OLIVER HAZARD PERRY (LST 1185) class guided missile frigate CLARK." 
Authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to transfer to the Government of the United States the "NEWPORT" class tank landing ships NORTH CAROLINA (LST 1179) and NEWPORT (LST 1185) and the "K

Volunteer Firefighter and EMS Support Act of 2008 - Amends the Federal Fire Prevention and Control Act of 1974 to direct the Secretary of Homeland Security (Secretary) to establish a program to provide funds to a state or local government, non-profit firefighter association, or governmental or nongovernmental emergency medical services organization that carries out a volunteer firefighter incentive program. Defines "volunteer firefighter" as an individual who provides firefighting service or emergency medical service to a state or local government or a governmental or nongovernmental organization without pay. Requires the Secretary to pay such government, association, or organization, out of any money in the Treasury, an amount equal to the total amount of expenditures of funds not received from the federal government made by such government, association, or organization for such fiscal year to carry out the program.

Preventing Illegal Radio Abuse Through Enforcement Act or the PIRATE Act (Sec. 2) This bill amends the Communications Act of 1934 to subject to a fine of up to $2 million any person who willfully and knowingly violates the enforcement rules, regulations, or international radio or wire communications treaty or convention regarding pirate radio broadcasting. The bill also requires the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to submit to Congress a report summarizing the implementation of enforcement activities for the previous fiscal year, which may include the efforts of the FCC to enlist the cooperation of federal, state, and local law enforcement personnel (including U.S. Attorneys and U.S. Marshals Service) to service the process, collection of fines or forfeitures, seizures of equipment, and enforcement of orders. The FCC must: (1) assign appropriate enforcement personnel to focus specific and sustained attention on the elimination of pirate radio broadcasting within the top five radio markets identified as prevalent for such broadcasts, and (2) conduct monitoring sweeps to ascertain whether the pirate radio broadcasting identified by enforcement sweeps is continuing to broadcast and whether additional pirate radio broadcasting is occurring. The FCC may not prevent a state or local law prohib

Skills Connection Act - Directs the Secretary of Labor to create a publicly available, easily navigable and searchable database of credentials (credentials that may be certificates, for purposes of enabling programs that lead to such a credential to receive priority under a covered provision of the Workforce Investment Act of 1998) for employment in the manufacturing sector, as determined by the Secretary of Labor for a health care occupation. Requires the Secretary to: (1) list such credentials if they are required by federal or state law for an occupation; (2) list them, and provide an assessment of their skills; and (3) enable job seekers to enter basic information through the statewide employment statistics system, or by consulting with an organization similar to the Manufacturing Institute, and information about shortages in certain skills or credentials available to be utilized by state workforce investment board established under the Workforce Investment Board of 1998 and others to inform decisions about how to allocate workforce development resources.

Supporting America's Protective Security Advisor Act of 2007 - Amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 to establish in the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) a Protective Security Advisor Program Office within the DHS Office of Infrastructure Protection.

Requires the Office to have the primary responsibility and be the lead office within DHS for: (1) encouraging state, local, and tribal governments and private sector owners and operators of critical infrastructure and key resources to participate and collaborate within the risk management framework of the National Infrastructure Protection Plan (NIPP); (2) coordinating national and international critical infrastructure and key resource activities with state, local, and tribal governments and owners and operators of critical infrastructure or key resources; (3) facilitating and conducting requirements, capabilities, and risk analysis that enhance critical infrastructure and key resources preparedness; (4) promoting information sharing and security awareness, particularly with state homeland security advisors and private sector security officials; (5) assisting state, local, and tribal governments in developing multi-jurisdictional security plans; (6) helping to ensure ongoing coordination between federal, state, local, and tribal governments, owners and operators of critical infrastructure or key resources, emergency response providers,

Civil Rights Commission Act of 1998 - Amends the the Civil Rights Commission Act of 1983 to extend and authorize appropriations for the Commission. 
Extends the authorization of appropriations for FY 2001. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) be made permanent by the end of FY 2001; and (2) be composed of 40 Commission members appointed by the Commission's chairperson. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) be independent; and (2) submit annual financial statements to the Commission. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) implement its recommendations for a reduction in the federal government's share of certain of its public services and programs; and (2) establish a management information system to enhance its oversight and project efficiency. 
Requires the Commission to:  (1) complete and submit a report on enforcement of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990; and (2) develop and carry out a study on the civil rights implications of regulatory obstacles confronting minority entrepreneurs. 
Requires the Commission to develop and carry out a study and report to the Congress on the civil rights implications

Workers' Political Rights Act - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to prohibit a labor organization from making contributions or expenditures unless the organization meets specified requirements, including that the organization: (1) provides written notification to all employees within the labor organization's bargaining unit or units of up to 30 days after commencement of their employment; (2) makes an annual examination by an independent certified public accountant of financial statements supplied by such organization; and (3) maintains procedures to promptly determine the costs that may properly be charged to agency fee payors as costs of exclusive representation, and to explain such procedures in the written notification required under this Act.

Telecommunications Trust Act of 1998 - Amends the Communications Act of 1934 to require the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to provide universal service support for the provision of telephone and broadcaster services through appropriations of the excise tax on certain telephone and broadcaster services. 
Establishes the Telecommunications Trust Fund to provide for such support.  Authorizes appropriations for FCC fiscal years from such Fund. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for the use of the Telecommunications Trust Fund for universal service support mechanisms.

This bill requires the Department of Education (ED) to pay Fort Lewis College an amount equal to the charges for tuition for all Indian students who are not residents of the state of Colorado and who are enrolled in Fort Lewis College for academic year 2010-2011. ED shall treat such payments as reimbursements from the state to Fort Lewis College for complying with the requirement that ED pay its Indian students a certain amount of tuition. Any such payments shall be treated as payments for complying with the requirement that ED pay its Indian students a certain amount of tuition.

Rebuilding Equity Act of 2013 - Requires the Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Freddie Mac) to establish a voluntary program for borrowers, under which the enterprises shall pay $1,000 toward the closing costs associated with applying for and receiving refinancing, during the 12-month period beginning on the enactment of this Act.  Requires the Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) to adjust the amount of the closing costs by an amount that results in such program being revenue neutral for such 12-month period and based on economic conditions generally affecting the mortgage and housing markets.  Requires the program to terminate three years after its initiation.

Rural Broadband Access Enhancement Act - Amends the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 to prohibit the Secretary of Agriculture from approving an application submitted pursuant to the Rural Electrification Program to serve an area in which at least 40 percent of the population does not have access to broadband service, unless the value of the assets of the applicant not pledged or hypothecated for any other purpose equals at least 10 percent of the national average median household income.  Directs the Secretary to: (1) reduce the paperwork required of applicants under such Act; (2) conduct outreach designed to inform the population of areas in which there is no or limited broadband service of the program carried out under such Act; (3) ban loan or loan guarantee for new broadband service in community with at least three service providers; (4) eliminate the limitation on the eligibility based on number of subscriber lines; and (5) report to specified congressional committees on the status of the rural broadband program.

Security Clearance Family Review Act This bill prohibits an office, agency, or other establishment within the White House or the Executive Office of the President from granting eligibility to a relative of the President for the purposes of federal employment without a favorable determination submitted to the head of the office.  An agency, including the Department of Defense (DOD), may not grant eligibility for access to classified information to a relative of the President for the purposes of federal employment unless a favorable determination is submitted to the head of the agency.  DOD may not grant access to classified information to a relative of the President if the President determines that a relative requires access to classified information for federal employment.  DOD shall: (1) review whether the relative has any ongoing and substantial commercial relationships with state-owned or privately owned foreign enterprises or financial institutions, and if so, whether the relative is ineligible for access to security clearance because of such relationships, for purposes of determining eligibility for access to such information; and (2) submit the determination made to the President.  DOD shall: (1) conduct a review to determine whether the relative has any ongoing and substantial commercial relationships with state-owned or privately owned foreign enterprises or financial institutions, and if so, whether the relative is inelig

States that Cape Fox Corporation shall not be required to select or receive conveyance of Federal land in the vicinity of its existing land conveyance.
Authorizes Cape Fox to select, and, upon receiving written notice of such selection, the Secretary of the Interior to convey, the approximately 99 acres of the surface estate of Tongass National Forest land located outside the exterior selection boundary of Cape Fox.
Directs the Secretary to convey to Cape Fox the subsurface estate of the Tongass National Forest land and to Sealaska Corporation the subsurface estate of the land selected.
Declares that the conveyance of land to Cape Fox and Sealaska Corporation under this Act is considered to fulfill the entitlement of the land to any subsurface interest in it.
This bill designates Gateway Arch and Old St. Louis Courthouse as National Historic Landmarks.  The Jefferson National Expansion Memorial is hereby designated as National Historic Landmarks.

Department of Defense Office of the Victim Advocate Act of 2004 - Establishes in the Department of Defense (DOD) an Office of the Victim Advocate, headed by a Director, to: (1) coordinate military programs and activities relating to victims of interpersonal violence among members of the armed forces or between members of the armed forces and family members and partners; and (2) serve as the headquarters program manager for the victim advocates and the victim service specialists in DOD's Department of Defense (DOD) armed forces. Requires the Director to carry out specified coordination functions, including: (1) evaluating the prevalence of interpersonal violence associated with members of the armed forces; (2) evaluating military programs to address sexual misconduct and intimate partner violence; (3) establishing system accountability standards; (4) developing protocols for accountability of commanders; (5) serving on any fatality review panel established by the Secretary of a military department; and (6) conducting programs of public education.

Amends the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act to repeal the ownership based on Aboriginal lands requirement for the study and recording of cultural items that were not discovered after November 16, 1990. 
Requires the recording and study of cultural items that are discovered after November 16, 1990, except those items whose ownership or control is established under specified circumstances. 
Authorizes the recording and study of cultural items that are discovered after November 16, 1990, except those items whose ownership or control is established under specified circumstances. 
Requires the recording and study of cultural items that are discovered after November 16, 1990, except those items whose ownership or control is established under specified circumstances. 
Authorizes the recording and study of cultural items that are discovered after November 16, 1990, except those items whose ownership or control is established under specified circumstances. 
Requires the recording and study of cultural items that are discovered after November 16, 1990, except those items whose ownership or control is established under specified circumstances. 
Authorizes the recording and study of cultural items that are discovered after November

Transparency and Accountability ofFailed Exchanges Act This bill amends the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act to require a state that is awarded a grant under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) to establish an Exchange and that terminates the operation of such Exchange or otherwise transfers the operation to an entity other than the state in which the state was awarded or transferred.  The state must report on its results and the state must provide to the Department of Justice (DOJ) any property acquired with amounts awarded to it pursuant to such grant.  Funds rescinded under this Act shall be retained in the general fund of the Treasury for federal budget deficit reduction.  The bill preempts any state enforcement action of alleged fraud, waste, or abuse of funds issued pursuant to PPACA.  The Attorney General may bring an action before the appropriate district court to enforce PPACA violations.

Transnational Criminal Organization Illicit Spotter Prevention and Elimination Act - Amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to impose enhanced penalties for the unauthorized entry, or attempted entry, of aliens smuggling, border control, and customs enforcement into the United States.

Amends the criminal code to: (1) increase the fine and imprisonment penalties for the crime of violence; (2) expand the criminal code to include crimes committed with intent to further a federal crime relating to U.S. immigration, customs, controlled substances, monetary instruments, or other border controls; and (3) impose criminal penalties for the conspiring or attempting to violate specified provisions of the criminal code.

Energy-Efficient Cool Roof Jobs Act - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to revise the depreciation recovery period for certain commercial property which is placed in service above conditioned or semi-heated space on an eligible commercial building. Defines "qualified energy-efficient cool roof replacement property" as any roof system placed in service above conditioned or semi-heated space on an eligible commercial building which has a slope equal to or less than 2:12, 3:12, or 7:8 and which replaces an existing roof system and includes insulation which meets or exceeds the minimum prescriptive requirements in tables A-1 to A-9 in the Normative Appendix A of ASHRAE Standard 189.1-2011, and in the case of an eligible commercial building located in a climate zone other than a zone 6,7, or 8, a primary roof covering which has a cool roof surface. Defines "cool roof surface" as a roof the exterior surface of which has a 3-year-aged solar reflectance of at least 0.55 and a 3-year-aged thermal emittance of at least 0.75, as determined in accordance with the Cool Roof Rating Council

Nye County Higher Education Campus Conveyance Act - Directs the Secretary of Education to convey to the University of Nevada, Nevada, and the Community College System of Nevada, Nevada, specified parcels of land in Pahrump Valley, Nevada, to the University system for use as a campus for the College.

Requires the Secretary to: (1) pay any administrative costs associated with such conveyance, including the cost of any environmental, wildlife, cultural, or historical resources studies; (2) use the federal land conveyed for educational and recreational purposes; (3) release and indemnify the United States from claims or liabilities that may arise from uses carried out on the federal land on or before this Act's enactment date by the United States or any person; (4) to erect an appropriate and centrally located monument that acknowledges the conveyance of the federal land for the purpose of furthering the higher education of citizens in Nevada; and (5) assist the Bureau of Land Management in providing information to the students of the college and the citizens of Nevada on public land and the role of the Bureau of Land Management in managing, preserving, and protecting the public land.

Protect Marriage from the Courts Act of 2015 This bill amends the federal judicial code to prohibit a court created by federal law from having jurisdiction, and the Supreme Court from having jurisdiction, to adjudicate or enforce any claim pertaining to the validity, under the Constitution, of a state law, or state administrative or judicial decision that:   defines marriage as limited to the union of one man and one woman; or   refuses state recognition of or allows the state to refuse recognition of same-sex marriages performed and licensed in other states.   The bill also prohibits a court created by federal law or the Supreme Court from entering a final judgment on a claim before the effective date of this Act.  A court created by federal law or the Supreme Court has entered a final judgment on a claim before the effective date of this Act.  Amend the bill to declare that this limitation on federal jurisdiction shall not be affected.

Fairness for Working Americans Act of 2004 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to increase the rate of the child tax credit to 10 percent beginning after January 1, 2005. Prescribes a formula for computing the credit's earned income.Prohibits the acquiring corporation from receiving a tax credit for investment in a U.S. corporation for taxable years beginning after 2003.
Higher Education Savings Plan Act of 1993 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide for a 10 percent penalty on premature distributions from annuity contracts for higher education expenses.

Grants a Federal charter to the National Academy of Inventors, a not-for-profit organization that meets the requirements under the internal revenue code and is organized under the laws of the State of Florida, as provided under its bylaws and articles of incorporation.

Accelerating Kids' Access to Care Act This bill amends title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to require a state Medicaid program to provide a streamlined screening and enrollment process for eligible out-of-state providers and suppliers. The bill defines "eligible out- of-state provider or supplier" as a provider or supplier of medical or other items or services furnished to a child for which Medicaid payment is available. The requirements for the streamlined screening and enrollment process shall be the same as for a process for enrolling in a state Medicaid program. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services must establish a process for permitting a provider or a supplier, as the case may be, to elect, at the same time, to enroll in the state Medicaid program.

Public Library Innovation Space Act - Amends the Museum and Library Services Act to direct the Director of the National Museum of Library Service to carry out a program to make competitive grants to eligible partnerships to establish makerspaces at public libraries. Requires the Director to consider: (1) the viability of the partnership making the grant; (2) the ability of the partnership to meet the matching requirement; (3) the potential of the project to provide social and economic benefits to the local community; (4) the support of local communities, government, and partnerships for the project; (5) the project's potential for strengthening the involvement of diverse and underserved communities in entrepreneurship and economic development; and (6) the project's ability to continue after the end of the grant period. Prohibits an eligible partnership that receives a grant from using grant funds, or matching funds contributed by the partnership, for construction activities at a public library that would provide extra square footage to house a makerspace.

Rural Equity Payment Index Reform Act of 2003 - Amends title XVIII (Medicare) of the Social Security Act to revise the work index for payment under Medicare. Prohibits the wage index applied for payment under Medicare from being less than: (1) 0.976 for services furnished during 2004 through 2006; (2) 0.987 for services furnished during 2005 through 2007; and (3) 1.000 for services furnished during 2007 and subsequent years.

Campaign Sunlight Act of 2012 - Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to direct the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to establish and operate the Campaign Accountability Site (a public website dedicated to the dissemination of political advertisements) through which members of the public may view the contents of political advertisements.

Requires the FEC to: (1) make the contents of a political advertisement available for viewing in the same format through which the advertisement was disseminated; and (2) make the sources of the content available on the website directly or through hyperlinks to the sources.

Requires sponsors of advertisements to provide the contents of the advertisement on the website, in the format they may require, directly or through hyperlinks to the sources.

Requires the FEC to pay the sponsors of political advertisements the amount of any such fee.

Defines a "political advertisement" as a communication that is subject to the 120-day period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act.

Veterans Justice Outreach Act of 2015 This bill directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to carry out a program to support veterans in contact with the criminal justice system by prohibiting unnecessary criminalization of mental illness and other nonviolent crimes. The VA shall establish coordinators to provide outreach to veterans at risk of homelessness.

Higher Education Family Opportunity Act of 1998 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow an individual a tax deduction for certain expenses incurred in order to qualify for a higher education tuition and related expenses tax credit.  Allows a tax deduction for qualified tuition and related expenses and a limited deduction for certain student expenses.
Grants a Federal charter to the Black Veterans of America.

Anti-Pyramid Scheme Act of 2016 This bill prohibits any person from establishing, operating, promoting, or causing to be promoted a pyramid promotional scheme. A violation is an unfair or deceptive act or practice in, or affecting, commerce that results in: (1) an unfair or deceptive act or practice in, or affecting, commerce under the Federal Trade Commission Act (FTCA); or (2) a violation of the Federal Trade Commission Act.  The FTCA shall be enforced by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) by the same means that it was enforced by the Federal Trade Commission Act under the Trade and Worker Protection Act.
Medical Savings Account Availability Act of 2001 - Amends the Internal Revenue Code to repeal limitations on the availability of individual medical savings accounts.

International Peacekeeping Reform Act of 1997 - Prohibits the use of funds made available to the Department of State for the United Nations Peacekeeping Activities or any other funds made available to the Department of State for the United Nations for the establishment, expansion, or modification in size, or the modification of a U.N. peacekeeping operation, unless the President certifies to Congress that the United Nations Peacekeeping operation meets certain requirements, including that the operation involves an international conflict in which hostilities have ceased and all significant parties agree to the imposition of U.N. peacekeeping forces for the purpose of seeking an enduring solution to the conflict.  Requires the President to certify to Congress that the U.S. armed forces participating in the operation directly advances U.S. national security interests and the participation of such units is critical to the success of the operation.
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to allow a tax credit for certain child disability education and training expenses. Limits the amount of such credit to $3,000 for the taxable year.

Amends the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act to recognize the village of Alexander Creek, Incorporated, a Group Corporation organized pursuant to such Act located within T. 15 N., R. 7 W., Seward Meridian, Alaska, as an eligible Native village.

Directs the Secretary of the Interior to negotiate with Alexander Creek to fairly and equitably settle any aboriginal land claims and any other claims that Alexander Creek has against the United States.

Requires the Secretary to enter into an agreement with Alexander Creek relating to the claims.

Rural Broadband Enhancement Act - Amends the National Telecommunications and Information Administration Organization Act to direct the Rural Utilities Service of the Department of Agriculture (USDA) to make loans or other extensions of credit to certain non-Federal public or private entities to provide funds for the construction, improvement, and acquisition of facilities and equipment for the provision of broadband service in eligible rural communities.

Requires a project meeting the requirements of this Act to be made available in accordance with the requirements of the Federal Credit Reform Act of 1990, which shall not affect the validity of any loan or extension of credit made under this Act before the date specified in that Act's provision of such credit.

Authorizes appropriations for the Department of Commerce for the cost of such loans or other extensions of credit.

Amends Federal military retired pay provisions to: (1) increase the retirement pay of members of the National Guard and reserve who perform qualifying hazardous duty and who retire on or after the date of enactment of this Act; and (2) provide for the special tax treatment of tax credit amounts for such employees. Directs the Comptroller General to study and report to Congress on the appropriateness of expanding the Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps program of each of the military departments, the Civil Air Patrol, the Naval Sea Cadet Corps, and the Young Marines of the Marine Corps League.

Rebuild American Manufacturing Act of 2013 - Directs the President to develop a national manufacturing strategy. Requires the President to include in the national manufacturing strategy short- and long-term goals for U.S. manufacturing, including goals to: (1) increase the aggregate number of manufacturing jobs so that such number is not less than 20% of the sum of all nonfarm jobs in the United States; (2) identify emerging technologies to strengthen the competitiveness of U.S. manufacturing in the global marketplace; and (3) strengthen the manufacturing sectors of the United States in which the United States is most competitive in the global economy. Requires the national manufacturing strategy to include: (1) a survey of all persons with headquarters in the United States that maintain manufacturing facilities outside of the United States to identify categories of products manufactured at such facilities, and (2) a survey of all federal agencies that provide assistance to U.S. manufacturers, including the Department of Commerce, the Department of Defense, the Department of Energy, the Department of the Treasury, the Small Business Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, the Office of Science and Technology Policy, and the National Science Foundation. Higher Education Fairness Act of 1997 - Amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to allow a tax credit for up to $2,250 of the value of a student's family contribution to an educational institution. 
Amends the Internal Revenue Code to provide a different income protection allowance for dependent students without dependent parents.
Grants a Federal charter to the American Military Retirees Association (a nonprofit organization that meets the requirements of the Internal Revenue Code and is organized under the laws of New York).

National Park Centennial Challenge Fund Act - Establishes in the Treasury the National Park Centennial Challenge Fund. Requires the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director, to develop a list of signature projects and programs eligible for funding from the Challenge Fund. Authorizes the Secretary, acting through the Director, to add any project or program to the list.

Air Traffic Supervisor Retirement Reform Act of 1995 - Amends Federal civil service retirement system provisions to provide for the separation of an individual from a position as a controller (for purposes of Federal employees' Retirement System provisions) if such individual was first appointed to any such position before the effective date of this Act.

Public Servant Priority Placement Act of 1995 - Amends Federal law to direct the Director of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to establish a government-wide program to facilitate employment placement for Federal employees affected by reduction in force actions.

Sportsmanship in Hunting Act of 2008 - Amends the federal criminal code to prohibit knowingly transferring, transporting, or possessing a confined animal for the purpose of allowing the killing or injuring of that animal for entertainment or for the collection of a trophy. Makes an exception for the killing or injuring of an exotic animal in a state or federal natural area reserve undertaking habitat restoration.

Defines "captivity" as a mammal of a species not historically indigenous to the United States, that has been held in captivity, whether or not the defendant knows the length of the captivity, for the shorter of: (1) the majority of the animal's life; or (2) a period of one year, with a period of not less than one year.

Authorizes the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to: (1) without a warrant, arrest any person that violates this Act; (2) execute any warrant or other process issued by an officer or court of competent jurisdiction to enforce this Act; and (3) with a search warrant, search for and seize any animal taken or possessed in violation of this Act.

Helping College Students Cross the Finish Line Act This bill amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to direct the Department of Education (ED) to award grants to institutions of higher education to establish financial assistance programs to assist undergraduates and vocational students with financial need to assist in completing their degree or certificate programs. ED shall create and submit to the Department a report on the number of students enrolled at each grant recipient's institution who received an award.
